title: PIPENUM-01: a check that passes against a tree that is not there
goal: After task_974, exactly one check still reports PASS against a root that does not exist: `check_pipeline_numbering: Pipeline numbering and ordinals verified dense`. Unlike the 54 stubs it DOES take `ctx` -- so it reads the tree, finds nothing, and calls an empty set dense.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd drift-check --root <nonexistent>` reports zero checks as PASS, and the remaining 20 ctx-reading checks are each audited for an empty-set path.

Progress -- the first half is DONE and the audit is done too.** `miosd drift-check --root <a directory that does not exist>` now reports **0 passed, 12 failed, 62 skipped**. Not one check claims a verdict about a tree that is not there.

Two measurement bugs of my own, both found by checking the checker.** First, `check_pipeline_numbering` was not a "ctx-reading check with an empty-set path" as filed -- it was a STUB, and `mios-gate drift-stubs` classified it as implemented because the predicate tested the PARAMETER NAME. It read `ctx.in_image` for an early skip and then returned a constant `Pass`. The gate now classifies by whether the body consults `ctx.root`, which is the property. Second, my own audit script reported a false positive for `check_names_registry` because rustfmt splits `ctx\n    .root` and the scan matched the literal `ctx.root`. Both are pinned by regression tests: `a_blind_check_named_ctx_is_still_blind` and `a_reader_whose_ctx_root_is_line_split_is_not_a_stub`.

Implemented rather than registered.** Adding it to `[drift.unimplemented]` meant raising `max_unimplemented` 54 -> 55, which `check_ratchet_direction` correctly rejected -- a shrink-only ceiling may not be raised, and the repo said so before I could rationalise it. So the check was ported from its bash twin's three assertions: no hand-written `[98-drift-checks] (N)` labels, `build.sh` not re-counting the chain via `ls|wc -l`, and `drift-gate-index.tsv` ordinals dense 1..N. Stub count stays 54, ceiling stays 54.

One deliberate divergence from the twin: bash SKIPS when `drift-gate-index.tsv` is absent, which is an Empty-Set Pass. The Rust version FAILS -- a missing SSOT projection is exactly what this suite exists to catch.

Verified: the real tree PASSES having read three files; a planted hand-written label, a planted ordinal gap, an emptied index, and a nonexistent root each FAIL with the specific reason. Fixtures restored.
Corrected count for the remaining audit: 17 ctx-reading checks read `ctx.root`, not 20.**

The audit is now DONE, with planted-but-empty fixtures rather than a missing tree.** Built a root where every directory the suite reads EXISTS and every file in it is zero bytes. Three checks reported PASS against it:
`check_ssot_parse` -- an empty file is valid TOML, so "parses successfully" was true of a zero-byte `mios.toml`. Now requires at least one top-level table; the real tree reports **157**.

`check_backfill_coverage` -- zero `emb vector` tables made "all covered" vacuously true. Now fails when the scan finds none, because the shipped schema always has them and finding zero means the scan failed. The real tree reports **25**.

`check_law_enforcers` -- **a third stub in disguise.** It called `ctx.root.join(...)`, tested `.exists()`, and returned `Pass("Law enforcers resolution validated clean")` without ever opening the file. Building a path is not reading the tree, which is why two successive stub detectors let it through.
Zero checks now pass against a present-but-empty tree**, and the real tree still reads `19 passed, 0 failed, 55 skipped`.

`check_law_enforcers` is implemented rather than registered**, for the same reason as `check_pipeline_numbering`: registering would raise `max_unimplemented` and `check_ratchet_direction` forbids that. CLAUDE.md calls `[laws]` the canonical registry, so the check now validates it -- ids dense 1..N, slugs present and unique, `applies_to` in {bootc, wsl, both}, `enforced_by` non-empty, and every named symbol actually present in the named `automation/` file. Real tree: **16 laws each resolve to an enforcer that exists.** Negative controls: a dangling enforcer name, an id gap, and an invalid `applies_to` each fail with the specific reason.

One scheme learned along the way: Law 15's `enforced_by` is `process:...`, which is legitimate -- triple-check-before-acting cannot be gated, only followed. The check accepts `process:` and still requires the descriptor to say something.

details.what_how:
Textbook Empty-Set Pass, and the last one visible in the native suite now that the constant-Pass stubs are silent. A check whose subject is absent must say so. The fix is the same shape as the two registers landed this session: if the scan finds zero phase scripts, that is could-not-run, never clean.
  Worth doing as the template for the other twenty implemented checks, which have not been audited for the same shape.
details.why: task_967's thesis, in the one place left where it was still demonstrably true.

extra.value: Law 15's descriptor names its parity gates by ORDINAL -- "98-drift-checks.sh checks 22+27" -- which is exactly the drift `check_pipeline_numbering` exists to prevent, and it is now stale besides: task_970 made `check_bootstrap_sync` the runnable gate for the mirrored-surface half of that law. Left alone deliberately; rewriting a law's descriptor is the operator's call.

title: STUBPRED-01: a path join is not a read, and two checks still claim without looking
goal: `mios-gate drift-stubs` classifies a check as implemented if its `run` body mentions `ctx.root` or passes `ctx` onward. That is the third version of this predicate and it is still wrong: `ctx.root.join("x")` builds a PATH, and `.exists()` asks whether a file is there. Neither reads anything. A check can do both and then return a constant `Pass`.
acceptance_criteria: the predicate requires a read or a delegation; no check reaches `Verdict::Pass` having only called `.exists()`; the eleven delegating checks still classify as implemented; and the ceiling has not risen. **All four hold.**

Done, and it found a FOURTH stub plus something worse.** The tightened predicate flushed out `check_names_registry` as well: it tested whether a DEBUG BUILD of `generate-names-registry` existed and, if so, returned `Pass("Names registry projection matches SSOT")` without running it -- and if the binary was absent it SKIPPED. Silent on an ordinary tree, lying on a developer's. All four are implemented rather than registered, because the ceiling may not rise:

`check_deploy_plane` -- ported from the bash twin: the kickstart must export `MIOS_FHS_TOTAL_ROOT_MERGE=1` (the Total Root Merge is what makes `.git` IS `/` true at install time) and carry `BOOTSTRAP_REPO`/`MIOS_REPO` overrides; `ventoy.json` must point its `Fedora-Server.iso` entry at `mios-kickstart.cfg`. Unlike the twin, an absent subject FAILS rather than printing a WARNING -- these are tracked deliverables.

`check_bib_single_config_invariant` -- every `config/artifacts/*.toml` parses, and every Justfile recipe invoking `bootc-image-builder` mounts **exactly one** `/config.toml`. Real tree: 4 BIB recipes, 5 artifact recipes.
`check_names_registry` -- a real regenerate-and-compare.

`regen_and_diff` does not diff.** Reading it to reuse it revealed the helper runs the generator and then asserts the target **exists**. That is only sound when the generator itself compares -- when `--check` is passed and its exit status is the verdict. All five existing callers do pass it, so this was a latent trap rather than a live defect. My first cut of `check_names_registry` called it WITHOUT `--check`, and the planted-drift control passed: the generator had rewritten the file before the "comparison". A helper named `regen_and_diff` that silently does neither is the trap that catches whoever reuses it next, so it now **refuses** to run without `--check` and names why. `regen_and_diff_shell` was audited too and is sound -- it renders into a scratch dir seeded from the committed artifact.

The replacement, `regen_and_compare_file`, snapshots the target, runs the generator, compares, and restores. The tree is left exactly as found whether it passes or fails. Its negative control is the one that had silently passed: planting a name into `referenced_names.txt` now reports `is stale: committed 26741 bytes, ... renders 26717`.

  - `check_law_enforcers` -- FIXED in task_980, implemented rather than registered.

title: MERGERATCHET-01: a shrink-only ratchet cannot see a base-branch merge
goal: `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` is shrink-only and its message is "This ratchet only comes DOWN: fold or delete, do not raise it." That rule is right for code the branch writes and wrong for code the branch *inherits*. Merging `origin/main` @`04fd07a4` into this branch raised the measurement by 14 lines that belong to main's own `a328b2fd`, and the only ways out are to raise a ceiling the check forbids raising, or to delete someone else's fix.
acceptance_criteria: merging a base branch that grew tooling Python does not trip the ratchet, while a commit on the branch that adds a single Python line still does -- both proved by planting; a ceiling raised in an earlier commit on the branch still FAILS (which it does not today); and the ceiling's recorded provenance names the base commit it was baselined against.

details.what_how:
Measured across the merge, not estimated. Merge base `193798e5` measures 121093 tooling-Python lines; `origin/main` @`04fd07a4` measures 121107, so main contributed **+14**. This branch's pre-merge measurement was 121254 against a ceiling of exactly 121254, and the merged tree measures 121269 -- 121254 + 14 + **1**, the one remaining line being a deliberate single-line comment in `tools/render-globals.py` marking why that line is not an f-string (the defect that stopped the file PARSING on the bake interpreter, task_968). So 14 of the 15 are unremovable by this branch by construction.
  The register has no concept of provenance. Give the ratchet a floor that moves with the merge base: record the base commit alongside the ceiling, and on a merge re-baseline by the base's own delta rather than by the total, so the branch remains accountable only for what it added. Equivalently: measure the branch's contribution as `measured - base_measured` and ratchet THAT.
  Until then a merge is indistinguishable from an author adding Python, and the honest raise this commit makes looks exactly like the dishonest one the check exists to stop -- which is the actual defect.
**Second defect, found while landing the merge above:** `check_ratchet_direction` compares the WORKTREE against `git show HEAD:usr/share/mios/mios.toml` and nothing else. So it guards the *edit*, not the *branch*: the moment a raise is committed, HEAD carries it and the check goes green. Proved, not predicted -- the 121254 -> 121269 raise failed the check while uncommitted and reported `OK: All 76 shrink-only ratchet ceilings are <= HEAD` immediately after the merge commit, with the raise still in the tree. A ceiling raised in any earlier commit on a branch is therefore invisible to it forever, and the only raise it can ever catch is one sitting unstaged in front of it. It should compare against the MERGE BASE with the target branch, not against HEAD; then a raise is visible for the life of the PR and the base-branch delta above becomes measurable in the same pass.

PROVED on a throwaway branch: raise a ceiling, COMMIT it, gate reports `80 shrink-only ceiling(s) are <= HEAD` at rc=0. CI always runs on a commit, so this gate has never caught a raise there -- the shrink-only guarantee it exists to enforce has never held across a commit. FIX: resolve the baseline as MIOS_RATCHET_BASE, else the merge base with the default branch, else HEAD -- and when it falls back to HEAD the summary SAYS it is comparing the worktree against its own parent, so the weakness is visible rather than silent. DECISIVE CONTROL: one tree, one binary, only the baseline differs -- merge base CATCHES `agent_pipe.max_consecutive_failures INCREASED from 3 to 99`, HEAD reports 80 clean. Three earlier probes proved nothing and each fault was the PROBE: 99999 was below the base's 121210; then the key did not exist at the base at all (introduced on this branch, so not a raise); only a ceiling present in BOTH trees is a valid subject. STILL OPEN as task_3398: CI checks out at depth 1, so no merge base exists there and it still falls back to HEAD -- correct behaviour today is preserved, but the gate is only live on a full clone

## task_984 -- BUDGETKEYS-01: the budget gate checked 9 of 128 keys and said "all"  (WS-DRIFT | P2 | M)
**Goal:** `check_agent_pipe_budgets` prints "all [agent_pipe] budget variables have code consumers". `BUDGET_KEYS` in `tools/native/mios-aiplane-lint` was a hardcoded list of **nine** names and the lint walked that list, never the tables. The tables hold **128** scalar leaves, so the check covered 7% of its own subject and announced the other 93%. Adding an unconsumed key to `[agent_pipe]` passed at rc=0 on both the Rust and the Python leg -- planted and measured, not suspected. It was also a registry of operator-tunable names living in Rust source rather than in SSOT (Law 7).
**What+How:** Replaced the constant with `budget_keys()`, which walks every scalar leaf under `[agent_pipe]` and `[dispatch]` including nested tables. Measured the residue rather than assuming it: **9 of 128 have no consumer**, itemised in `[drift.budget_keys].unconsumed` with `max_unconsumed = 9`, shrink-only, ceiling-may-not-exceed-measurement.
  The search surface was also too narrow and would have produced a FALSE positive. The lint read `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe` alone; `[dispatch].gpu_profile` is read by `usr/libexec/mios/mios-swarm-pack-firstboot`, so widening the key set without widening the search would have reported a load-bearing key dead. `CONSUMER_DIRS` now covers `usr/lib/mios`, `usr/libexec/mios`, `src/mios-rs` and `tools/native`, across `.py`/`.sh`/`.rs` plus the extensionless libexec verbs, excluding `target/`, `.venv/` and `node_modules/`. That is what takes the residue from 10 to 9.
  Two of the nine -- `reflexion_limit` and `tool_loop_limit` -- appear in `tools/drift-checks.py`, but only as key names it asserts are PRESENT in the TOML. Naming a key is not consuming it, and that is precisely how they stayed dead while looking alive to a grep. Registered as dead, with that noted.
  The register is itemised rather than a count, for the reason the `[docs]` ratchet already demonstrates: a bare ceiling lets one dead key swap for another with the gate none the wiser.
**Verified** (each control fails for its planted reason, fixtures restored):
  - an unconsumed key added to `[agent_pipe]` -- **the exact case that passed at rc=0 before** -- now exits 1 naming it;
  - a registered key that gains a consumer exits 1 with "registered key(s) now HAVE a consumer";
  - a ceiling above the measurement exits 1 with "a ceiling above the measurement is slack";
  - a manifest declaring neither table exits 1 with "nothing was checked" rather than reporting that all zero keys are consumed;
  - clean tree: `119 of 128 keys consumed, 9 registered unconsumed (ceiling 9)`, rc=0.
  Crate tests 3 -> 6, the three new ones covering the enumeration, the empty-table case and the regression itself.
**Remaining:** the nine registered keys are knobs an operator can set to no effect. Each wants wiring or deleting; the register exists to keep them visible, not to bless them.
**Dep:** task_962
**Status:** done | **Domain:** Gates/Honesty | **Who:** architect

title: PROJREG-01: the Law 8 registry is never checked for completeness
goal: `check_projection_registry` walks `[laws.projection_registry].surfaces` and asserts, for each entry, that the generator exists on disk and the check function exists in `98-drift-checks.sh`. That is the forward direction only. Nothing asks the reverse -- *is every generator ON the registry* -- so a generator can write a tracked artifact with no drift check and the registry reports clean. A one-directional check over a register is the same shape as an unanchored allowlist: it validates what it was told about and is silent on what it was not.
acceptance_criteria: a generator added to `tools/` that writes a tracked file and is not registered FAILS the gate -- proved by planting one; every one of the 15 is either registered with a check that exists or itemised as exempt with a reason; and the negative test fails against the pre-repair check so it is not vacuous.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Measured, not sampled. 21 generators on disk (`tools/generate-*.py` + `tools/render-*.py`); the registry names **5** of them. Splitting the other 16 by whether `98-drift-checks.sh` or `tools/drift-checks.py` mentions the generator at all:
  - **15 are a bookkeeping gap** -- unregistered, but the gate does exercise them under some other name (`generate-adr-index`, `generate-bake-plan`, `generate-bib-configs`, `generate-blade-karg`, `generate-cargo-manifests`, `generate-cockpit-conf`, `generate-egress-firewall`, `generate-gate-index`, `generate-ipa-enroll-env`, `generate-metal-vs-hosted`, `generate-names-registry`, `generate-pipeline-index`, `generate-uki-cmdline`, `render-manpages`, `render-ports`). The register is incomplete as a register; those surfaces are not unguarded.
  - **1 was a real hole** -- `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py`, unregistered AND unmentioned: a security artifact projected from SSOT with neither half of Law 8. Closed in task_984's follow-up by `mios-gate signature-policy` + the registry entry. It is named here because *how it stayed invisible* is this task, not that one.
  **The generator -> check mapping is now established and verified**, so the next pass does not repeat it. Every one of the 15 has a `check_*` function that exists in `98-drift-checks.sh` (confirmed by regex against the file, not assumed):

  | generator | check |
  |---|---|
  | `generate-adr-index.py` | `check_adr_index` |
  | `generate-bake-plan.py` | `check_bake_plan` |
  | `generate-bib-configs.py` | `check_bib_configs_projection` |
  | `generate-blade-karg.py` | `check_blade_karg` |
  | `generate-cargo-manifests.py` | `check_cargo_manifest_generated` |
  | `generate-cockpit-conf.py` | `check_cockpit_projection` |
  | `generate-egress-firewall.py` | `check_egress_firewall` |
  | `generate-gate-index.py` | `check_gate_index` |
  | `generate-ipa-enroll-env.py` | `check_ipa_enroll_projection` |
  | `generate-metal-vs-hosted.py` | `check_metal_vs_hosted` |
  | `generate-names-registry.py` | `check_names_registry` |
  | `generate-pipeline-index.py` | `check_pipeline_numbering` |
  | `generate-uki-cmdline.py` | `check_uki_cmdline_projection` |
  | `render-manpages.py` | `check_manpages` |
  | `render-ports.py` | `check_ports_category_schema` |

  **Two ways the mapping can be got wrong, both hit while deriving it:**
  - Matching the *enclosing* function of any mention attributes `render-ports.py` to `check_renderer_gate_coverage`, which is a META-check that merely lists `35-render-ports.sh` in an allowlist. Its real check is `check_ports_category_schema`. Mention is not subject.
  - Filtering invocations on a literal `python3` misses `check_pipeline_numbering`, which invokes its generator via `"$PYTHON"`. That produced a false "NOT INVOKED -- possible hole" for `generate-pipeline-index.py` until it was checked by hand. It IS guarded.

  What remains: each entry also needs its `output` field, and that must be read from the generator rather than inferred -- several take `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` as INPUT, so a naive path scan attributes the SSOT to them as output. Add the reverse assertion first: every generator that writes into the tracked tree appears in `[laws.projection_registry].surfaces` with a check that exists. Anything genuinely exempt (writes only to `/etc` at runtime, or emits nothing tracked) goes on an itemised shrink-only register with its reason, not a bare count.
  Belongs in `mios-gate` (Rust): the standing directive, and `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` has no headroom for a new Python check.

extra.value:
`mios-gate projection-coverage` (`src/mios-rs/mios-gate/src/projreg.rs`), wired as `check_projection_coverage`. It reads `[laws.projection_registry].generator_globs` from SSOT, enumerates what they match (21 generators), and asserts each is on `.surfaces` or itemised on `.exempt` with a reason. All 15 rows added with their `output` read from each generator's writer, not inferred -- `render-ports.py` is the case that proves the difference: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` is BOTH its input and, for the flat `[ports]` table, its output. `exempt = []`, `max_exempt = 0`, so a new generator cannot ship unregistered.
  **Non-redundancy is measured, not argued.** With an unregistered generator planted under `tools/`, the pre-repair `check_projection_registry` exits 0 and reports "registry verified clean"; `check_projection_coverage` exits 1 and names the file. Same tree, same plant, opposite verdicts.
  **The first draft reproduced the defect it was written to catch.** Its scope came from the SSOT globs, which made those globs its own allowlist: deleting `"tools/render-*.py"` took the scope from 21 generators to 17 and still exited 0. The register now anchors the globs from outside -- any directory a glob names is in scope, so a registry row living there that no glob matches is a finding. Caught by running a negative control that was not on the plan, not by review.
  **Not done here, deliberately:** `check_projection_registry` (bash+Python, forward direction) is left in place rather than folded in. It is one of `[laws]` id 8's two named enforcers and has its own negative test; consolidating it is an ADR-0021 strangler step, not a side effect of this one.

title: LAWPTR-01: four laws name an enforcer that is a comment after `exit 0`
goal: `[laws]` ids 3, 5, 10 and 11 declare `enforced_by = "99-postcheck.sh:item14 / item12 / item16 / item17"`. No `item12`, `item14`, `item16` or `item17` exists anywhere in `automation/99-postcheck.sh` -- it defines two functions, `_sysusers_effective` and `_gid_in_etc_group`, and nothing else. All four names occur exactly once in the repo: the file's LAST line, `# References for laws: item14 item12 item16 item17`, sitting after `exit 0` where it can never execute.
acceptance_criteria: every `[laws].enforced_by` target resolves to live code under a predicate that rejects a comment and rejects text after `exit 0`; deleting the `# References for laws:` line leaves the gate green; planting a law whose enforcer name appears only in a comment FAILS; and the same predicate strength applies to both files, so `99-postcheck.sh` is no longer the weak side.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
The reason nothing notices is the shape of the checker, not an oversight in the register. `check_law_enforcers` splits `enforced_by` on `:` and then branches on the filename:
  - for `98-drift-checks.sh` it requires a FUNCTION DEFINITION -- `re.search(rf"^{ref}\s*\(\)", drift_code, re.MULTILINE)`;
  - for `99-postcheck.sh` it requires only `ref in postcheck_code` -- a bare substring, anywhere, comments and dead code included.
  So the weaker predicate is applied to exactly the file that carries a comment naming the four missing refs. The check reports "all `[laws].enforced_by` targets resolve in codebase" and is, for a quarter of the laws, resolving against its own epitaph. Self-Certifying Predicate: the artifact that satisfies the check exists only because the check exists.
  **The laws themselves ARE enforced -- this is a pointer defect, not an enforcement hole.** Measured rather than assumed, because the first reading of this was wrong: `99-postcheck.sh` was restructured (026e4f70) from numbered items into inline top-level blocks, each of which `die`s with its law's slug. Present and live: `BOUND-IMAGES: Quadlet/binder drift` and `BOUND-IMAGES-RESOLVE: Image '...' was not baked` (Law 3), `UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS: vendor cloud URL found in active config` and two siblings (Law 5), `UNPRIVILEGED-QUADLETS: Quadlet privilege check failed` (Law 6), five `BARE-SAFE-ENV:` dies (Law 10), `SECRETS-NEVER-IN-ENV: a secret-bearing env file is not mode 0600` (Law 11). What was lost in the restructure is the NAME each law points at, and the comment was appended to keep the pointer check green rather than to repoint it.
  The fix is small and has an obvious anchor: the slug is already in every `die` message, so point `enforced_by` at `99-postcheck.sh:<SLUG>` and require the marker to appear in EXECUTABLE text -- before the file's terminating `exit 0`, outside comments -- not merely somewhere in the bytes. Then delete the trailing comment; if the check is honest, deleting it must not change the verdict, and that is the negative test.

extra.value:
`mios-gate law-enforcers` (`src/mios-rs/mios-gate/src/laws.rs`); the Python twin in `tools/drift-checks.py` is deleted in the same commit per ADR-0021, which is why `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` comes DOWN 56 to 121213 rather than needing headroom it did not have. A `99-postcheck.sh` target must now appear in *executable text* -- before the file's top-level `exit 0`, not on a comment line -- and the four laws are repointed at the slug their own `die` messages already carry (`BOUND-IMAGES`, `UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS`, `BARE-SAFE-ENV`, `SECRETS-NEVER-IN-ENV`). The `# References for laws:` line is gone and the gate stayed green without it, which is the proof it was load-bearing for nothing but the check.
  **Two more silent drops found while porting, neither in the original report.** The old reader split `enforced_by` on `,` FIRST and then skipped any piece without a `:`, so Law 12's second enforcer `check_firstboot_degrade_open` was never verified (it does exist and is invoked -- checked, not assumed). And any enforcer kind that was neither `98-drift-checks.sh` nor `99-postcheck.sh` matched no branch and fell through to silence, which is what happened to Law 15's `process:` pointer. So the check verified 12 of 18 targets and reported all 18 clean. Both are closed: a bare target now inherits the file from the one before it, `process:` is a declared category counted in the summary, and any other kind is a finding.
  **Verified before and after:** against the unrepaired SSOT the new check names all four stale pointers with the alibi "it appears only in a comment or after the file's `exit 0`"; after the repair it reports `16 law(s): 12 drift-check function(s), 4 postcheck marker(s) in executable text, 1 declared process-enforced` -- 17 targets, versus the 12 the old predicate actually examined.

title: LAW11KEYS-01: the secret-bearing key list is three hardcoded names, and a projected OTP is not one of them
goal: Law 11's live enforcement in `automation/99-postcheck.sh` decides which files are "secret-bearing" from one literal: `_law11_secret_re='(MIOS_USER_PASSWORD_HASH|MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_PASSWORD|MIOS_GITHUB_TOKEN)=|[$]6[$]|[$]y[$]'`. Three names and two crypt-hash shapes, hardcoded in the enforcement script rather than resolved from `mios.toml`. Any credential whose variable is not one of those three, and whose value has no recognisable shape, is invisible to the law that exists to contain it.
acceptance_criteria: the secret-bearing key list resolves from `mios.toml` in both consumers with no literal left in either; `MIOS_IPA_OTP` is on it; a 0644 tracked env file carrying a registered secret key FAILS the gate -- proved by planting one; the IPA OTP no longer reaches a tracked world-readable file; and removing a key from the SSOT registry is itself caught, so the register cannot be drained silently.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
`tools/generate-ipa-enroll-env.py` projects `[identity.ipa]` into the tracked file `etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env`, which is **mode 0644** and carries `MIOS_IPA_OTP`. A FreeIPA one-time enrollment password is a credential by definition. title: SIZERATCHET-01: the tracked-size ratchet is 83% a measurement of the baked payloads it can never shed
goal: `[legibility].max_tracked_mb = 202` is a shrink-only ceiling whose breach message says "do NOT raise". It is measured as `round(nbytes / 1048576)` over every tracked blob. 83% of those bytes are `usr/share/mios/vendored/`, which Law 12 BAKE-NOT-FETCH requires the image to carry -- so the ratchet's stated remedy, shed bytes, is closed against the thing that dominates its measurement, and the 17% it *can* govern is drowned out.
acceptance_criteria: the tracked-size ratchet measures a quantity the project can actually shrink; a vendored blob added or removed does not move it; the authored tree crossing its ceiling FAILS -- proved by planting; and the gate reports headroom rather than only a pass/fail, so `202/202` can never again mean "15 KiB from red".
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Measured from the git index, not estimated:
  | slice | size |
  |---|---:|
  | `usr/share/mios/vendored/` | **168.24 MiB** |
  | everything else (the authored tree) | **34.30 MiB** |
  | total | 202.54 MiB |
  Two blobs -- `vendored/k3s/k3s` (63.29 MiB) and `vendored/wheels/hermes_agent.tar.gz` (41.21 MiB) -- are **104.50 MiB between them**, more than half the ceiling. Adding one vendored wheel moves this ratchet further than every line of source the project will write this year, and deleting one is a Law 12 violation.
  **The 1 MiB resolution is the second half of the defect.** `round()` means the ceiling `202` encodes any measurement in [201.5, 202.5) MiB, so the slack a branch has depends on where in that window the base happens to sit -- invisible from the ceiling itself:
  | ref | bytes | MiB | rounds to | slack to the boundary |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | `origin/main` | 211,808,325 | 201.9962 | 202 | 528 KiB |
  | `d4b3e871` (branch, before this batch) | 212,321,647 | 202.4857 | 202 | **15 KiB** |
  | `9397d259` (task_985) | 212,371,842 | 202.5336 | **203** | over by 35 KiB |
  So the branch had already consumed 513 KiB of main's 528 KiB and was one small source file from red, while the gate still printed `202/202` -- a PASS that carried no signal about how close it was. task_985's commit (a Rust check, its tests, a negative test, task records) added ~50 KiB and crossed it. Nothing in that commit is removable waste; it is the deliverable.
  **The fix has precedent in the same function.** `_is_generated` already excludes machine-projected files from the shell and PowerShell ceilings, with the reasoning written out: counting them "measured the wrong thing", and excluding them "LOWERS both floors ... so the ratchet binds strictly tighter on the code it actually governs". `vendored/` is the same argument with a bigger number. Excluding it by SSOT prefix (as `[legibility].python_ai_plane_prefixes` already does for the AI plane) takes the ceiling from 202 to ~34 and makes it bind on authored content. That is a TIGHTENING, not a raise, and it must be committed as one -- with the new ceiling set from `origin/main`'s authored size, so the branch does not bank its own growth.
  **The alternative reading is real and should be answered, not assumed away:** that the ratchet is working -- the branch genuinely added ~500 KiB and ought to shed some. It is weak because the 500 KiB is Rust gates, their tests, and the task/ledger record the project's own conventions require ("every artifact is tracked"), but the choice of which reading governs is the operator's, not something to improvise inside a PR.
  **Do not fix by raising `max_tracked_mb` to 203.** That buys one commit and restores the same zero-headroom state one rounding window later.

extra.value:
the operator chose the generated-with-declared-headroom form over excluding `vendored/`. `max_tracked_mb` is now EMITTED by `tools/native/mios-size-ceiling` as `round(tracked MiB) + [legibility].tracked_mb_headroom`, and `check_size_ceiling` fails when the committed value falls outside `[floor, floor + headroom]` -- below it the tree already exceeds its budget, above it is slack nobody declared. Headroom is 1 MiB and is the only operator-tunable half. The tradeoff was stated before the choice and stands: this ratchet can now drift upward one allowance at a time. What it buys is that every raise is a committed diff with the measurement attached, instead of a hand-typed number nobody can date.
  **It is no longer shrink-only, so it says so.** `[drift].generated_ceilings` itemises it with a reason, and `mios-gate ratchet-direction` lets exactly the keys on that list rise -- reporting how many did, rather than skipping them silently. An entry with no reason is a finding; so is an entry naming something that is not a ceiling, which stops a stale exemption lying in wait for a future key of that name.
  **The gate this needed did not exist in a form that could carry an exemption.** `check-ratchet-direction.py` was ported to `mios-gate ratchet-direction` and the Python twin deleted in the same commit (ADR-0021), which also freed the 132 Python lines the ceiling had left no room for. Parity was proved on BOTH paths first, not just the passing one: 78 ceilings on each side, and on a planted raise both name `docs.max_unmigrated_narrative` and exit 1. The port found two `RATCHET_SECTIONS` entries that can never match -- filed as task_992 and deliberately NOT fixed here, because widening them captures `build.rechunk_max_layers` and a port that changes a gate's verdict is not a port.
  **The exemption's SHAPE was decided by another law.** Written first as an array of inline tables -- the obvious form, and the one every neighbouring register uses -- it took `check_resolver_differential_parity` from 12 divergences to 13 and breached that shrink-only ceiling: arrays of inline tables render differently in the bash and Python resolver twins, and the 12 that exist are the registered debt. Re-expressed as a TABLE of `key = "reason"`, which both twins render identically. Law 13 costs a shape here, and the cost is worth recording because the next register added to `mios.toml` will face the same choice.
  `tracked_mb` is green at 203/204, and the gate is back to 19 violations from the standing six checks.

title: VARCLOSURE-01: Law 9's gate has been deciding the empty set is a subset, every run
goal: `check_var_closure` enforces Law 9 ONE-CANONICAL-NAME by asserting R ⊆ E -- every `MIOS_*` a consumer references is emitted by the resolver. Run it and it prints `emitted=2879 referenced=0 missing=0` followed by `PASS: all referenced MIOS_* variables are emitted by SSOT.` **R is empty.** ∅ ⊆ E is true for every E, so the gate has never been able to fail, and the drift gate reports "MIOS_* referenced-set is a subset of emitted-set" on the strength of it.
acceptance_criteria: the scan reaches the consumer trees; a planted `${MIOS_NEVER_EMITTED}` in a real consumer under `automation/`, `tools/` and `usr/libexec/mios/` each FAIL; a scan that reaches zero files is cannot-run rather than a pass -- proved by a negative test that empties the scan and asserts exit 2; the 461 are itemised on a shrink-only register rather than absorbed by a count, with env-file-projected names either emitted or classified so the register is not padded with them; and task_990's two names are caught by it.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Two causes, both measured in `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py`:
  - `INTERNAL_PATHS` is applied as `if any(rel.startswith(p) or fn.startswith(p) for p in INTERNAL_PATHS): continue` and contains `usr/lib/mios/`, `usr/libexec/mios/`, `config/`, `tools/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `installation/`, `automation/`, `usr/share/mios/`, `var/lib/mios/` -- which between them are very nearly the whole repository, and specifically every place a `MIOS_*` consumer lives.
  - The line filter `if re.search(rf"\b{v}\s*[:=]", code_part) or "Environment=" in code_part or "$env:" in code_part or "export " in code_part: continue`, which drops any line that also looks like an assignment.
  **Each filter's contribution, measured by disabling them one at a time** (this replaces an earlier unmeasured claim that the line filter was what emptied the `usr/lib/systemd/` and Quadlet trees -- it contributes, but it is not the dominant term):
  | variant | referenced-but-unemitted found |
  |---|---:|
  | as shipped | **0** |
  | without `INTERNAL_PATHS` | 376 |
  | without the line filter | 25 |
  | without either | **461** |
  So the two together hide 461 real findings, `INTERNAL_PATHS` is responsible for the bulk, and their interaction accounts for the remaining ~60. Note what `R` actually holds: `referenced_set` already skips any name in `E`, so `R` IS the violation set, and `referenced=0 missing=0` means "the scan found nothing to judge", not "nothing was referenced". The gate cannot fail; it has no reachable failing input.
  **Where the 461 live** -- this is a Law 7 signal as much as a Law 9 one:
  | tree | findings |
  |---|---:|
  | `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/` | 224 |
  | `automation/` | 62 |
  | `usr/libexec/mios/` | 32 |
  | `usr/` (other) | 30 |
  | `tools/` | 25 |
  | `build-mios.ps1` | 24 |
  | remainder (`usr/lib/mios/` other, tests, installation, `Get-MiOS.ps1`, config, etc) | 64 |
  **A design constraint the measurement exposed:** all eleven `MIOS_IPA_*` names are reported, including `MIOS_IPA_REALM`, `MIOS_IPA_DOMAIN` and `MIOS_IPA_SERVER` -- which DO reach their consumer, because it sources the projected `etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env` rather than the resolver. So the emitted set must also account for names emitted by tracked env-file projections, or that class becomes noise and the register fills with false positives. The genuinely broken pair (task_990) is `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL` / `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`, which no file emits at all.
  **The asymmetry in `main()` is the tell.** It guards the emitted side twice, each with a comment explaining why: `if not E: FAIL -- emitter produced 0 vars (resolver broken?)` returns 2, and `if EMIT_ERRORS:` refuses to "report on an emitted set it knows is partial" and returns 2. There is no `if not R:`. The author reasoned carefully about one side of the subset and never about the other, which is the Empty-Set Pass in its purest form: the same care that produced two guards would have produced a third if the question had been asked.
  **This is not theoretical -- it is already hiding a live break.** See task_990: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-freeipa-enroll.sh` requires `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL` and `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`, neither of which anything emits, and the gate whose entire job is to catch that reports clean.
  **Fix shape:** scope the scan to what a consumer actually is rather than to what it is not -- an INTERNAL_PATHS list that excludes `automation/`, `tools/` and `usr/libexec/mios/` is excluding the consumers, not the emitters. Emitters are already handled precisely by `EMITTER_SUFFIXES`; that is the right mechanism and it does not need a path-prefix sledgehammer beside it. Then floor R in SSOT (`[laws].min_referenced_vars`, shrink-only in the other direction) so the set can never silently empty again, and make `not R` a cannot-run (exit 2), not a pass. Belongs in `mios-gate` per ADR-0021 and because `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` has no headroom.

extra.value:
the scan now reaches the consumers and the gate is a ratchet against an itemised ledger. `INTERNAL_PATHS` and its use are deleted -- `EMITTER_SUFFIXES` already excluded the emitters precisely, and the prefix list beside it excluded only consumers. The line filter drops just an assignment TO the name (`\b{v}\s*=`) instead of skipping any line containing `Environment=`, `export ` or `$env:`, which is how every unit and Quadlet references its variables. A second bug surfaced while writing the negative test: the tests-tree exclusion read `"tests/" in reldir`, which is false for a file sitting directly in `tests/`, so the test corpus was being scanned as a consumer -- the negative test's own planted name came back as a finding. Fixed to compare path components; the ledger fell 436 -> 425.
  **425 names are now registered** in `usr/share/mios/reference/var-closure-baseline.tsv` with a sample location, `#!ceiling 425`, EXACT in both directions -- a name that disappears is "tighten the ledger", the same discipline `value-dup-baseline.tsv` uses, so the register drains rather than settling. `check_var_closure` compares the name SET, not the locations, because line numbers move.
  **Not vacuous, measured on the same tree:** with `${MIOS_NEVER_EMITTED_PROBE}` planted, the pre-repair tool exits 0 and prints "PASS: all referenced MIOS_* variables are emitted by SSOT"; the repaired one names it. **Goal:** `check_var_closure` enforces Law 9 ONE-CANONICAL-NAME by asserting R ⊆ E -- every `MIOS_*` a consumer references is emitted by the resolver. Run it and it prints `emitted=2879 referenced=0 missing=0` followed by `PASS: all referenced MIOS_* variables are emitted by SSOT.` **R is empty.** ∅ ⊆ E is true for every E, so the gate has never been able to fail, and the drift gate reports "MIOS_* referenced-set is a subset of emitted-set" on the strength of it.
**What+How:** Two causes, both measured in `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py`:
  - `INTERNAL_PATHS` is applied as `if any(rel.startswith(p) or fn.startswith(p) for p in INTERNAL_PATHS): continue` and contains `usr/lib/mios/`, `usr/libexec/mios/`, `config/`, `tools/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `installation/`, `automation/`, `usr/share/mios/`, `var/lib/mios/` -- which between them are very nearly the whole repository, and specifically every place a `MIOS_*` consumer lives.
  - The line filter `if re.search(rf"\b{v}\s*[:=]", code_part) or "Environment=" in code_part or "$env:" in code_part or "export " in code_part: continue`, which drops any line that also looks like an assignment.
  **Each filter's contribution, measured by disabling them one at a time** (this replaces an earlier unmeasured claim that the line filter was what emptied the `usr/lib/systemd/` and Quadlet trees -- it contributes, but it is not the dominant term):
  | variant | referenced-but-unemitted found |
  |---|---:|
  | as shipped | **0** |
  | without `INTERNAL_PATHS` | 376 |
  | without the line filter | 25 |
  | without either | **461** |
  So the two together hide 461 real findings, `INTERNAL_PATHS` is responsible for the bulk, and their interaction accounts for the remaining ~60. Note what `R` actually holds: `referenced_set` already skips any name in `E`, so `R` IS the violation set, and `referenced=0 missing=0` means "the scan found nothing to judge", not "nothing was referenced". The gate cannot fail; it has no reachable failing input.
  **Where the 461 live** -- this is a Law 7 signal as much as a Law 9 one:
  | tree | findings |
  |---|---:|
  | `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/` | 224 |
  | `automation/` | 62 |
  | `usr/libexec/mios/` | 32 |
  | `usr/` (other) | 30 |
  | `tools/` | 25 |
  | `build-mios.ps1` | 24 |
  | remainder (`usr/lib/mios/` other, tests, installation, `Get-MiOS.ps1`, config, etc) | 64 |
  **A design constraint the measurement exposed:** all eleven `MIOS_IPA_*` names are reported, including `MIOS_IPA_REALM`, `MIOS_IPA_DOMAIN` and `MIOS_IPA_SERVER` -- which DO reach their consumer, because it sources the projected `etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env` rather than the resolver. So the emitted set must also account for names emitted by tracked env-file projections, or that class becomes noise and the register fills with false positives. The genuinely broken pair (task_990) is `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL` / `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`, which no file emits at all.
  **The asymmetry in `main()` is the tell.** It guards the emitted side twice, each with a comment explaining why: `if not E: FAIL -- emitter produced 0 vars (resolver broken?)` returns 2, and `if EMIT_ERRORS:` refuses to "report on an emitted set it knows is partial" and returns 2. There is no `if not R:`. The author reasoned carefully about one side of the subset and never about the other, which is the Empty-Set Pass in its purest form: the same care that produced two guards would have produced a third if the question had been asked.
  **This is not theoretical -- it is already hiding a live break.** See task_990: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-freeipa-enroll.sh` requires `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL` and `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`, neither of which anything emits, and the gate whose entire job is to catch that reports clean.

Emitters are already handled precisely by `EMITTER_SUFFIXES`; that is the right mechanism and it does not need a path-prefix sledgehammer beside it. Then floor R in SSOT (`[laws].min_referenced_vars`, shrink-only in the other direction) so the set can never silently empty again, and make `not R` a cannot-run (exit 2), not a pass. Belongs in `mios-gate` per ADR-0021 and because `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` has no headroom.
**Done When:** the scan reaches the consumer trees; a planted `${MIOS_NEVER_EMITTED}` in a real consumer under `automation/`, `tools/` and `usr/libexec/mios/` each FAIL; a scan that reaches zero files is cannot-run rather than a pass -- proved by a negative test that empties the scan and asserts exit 2; the 461 are itemised on a shrink-only register rather than absorbed by a count, with env-file-projected names either emitted or classified so the register is not padded with them; and task_990's two names are caught by it.

Planted separately in `automation/`, `tools/` and `usr/libexec/mios/` -- one plant would not distinguish "the exclusion list is gone" from "it is merely shorter".

It has one now: three plants, a name dropped from the ledger, a stale ledger entry, a missing `#!ceiling`, and an absent ledger -- the last two being the cases where a gate with no data must not report green.

title: IPANAME-01: zero-touch FreeIPA enrollment reads two variable names nothing emits
goal: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-freeipa-enroll.sh` sources `/etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env` and then requires five variables, exiting 1 on any that is empty: `MIOS_IPA_REALM MIOS_IPA_DOMAIN MIOS_IPA_SERVER MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`. The file it sources is projected by `tools/generate-ipa-enroll-env.py` from `[identity.ipa]`, and that generator emits `MIOS_IPA_ENROLL_PRINCIPAL` and `MIOS_IPA_OTP`. The names do not meet. Enrollment cannot succeed.
acceptance_criteria: one canonical name per value across `[identity.ipa]`, the generator, and the consumer; every variable the enrollment script reads is emitted by the resolver; the closure gate from task_989 catches a reintroduction; and the enrollment path is exercised far enough to prove the guard loop passes with a configured SSOT.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Measured, not inferred. `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL` and `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD` occur in the entire tree ONLY inside the consumer that requires them -- four lines of `mios-freeipa-enroll.sh` (the guard loop, the two `ipa-client-install` arguments, and the post-success overwrite). Nothing produces either name: both are absent from `usr/share/mios/reference/env-baseline.txt`, as are `MIOS_IPA_ENROLL_PRINCIPAL` and `MIOS_IPA_OTP`. So an operator who sets `[identity.ipa].enabled = true` gets `mios-freeipa-enroll.service` running, sourcing a file that parses fine, and dying on `missing required var MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL`. The feature has never been able to work.
  This is a Law 9 ONE-CANONICAL-NAME violation of the plainest kind -- one value, two names -- and it survived because the gate for Law 9 measures the empty set (task_989). It also sits inside task_987's artifact: the same projected file is mode 0644 and carries the OTP, so the two should be settled together, with the naming fixed first because it decides what the split-out file must be called.
  **Which name wins is a real decision, not a rename.** `enroll_principal`/`otp` describe FreeIPA's actual concepts (a one-time enrollment password is not an account password), while `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD` is what the consumer's `--password=` argument reflects. The SSOT names are better; the consumer should move. But `MIOS_IPA_HOSTNAME`, `MIOS_IPA_NTP` and `MIOS_IPA_AUTOMOUNT` are also read by that script with `:=` defaults and are likewise emitted by nothing, so the whole surface needs one pass rather than a two-name patch.

title: VARCLOSURE-02: a tracked .env projection emits names the closure gate cannot see
goal: task_989's ledger holds 425 referenced-but-unemitted names. Eleven of them are not breaches: `etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env` is a TRACKED projection of `[identity.ipa]`, guarded by its own drift check, and its consumer reaches those names by `source`-ing it rather than through the resolver. `emitted_set()` knows about the Python resolver, the `mios.toml` table prefixes and `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh`, but not about env-file projections, so the whole class reads as unemitted.
acceptance_criteria: names emitted by a tracked, drift-checked `.env` projection are in the emitted set; the ledger and `#!ceiling` come down by exactly the number removed in the same commit; a planted projection name is NOT reported while a planted non-projection name still is; and the remaining `MIOS_IPA_*` rows are precisely task_990's five.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Measured while building task_989: teaching `emitted_set()` to read the tracked `.env` projections takes the finding count from 436 to 433 on the pre-tests-fix scan, and it is exactly the names the projection writes -- `MIOS_IPA_ENABLED`, `MIOS_IPA_REALM`, `MIOS_IPA_SERVER`, `MIOS_IPA_DOMAIN`, `MIOS_IPA_ENROLL_PRINCIPAL`, `MIOS_IPA_OTP`. What is left after that is the genuinely broken set task_990 owns: `MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL`, `MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD`, `MIOS_IPA_HOSTNAME`, `MIOS_IPA_NTP`, `MIOS_IPA_AUTOMOUNT`, which no file emits at all. That the refined predicate lands on exactly the set established independently by hand is the evidence it is right.
  **Why it is not already done:** it costs 7 Python lines and `[legibility].max_tooling_python_lines` had none -- task_989's repair had to fit inside the ceiling rather than ask for room. The clean way to pay for it is to port the check to `mios-gate` per ADR-0021, which deletes 171 Python lines; the obstacle there is that the emitted set is built by importing `tools/render-globals.py`, so it waits on `mios-resolver` owning that (task_952).
  **The shape matters more than the eleven rows.** A gate whose ledger contains entries that are not breaches teaches its readers to skim the ledger, and a ledger nobody reads is a count. Fixing this is also a demonstration of the ratchet working in the intended direction: the ceiling comes DOWN in the same commit.

title: RATCHETSEC-01: two RATCHET_SECTIONS entries name a path the comparison can never see
goal: The ratchet-direction gate widens its ceiling test for keys inside certain sections: a key that merely *contains* `max_`/`ceiling` counts when its section is on `RATCHET_SECTIONS`. Two of that list's entries are `build.ratchet` and `security.privileged_quadlets` -- dotted paths -- while the comparison is against the FIRST path component only (`full_key.split(".")[0]` in the predecessor, `full.split('.').next()` in the port). No key's first component is ever `build.ratchet`, so both entries have always been inert.
acceptance_criteria: no entry in the ratchet-section list can fail to match by construction -- proved by a test that asserts each entry is a possible first path component; and every ceiling the widened scope captures is either shrink-only on purpose or itemised as a budget with a reason.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Measured while porting `check-ratchet-direction.py` to `mios-gate ratchet-direction` (task_988). Replacing the two dotted entries with `build` and `security` takes the guarded ceiling count from **78 to 79**; the single key it newly captures is `build.rechunk_max_layers`. The port deliberately kept the behaviour at 78 rather than banking a tightening inside a like-for-like replacement -- a port that silently changes a gate's verdict is not a port.
  **The question is not "fix the typo", it is "should these be ratchets".** `rechunk_max_layers` reads like a tuning value: an operator raising it is making the image build differently, not admitting debt. Shrink-only is the wrong shape for that, the same way it turned out to be the wrong shape for `max_tracked_mb` (task_988). So the options are (a) widen the sections and accept the new ceiling as shrink-only, (b) widen them and declare `build.rechunk_max_layers` a generated or tunable budget in `[drift.generated_ceilings]`, or (c) delete the two dead entries as the honest expression of what the gate actually does.
  Whichever is chosen, the dotted entries must not stay: a list whose entries cannot match is a register that teaches its reader the wrong thing about the gate's scope.
  Check every OTHER key that a widened scope would newly capture before choosing -- the 78-vs-79 delta is one key today, but `security` is a large section and the answer may differ once `security.privileged_quadlets`'s own numeric keys are in view.

**Goal:** The ratchet-direction gate widens its ceiling test for keys inside certain sections: a key that merely *contains* `max_`/`ceiling` counts when its section is on `RATCHET_SECTIONS`. Two of that list's entries are `build.ratchet` and `security.privileged_quadlets` -- dotted paths -- while the comparison is against the FIRST path component only (`full_key.split(".")[0]` in the predecessor, `full.split('.').next()` in the port). No key's first component is ever `build.ratchet`, so both entries have always been inert.
**What+How:** Measured while porting `check-ratchet-direction.py` to `mios-gate ratchet-direction` (task_988). Replacing the two dotted entries with `build` and `security` takes the guarded ceiling count from **78 to 79**; the single key it newly captures is `build.rechunk_max_layers`. The port deliberately kept the behaviour at 78 rather than banking a tightening inside a like-for-like replacement -- a port that silently changes a gate's verdict is not a port.
  **The question is not "fix the typo", it is "should these be ratchets".** `rechunk_max_layers` reads like a tuning value: an operator raising it is making the image build differently, not admitting debt. Shrink-only is the wrong shape for that, the same way it turned out to be the wrong shape for `max_tracked_mb` (task_988). title: NAMESGEN-01: a Rust generator is built, tested and never called
goal: `tools/native/generate-names-registry/` is a Rust crate that builds, and `tools/sync-generated.sh` step 4/6 still runs `tools/generate-names-registry.py`. acceptance_criteria: one generator per artifact; the surviving one is invoked by `sync-generated.sh`; byte-equality was proved before the other was deleted; and something enumerates `tools/native/` crates that no pipeline invokes, so a fourth instance cannot accumulate silently.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
Found while looking for a Rust-generator precedent to model `mios-size-ceiling` on. The crate exists with `mios-resolver` as a dependency, so it is not a stub; nothing in `sync-generated.sh`, `automation/`, or the `Justfile` calls it. The operator's disposition on the equivalent bake-plan case was *native Rust canonical, delete the shell-out*, and the same likely applies here -- but it needs the same evidence first: run both against the real tree and diff `usr/share/mios/referenced_names.txt` and `usr/share/mios/names.generated.txt` byte for byte. A degenerate result (both delegating to the same logic) must be reported as degenerate rather than presented as parity.
  **Do not delete the Python twin before the diff.** `check_names_registry` guards the Python one's output today; swapping the producer without proving byte-equality moves a tracked, gated artifact on a guess.
  A third instance is worth counting: this, bake-plan, and whatever else `tools/native/` holds that `sync-generated.sh` does not call. The register that would have caught all three is `[build.tool_dispatch]`, which only sees `command -v` gates in automation stages -- it does not see a generator that is simply never named.

Running it once would have rewritten the registry and turned check_names_registry red. The five divergences, by blast: (1) WalkDir census with a hardcoded skip-list still containing `build`, silently dropping tracked files, vs git ls-files that REFUSES on an unanswerable census; (2) four missing emitter_suffixes (globals.sh, globals.ps1, render-globals.py, render-ports.py) -- the generated namespace-DEFINING files were scanned as consumers, so 2273 of the 2340 extra names were the registry citing itself; (3) a line-wide assignment skip losing 16 names that ride on env-prefix lines; (4) no rstrip of a trailing `_`, producing 73 junk names and losing their 48 real forms; (5) the 19 static non-MIOS_ lines dropped on rewrite. Plus `starts_with("Containerfile")` where fnmatchcase needs the dot, and a non-atomic write. A SIXTH found while fixing: toml::Value::Table is a BTreeMap, so the section walk was alphabetical while check_names_registry compares line ORDER -- document order is now derived from one linear scan of the SSOT text rather than unifying the toml crate's preserve_order feature across all 17 workspace crates. title: BAKEPARITY-01: the bake stage prefers a generator two fixes behind the one the gate checks
goal: `automation/85-bake-plan.sh` dispatches `miosd bake-plan` → `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-plan` → `tools/native/target/release/mios-bake-plan` → `python3 tools/generate-bake-plan.py`, while `check_bake_plan` validates **only** the Python's output. There are THREE implementations: `tools/generate-bake-plan.py` (290 lines), `tools/native/mios-bake-plan/src/main.rs` (539), and `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/bake_plan.rs` (484, a declared mirror of the second). `miosd`'s `run_bake_plan` does not call its own module -- it shells out to the Python. So the producer the stage prefers and the producer the gate certifies are different programs.
acceptance_criteria: one generator produces the plan and the same one is what `check_bake_plan` validates; the Rust resolves floated tags from SSOT rather than only from `env`, proved by a bare run (no exported `MIOS_VERSION_*`) rendering all 6 artifacts byte-identically to the Python's; an unresolvable placeholder names the VARIABLE, not the core image -- proved by planting one; the miosd module and `tools/native` copy do not drift again (one of them is deleted, or a gate diffs them); and `85-bake-plan.sh` dispatches by absolute path so the branch taken is not a function of PATH.

details.what_how:
Measured by rendering each into an EMPTY directory from the SSOT and diffing, not by reading them.
  - Run bare, the Python writes all 6 artifacts and exits 0. The Rust writes **nothing** and exits 2 with three `VALIDATION ERROR: Core image '<X>' is not referenced by any Quadlet` lines naming `codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:12`, `docker.io/rancher/k3s:v1.36.3-k3s1`, `quay.io/ceph/ceph:v19`.
  - Those three are precisely the core images whose Quadlets float the tag: `Image=quay.io/ceph/ceph:${MIOS_VERSION_CEPH}` and siblings. The one forgejo image that passes, `code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner:7`, is literal on both sides.
  - Cause, exactly: the Rust's `resolve_image_val` resolves `${VAR}` from `env::var` only, plus sidecars for `MIOS_*_IMAGE` names. `MIOS_VERSION_CEPH` is neither, so the placeholder survives, `resolved.contains('$')` sends the Quadlet to `continue`, and the core-side set difference then blames the SSOT. **The image IS referenced by a Quadlet; the tool could not resolve the tag, dropped the Quadlet silently, and reported the wrong subject.**
  - **The Python already carries the fix, with the bug written in its comments:** it resolves through `mios_toml.emit_exports()` -- "the same canonical key map every other consumer uses" -- and collects an `unresolved` list so it can "name the variable that did not resolve instead". Its comment states the failure mode verbatim: "a floated tag turned into 'core image is not referenced by any Quadlet' three lines of SSOT away from the actual cause."
  - **Parity DOES hold once the environment is supplied.** With `MIOS_VERSION_*` exported from `env-baseline.txt`, the Rust renders the same 6 paths and all six are byte-identical to the Python's. Not a degenerate diff: two independent implementations, proven to differ in one respect first.
  **So the Rust is the older logic, and making it canonical as-is would regress a fix the Python already has.** The direction (native canonical) is unchanged; the prerequisite is not optional.
  **Also unresolved by this task:** `85-bake-plan.sh` still gates on `command -v miosd`, one of the 3 entries on `[build.tool_dispatch].unreachable` (task_962), so on a bake where that lookup fails the stage silently falls to the next branch -- and which branch that is decides whether the build gets the fixed generator or the stale one.
  **Decisions taken, remaining work in this task.** The resolver fix landed in `0c847bbc`, so the bare-run parity the Done-When demanded now holds. Two of the three open questions are answered. (1) `check_bake_plan` is repointed at the **native** producer: the gate should certify what actually bakes, and byte-identical bare output makes that a verifiable move rather than a leap -- left as-is, a native-only regression passes. Gating both and asserting agreement was the runner-up and was declined because it keeps the Python alive as a permanent build dependency. (2) The dead `miosd/src/bake_plan.rs` mirror is **audited before any delete** -- diffed against both live generators first, because logic present only in the unreachable copy is a finding rather than dead weight, and that is worth knowing before proposing its removal.
  **The repoint landed.** `check_bake_plan` now dispatches by absolute path to `tools/native/target/{release,debug}/mios-bake-plan` then `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-plan`, and **does not fall back to the Python**: an absent binary is a cannot-run violation, because a check that silently certifies a different program than the one that bakes is the defect being closed. `-p mios-bake-plan` added to the CI build line so the check can run there rather than reporting cannot-run on every PR.
  **Proved by the regression the old check could not see.** Removing the SSOT layer from `resolve_image_val` in the native producer ONLY -- the exact task_994 defect -- makes the repointed check exit 1 naming `${MIOS_VERSION_CEPH}` and `${MIOS_VERSION_FORGEJO}`, while `python3 tools/generate-bake-plan.py --check` on the same tree exits **0**. That is the whole argument for the repoint, measured rather than asserted. Also verified: a planted stale `.list` is caught and named; both native paths absent is cannot-run rather than a silent Python pass (the first attempt at this control wrongly passed because only the debug binary had been moved -- the release one was still resolving); tree byte-identical after every control.
  **AUDIT OF THE DEAD MIRROR (task_994 decision: audit before deciding).** `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/bake_plan.rs`, 484 lines, `pub mod` in lib.rs with **zero call sites** -- `run_bake_plan` shells out to the Python and nothing references `bake_plan::`. Function-by-function against the live `tools/native` binary: `get_root` **identical**; `classify` **identical**; `resolve_image_val` differs only by **lacking** the SSOT layer and the `unresolved` variable-naming error, i.e. it is the pre-`0c847bbc` version; the entry point differs as `pub fn run` returning `Result` versus `fn main` calling `process::exit`, which is the lib/bin boundary and not logic. Its own comment declares it "mirrored from tools/native/mios-bake-plan per Law 15".
  **Verdict: it carries no unique logic. Every difference is it being behind.** The single thing it does better is descriptive `.expect()` messages where the live binary uses `.unwrap()` on two compile-time-literal regexes -- worth porting so a deletion loses nothing at all. Recommendation is to delete it; per the standing rule that is proposed, not taken.

title: SOCKETREND-01: a shipped socket unit carried an unsubstituted placeholder
goal: `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-cockpit-link.socket:8` shipped `ListenStream=0.0.0.0:${MIOS_PORT_COCKPIT_LINK}` verbatim. systemd does not expand `${VAR}` in `ListenStream=`, so the unit fails to parse and the socket does not listen. This was live in the tree, not latent.
acceptance_criteria: no tracked file under the render scan trees carries a placeholder the renderer will not substitute -- gated, with the socket case as the negative control; and the renderer and its gate read one SSOT list so neither can drift from the other.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
`automation/34-render-quadlets.sh` walks `QUADLET_DIRS` -- which includes `/usr/lib/systemd/system` -- but filtered with `find ... \( -name '*.container' -o ... -o -name '*.service' \)`, ten extensions with **no `*.socket`**. The directory was in scope; the file type was not. One tracked socket unit exists and it is the one that carries a placeholder, so the omission had exactly one victim and no margin.
  **Fixed at the class, not the instance.** The extension list is lifted into `[build.quadlet_render].extensions` (11 entries, `socket` added) and the renderer builds its `-name` predicate from it, refusing to run on an empty list rather than rendering nothing. `mios-gate render-coverage`, wired as `check_render_extension_coverage`, then asserts that every tracked file under the repo-relative scan trees carrying `${MIOS_*}` has an extension on that list: 34 such files across 245 scanned today, all covered.
  **The negative control reproduces the original defect exactly:** remove `socket` from SSOT and the gate names `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-cockpit-link.socket`. An empty list is cannot-run rather than a flood of findings, so a configuration error cannot masquerade as 34 violations.
  **Not fixed here:** task_977's other two findings in the same stage -- `envsubst` mangling systemd's `$$` escaping, and the single-pass nested-default regex rendering `base_url = ".../v1/v1}"`. Both remain, and both are why that task stays open. This closes only the file-type hole, which was the one shipping a broken unit.

title: TOOLCHAIN-01: nothing pins a Rust toolchain, so CI lints against a version the tree never chose
goal: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` can be clean on a contributor's machine and fatal in CI on identical bytes, because the two run different clippy versions and neither is declared anywhere in the repository.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust toolchain version is a single SSOT value, projected rather than hand-written, and a local `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and CI's cannot disagree about which lints are in force.
verification_evidence: migrated from MiOS:TASKS.md (status_raw: done); see provenance.sources

details.what_how:
There is no `rust-toolchain.toml` in `src/mios-rs`, in `tools/native`, or at the root, and `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` installs the linter with a bare `rustup component add clippy rustfmt`. CI therefore lints with whatever the GitHub runner image ships at that moment. The first casualty: `clippy::for_kv_map` fired on `mios-gate/src/ratchet.rs:224` under rust-1.98.0 and killed four consecutive pushes at exit 101, while the same source linted clean under 1.94.1 locally. The lint is correct; the point is that nothing in the tree asked for it and nothing warned that the bar had moved. A runner-image bump is a silent, unversioned change to this project's definition of "compiles".
  **The gate that exists cannot see this.** Every other derived surface in this repo is projected from `mios.toml` and guarded by regenerate-and-diff. The toolchain is the one build input with no SSOT row, no projection and no drift check -- so a divergence between local and CI is not a violation of anything, it is simply invisible until a push turns red.
  **Decided: pin via SSOT projection.** A version in `mios.toml` (`[versions].rust`, alongside the tags every Quadlet already floats on), projected into a `rust-toolchain.toml` per workspace by a generator registered in `sync-generated.sh`, guarded by the regenerate-and-diff check. That makes local and CI the same by construction and makes a bump a reviewable commit. Two generated files rather than two hand-maintained ones, which is Law 8 applied to the compiler itself.
  **The tension, and how it was settled:** a pin argues with the standing "latest packages" convention -- it freezes the linter, and new lints then arrive only when someone bumps the row rather than on the day the runner changes. Put to the operator as reproducibility against staying current; they chose reproducibility. "Latest packages" still governs the value in the row, which is bumped forward on next touch like every other pin -- what changes is that the bump is a commit somebody reviews instead of a runner-image change nobody sees.
