title: Turn the "PostgresOS" research into shipped accounts wiring: userdb projection, lldap decision, ADR, peer-OS cleanup
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- PostgreSQL becomes the accounts SSOT with a lossless projection to the OS, instead of a flag that ships inert.
acceptance_criteria: `db_backed` is no longer inert and its derivation is drift-gated; the `/usr/lib/userdb/*.user` projection lands and regenerate-and-diff is green; the lldap decision and the PostgresOS ADR are committed; no doc still references a distinct "PodmanOS"; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Execute `docs/design/doc-postgresos-accounts.md` and `doc-peer-os-landscape.md`. "PostgresOS" is the operator's COINAGE, not a product, which is exactly why `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED` ships inert -- it must be assembled from FOSS bricks. (P1) Add/verify the bridge so `tools/lib/userenv.sh` auto-derives `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED` from `[accounts].db_backed` at build time, plus a drift-check asserting the derivation, so `17-accounts-db.sh` stops defaulting the service off. (P2) Project each `[accounts]` row into a generated `/usr/lib/userdb/<name>.user` JSON drop-in -- systemd userdb, with nss-systemd synthesizing passwd/shadow/group -- the same render+gate shape as `mios-theme-render` and the dotfiles registry; mine libnss-pgsql's schema but do NOT ship it (archived/dead). (P2) Evaluate lldap-over-Postgres as the cross-platform SSOT LDAP face (RFC2307 to SSSD/nslcd) so Postgres stays authoritative without a second directory store; record OpenLDAP back-sql and Keycloak+SCIM as the alternatives. (P2) Write an ADR stating that "PostgresOS" is a MiOS concept name mapped to a concrete stack (systemd userdb projection + lldap + SCIM-as-pattern + the Windows autounattend/SetupComplete `New-LocalUser` path) with no upstream repo. (P3) Close every ROADMAP/doc reference to a distinct "PodmanOS" (reality: `quay.io/podman/machine-os`, FCOS + bootc-switch) and repoint the archived bootc-image-builder reference at osbuild/image-builder. Windows half is already landed in mios-bootstrap (RID-500 rename moved from the specialize pass into SetupComplete.cmd; the `MiOS-AccountSync` minute-task reconciles DB to Windows accounts).
details.why: the accounts workstream currently ships a true SSOT value that reaches nothing, and contributors chase two products ("PostgresOS", "PodmanOS") that do not exist.

title: Drift-gate every build-time network fetch for a retry flag
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- the network-at-build bakers stop being a "one transient 504 kills the bake" class.
acceptance_criteria: the gate flags an injected retry-less `curl`, passes clean on HEAD (all fetches now retried), a negative test proves the injected case is caught, and `just drift-gate` is green.

details.what_how: The build died repeatedly on a transient GitHub `504` because the AdGuard `RUN curl … | tar` in `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` carried no `--retry`. Claude hand-swept every fetch; now enforce it. title: Fix scurl's binary-stream corruption and harden its argument parser
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- the credential-masking fetch wrapper stops being a data-corruption hazard on the dominant build pattern.
acceptance_criteria: `curl … | tar` through scurl is byte-identical to raw curl, the parser handles all three edge cases, the new test is green, and `just drift-gate` is green.

details.what_how: `scurl()` in `automation/lib/masking.sh` sets `is_binary` only when it sees `-o` / `-O` / `--output`, but the build's dominant pattern is `curl … | tar` (stream to stdout, no `-o`), so scurl classifies a tarball as TEXT and pipes it through `mask_filter` (`sed -u`), corrupting the stream. (1) Fix classification so `mask_filter` never touches a body destined for a pipe or download -- gate masking on stdout being a TTY, or skip `mask_filter` for any non-`-o` streamed body. (2) Harden the naive parser, which takes the FIRST `https?://` argument as the URL and therefore misses `--output=FILE` and `--url X` and mis-detects a `-H` header value that looks like a URL. (3) Add `automation/lib/test_masking.sh` asserting: a piped binary body is byte-identical (no sed mangling), a github URL gets the auth header AND the token is masked in text output, and `--output=` is detected. Wire the test into the shell-test/lint gate.
details.why: every streamed tarball fetched through scurl is silently corruptible today, and the parser can leak or misroute credentials on ordinary flag spellings.

extra.value: next -- this is a real DATA-CORRUPTION bug, not just hygiene.

title: One shared empty-`MIOS_*` strip helper plus an import-clean-under-empty-env test
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the ~734-key var closure stops emitting values that break the consumers it exists to serve.
acceptance_criteria: exactly one strip helper exists (no duplicate implementation), the empty-env import test is green across all agent-pipe modules, and `just drift-gate` is green.

details.what_how: The SSOT var closure (`usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` around line 598) exports ~734 `MIOS_*` keys, many of them EMPTY. An empty value (unlike an absent one) defeats `os.environ.get(K, D)` -- the default only applies when the key is absent -- so int/float coercion raised `ValueError` and crashed the 56-test gate. Claude patched two ad-hoc spots: `mios_pipe/__init__._strip_empty_mios_env()` and a `{ unset $(compgen -v MIOS_); … }` wrapper in `automation/build.sh`. Consolidate: (1) one helper `usr/lib/mios/mios_env.py::strip_empty_mios_env(env=os.environ)` used by `mios_pipe/__init__.py`, dropping the private copy; (2) a `test_mios_env.py` that sets EVERY closure-emitted `MIOS_*` key to `""` and asserts every `agent-pipe/mios_*.py` module still imports and its config coercion falls back to defaults with no `ValueError`; (3) evaluate making the closure not emit purely-empty keys at all -- that is the ROOT fix and would demote the strip to belt-and-suspenders.
details.why: two divergent ad-hoc strips guard a crash class that can reappear in any new module or test that does not repeat the dance.

extra.value: independent.

title: Assert the baked image still fits a standard GitHub runner's disk budget
goal: E-16 The bake plane -- the BAKE gate answers presence and capacity, so `PUBLISH=true` stays safe on a stock runner.
acceptance_criteria: the gate flags a whale added to a baked group, passes on HEAD (whales firstboot-tier'd out), the budget is SSOT-defined, and `just drift-gate` is green.

details.what_how: GitHub publish is capacity-gated: the vLLM+SGLang whales (~47GB) blow a standard runner's disk, and the firstboot-tier evicts them from the bake so the image fits. details.why: re-bloating the bake breaks GitHub publish only after a full multi-hour bake run, and the cause is invisible until the runner hits ENOSPC.

title: Prove `90-generate-sbom.sh` can never fail the build
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- provenance generation is degrade-open by contract, and the contract is now tested rather than assumed.
acceptance_criteria: the test proves `exit 0` under all four failure modes and `just drift-gate` is green.

details.what_how: `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` must `exit 0` under every failure mode -- no egress, missing syft, unbound `MIOS_USR_DIR`, a syft scan hiccup -- because SBOM output is provenance, not a build prerequisite; a prior FATAL regression killed a 17-minute bake. Nothing tests that invariant. Add `automation/test_generate-sbom.sh`, wired into the shell-test gate, that runs the script under each of four modes: (a) `syft` absent with no egress, (b) unset `MIOS_USR_DIR`, (c) unwritable `ARTIFACT_DIR`, (d) a stubbed failing `syft scan` -- asserting `exit 0` plus a WARN line each time. Also assert the syft-installer `curl` carries `--retry`, regression-guarding the task_1128 sweep.
details.why: an SBOM hiccup can kill a full bake near the end of the run, and there is currently nothing to stop that regression from returning.

title: Pre-flight probe for build-download URL rot, run before cutting a release
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- rotted upstream assets are caught by a probe rather than by a mid-build hard failure.
acceptance_criteria: the probe lists every build URL with its status, flags a deliberately-broken URL, is documented as a pre-release step, and is `bash -n` clean.

details.what_how: Three build downloads (`forgejo-runner`, `jaeger`, `crowdsec`) silently rotted -- moved assets and renamed tarballs -- and only surfaced as a hard failure roughly an hour into a build. Add a NON-build-blocking probe `tools/check-build-urls.sh` plus a `just check-build-urls` target that extracts every build-time download URL from the Containerfiles and `automation`, resolves SSOT versions FIRST (SBOM-not-hardcode: versions are SSOT, so resolve the ref, then probe), issues `curl -sI --retry` / HEAD, and REPORTS each URL with its HTTP status, flagging non-2xx/3xx. This is a pre-flight, not a gate -- it is network-dependent, so it runs before cutting a release and may optionally hook a documented scheduled CI job, never the build gate.
details.where: new `tools/check-build-urls.sh`, `Justfile` (`check-build-urls` target), a note in the release runbook
details.why: upstream asset rot is currently discovered an hour into a build, wasting the whole run and blocking the release.

extra.value: independent.

title: Fold `build-mios.sh` into `mios-install.sh` so Linux is one installer file plus one contract
goal: E-21 One deploy front door -- `installation/mios-install.{sh,ps1,bat}` becomes the single guided dispatcher for every target.
acceptance_criteria: a bootc host defaults to bootc-switch and everything else to the fedora FHS path; the redirector preserves the web-entry one-liner; `bash -n` is clean; `just drift-gate` is green.

statements: a bootc host takes bootc-switch and everything else the FHS path, both exercised, and the redirector preserves arguments verbatim.

details.what_how: `build-mios.sh` is misnamed: it is a Linux BOOTSTRAP INSTALLER (bootc switch, FHS git-init root merge), not an OCI builder. Move its bootc-switch and FHS-root-merge logic -- preserving the `MIOS_FHS_TOTAL_ROOT_MERGE` gate and its prompt intact -- into the `fedora` and `bootc` stage paths of `installation/mios-install.sh`, then reduce `build-mios.sh` to a thin `exec installation/mios-install.sh fedora|bootc "$@"` redirector so the `curl .../build-mios.sh | bash` web entry (via install.sh / bootstrap.sh) keeps working. This is the change that makes Linux genuinely "one installer file plus one contract".
details.why: two Linux installers with divergent functionality means a fix landed in one silently misses the other, and the web one-liner reaches the weaker path.
details.do_not: delete the old entry point before its doc references are repointed. They are doc-bundled.

title: Declare the `[mini]` split-plane block in SSOT and project the all-dGPU vfio-pci bind from it
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- the MiOS-Metal router-host topology becomes SSOT-declared and drift-gated instead of living only in prose.
acceptance_criteria: the generator writes real vfio bind config (not just env echoes) derived from every `[mini]` key; the new drift-check fails if the projection is stale or the generator is deleted; `just drift-gate` exit 0; the feature ships disabled by default.

Write a generator that projects those keys into real `vfio-pci` bind material -- `vfio_pci.ids=` kargs under `usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d` and/or a `modprobe.d` bind -- and a regenerate-and-diff drift-check over that output. Static projection only; ships inert, no live hardware touched.
details.why: without it the split-plane design exists only in a doc, so nothing enforces the GPU-passthrough topology and any future host build silently diverges from the north star.

title: Fix the configurator port resolution and revert the unrequested `.ps1` special-target regression
goal: E-11 Unified config surface: mios.toml, the configurator and the Portal are one door at :8640/ -- the installer opens the SSOT-resolved door on both platforms.
acceptance_criteria: the Linux `config` route prints a URL with a resolved port and no literal `8640` remains in that path; `monitor`, `update` and `repos` reach their own handlers on Windows; `Get-MiosSsotValue` resolves at runtime; no-browser hosts get the offline configurator HTML.

statements: the Linux `config` route prints a URL with a resolved port and `grep -rn ':8640' <that path>` finds no literal.

details.what_how: `mios-install.sh:377` calls `mios_ssot_value 'ports.agent_pipe' '8640'` (2 args) instead of the resolver's `mios_ssot_value SECTION KEY DEFAULT` convention, so it returns empty and the URL becomes `http://localhost:/configure`; the literal `8640` is passed as the KEY argument, so it also never acts as a fallback. Correct the call to `mios_ssot_value ports agent_pipe "$default"` with the default sourced from SSOT, not inlined. On the PowerShell side, restore the `if ($entry['special'] -eq 'configure')` guard and its closing brace removed at mios-install.ps1:217-220 (which made every special target -- monitor/update/repos -- open the configurator and exit 0, leaving their handlers at :221/:228 dead), and fix the call to the non-existent `Get-MiosTomlValue` to the real `Get-MiosSsotValue` (mios-common.ps1:30). Add the missing "else offline configurator HTML" fallback in the Linux path, where `resolve_config` currently only warns when no browser launcher exists.
details.why: today the installer's config route opens a portless URL on Linux and hijacks three working targets on Windows with a command-not-found call -- the single config door is unreachable from the installer on both platforms.
details.do_not: leave the unrequested `.ps1` special-target regression in place while fixing the port.

title: Turn `check_clevis_luks` into a real regenerate-and-diff gate
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- clevis/LUKS TPM binding is SSOT-projected and provably gated, per Law 8.
acceptance_criteria: deleting the generator turns the gate RED; a broken SSOT read turns the gate RED; a committed golden artifact exists and a second generator run diffs clean; no `MIOS_OLLAMA_*` token remains in `referenced_names.txt`.

statements: deleting the generator turns `check_clevis_luks` RED, and a broken SSOT read turns it RED -- not skipped.

details.why: the gate is currently green by construction, so the entire clevis/LUKS SSOT read can be broken (or the projector deleted) with zero signal -- and a purged legacy token has crept back into the names registry.

title: Repair the greenboot coverage check: undefined `_fail`, shadowed function, hardcoded service list
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- greenboot health COVERAGE is gated so every critical service has a check and a rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: removing a greenboot check script for a listed service turns the gate RED (not exit 127); check-54's original assertions still run; `critical_services` is read from mios.toml; `hermes` appears in the list and has a health script; `just drift-gate` exit 0.

statements: removing a greenboot check script for a listed service turns `check_greenboot` RED -- and not with exit 127.

details.what_how: Four defects, all in `automation/38-drift-checks.sh`: (1) `_fail` at :3950 and :3964 is undefined -- only `_violation` (:85) increments `VIOLATIONS` -- so an uncovered service can never register drift; under `set -euo pipefail` (:55) `_fail` returns 127 and crashes the ENTIRE drift-gate (proven EXIT=127). Replace both with `_violation`. (2) The new `check_greenboot()` at :3946 shadows the pre-existing one at :3085 (bash last-def-wins), silently killing check-54's service-enablement and executable-script assertions -- rename the new check or merge the two. (3) The `critical_services` list at :3953 is hardcoded, violating Law 7 NO-HARDCODE and the spec's Where -- read it from a new mios.toml list. (4) The spec-named critical service `hermes` (:8642) is omitted and has no greenboot check script -- add both.
details.where: `automation/38-drift-checks.sh:3085,3946-3964`, `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (new critical-services list), the greenboot check-script directory
details.why: this is a live P0 -- the drift-gate itself crashes with exit 127 on exactly the condition it exists to detect, and it silently deleted a previously-working check while doing so.
details.do_not: leave the undefined `_fail` and the shadowed function. Exit 127 is a crash reported as a failure, which hides the real one.

title: Make the Rust names-registry generator emit byte-identical output and put it on check-30's path
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- ports are proven byte-parity before the shell/Python original is trusted less.
acceptance_criteria: `diff <(rust-gen) <(python3 tools/generate-names-registry.py)` is empty for both outputs; check-30 invokes the Rust binary (or the task states it does not); the crate fails to build if the parity harness diverges.

statements: `diff <(rust-gen) <(python3 tools/generate-names-registry.py)` is empty for both outputs, and the check invokes the Rust path.

details.what_how: `main.rs` is a `println!` stub and the crate's `[dependencies]` is empty (no `toml`/`serde`), so it cannot parse mios.toml or replicate the Python walk/alias/referenced-vars logic -- byte-identical output is not merely unmet but impossible. Add the toml/serde dependencies, port the walk, alias and referenced-vars logic from `tools/generate-names-registry.py`, and prove parity with a golden/characterization harness diffing the Rust output against the Python output for `names.generated.txt` and `referenced_names.txt`. Then either switch `automation/38-drift-checks.sh:1918` (which today runs `sys.executable + tools/generate-names-registry.py`) to the Rust binary, or state explicitly that the crate is not yet on the path -- claiming "check-30 green via the Rust path" while the binary is never invoked is the failure being corrected.
details.why: a workspace member that compiles trivially and emits nothing was marked done -- the exact "byte-identical Rust port that isn't" failure, which erodes trust in every subsequent port claim.
details.do_not: declare parity from a spot check. Diff the whole output.

title: Make the twins actually consume `mios-ssot-walk` instead of duplicating the walk verbatim
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one materializer owns the SSOT walk so the resolver twins stop diverging.
acceptance_criteria: grep finds the exclusion/keep lists in exactly ONE place; editing that place changes the output of resolver-twin (check 45) and names (check 30); the crate has a real consumer beyond the workspace manifest.

statements: `grep -rn` finds the exclusion/keep lists in exactly ONE place, and editing that place changes the twins' output.

details.what_how: The duplication the task exists to kill is fully intact: the `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS`/`WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD`/`WALK_EMIT_KEEP` logic is still copied verbatim across `check-resolver-twin.py:117-139` and both `userenv.sh:549-573`. The crate is a dead stub with WRONG data -- `lib.rs` declares `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS = ["meta","laws"]`, not the twins' real exclusion set, and captures no `WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD`/`WALK_EMIT_KEEP` and no `walk()` traversal; its only repo references are the workspace-member list in `Cargo.toml` and `generate-cargo-manifests.py`. Port the REAL walk into the crate, have it emit the exclusion/keep sets as a generated artifact, and make both `check-resolver-twin.py` and both `userenv.sh` read that single artifact rather than carrying their own copies.
details.why: three verbatim copies of the walk rules remain, so any future exclusion change must be made three times or the twins silently disagree -- and the "gates green" claim proves nothing because the crate is bypassed entirely.
details.do_not: duplicate the walk verbatim again. The duplicate is why the lists drifted.

title: Pure pre-execution validator for the runtime agent DAG
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails: the agent plane cannot starve its own host -- a malformed plan is rejected before it can burn a fan-out.
acceptance_criteria: `dag_validate` is invoked pre-schedule and returns a typed verdict; `test_mios_dag_validate.py` green with negative cases for cycle, self-loop, dangling dep and duplicate id; drift checks 6 (server-free import) and 11 (sibling test) pass; `just drift-gate` green.

statements: `dag_validate` is invoked pre-schedule, returns a typed verdict, and `test_mios_dag_validate.py` is green including negative cases.

details.what_how: `routing/dag_exec.py` (1585 lines) handles a malformed plan only REACTIVELY at runtime -- around line 918, "nothing ready + nothing running -> cycle/dangling dep: force one" -- so a cycle, self-loop, dangling dependency or duplicate node id consumes an entire fan-out before the nondeterministic "force one" recovery fires. Add a pure sibling `dag_validate.py` running Kahn topological classification over the plan node list BEFORE scheduling, returning a typed verdict (acyclic | cycle-nodes | dangling-deps | duplicate-ids | orphan-roots). `dag_exec` calls it and, on an invalid verdict, degrades to a deterministic linearization or single-agent path instead of live improvisation. Pure stdlib; must never import server.
details.why: today a single bad plan node costs a full fan-out of model calls before a nondeterministic recovery guesses its way out -- unbounded waste on the operator's own hardware.
details.do_not: validate after scheduling. Pre-execution is the point.

title: Deterministic quality-gate producer for smartroute escalation
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails: the agent plane cannot starve its own host -- the cost/quality cascade escalates on quality, not only on exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: a failing-quality local output makes `should_escalate()` return True and a good output keeps it False in `test_mios_quality_gate.py` (green); thresholds read from mios.toml; checks 6/11 green; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `routing/smartroute.py should_escalate(quality_ok, local_exhausted)` exists, but a grep across `mios_pipe/server.py` and `mios_dispatch` confirms NO producer of `quality_ok` anywhere -- so escalation only ever fires on `local_exhausted` and the whole quality dimension is dead code. Add a pure `quality_gate.py` scoring a local lane's output over deterministic signals (empty/whitespace, refusal/punt by reusing `native_loop._is_punt`, unterminated or malformed JSON via `mios_jsonsalvage`, a min-length/entity floor) returning `(ok, reason)`. Thresholds resolve from SSOT `[agent_pipe.quality]`; degrade-open on an unknown signal (`ok=True`) so it can never force a false paid escalation. Feed its bool as the `quality_ok` argument at the smartroute escalation seam.
details.where: new `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/routing/quality_gate.py`; `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/test_mios_quality_gate.py`; wire at `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/routing/lanes_resolver.py` (or the server escalation call); `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [agent_pipe.quality]`
details.why: half the routing cascade is inert -- a local lane that returns a refusal or malformed JSON is accepted as final output, and the escalation parameter it was designed around is permanently False.

title: Wire the dead cross-provider remote adapter behind an injected transport (code-only)
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired capabilities -- a capability MiOS already ships is either wired and gated or explicitly removed, never left inert.
acceptance_criteria: `remote_adapter.call(node_cfg, oai_request, transport)` round-trips a canned Anthropic AND a canned Gemini payload back to an OpenAI-shaped result using a fake transport (NO network); `openai`/unset api passes through unchanged; checks 6/11 green; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `routing/provider_translate.py` is a complete bidirectional OpenAI<->Anthropic/Gemini wire translator, but grep for `_anthropic_resp_to_oai(` / `_oai_msgs_to_anthropic(` call sites in server.py returns ZERO, and `lanes_resolver.py` remote_escalation is inert -- so escalating to a remote `[nodes.*]` with `api='anthropic'|'gemini'` would ship OpenAI-shaped bodies to a non-OpenAI endpoint. Add a pure `remote_adapter.py` composing provider_translate with an INJECTED async transport (no live client): translate request -> provider shape, await transport, translate response -> OpenAI shape; gated on `[nodes.*].api` + `[ai].remote_escalation`; degrade-open (api unset/openai -> passthrough).

title: De-hardcode the firstboot whale image refs in the bake-plan generator (Law 7)
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES -- no code path, least of all a generator, may carry an image-ref literal that SSOT already declares.
acceptance_criteria: grep for `docker.io/vllm` / `lmsysorg` in generate-bake-plan.py returns empty; a firstboot_token matching no core image makes `python3 tools/generate-bake-plan.py --check` exit non-zero; the negative test flips red-on-injection / green-on-restore; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-bake-plan.py` lines 140-145 hardcode two literal refs (`vllm_whale='docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai:latest'`, `sglang_whale='docker.io/lmsysorg/sglang:latest'`) for its "whale must be in core" validation -- a direct Law 7 violation inside a generator. Derive both from the already-loaded `[build.bake].firstboot_tokens`: for every token assert at least one `core` image substring-matches it (a token matching nothing is a dead/typo token -> validation error), and assert every image the existing `is_firstboot()` classifier pulls out is also in `core`. Extend `check_bake_plan` (check 35) so `--check` reds on a token matching no core image, and add a bogus-token negative test.
details.why: Renaming or retagging a whale in SSOT leaves the generator validating against a stale literal, so the eviction logic that keeps the bake inside a standard runner silently stops matching.

title: Reconcile [build.bake].core against the Quadlet-discovered bound-image set (anti-rot gate)

title: Retry-wrap and post-build verify the mios-sys / mios-cuda nested podman builds
goal: E-16 The bake plane -- the transient-failure classes that break a publish are systemically fixed, not re-hit per release.
acceptance_criteria: both builds run inside retry-with-backoff and are followed by an image-exists verification; the drift-check reds if either wrapper is removed and greens on HEAD; `bash -n usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh` runs two heavy nested `podman build`s (lines 66-76 mios-sys, 79-89 mios-cuda) that pull docker.io FROM stages and do pip/npm/git installs (searxng, crawl4ai, firecrawl, open-webui) with NO retry and NO post-build verification -- grep for `retry` in the file is empty. A transient Docker Hub 429 or GitHub 504 mid-build hard-fails the whole OCI build (the class task_1128 hardened for curl fetches but never applied to the podman invocation). Wrap each build in a bounded retry-with-backoff mirroring `mios-bake-group`'s loop shape, follow each with `podman image exists localhost/mios-sys|mios-cuda` so a silent no-op is caught, surface persistent failure loudly, and add a static gate asserting both builds are retry-wrapped.
details.why: One upstream 429 currently throws away an hour-plus of build and fails the publish, and a build that silently produced no image is indistinguishable from success.

title: MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS: fail closed on absent tooling to kill the vacuous-pass class
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- a critical check can never report green because the tool that would run it was missing.
acceptance_criteria: with python3 hidden from PATH and `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`, a critical check exits 1 (fail-closed); with the flag unset it still exits 0 exactly as today; both CI workflows set the flag; a negatives-harness case proves both modes; `just drift-gate` green on HEAD.

details.what_how: `38-drift-checks.sh` contains ~163 return-0/skip paths and its own header admits checks "Vacuous-passes where python3 or the copies are absent" -- so on a runner without python3 the security gates silently PASS. Define a documented CRITICAL set (the python3-dependent ones: `check_no_hardcode`, `check_cli_eval_safety`, `check_cli_sql_safety`, `check_agent_schema`, `check_drift_projection`) and an env switch `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1` converting their tool-absent skip into a hard `_violation`; leave the default fail-open behavior byte-identical so nothing regresses. Set the flag in both CI workflows, where python3 is guaranteed.
details.why: A runner missing python3 turns the entire security tier -- eval safety, SQL safety, NO-HARDCODE -- into a green rubber stamp, which is worse than having no gate at all.

title: Disambiguate the install.sh family with a role-marker contract and collision gate

goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- kargs projection is gated end-to-end so a boot-critical flatten cannot silently drop an entry.

title: Author the chrony PTP first-boot drop-in the render script itself defers
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- a documented deferred TODO becomes a real hardware-detected deploy-time behavior.

title: cfg-gate the Windows-only mios-wallpaperd crate so `cargo build --workspace` compiles on the Linux CI runner
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- a single Cargo workspace that the Containerfile can build on a stock Linux runner, which every later crate port depends on.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build --workspace --offline` succeeds on a Linux host; the new Cargo.toml-parsing check is green on HEAD; a negative-test that moves a windows dep back into `[dependencies]` trips it.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-wallpaperd/Cargo.toml` declares `wry`, `tao`, `windows-service` and `windows` as unconditional dependencies of an unconditional workspace member, so a Linux `cargo build --workspace` / `cargo test` fails outright and takes the task_1176 test gate and the task_1179 build stage down with it. Move those four crates under a `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]` table and put `#![cfg(windows)]` on the `[[bin]]` and its `main`/`host`/`workerw`/`guiwatch` modules so off-Windows the crate resolves to an empty artifact. Add a drift-check that parses every `tools/native/*/Cargo.toml` and fails when a Windows-only crate appears outside a `cfg(windows)` target table.
details.why: Until this lands the Rust workspace cannot be built or tested anywhere except a Windows box, so the compiled tier has no CI at all and no native binary can be baked into the image.

title: Make generate-cargo-manifests.py enumerate crate dirs and add a generator-clean gate over tools/native/Cargo.toml
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the workspace manifest becomes a projection of the filesystem rather than a hand-maintained list, so new crates cannot fall out of the build.
acceptance_criteria: generator output equals the committed `tools/native/Cargo.toml` byte-for-byte; dropping in a new crate dir and regenerating updates `members` deterministically; the new "cargo-manifest generator-clean" check is green on HEAD and a hand-edit of the members list reds it.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-cargo-manifests.py` hardcodes `members=[...]` and emits the `[workspace.package]` version/edition block, while the existing gate near `automation/38-drift-checks.sh:3427` only compares the version STRING -- so a fifth crate could be added and silently never join the workspace. Change the generator to ENUMERATE member directories (any dir under `tools/native/` containing a `Cargo.toml`), keep projecting the version via workspace inheritance, and add a drift-check that regenerates into a temp file and diffs it against the committed `tools/native/Cargo.toml`.
details.why: A crate that is on disk but missing from `members` is never compiled, never tested and never shipped -- and today nothing would report it.

title: Add a cached Rust builder stage to the Containerfile plus COPY lines for every portable bin, gated by a bins-installed check
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- native binaries actually reach `/usr/libexec/mios/` in the baked image, so the runtime stops falling back to Python for gates that already have a compiled implementation.

Add a cached Rust builder stage that statically builds the portable crates for `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, add one `COPY --from` per binary into `/usr/libexec/mios/`, and add a drift-check that enumerates non-Windows `[[bin]]`/binary crates from `cargo metadata` and asserts each has a matching COPY line. details.why: Compiled tools that never enter the image are dead code -- every runtime gate keeps using the fragile Python fallback the port was meant to retire.

title: Harden mios-version-check's hand-rolled TOML scan against subsections, comments and prefix keys, with regression tests
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the compiled version oracle agrees with the shell gate on malformed input, so the version SSOT check cannot be fooled.
acceptance_criteria: unit tests cover all four malformed-input classes and pass; the binary's verdict still matches the bash `check_version_ssot` on HEAD; the task_1176 cargo-test gate runs them; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-version-check/src/main.rs` finds `[meta].mios_version` with a naive line loop (`starts_with('[')` toggles the section, `starts_with("mios_version")` matches the key). That mis-reads a `[meta.sub]` subsection header as leaving `meta`, accepts a commented-out `mios_version` line, prefix-matches a sibling like `mios_version_extra`, and never strips inline comments from the value. Rewrite it as exact-key plus section-path aware parsing, staying zero-dependency stdlib, and add `#[cfg(test)]` cases for subsection headers, commented lines, prefix-key false matches, and quoted / inline-comment values.
details.why: A version checker that reads the wrong line will bless a tree whose version SSOT has actually drifted -- the exact 37x-hardcoded-version class this tool exists to prevent.

details.what_how: `tools/ascii-sweep.py` (294 lines) is a pure typographic-Unicode-to-ASCII scrubber with a fixed substitution table, run across ALL MiOS-owned text (docs, shell, TOML, JSON), and its output is verifiable offline. details.why: A text scrubber that runs over the whole tree with no parity oracle can silently mangle content on port; without the golden fixture the Python can never be retired.

title: Normalize HNSW index params and emb_version widths across the emb schema, gated by check_vector_schema_hygiene
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- pgvector recall behaves the same for every embedded table instead of half the fleet riding silent defaults.
acceptance_criteria: `psql -f schema-init.sql` re-applies idempotently; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED on a fixture where an HNSW index loses its params or an emb column loses provenance; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: `schema-init.sql` is inconsistent: the 4 original vector indexes (knowledge:42, agent_memory:72, mios_rag:452, config_kv:567) carry the canonical `WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64)`, but the ~19 newer HNSW indexes added by task_1032/11/18/22 (skill/verb/tool_call/directory_entry:635-638, package_set..preset:654-776, event/session:783-788, account_preference:819) omit the params, contradicting the task_1028/7/11 "mirror the exact DDL" rule. `mios_identity.account_preferences.emb` (1139) has NO index at all and an outlier `emb_version varchar(32)` against varchar(64) everywhere else. Add the explicit params to every param-less HNSW index (idempotent -- `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` makes it a no-op on live DBs but pins intent), unify the width, and add `check_vector_schema_hygiene` at the next free number (63+) that greps every `USING hnsw` line for the canonical params and asserts every `emb vector(768)` column has sibling `emb_model` + `emb_version`.
details.why: Indexes on pgvector defaults give measurably worse recall than the canonical tuning, and an emb column with no `emb_model`/`emb_version` cannot be invalidated when the embedding model changes.

title: Extend embed-backfill to config_kv and account_preference plus a schema-to-backfill binding gate
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the embed-backfill worker actually fills every declared vector column, so no `emb` column is decorative.
acceptance_criteria: backfill populates `config_kv.emb` / `account_preference.emb` with provenance (verified against a monkeypatched pg + embed client); a second run is a near-noop; the coverage gate is GREEN on HEAD and RED when an emb column is added with no PK_MAP or exempt entry; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: `embed_backfill.py`'s `PK_MAP` (lines 95-102) covers only {skill, verb, tool_call, directory_entry, event, session}, yet ~13 other tables declare `emb vector(768)` plus an HNSW index with nothing populating them -- most valuably `config_kv` (operators cannot semantic-search settings) and `account_preference`. Extend `PK_MAP` and `get_text_projection()` (line 113) to cover `config_kv` (projection: `scope.key` + description + value) and `account_preference` (projection: key + value), reusing the worker's existing idempotent (`emb IS NULL` / stale `emb_version`), provenance-stamped, 3x-retry, fail-open pattern. Then add `check_backfill_coverage` at the next free number: statically parse every `emb vector(768)` table out of `schema-init.sql` and assert each is either in `PK_MAP` or on an explicit commented `_BACKFILL_EXEMPT` allow-list.
details.why: Every unfilled `emb` column is index storage and schema surface paying for a feature that returns nothing -- and today a new dead vector column can be added with zero signal.

title: Reconcile the duplicate account-preference tables and fix allocate_gid()'s shared-sequence UPG collision
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- one canonical account surface in the agent datastore, and UID/GID allocation that produces a valid user-private group.
acceptance_criteria: the schema applies idempotently; only one preference surface remains and the new gate goes RED if a second `*account_preference*` table reappears; `allocate_uid`/`allocate_gid` yield a UPG-consistent pair asserted in a test; `materialize-user-config` still round-trips a seeded pref; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: Two competing preference tables exist: `account_preference` (public, task_1047 line 809 -- layer-based, HNSW-indexed, carries `emb_model` + `emb_version`, and the only one read, by `materialize-user-config.py:87`) and the dead `mios_identity.account_preferences` (task_224, line 1134 -- UUID/pref_key, no reader or writer anywhere, no HNSW index, no `emb_model`, mismatched `emb_version varchar(32)`). Reconcile to ONE surface: either drop the task_224 table or replace it with a compatibility VIEW onto `account_preference`, and record which and why. Separately, `allocate_gid()` (lines 803-807) draws from the SAME `uid_alloc` sequence as `allocate_uid()`, so a fresh user gets uid=1000 / gid=1001 and user-private-group is impossible -- give gid its own sequence or make `allocate_gid` mirror the uid. Add a drift-check asserting exactly one preferences table and no shared alloc sequence.
details.why: Two tables named for the same fact is a split-brain waiting for the next writer to pick the wrong one, and uid != gid breaks the user-private-group model every projected Linux account assumes.

title: Close the verb `i18n` round-trip gap in the DB-to-TOML materializer and widen check 31's compared field set
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the DB-to-TOML materializer is a LOSSLESS projection of the SSOT, which is the whole premise of the DB-driven config plane.
acceptance_criteria: a verb seeded with an `i18n` table survives TOML -> DB -> TOML byte-for-byte (diff clean); check 31 is GREEN on HEAD and RED when `i18n` is dropped from the materializer; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: The `verb` table carries an `i18n jsonb` column (schema line 586 region) that `seed-db-config.py` can populate from mios.toml, but `materialize-config-toml.py`'s verb SELECT (lines 163-171) never reads or emits it, so localized verb text is LOST on any DB-to-TOML materialize. Check 31 (`drift_projection`, `38-drift-checks.sh:1962`) cannot catch it because it only diffs fields both sides already handle. Add `i18n` to the materializer SELECT and emit, ensure the seeder re-ingests it, verify the `aliases` -> `hidden_aliases` remap (materialize line 205) survives the trip, then extend check 31's compared field set to include `i18n` and assert `hidden_aliases` parity.
details.why: A materializer that silently drops a column means any operator who round-trips config through the DB loses their localized verb text with no error and no diff.

title: Add config-restore.py, the V5 point-in-time rollback writer over the config_event log
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- config time-travel gains its write half, so an operator can revert a setting, not merely read that it changed.
acceptance_criteria: against a monkeypatched pg seeded with an old -> new -> newer event chain, `--dry-run` emits the correct as-of value and UPDATE, and `--apply` reverts the `config_kv` row to the historical value; a unit test asserts the reconstructed value for a chosen timestamp; `bash -n` / py-compile clean; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: task_1049 shipped the append-only `config_event` audit plus a READ-ONLY `config-history.py`; there is no writer, so history is visible but not revertible. Add `usr/libexec/mios/config-restore.py` which, given a `scope.key` plus a target timestamp or event id, reconstructs the as-of value from the `config_event` log (schema line 823) and re-applies it to `config_kv`. Because the write re-fires the existing `config_kv_audit_trigger`, the revert is itself a new event -- proper event-sourcing, no history rewrite. Default `--dry-run` prints the exact UPDATE; `--apply` executes. Fail-open: DB down means a log line and a non-zero exit, never a stack trace. Reuse the shared pg-config helper from task_1183 if landed, else the local one.
details.why: Without a writer, a bad config change is diagnosable but not undoable -- the operator must hand-craft SQL against the live config plane to recover.

title: Capture `actor` on the verb / domain_verb audit triggers and surface it in config-history
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the config audit log attributes every change, not just the config_kv half.
acceptance_criteria: a simulated verb INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE records a non-NULL actor in `config_event` (asserted in the audit test against a monkeypatched/psql fixture); `config-history.py` shows the actor for a verb change; the schema re-applies idempotently; `just drift-gate` passes.

details.what_how: `log_config_kv_change()` records `actor` (owner_user) on every `config_event` (schema lines 909-922), but `log_verb_change()` / `log_domain_verb_change()` (lines 951-993) insert only `(scope, key, new_value, source)` with NO actor, so verb history has a NULL actor and nobody can be attributed to a verb change. There is no `NEW.owner` column on `verb`, so read the actor from a session GUC the writer sets -- `current_setting('mios.actor', true)` defaulting to `session_user` -- and write it into the `config_event.actor` column in ALL THREE branches of both triggers; have `seed-db-config.py` set that GUC when it applies changes. `config-history.py` already selects `actor`, so the value surfaces once populated.
details.why: A verb -- an executable capability -- can be changed today with no record of who changed it, which makes the audit log unusable for the one class of change that most needs attribution.

title: Harden redact.py: add the high-value credential patterns and recurse structured payloads
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails: the agent plane cannot starve its own host -- specifically its secret/PII redaction clause on every persist and every A2A federate.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_redact.py` gains a case per new pattern (PEM/JWT/glpat/xox/AKIA/generic assignment), a nested-dict case where a secret under a benign scope is masked, and a negative case leaving benign text unchanged; all redact tests green under `just drift-gate`.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/redact.py` (49 lines) is the task_1033 persist + federation sanitizer, but it only matches `sk-` / `sk-ant-` / `hf_` / `ghp_` / `Bearer` / email / `MIOS_*=`, and `redact()` takes a FLAT string while the federation seam (`mios_pipe/federation/a2a.py`) and memory persist both serialize dicts and JSON. Add PEM private-key blocks (`-----BEGIN (RSA|EC|OPENSSH|PRIVATE) KEY-----`...`-----END...`), JWTs (`eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.eyJ...\....`), GitHub fine-grained (`github_pat_`), GitLab (`glpat-`), Slack (`xox[baprs]-`), AWS keys (`AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`), and generic `(password|passwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key)\s*[=:]\s*<val>` assignments. Add `redact_obj(obj)` that walks dict/list recursively, redacting string leaves and masking any dict KEY matching the secret-name regex, returning `(obj, is_redacted)`; wire it at the JSON persist and federate call sites. Do NOT redo the task_1057/33 `config_event` SQL-trigger work -- this is the Python `redact()` seam only.
details.why: A private key or JWT inside a nested payload passes the current flat-string redactor untouched and is persisted to the memory store and shipped to every federated A2A peer.

title: Project systemd userdb `.user` records from SSOT accounts, with a regenerate-and-diff gate
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall (WS-ACCT) -- the Linux account model becomes an SSOT projection instead of an imperative daemon editing /etc/passwd.
acceptance_criteria: a new regenerate-and-diff drift-check (Law 8 SSOT-PROJECTION) is green; tampering a committed `*.user` reds it; a negative-test proves an added `[[autounattend.accounts]]` row projects a new record and that no password field appears in any `.user`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: task_1127 P2 named `/usr/lib/userdb/<name>.user` (systemd userdb, with nss-systemd synthesizing passwd/group) the PRIMARY Linux account mechanism, but it does not exist: `automation/17-accounts-db.sh` only installs the runtime `mios-account-sync` daemon, which imperatively edits `/etc/passwd`, and there is no `/usr/lib/userdb` in the tree at all. Add a generator projecting the SSOT identity rows -- `[identity]` (username / fullname / shell / groups / hostname) plus every `[[autounattend.accounts]]` -- into one JSON drop-in per account (userName, uid slot, realName, homeDirectory, shell, memberOf) following the systemd userdb record schema. Per Law 11 store NO password hash in the `.user` file: it references `/etc/mios/secrets.env` / shadow and carries only non-secret identity. Ship it as a static, always-on projection independent of `[accounts].db_backed`, which gates only the live sync daemon.
details.where: new `tools/generate-userdb.py`, generated `usr/lib/userdb/*.user`, source `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (`[identity]` + `[[autounattend.accounts]]`), gate in `automation/38-drift-checks.sh`, install wire in `automation/17-accounts-db.sh` (or a new `18-userdb.sh`)
details.why: Today accounts exist only as imperative runtime edits to `/etc/passwd` on a `/usr`-read-only image -- nothing declarative, nothing gated, and nothing that survives a `bootc rollback` predictably.

title: caller-keys.json schema, example fixture, fail-closed validator and gate for the inbound /v1 auth boundary
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the security boundary in front of the ONE OpenAI /v1 door is a validated, gated artifact rather than an unchecked file.
acceptance_criteria: the example file validates green in a new drift-check; a unit test proves malformed / duplicate-id / unbound-account inputs are rejected and that load fail-closes under `api_require_auth=true`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `[security].api_caller_keys_path=/etc/mios/ai/v1/caller-keys.json` is consumed by `server.py` for the FED-G1 inbound auth gate and by `principal_bind_mode` to bind an authenticated key to an `account` (owner -> RLS), but there is no schema, generator or validator -- a malformed, duplicate-id or unbound-account file silently degrades the auth boundary. Add a validator over the schema `list of {id, key, account?/owner?, scope?}` that rejects duplicate ids, empty keys, and any `account` naming no seeded account; have `server.py` call it at load and FAIL-CLOSE when `api_require_auth=true` and the file is present-but-malformed, degrading open only when the file is ABSENT so today's single-user default is preserved. Ship a committed `caller-keys.example.json` beside the existing `etc/mios/ai/v1/a2a-peers.json` as the gated fixture.
details.where: new `usr/libexec/mios/mios-caller-keys-validate` (or a `mios_pipe/access` module + import), new `etc/mios/ai/v1/caller-keys.example.json`, auth path in `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/server.py`, gate + negative-test in `automation/38-drift-checks.sh`, unit test `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/test_mios_caller_keys.py`
details.why: A typo in caller-keys.json today can quietly disable inbound authentication or bind a caller to the wrong RLS owner, exposing another account's data through the public /v1 surface.

title: Static SECRETS-NEVER-IN-ENV (Law 11) source-tree drift-gate with a planted-secret negative test
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- Law 11 gains a source-tree enforcing check, because a law with no check is not enforced.
acceptance_criteria: the new check passes on the clean tree; a negative-test planting `MIOS_PG_PASS=hunter2` into a scanned env fixture reds the gate; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Law 11 is enforced at BAKE by `99-postcheck` but has NO source-tree drift-check, so a secret committed into a group/world-readable env file (`install.env`, `agent-pipe.env`, `hermes/api.env` -- all referenced via `EnvironmentFile=` in `usr/lib/systemd/system/`) ships un-flagged until bake time. Add a drift-check that enumerates every committed file targeted by an `EnvironmentFile=` line, runs the `redact.py` secret-shape patterns over each, and FAILS if any carries a plaintext secret value; additionally assert any file named `secrets.env` is referenced with 0600 intent and never made world-readable via tmpfiles or sysusers. title: Property-test the PDP invariant that a pruned verb can never dispatch (harden WS-A9)
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails: the agent plane cannot starve its own host -- the access decision point is proven to fail closed on both the surface and the dispatch axis.
acceptance_criteria: the parity property-test runs N randomized cases with zero surface-not-subset-of-dispatch violations and confirms unknown-ceiling fail-closed on both axes; test green under `just drift-gate`.

details.what_how: The WS-A9 invariant is that a verb pruned from a caller's tool surface (`mios_policy._agent_rbac_filter` / `_user_rbac_filter`) can NEVER still dispatch (`mios_policy._dispatch_pdp_reason`), because both route through the single `mios_pdp.decide()` / `resolve_ceiling()` core in `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/access/pdp.py`. `test_mios_pdp.py` covers `decide()` in isolation but nothing property-tests the PARITY. Add a property/fuzz test over randomized policies (denied / allowed / `max_permission` including unknown-tier typos) and randomized verb catalogs asserting that every verb the surface filter drops is also denied at the dispatch gate -- no dispatchable-but-pruned verb -- and that an unknown `max_permission` fails CLOSED on both paths, regression-guarding the old fail-OPEN defect that `resolve_ceiling` fixed.
details.where: new `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/test_mios_pdp_parity.py`, exercising `mios_pdp` plus the filter/dispatch semantics from `mios_pipe/access/policy.py`, run via the agent-pipe test gate
details.why: If the two paths ever diverge, a caller sees a verb hidden from its surface but can still invoke it directly -- a privilege escalation that unit tests on `decide()` alone cannot detect.

details.why: every desktop session today boots a stub bar with frozen Catppuccin colors while the real, theme-driven shell sits unused in the image -- all Quickshell work downstream of it is dead on arrival.

title: Gate ship-completeness of the QML component graph: every surface Config.qml pulls in must exist in the image
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- the shell's file set is declared and enforced, not an accident of a wholesale directory copy.

details.what_how: only `Theme.qml` is registered in mios.toml `[dotfiles.registry.quickshell]`; the other six surfaces (Config / PanelWindow / Sidebar / Notifications / NotifModel / PortalData) ship only because `08-system-files-overlay` copies the `usr/` tree wholesale, so nothing gates their presence and deleting one silently breaks the shell -- `Config.qml`'s `Sidebar{}` / `Notifications{}` would fail to resolve at runtime. details.why: a shell surface can be dropped or renamed in a refactor and the build stays green -- the breakage only shows up as a blank desktop on a real machine.

title: Define the canonical `[mini]` / `[mini.mesh]` SSOT tables so both mini generators stop falling through to defaults
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- the MiOS-Metal split-plane is SSOT-reachable instead of permanently inert.
acceptance_criteria: the generators resolve real committed keys, not defaults -- `mios-metal-vfio-gen` prints `MIOS_METAL_ENABLED=true` when `[mini].enabled=true`; the new drift-check asserts every referenced mini key exists; a negative test in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` deletes one key and proves non-zero exit; `just drift-gate` green on HEAD.

Add a canonical `[mini]` block adjacent to `[mini.gpu]` (`enabled`, `bind_dgpu_vfio`, `host_floor_cores`, `host_floor_ram_gb`) plus a real `[mini.mesh]` (`enabled`, `headscale_domain`), each key commented per `doc-mios-metal.md` §1.1/§2e, and add a gate that parses every `d.get('mini',...)` key the two generators reference and asserts it exists in mios.toml (fail-open only when python3 is absent, mirroring check 53).
details.why: an operator can set nothing about the Mini split-plane today -- both generators ignore mios.toml entirely and emit fixed defaults, so the whole feature is unconfigurable.

title: Project the master `inet mios-router` nftables table and gate against cross-table conflicts
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- the router's packet policy is SSOT-projected, syntax-validated and provably not stepping on another writer's table.
acceptance_criteria: the master table projects from SSOT and passes `nft -c`, or skips-with-warning when nft is absent (fail-open); the gate asserts default-drop plus masquerade are present and no foreign table name is duplicated; a negative test flipping the forward policy to accept makes the gate fail; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `doc-mios-metal.md` §3b-cross and steps 10/13 specify a hand-owned master `inet mios-router` table (WAN masquerade, default-drop forward, per-bridge isolation, `flow add @ft` / `flags offload`) with libvirt, netavark and tailscale each owning their OWN table and coexisting by hook priority, and NO firewalld. The only nft artifact in the tree is `usr/share/mios/security/egress.nft`, an unrelated egress ruleset. Add `usr/libexec/mios/mios-metal-router-nft-gen` projecting the master table from `[mini]`/`[mini.mesh]` (bridge names, WAN iface, subnets), plus a gate that (a) validates the render with `nft -c -f` (syntax-only, never a live apply) and (b) asserts the table declares default-drop forward + masquerade and does NOT redefine another writer's table name.
details.why: without the master table the router forwards by default and NATs nothing, and a hand-written ruleset that redefines libvirt's or tailscale's table silently flushes their rules on load.

title: Gate the router core/RAM budget: the guest allocation may not breach the host floor
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- the hypervisor-router keeps enough CPU and RAM to route, enforced arithmetically at commit time.

details.what_how: `doc-mios-metal.md` §2e requires the SSOT to compute the guest CPU/RAM share from the RESERVED router housekeeping floor and the drift-gate to fail when the guest allocation would leave the router under that floor (indicative floors: >=2 cores + 2-4GB for Wi-Fi7/2.5GbE, >=4 cores for 10GbE without offload). Using `[mini].host_floor_cores`/`host_floor_ram_gb` plus a `[mini].guest_cpu_pct`/`guest_ram_pct` (or absolute) allocation, add a generator computing the guest share and a drift-check asserting `host_total - guest_share >= host_floor` for BOTH CPU and RAM. Pure arithmetic over SSOT -- no live hardware needed.

title: Project a second, non-vfio safe-mode recovery UKI cmdline so an all-GPU-bound router is not a brick
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- there is always a boot path that yields a real console on a machine whose GPUs are all bound to vfio.
acceptance_criteria: both the vfio-bound and the non-vfio recovery cmdlines project from SSOT; the drift-check asserts the recovery entry carries no vfio-pci binding while the primary does; a negative test injecting vfio-pci into the recovery entry makes the gate fail; drift-gate green.

title: SSOT-project the Linux target-prereq catalog, wire the Rust toolchain, and show the plan in `--dry-run`
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- one prereq resolver keyed off the chosen target, readable before anything is installed.

details.what_how: `resolve_target_prereqs()` in `installation/mios-install.sh` (line 416) HARDCODES `for pkg in git curl podman` instead of resolving from SSOT, never ensures the Rust toolchain that native/build targets need -- `mios-common.sh` already ships `mios_ensure_rust` at line 118 and nothing calls it -- and runs at line 473, AFTER the `--dry-run` early exit at line 456, so a dry run never reveals what it would install. Add an `[install.prereqs.<target>]` SSOT block (or a linux sub-table under the existing `[bootstrap.prereqs]`, mios.toml:8893) enumerating the dnf packages per target; make `resolve_target_prereqs` read it via `mios_ssot_value`; call `mios_ensure_rust` for build/update/native targets; and move the prereq PLAN print into the `--dry-run` block so the dry run shows the resolved package list and rust decision without executing (still exit 0). title: Harden `mios_ensure_repo` to the bootstrap.sh fetch pattern (retry + Forgejo fallback + body validation) and widen the retry gate
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- one repo fetch, hardened once, on both equal publishers.
acceptance_criteria: `mios_ensure_repo` carries `--retry`/`--max-time` + a body check + an SSOT-resolved Forgejo fallback; the gate flags a retry-less fetch anywhere in `installation/*.sh` and passes at HEAD; the mock-curl test proves the fallback fires when the primary host fails; `bash -n` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mios_ensure_repo` in `installation/mios-common.sh` (line 107) fetches the bootstrap tarball with a bare `curl -fsSL ... | tar` -- no `--retry`, no `--max-time`, no validation of the downloaded body, and GitHub-only -- while sibling `bootstrap.sh` already implements the hardened pattern (`--retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --retry-connrefused --max-time 120`, `-s` non-empty check, cache-bust). This also evades the task_1128 curl-retry gate (check 64), which does not scan `installation/*.sh`. Bring `mios_ensure_repo` up to the gold pattern and add a Forgejo mirror fallback (GitHub and Forgejo are equal publishers), resolving org/repo/mirror hosts from SSOT `[bootstrap]` (mios.toml:8710) rather than the literal `github.com`. Then extend coverage: add a drift-check, or widen check 64's file glob via the multi-path `../mios-bootstrap` resolver, asserting every network fetch in `installation/*.sh` carries `--retry`/`--tries`.
details.where: `installation/mios-common.sh`, `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (extend or sit adjacent to check 64), `installation/test_mios_common_fetch.sh` (new, mock curl)
details.why: a single transient network blip aborts an install mid-fetch with a truncated tree, and a GitHub outage takes the whole install front door down even though an equal mirror exists.

title: Unit-cover the awk SSOT resolver in mios-common.sh and wire a shell-test gate
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- the most load-bearing shared installer contract is protected by tests, not by luck.
acceptance_criteria: the test passes at HEAD; deliberately deleting the quoted-value awk branch (line 35) makes the hex-color case FAIL; the shell-test gate invokes it; `bash -n` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mios_ssot_value` in `installation/mios-common.sh` (lines 26-45) is the single contract every installer surface resolves ports and colors through, and it has ZERO tests. Its awk is subtle: it must return a quoted value even when the value contains `#` (the hex-color case, line 35), strip an inline `# comment` from an unquoted value (line 37), honor layer precedence user > host > vendor (`mios_ssot_layers`, lines 14-24), fall back to the DEFAULT argument on a missing key, and never break callers under `set -o pipefail`. Write `installation/test_mios_common.sh` with a fixture per behavior -- including a `#1A407F`-style value and a value with a trailing inline comment -- and wire it into a shell-test gate mirroring `automation/test_generate-sbom.sh` and its existing gate.
details.why: a one-character awk change silently returns an empty port or a truncated hex color to every installer surface, and today nothing would catch it before an operator's machine does.

title: Derive the law-id ceiling in roadmap-index.py from [laws] instead of the hardcoded 1..13
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- the docs tooling that enforces governance must not itself violate Law 7 (NO-HARDCODE) / Law 8 (SSOT-PROJECTION).

details.what_how: `tools/roadmap-index.py` line 145 validates roadmap `laws[]` refs with `law < 1 or law > 13`, while mios.toml `[laws]` now registers 15 (14 TARGET-LANGUAGES, 15 DOUBLE-REPO-TRIPLE-CHECK) -- so any ROADMAP workstream legitimately citing Law 14/15 is falsely flagged. The script already loads mios.toml via `tomllib` (lines ~37-41); add a helper deriving the valid id set from the `{ id = N, ... }` rows and replace the numeric bound with membership in that set, erroring with a message naming the max known law id.
details.why: every new law added to the registry is unusable in the ROADMAP until someone remembers to edit a magic number in Python -- the exact drift class the gate exists to prevent.

details.why: headers pointing at files that were moved or deleted send agents chasing dead paths, and the rot only ever grows because nothing measures it.

title: W3C Trace Context: adopt inbound traceparent, propagate it outbound
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails -- a request crossing agent, MCP and A2A hops is one traceable causal chain, including across federated peers.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_trace.py` asserts `parse(format(id, span, True))` round-trips, rejects a malformed traceparent, and confirms `new_trace_id()` is 32-hex; a test drives an outbound call stub and asserts a valid `traceparent` header is set; existing trace tests still pass; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `observability/trace.py:new_trace_id()` mints a 16-hex (64-bit) id and server.py (~335-345) propagates only a custom `X-MiOS-Trace` header, so MiOS traces never stitch to a standard collector or peer. Widen `new_trace_id()` to 32-hex (128-bit) while keeping `new_span_id()` at 16-hex; add pure helpers `format_traceparent(trace_id, span_id, sampled)` and `parse_traceparent(header)` validating `00-<32hex>-<16hex>-<2hex>`; adopt an inbound `traceparent` in server.py's request-mint path; and emit it outbound on the A2A (`a2a_client._a2a_send_message_to_peer`), MCP (`mcp._mcp_http_rpc`) and Hermes hops alongside the legacy header.
details.why: every federated hop starts a fresh, non-standard trace, so a slow or failed multi-peer request cannot be followed end to end.

title: Sign A2A push-notification webhooks with a detached JWS
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails -- what the agent plane pushes to a peer is attributable and tamper-evident, not a bare bearer token.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_a2a.py` performs a real Ed25519 sign->verify round-trip of a push payload (tampering yields verify False) using the file's existing fake-signer stub pattern, and asserts the header is absent when the flag is off; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `a2a.py:_a2a_fire_push_notifications` (~line 1096) POSTs the Task envelope with only a static `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, so a receiver cannot verify issuer or integrity -- even though `a2a.py` already owns the Ed25519 passport key and detached-JWS primitives (`_agent_card_signature`, `_agent_card_signing_input`, `_jcs_canonicalize`, `_b64u`). Add `_sign_push_payload(task)` emitting a detached JWS over `JCS(task)` into an `X-A2A-JWS` header, plus a receive-side `verify_push_jws(body, header, pubkey)`, gated by a new `[a2a].sign_push_notifications` SSOT flag (default off, degrade-open when no key is present).
details.why: a leaked or replayed bearer token lets anyone forge task-completion webhooks into a peer, with no way for the receiver to tell.

title: Enforce AgentCard signature verification on peer probe
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails -- federated peers are trusted only after verification, so a forged card cannot inject skills into the agent plane.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_a2a_client.py` feeds the probe a tampered-signature card and asserts rejection plus demerit under the flag, and acceptance when the flag is off; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `a2a_client._a2a_fetch_card` / `_a2a_probe_peer` fetch a peer's AgentCard and index its skills without ever calling `a2a.py`'s `_verify_agent_card_signature`, so a signed card's issuer is never checked. Wire verification into the probe behind a new `[a2a].require_signed_cards` SSOT flag: when set, an invalid signature makes the probe reject with status `card-signature-invalid` and record a reputation demerit via the injected `_A2A_REPUTATION`; unsigned cards and flag-off keep today's fail-open behavior. Inject the verifier through `configure()` to preserve the one-way module boundary (no new `a2a_client` -> `a2a` import edge beyond the existing helper import).
details.why: a signed card is currently trusted exactly as much as a forged one -- an attacker advertising skills gets them registered and dispatched to.

title: MCP tools/list pagination: follow nextCursor instead of registering page 1 only
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails -- the agent plane's tool surface is complete and bounded, not silently truncated.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_mcp.py` stubs a fake RPC returning two pages (page 1 with `nextCursor`, page 2 without) and asserts ALL tools from both pages register as `mcp.<sid>.<tool>`, and that the page cap prevents an infinite loop; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mcp._mcp_probe_server` (~line 490) calls `tools/list` exactly once (rid=2), reads `result.tools` and IGNORES `result.nextCursor`; per the MCP spec a server with more tools than one page returns a cursor, so MiOS registers page 1 and drops the rest. Replace the single call with a bounded cursor loop (pass `params={'cursor': nextCursor}` until absent or a max-page cap is hit), accumulating tools before the `allowed_tools` filter and the registry write, and mirror the same fix in the stdio path `_mcp_probe_stdio`. Keep the existing fail-open-per-server behavior.
details.why: any MCP server with more than one page of tools is half-registered, so agents cannot call tools the operator installed and the failure is invisible.

title: Single-source the MCP protocol_version across consume side, published server and SSOT
goal: E-09 One value, one name -- one fact has one representation, enforced so it stays collapsed.
acceptance_criteria: the check flags an injected version skew between the published server and SSOT and passes clean at HEAD; the negative case is in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`; the check is registered in the dispatch list; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mcp.py` takes the consume-side revision from `[mcp].protocol_version` (`MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, used in the initialize handshake ~line 476) while the PUBLISHED server `usr/libexec/mios/mios-mcp-server` advertises its own revision string, and nothing asserts they agree. details.why: MiOS can advertise one MCP revision as a server and negotiate another as a client, producing handshake failures that look like a peer's bug.

title: Record-and-replay cassette harness for A2A/MCP federation HTTP
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- federation paths are hermetically testable with zero network, like the rest of the gated tree.
acceptance_criteria: `test_mios_federation_replay.py` drives `_a2a_send_message_to_peer` end to end from a recorded cassette with no network and asserts the extracted answer text, and asserts an unmatched request raises; `just drift-gate` green with the test in the `test_mios_*.py` glob.

details.what_how: The federation outbound calls (`a2a_client._a2a_send_message_to_peer`, `_a2a_fetch_card`, `mcp._mcp_http_rpc`, `_mcp_call_tool`) all go through the injected httpx client and can only be tested by hand-stubbing each call. Add a pure-stdlib cassette harness `mios_pipe/federation/replay.py` that records JSON-RPC request->response pairs to a JSON fixture and provides a `CassettePlayer` async client matching the httpx `get`/`post` surface that `configure()` injects, replaying offline with strict matching and an assertion on any unmatched request. This complements task_40's record-and-replay, which covered LLM dispatch rather than federation.
details.why: without it every federation test hand-rolls stubs, so the real request/response shapes go unexercised and peer-protocol regressions surface only against a live peer.

title: Give mios_toml a public emit()/`--shell` projection face and thin userenv.sh onto it
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- the canonical key->env projection becomes callable as a library, not only as a shell side effect.
acceptance_criteria: `tests/test-resolver-emit.py` asserts `mios_toml.emit()` equals the `MIOS_*` set userenv.sh exports (same comparison shape as check-resolver-twin) and passes; `python3 -m mios_toml --shell | bash` yields byte-identical env to sourcing userenv.sh; a perturbed expectation flips the test red.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` exposes only `load_merged`/`get`/`section`/`colors` (L30-203) and cannot produce the aliased `{MIOS_*: value}` map that userenv.sh evals, so every Python/Rust consumer must shell out to userenv.sh or scrape `os.environ`. Building on the task_1173 shared helpers, add `emit(layers=None) -> dict[str,str]` plus a `python3 -m mios_toml --shell` CLI printing shell-quoted `export MIOS_X=...` lines that reproduce userenv.sh exactly -- aliases, `[env]` passthrough, `referenced_names.txt` padding, and the `MIOS_PG_BIND_ADDR` + ports stack-offset transforms. Reduce the userenv.sh heredoc to call `emit()` wherever it is safe to do so.
details.why: Without a library face, every non-shell consumer of the SSOT either forks a subshell per lookup or reads a possibly-stale environment, which is exactly how the emitted-vs-consumed key mismatches got in.

title: Derive the names-generator's section set from the resolver's EXCLUDED_SECTIONS instead of a hand allowlist
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- one section policy, shared by the emitter and the catalog.

details.what_how: The registry generator uses a hand-maintained `TARGET_SECTIONS` allowlist (`generate-names-registry.py` L16-23: ports/ai/identity/.../mini) while userenv.sh walks every top-level table EXCEPT `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS` (`userenv.sh` L549). details.why: Every new SSOT section added today enters the environment invisible to the registry, so the "one canonical name" gate under-reports exactly at the moment new names are minted.

title: Add a schema-validation drift-gate for every [dotfiles.registry.*] surface
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- a malformed surface declaration fails at gate time, not at a user's firstboot.
acceptance_criteria: `check_dotfiles_registry` green at HEAD; a new negative case in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (a surface declaring `kind=json-merge` but missing its fixture) flips it red, then restores green.

details.what_how: About 15 surfaces declare kinds (template/json-merge/ini-merge/ssh-merge/registry, `mios.toml` L8648-11146) but no drift-check validates their well-formedness: a surface can declare `kind=json-merge` with no fixture, or a `template`/`apply.target` that does not exist, and only fail at runtime. Add `check_dotfiles_registry` to `38-drift-checks.sh`, reading the SSOT via `mios_toml.load_vendor()` and asserting per surface: the `kind` is a known one; merge kinds have both `fixture.base` and `fixture.expected` present on disk; template kinds' template file exists; `section` names a real mios.toml table; `apply.target` is present where the kind requires it.
details.why: The dotfiles engine is the projection path onto live HOME on two platforms; an unvalidated registry row turns an SSOT typo into a broken first boot on real hardware.

title: Second-apply idempotency test for every merge-kind surface, wired into the drift-gate
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- re-provisioning is safe, so firstboot can deploy every time.

title: DRY the triplicated DB-authoritative overlay branch in mios_toml.py
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- one DB-overlay policy in the resolver, cache included.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile` clean; check 45 (resolver-twin) and the existing resolver tests still green; a unit test asserts the DB overlay is applied identically through the single `_db_overlay` helper across `load_merged`/`get`/`colors`.

details.what_how: The `import mios_db_config; if is_db_authoritative(): deep_merge(db_cfg)` block is copy-pasted three times in `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` -- `load_merged` (L116-124), `get` (L158-167), `colors` (L192-200) -- so any DB-overlay policy change must be made in three spots, and `clear_cache()` (L102) does not account for the DB path. title: Extract ONE shared build-time latest-tag resolver (releases/latest redirect, no GitHub API)
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- a single resolver every build path uses to turn "latest" intent into a concrete tag without a rate limit.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n automation/lib/common.sh usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolve-latest` clean; the unit test passes (stubbed-curl tag extraction plus the degrade-open empty case); `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` inlines the SAME `t="$(curl -fsSL -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' --retry 5 --connect-timeout 20 <repo>/releases/latest | sed 's#.*/tag/##')"` one-liner eight times (matchbox L46, forgejo L49, forgejo-runner L52, jaeger L55, crowdsec L59, k3s L62, code-server L65, firecrawl L10 and L111), and no shared helper exists (grep for `url_effective` across `automation/lib` returns nothing). Author ONE resolver in both shapes: (1) a bash function `mios_resolve_latest_tag <releases-base-url>` in `automation/lib/common.sh` next to `record_version` (L103) doing the redirect-follow and echoing the bare tag, non-fatal (empty on failure so callers degrade open); (2) a standalone dependency-free `usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolve-latest` (`#!/bin/bash`, `set -uo pipefail`) with the same logic, so the sys Containerfile can COPY+RUN it inside the nested build where `lib/common.sh` is not sourced. Use the redirect, NOT `api.github.com`. Add `usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_resolve_latest.sh`, stubbing `curl` via a PATH shim, asserting a `/tag/v1.2.3` effective URL yields `v1.2.3` and a curl failure yields empty plus exit 0.
details.why: Eight copies of one curl incantation means eight places to fix when a forge changes its redirect, and no single place to make float-latest resolution rate-limit-free and testable.

title: Create the [build.float] SSOT allowlist for legitimately-pinned build inputs
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- there is exactly ONE documented place a pin may legally live.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 -c "import tomllib,sys; tomllib.load(open('usr/share/mios/mios.toml','rb'))"` parses; `[build.float].allow` lists the 3 seed exceptions each with non-empty `ref`/`reason`/`upstream`; `just drift-gate` green (no gate references it yet).

details.what_how: A handful of inputs are genuinely capped by an upstream compatibility constraint, and today those pins live inline with only prose comments (`usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile:88-92` uses `python3.12` because every open-webui release caps `requires_python <3.13`; `usr/share/mios/webtools/firecrawl.Containerfile:74` pins `pnpm@9.15.4` for Node-20 `node:sqlite` compat; `[image.sidecars].pgvector = 0.8.3-pg17` is pinned for `hnsw.iterative_scan`). Add a `[build.float]` table to `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` next to `[build.bake_refs]` (~L8554) with an `allow` array of inline tables `{ key, ref, reason, upstream }`. Seed the three known-legit pins plus a comment block stating that ANY entry is an EXCEPTION to float-latest and MUST carry a real upstream reason. Include a commented `mios_toml.get('build.float', 'allow')` reader example; do NOT wire enforcement here (task_1321/271).
details.why: With no allowlist there is no way to distinguish a justified upstream cap from an accidental hand-pin, so a no-hand-pin gate cannot be written at all.

goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- the firecrawl wrapper matches the sys image's float behaviour, with its one real cap recorded as an exception.
