title: Float the git-clone bake refs (quickshell, lookingglass) at build instead of hand-pinned tags
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- source-built components carry `latest` intent in SSOT, resolved at bake.
acceptance_criteria: both bakers resolve latest at build when SSOT is `latest`, honor an explicit override otherwise, and keep non-empty `:-` defaults; `check_bake_ref_defaults` (47) green; `bash -n` clean on both bakers; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/55-bake-quickshell.sh:14` (`PIN_REF="${MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_QUICKSHELL:-v0.3.0}"`) and `automation/53-bake-lookingglass-client.sh:42` (`LG_BRANCH="${MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_LOOKINGGLASS:-B7}"`) clone hand-pinned tags sourced from `[build.bake_refs]`. Set those SSOT values to the sentinel `"latest"`; when the resolved value is `latest`, the baker calls `mios-resolve-latest` against the quickshell / looking-glass repos to get the newest tag at build, while a concrete non-`latest` value is still honored as an explicit operator override. Keep the task_1095 non-empty-default guard (`check_bake_ref_defaults`, check 47) satisfied by using `:-latest`, which then triggers resolution. `hyprland="main"` and `surfer=<sha>` are already moving/immutable refs consistent with float -- leave them, but add a one-line comment noting the `surfer` commit-sha is intentional (upstream has no tags); if `surfer` does have upstream tags, switch it to `"latest"` too.
details.why: The desktop shell (quickshell) and the VM display client stay stuck at whichever tag someone typed once, so upstream fixes never reach the image without a manual SSOT edit.

details.what_how: Several `[image.sidecars]` entries (mirrored verbatim into `[build.bake].core` ~L6611) carry hand-pinned upstream tags: `k3s = docker.io/rancher/k3s:v1.32.1-k3s1`, `ceph = quay.io/ceph/ceph:v19`, `forge = codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo:12`, `forge_runner = code.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner:7`, `pgvector = docker.io/pgvector/pgvector:0.8.3-pg17`. details.why: Frozen patch tags mean shipped CVE fixes never reach the fleet, and the duplicated literal in two tables makes a one-sided edit a silent bake/runtime mismatch.

title: Record every build-time-resolved latest version into the SBOM manifest
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- floating is safe only because the SBOM records what actually resolved (ADR-0003).
acceptance_criteria: a sys build emits `resolved-latest.tsv` with one row per floated component; those rows are merged into `binaries.tsv` (name/version non-empty, `sha256=unknown` allowed); `check_sbom_metadata` (49) green; `bash -n automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The sys Containerfile floats ~11 components (matchbox, forgejo, forgejo-runner, jaeger, crowdsec, k3s, code-server, AdGuard, searxng, open-webui, firecrawl) but records NONE: they run inside the nested `mios-sys` podman build where `automation/lib/common.sh`'s `record_version` is not sourced, so resolved tags never reach the SBOM (only bound-image digests land in `bound-images.tsv` via `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-group:135`). After each `mios-resolve-latest` call in `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile`, append `printf '%s\t%s\n' <component> "$t" >> /usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/resolved-latest.tsv` (mkdir first, degrade-open). Then in `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` (or `mios-bake-group`'s SBOM step) merge those rows into `binaries.tsv` as `name<TAB>version<TAB>unknown` so `check_sbom_metadata` (check 49) validates them -- it already tolerates `sha256 == "unknown"`. Keep everything degrade-open (missing file -> skip).
details.why: Right now floating eleven components makes the image un-reproducible in practice -- nothing in the shipped artifact says which forgejo, k3s or open-webui version is inside it.

goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- the campaign becomes an enforced invariant instead of a one-time cleanup.

details.what_how: Add `check_float_no_handpin` to `automation/38-drift-checks.sh`, registered in `main()` after `check_containerfile_pinned_clones` and labelled (72). title: Bake-time per-stack smoke RUN in sys/Containerfile (import+exec assert)
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image, and can a stock runner hold it -- a stack that cannot start never ships.
acceptance_criteria: the Containerfile still parses and `bash -n` on the extracted RUN body is clean; the smoke block names all four stacks; `just drift-gate` stays green (no new violation); stage ONLY `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile`.

details.what_how: The mios-sys stacks install into `/opt/*-venv` but nothing proves they can START before the image ships -- the SearXNG `msgspec`/`setuptools.build_meta` class of failure installs "successfully" then dies at import. Append a smoke-verification `RUN` at the END of `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` (after the firecrawl COPY at L119; there is no `bootc container lint` final-line requirement on the sys Containerfile -- check 38 only scans the root `Containerfile`/`Containerfile.minimal`, so appending a RUN is legal). The RUN must `set -e` and fail the whole build on the first broken stack: SearXNG `/opt/searxng-venv/bin/python -c "import searx, msgspec"` (msgspec explicit -- that was the real runtime miss); Open WebUI `/opt/open-webui-venv/bin/python -c "import open_webui"` AND `/opt/open-webui-venv/bin/open-webui --help >/dev/null`; Crawl4AI `/opt/crawl4ai-venv/bin/python -c "import crawl4ai, camoufox, playwright, fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic"`; Firecrawl `test -d /opt/firecrawl/apps/api/dist` plus `node -e "process.exit(0)"` under the image's node. Each assertion echoes `[sys-smoke] <stack> OK` so a bake log shows which stack passed. Add NO retries -- a smoke failure must be fatal.
details.why: Without it a green bake can publish an image whose search, chat or crawl stack dies on first import, and the failure is discovered by an operator on real hardware instead of by CI.

provenance.owner_raw: you (Containerfile / bash). **When:** first -- it is the foundation the other WS-BAKE tasks harden.

title: Factor the bake-time stack smoke assertions into a COPY'd `smoke.sh` + a host-side Containerfile/smoke parity test
goal: E-16 Bake plane: what is present in the image, and can a stock runner hold it -- makes the per-stack bake-time smoke RUN (import+exec presence proof) maintainable and self-extending instead of an unmaintainable inline blob.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n usr/share/mios/sys/smoke.sh` and `bash -n tests/sys-smoke-parity.sh` are clean; the parity test PASSES on the current tree and FAILS when a `*-venv` line is added to a scratch Containerfile copy with no matching `smoke.sh` reference; `just drift-gate` green; only those four paths staged.

details.what_how: The task_1325 assertions currently live inlined inside a Containerfile `RUN`, so they cannot be linted or unit-checked. Extract them into a real script `usr/share/mios/sys/smoke.sh` (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, one assertion per stack, exit non-zero on first failure), `COPY smoke.sh /tmp/smoke.sh` into the sys image and reduce the task_1325 RUN to `RUN bash /tmp/smoke.sh`. Then add a host-side STATIC test `tests/sys-smoke-parity.sh` that parses `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` for every `python3 -m venv /opt/<name>-venv` (plus the two symlink/venv stanzas) and asserts `smoke.sh` references each `/opt/<name>-venv` — a new stack added without a smoke assertion FAILS. Wire `tests/sys-smoke-parity.sh` into the `drift-gate` recipe in `Justfile`, beside the existing `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` invocation.
details.why: Today a stack can be added to the sys image with zero smoke coverage and nothing notices — the image publishes with a stack that imports-broken at runtime, which is exactly the bake failure class E-16 exists to close.

extra.value: after task_1325

title: Resolve the newest supported interpreter at build time instead of hardcoding `python3.12`
goal: E-16 Bake plane -- removes a hand-maintained compatibility literal from the bake so version INTENT floats (ADR-0003) and the venv interpreter is resolved, not pinned.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n usr/share/mios/sys/pick-python.sh` clean; run against PATH-shimmed `python3.12`/`python3.14` stubs it selects the newest satisfying interpreter and degrades-open when the JSON fetch fails; no bare `python3.12` literal remains in the Containerfile outside a comment; `just drift-gate` green; only the two paths staged.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` L92 hardcodes `python3.12` for the Open WebUI venv because open-webui caps `requires_python <3.13` while Fedora 44's default `python3` is 3.14 — a constraint the operator must never hand-maintain. Write `usr/share/mios/sys/pick-python.sh <pkg>` that (1) enumerates the `python3.N` interpreters on PATH (`compgen -c 'python3.'` / glob `/usr/bin/python3.[0-9]*`) newest-first; (2) resolves the floated package's `requires_python` from `https://pypi.org/pypi/<pkg>/json` (`.info.requires_python`) with `curl --retry 5` (check 64 requires `--retry`), degrading OPEN to the newest interpreter when the API is unreachable; (3) prints the newest `python3.N` satisfying the specifier via a small `packaging.specifiers`/`SpecifierSet` evaluation run under a candidate interpreter, else the base `python3`. COPY the helper in and replace L92's literal with `"$(bash /tmp/pick-python.sh open-webui)"`; update the L88-91 comment to point at the helper.
details.why: Every Fedora base bump silently strands the pinned `python3.12` — the venv either fails to create or silently builds on a dead interpreter, and a human has to notice and hand-edit the Containerfile.

extra.value: independent of 274/275

title: Verify the Firecrawl `html-to-markdown.so` runtime load path at bake time
goal: E-16 Bake plane -- converts a silent runtime break into a loud bake failure, so presence in the image means functional presence.

title: Add EXIT-trap mount/scratch teardown to the nested-podman builders (mount-leak hardening)
goal: E-16 Bake plane -- lets a standard runner survive a retried bake instead of filling its disk with leaked overlay mounts.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n` clean on both; the trap fires on both success and forced-failure paths (test with an injected `false`) and never alters the propagated exit code; the `${SCRATCH:?}` guard is present so an unset var cannot `rm -rf /`; `just drift-gate` green; only the two scripts staged.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh` and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-group` both run a NESTED `podman --root "$STORE" --runroot "$SCRATCH/run" build/pull` inside the outer OCI build. Under `set -euo pipefail` a mid-build failure exits WITHOUT tearing down the inner store's overlay mounts or purging `$SCRATCH`, leaking overlay/loopback mounts on retried CI runners. Add `trap '_cleanup' EXIT` to BOTH scripts: best-effort `podman --root "$STORE" --runroot "$SCRATCH/run" unshare umount ...` / `podman ... system prune`, force-unmount lingering mounts under `$SCRATCH` (`awk '$2 ~ SCRATCH {print $2}' /proc/self/mountinfo | xargs -r umount -l`), then `rm -rf "${SCRATCH:?}"` — every step `|| true` and the original `$?` preserved so cleanup never masks the real exit code. In `mios-bake-group` respect the existing `MIOS_BAKE_BOUND_IMAGES=0` early-exit (L47-50) so the trap is a no-op there; reference the existing partial cleanup at L58/L140.
details.why: A documented WS-BAKE failure mode: one failed bake poisons the runner so every subsequent retry fails on disk-full, and the cause looks unrelated.

title: Make the SBOM `bound-images.tsv` append idempotent (retry-safe, last-wins)
goal: E-16 Bake plane -- keeps the build-time provenance record unambiguous when a bake is retried, which is the whole point of the robustness work.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n` clean on both; running either writer twice for the same image yields exactly ONE row (verify against a scratch `$SBOM_DIR`); the header line survives; `just drift-gate` green; only the two scripts staged.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh` L99-100 and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-group` L135 append (`>>`) rows to `$SBOM_DIR/bound-images.tsv` with no dedup, so a retried build writes DUPLICATE rows for the same image; `tools/generate-bake-plan.py`'s SBOM reader (L181-190) keeps the LAST digest, making duplicates silent bloat and ambiguity. Make the append idempotent — before writing a row, drop any existing line for that `image` key (`grep -v -P "^\t"` to a tmp then append the fresh row, or an awk last-wins rewrite) — keeping the TSV header handling intact. Implement via a tiny `_sbom_put ` function defined INLINE in each script; the two do not share a lib today and a new sourced lib is not warranted for two call sites.
details.why: The SBOM is the provenance record (NS-4); duplicate rows make "which digest did we actually bake" a matter of file ordering rather than fact.

extra.value: independent

title: Retry the Firecrawl pnpm registry ops and degrade `--frozen-lockfile` to a warned unfrozen install
goal: E-16 Bake plane -- makes a floated upstream tag's benign lockfile bump a warning instead of a publish-stopping bake failure.

title: Kill the divergent BIB target matrix: gate the `Justfile` `all` recipe against `[deployment].target_*`
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- makes SSOT the only definition of which install artifacts MiOS ships, so enabling a target actually builds it.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n automation/38-drift-checks.sh` clean; `just --evaluate` parses; the new check is GREEN on HEAD; flipping `target_vmdk = true` in `[deployment]` (or dropping `qcow2` from the `Justfile` `all` list) turns it RED; `just drift-gate` exits 0.

details.what_how: Two BIB-invocation surfaces disagree on the shipped artifact set. `usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-driver` (L855-894) derives `BIB_FORMATS` by awk-scanning `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[deployment]` for `target_<key> = true` (the SSOT matrix), while the `Justfile` `all:` target (L296) hardcodes `build raw iso usb-installer qcow2 vhdx wsl2` and reads nothing from SSOT — so flipping `target_vmdk`/`target_ami` on silently builds nothing. Add `check_bib_matrix_parity` to `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (next free number, 72): parse the enabled `target_*` set from `[deployment]` reusing the exact awk idiom at mios-build-driver:872-878, normalize with the same `_`/`-` and `vhdx→vhd`/`wsl` rules the driver applies (L911-928), then assert the `Justfile` `all` recipe's BIB-producing prereq list is the SAME set, allowing `build`/`usb-installer`/`wsl2` as documented non-BIB extras. Register it in `main()` next to `check_deploy_plane`. Stage ONLY the explicit paths — the tree is shared, never `git add -A`.
details.where: `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new `check_bib_matrix_parity` + `main()` registration ~L4273), `Justfile` (`all:` L296 — add a comment cross-referencing `[deployment]` as SSOT), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[deployment]` (L6630)
details.why: An operator can enable a deploy target in SSOT and get no artifact, with no error anywhere — the exact SSOT-projection bypass Law 8 forbids.

title: Migrate the installer ISO to BIB `--type anaconda-iso` and gate that it is bootc-native, not a package install
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- one installer-ISO spelling, one SSOT toggle, and proof the ISO installs the container rather than DNF packages.
acceptance_criteria: `just --evaluate` parses; grep shows no remaining space-terminated `--type iso ` anywhere; the new check is GREEN; injecting a `%packages`/`@core` block into iso.toml turns it RED; `bash -n mios-build-driver` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The `Justfile` `iso:` recipe (L208-216) invokes BIB with `--type iso` — the deprecated alias — while `[deployment]` (mios.toml:6637-6638) enables BOTH `target_iso` AND `target_anaconda_iso`, so the SSOT-driven `mios-build-driver` (L942) emits two overlapping installer ISOs. Consolidate on the current spelling: change `iso:` to `--type anaconda-iso`, retire the redundant `target_iso` toggle leaving one `anaconda_iso` boolean as the single installer-ISO SSOT, and update the driver fallback default at mios-build-driver:891 (`"vhd qcow2 iso raw"` → `anaconda-iso`). Because BIB's `anaconda-iso` built FROM a bootc image installs via `ostreecontainer` and not a `%packages` DNF install, add `check_installer_is_bootc` (next free check) asserting (a) the `iso`/`usb-installer` recipes use `--type anaconda-iso` and (b) `config/artifacts/iso.toml`'s kickstart carries NO `%packages` stanza and NO `url --mirrorlist` package source — the bootc image is the install source.
details.why: Two overlapping installer ISOs waste an entire build leg, and nothing today stops the shipped ISO from quietly becoming a plain-Fedora package install — the headline deploy-plane defect.

title: Author a bootc-native offline kickstart (`ostreecontainer` from oci-archive, zero `%packages`)
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- gives the Ventoy media an immutable install path that lands the MiOS OCI image itself, fully offline.
acceptance_criteria: the new kickstart is syntactically well-formed (`%post`/`%end` balanced if present); the new check is GREEN; adding a `%packages` line or removing `ostreecontainer` turns it RED; `bash -n automation/38-drift-checks.sh` clean; `just drift-gate` green; only the explicit paths staged.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/ventoy/mios-kickstart.cfg` deliberately installs a MUTABLE plain Fedora base (`cdrom`, `autopart --type=plain --fstype=ext4`, `%packages @core @virtualization …`, then overlays via build-mios.sh) — precisely the "installs plain Fedora, not the immutable MiOS OCI image" gap. Author a SIBLING `usr/share/mios/ventoy/mios-bootc-kickstart.cfg` that installs the image directly: `ostreecontainer --url oci-archive:/run/install/repo/mios-latest.tar --transport oci-archive --no-signature-verification` (Law 12 zero-network — the archive is staged on the boot media, mirroring tools/install.sh:7's default `/mnt/mios-repo/mios-latest.tar`), plus `zerombr`, `clearpart --all --initlabel --disklabel=gpt`, `reqpart --add-boot`, `part / --grow --fstype xfs`, `bootloader`, a bootstrap `user` from `[identity]` (no `rootpw` package churn), and NO `%packages` section at all. Add `check_bootc_kickstart` (next free check) asserting the new file contains `ostreecontainer` and an `oci-archive`/`--transport` source and has ZERO `%packages`/`cdrom`/`@core` tokens — the negative that separates it from the mutable variant.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/ventoy/mios-bootc-kickstart.cfg` (new), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + `main()` registration near `check_deploy_plane`), `usr/share/mios/ventoy/mios-kickstart.cfg` (header cross-note that the immutable sibling exists)
details.why: Today the USB media provisions a mutable Fedora that merely resembles MiOS — no `bootc upgrade`, no rollback, no image identity, which defeats NS-1 at the point of install.

title: First-boot verifier asserting the installed system is bootc-managed MiOS, not plain Fedora
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- turns the WS-BOOTC acceptance criterion into a running, self-reporting check on the landed deployment.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n usr/libexec/mios/mios-verify-bootc-install` clean; running it in a non-bootc shell exits non-zero with the explicit message (self-testable offline); the new check is GREEN; hardcoding an image literal into the script turns it RED; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The acceptance is "the installed system reports `bootc status`, not plain Fedora", but nothing checks it — `bootc-switch-from-build.sh` only stages switches and never verifies the landed deployment. Author `usr/libexec/mios/mios-verify-bootc-install` that runs `bootc status --format=json`, parses `.status.booted.image.image.image` (falling back to `.spec.image` per the bootc JSON schema) and asserts it matches the SSOT ref resolved from mios.toml `[image].ref`/`[image].name` (`ghcr.io/mios-dev/mios`, L6586/6598), exiting non-zero with a loud `SYSTEM IS NOT bootc-managed MiOS (got: <x>)` when `bootc` is absent or the image is unset/Fedora. Ship a oneshot `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-verify-bootc-install.service` (`WantedBy=multi-user.target`, degrade-open via `ConditionPathExists=/run/ostree-booted`). Add `check_verify_bootc_install` (next free check) asserting the script exists, references `bootc status`, resolves the ref through the mios_toml resolver with NO hardcoded `ghcr.io/...` literal, and that the unit points at it.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-verify-bootc-install` (new), `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-verify-bootc-install.service` (new), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[image]` (SSOT source, no edit needed)
details.why: Without it a mis-installed machine looks fine for months — the whole install plane can regress to plain Fedora and no signal ever fires.

title: Project install-time kernel args from `[kargs]` into `bootc install to-disk`
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- the initial deployment boots with the SSOT-declared kargs instead of only whatever the image fragments apply later.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n tools/install.sh` clean; `tools/install.sh --dry-run --target-disk /dev/sda` prints the resolved `--karg` list sourced from `[kargs]` with no network and no hardcoded karg; the check is RED when a bare karg literal is hardcoded and GREEN on HEAD; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/install.sh:71` runs `bootc install to-disk --target-no-signature-verification --source-imgref "oci-archive:$OCI_ARCHIVE" "$TARGET_DISK"` with NO `--karg`, so the vfio/hardening/console kargs shipped in `usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml` (00-mios.toml, 01-mios-hardening.toml, 20-vfio.toml, 30-security.toml, …) apply only post-install, and any install-time-only kargs from `[kargs]` (mios.toml:11361) never reach the first deployment at all. Add a helper in install.sh that resolves the install-time karg list from `[kargs]` through the shared `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` resolver (or a tomllib one-liner — NO hardcoded karg literals) and appends one `--karg <k>` per entry to the `to-disk` invocation, echoing the resolved set under `--dry-run`. Extend the task_1204-adjacent install.sh gate, or add `check_install_kargs`, asserting install.sh sources kargs from SSOT and emits `--karg` in the dry-run plan.
details.where: `tools/install.sh` (karg-resolve helper + invocation at L50/71), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[kargs]` (SSOT, no schema edit), `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` (resolver, reuse only), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new/extended check)
details.why: A machine installed today first-boots without its declared vfio/hardening kargs — GPU passthrough and hardening silently do not apply until a later reboot, if ever.

title: Make to-disk signature verification an SSOT policy instead of an unconditional `--target-no-signature-verification`
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- lets an operator running a signed MiOS actually get signature enforcement at install time.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n tools/install.sh` clean; `--dry-run` reflects the resolved policy in the printed `bootc install` plan for BOTH flag values; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED if `--target-no-signature-verification` is re-hardcoded unconditionally; `just drift-gate` green; only the explicit paths staged.

details.what_how: `tools/install.sh:71` hardcodes `--target-no-signature-verification`, permanently disabling image signature enforcement even though the repo already carries signed-UKI/sigstore machinery. Add a `[deploy].verify_signatures` SSOT key defaulting to `false` (preserving today's offline oci-archive behavior) and have install.sh resolve it: when true, DROP the no-verify flag and pass the sigstore policy path instead; when false, keep the flag but log a visible `signature verification DISABLED (SSOT [deploy].verify_signatures=false)` warning. Add `check_install_sig_policy` asserting install.sh reads the flag from SSOT rather than unconditionally emitting the no-verify flag, and that the key is documented in mios.toml.
details.where: `tools/install.sh` (L71 invocation + flag resolution), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (new commented `[deploy].verify_signatures` key), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration)
details.why: Supply-chain provenance is unusable at the one moment it matters most — a tampered archive installs exactly as readily as a signed one, with no operator opt-in available.

title: Verify the staged oci-archive against a build-recorded digest BEFORE the destructive to-disk
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- refuses to wipe a disk for a truncated or wrong-version archive, using SBOM digest data rather than a hand-pinned constant.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n tools/install.sh` clean; with a fixture archive plus matching sidecar the dry-run reports `archive digest OK`; a mutated sidecar makes the dry-run abort non-zero; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED if the verify guard moves after the destructive step; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/install.sh:59-62` only checks that the oci-archive EXISTS before wiping `$TARGET_DISK` at L64-71, so a truncated/tampered/wrong-version archive installs silently. Per ADR-0003 (SBOM-not-hardcode) the archive digest is build-time SBOM data: have the oci-archive producer (the task_1203 `just oci-archive` recipe, or a stopgap here) write a sidecar `<archive>.sha256` next to the tarball, and add a `verify_archive()` step in install.sh that, when the sidecar is present, `sha256sum`s `$OCI_ARCHIVE` and ABORTS before any destructive action on mismatch — skipping with a warning when the sidecar is absent so offline media without it still installs. Print the verification result under `--dry-run`. Add `check_install_archive_verify` asserting install.sh computes and compares a checksum before the `bootc install to-disk` line, by grepping the ORDERING: the `sha256sum` guard must precede the destructive `read -rp`/`bootc install`.
details.where: `tools/install.sh` (new `verify_archive` before L64), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration); cross-reference the task_1203 producer path — do not re-implement the producer
details.why: The current worst case is an irreversibly wiped disk followed by an unbootable half-installed image, with no diagnosis available afterwards.

title: Gate the anaconda-ISO container prerequisites (`dracut-live` + `squashfs-tools` + `anaconda`) when the target is enabled
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- converts iso.toml's prose build contract into a ships-green gate so the installer-ISO leg cannot silently break at BIB time.

title: SSOT-project rootfs type and root `minsize` across every artifact toml (kill the 80-vs-150-GiB divergence)
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- filesystem geometry becomes one declared value projected into every artifact, not four hand-edited literals.
acceptance_criteria: re-render is deterministic and byte-compares against the committed tomls; mutating `[deployment.filesystem].root_minsize` and re-rendering updates all four tomls idempotently; hardcoding a stray `"200 GiB"` into qcow2.toml turns the check RED; `bash -n` on the renderer clean; `just drift-gate` green; only the explicit paths staged.

details.what_how: The BIB artifact configs hardcode conflicting geometry with no SSOT: `config/artifacts/bib.toml` sets root `minsize = "80 GiB"` while `iso.toml`, `qcow2.toml` and `vhdx.toml` each independently set `"150 GiB"`, and the `Justfile` recipes pass `--rootfs ext4` inline (L202/215/232/251). Add a `[deployment.filesystem]` SSOT block (`root_minsize`, `rootfs_type`, optional `var_home_minsize`) and a small renderer (`usr/libexec/mios/mios-render-artifact-fs`, or extend an existing artifact-render step) that projects those values into each `[[customizations.filesystem]]` mountpoint/minsize and the `--rootfs` flag. Add `check_artifact_fs_projection` as a round-trip check mirroring the `check_kargs_projection` (check 53) pattern, asserting every artifact toml's root minsize and the `--rootfs` args equal the SSOT-rendered values, with no bare `"80 GiB"`/`"150 GiB"`/`ext4` literal outside the generated files.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (new `[deployment.filesystem]`), `config/artifacts/{bib,iso,qcow2,vhdx}.toml` (become rendered projections), `Justfile` (recipes read the SSOT rootfs type), new/extended renderer under `usr/libexec/mios/`, `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration)
details.why: The same OS ships with two different root sizings depending on which artifact you install, and there is no single place to change it — a Law 7 / Law 8 violation baked into every deploy target.

title: Extend `verify-images` to prove the installer artifacts are bootc-managed, not merely non-empty
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- artifact verification distinguishes a real bootc installer from a plain-Fedora one, statically and without booting.
acceptance_criteria: `just --evaluate` parses; the verify step is fail-open when introspection tools are absent (prints SKIP, exits 0) but FAILS on an ISO carrying a `Packages/` tree; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED if the ostree/container marker grep is deleted from the recipe; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The `Justfile` `verify-images:` target (L335-358) only checks size and magic bytes, so an ISO that installs plain Fedora passes identically to a bootc installer ISO. Add a `verify-bootc-artifacts` recipe, invoked from `verify-images` and `all`, that statically introspects the produced media: for the anaconda-iso, mount / `isoinfo` / `7z l` it read-only and assert it embeds an ostree/container commit (grep for `ostree/`, `container`, or the embedded kickstart's `ostreecontainer` directive) rather than a `Packages/` RPM tree; for `raw`/`qcow2`/`vhd`, assert a `/ostree` deployment via `guestfish`/`virt-cat` when available, else skip-with-warning. Add `check_verify_bootc_artifacts` asserting the recipe exists and greps for the bootc/ostree markers, so the verification itself cannot silently degrade to a no-op.
details.why: "Artifacts verified" currently means "the file is big and starts with the right bytes" — it would pass a completely wrong OS, which is how the plain-Fedora install gap survived undetected.

title: Make the offline bare-metal installer discoverable: `just to-disk-install` plus a `--dry-run` plan target
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- the real offline to-disk leg sits beside the VM artifact recipes where an operator will actually find it.
acceptance_criteria: `just --evaluate` parses; `just to-disk-plan` prints the resolved plan with no side effects and no network; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED if the recipe's archive default diverges from install.sh; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/install.sh` (the real `bootc install to-disk` offline leg) has NO Justfile entry point, so it is undiscoverable next to `raw`/`iso`/`qcow2`/`vhdx` and an operator asking "how do I install MiOS to a disk?" lands on the VM recipes. Add a `to-disk-install:` recipe forwarding to `tools/install.sh` (passing `MIOS_OCI_ARCHIVE`/`--target-disk` through) and a `to-disk-plan:` alias running `tools/install.sh --dry-run` that echoes the resolved `bootc install to-disk` plan with a loud "DESTROYS the target disk" warning, mirroring the `usb-installer:` flash-recipe pattern at Justfile:326-331. Add `check_to_disk_recipe` asserting the recipe references `tools/install.sh`, that the `MIOS_OCI_ARCHIVE` default equals the consumer default at install.sh:7 (`/mnt/mios-repo/mios-latest.tar`) so the two cannot diverge, and that a `--dry-run`/plan alias exists.
details.where: `Justfile` (new `to-disk-install:` / `to-disk-plan:` recipes near `usb-installer:`), `tools/install.sh` (consumer default, no change), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration)
details.why: The one leg that reaches real bare metal is effectively hidden, so operators fall back to VM images or a manual invocation with a mistyped archive path.

title: Collapse the byte-identical `automation/install.sh` ≡ `automation/install-fhs.sh` FHS-overlay installers
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- one canonical FHS-overlay installer body, so the two names cannot drift apart.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n` clean on both files; the two are no longer independent full copies (redirector verified); every prior caller still resolves; the new check is GREEN on HEAD and RED if a second full-body copy is reintroduced; `just drift-gate` green; only the explicit paths staged.

details.what_how: `automation/install.sh` and `automation/install-fhs.sh` are byte-for-byte identical apart from a one-line `# AI-related: install.sh` comment (both: bootc-guard → rsync `usr etc var srv` overlay → sysusers/tmpfiles/daemon-reload) — a live duplicate under two names. First grep the tree AND the kickstart for `automation/install-fhs.sh` vs `automation/install.sh` references to pick the name callers actually use, then make the loser a thin redirector (`exec bash "$(dirname …)/install.sh" "$@"`, or the reverse) keeping the canonical body in exactly ONE file. Add `check_no_dup_fhs_installer` asserting the two paths are not two independent full copies — one must be a redirector or symlink to the other. Coordinate with task_1205: this is the dedupe, that is the role marker.
details.where: `automation/install.sh`, `automation/install-fhs.sh` (one becomes a redirector), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + registration), plus any caller referencing the retired name
details.why: A fix applied to one installer silently misses the other, so installs behave differently depending on which name the caller happened to use.

title: greenboot: un-shadow the dead `check_greenboot` and derive `critical_services` from `[greenboot]` SSOT
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- greenboot health coverage is real and SSOT-driven, so every critical service has a check and a rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: both greenboot checks run from `main()` with no shadowed definition (the rename shows in `grep -c 'check_greenboot()'`); adding a 4th entry to `[greenboot].critical_services` with no matching `required.d` script turns the coverage check red; a case in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` proves it bites; `bash -n automation/38-drift-checks.sh` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` defines `check_greenboot()` twice: line 3120 (verifies `46-greenboot.sh` symlink commands and `etc/greenboot/*.sh` exec bits) and an unrelated one at line 3981 (health coverage over `usr/lib/greenboot/check/required.d`). Under bash the later definition wins, so `main()`'s call at line 4266 runs only the 3981 body and the 3120 exec-bit/symlink logic is silently DEAD. The surviving check also hardcodes `critical_services=("agent-pipe" "llm-light" "pgvector")` at line 3988, duplicating `[greenboot].critical_services` in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (near `[security.luks]`, ~line 8663), so the two diverge on the next edit. Rename the 3120 function to `check_greenboot_scripts` and register it in `main()`; rewrite the 3981 body to resolve `critical_services` from SSOT via a `python3 -c tomllib` read, degrading open with a WARN when python3/tomllib is absent (mirror `check_cephfs_ssot`, line 3036).
details.why: today the symlink/exec-bit assertions never execute (a broken greenboot script ships undetected), and the hardcoded service list means adding a critical service to SSOT gains no health check or rollback trigger.

title: clevis/LUKS: collapse the two conflicting disk-encryption SSOT tables into one canonical block
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- TPM-bound LUKS is configured from ONE SSOT table that the live enrollment path actually reads.
acceptance_criteria: one canonical disk-encryption table remains and grep proves neither script reads a second one; `pcrs` has a consistent type across both consumers; the new drift-check reds if an orphan table reappears; `bash -n` clean on both scripts; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: LUKS/clevis is configured from two disjoint tables. `usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen` (lines 7-9) reads `[security.luks]` (`enabled`/`pin`/`pcrs`, mios.toml:8658, where `pcrs="7"` is a STRING), while `usr/libexec/mios/mios-luks-enroll` -- the script `mios-luks-enroll.service` actually runs (enabled in the preset, line 70) -- reads `[security.disk_encryption]` (`mode`/`backend`/`pcrs`/`recovery`, mios.toml:1083, where `pcrs=[7]` is a LIST). Nothing consumes the generator's output, so it is an orphan whose SSOT already disagrees with the live path (`enabled=false` vs `mode="tpm2"`). Adopt `[security.disk_encryption]` as canonical (it is richer and already live), fold the `pin` concept into it via `pin`/`backend` reconciliation, repoint `mios-clevis-luks-gen` at it (deriving `CLEVIS_LUKS_ENABLED` from `mode != "none"`), and either delete `[security.luks]` or make it an alias the resolver rejects. Both surfaces keep shipping INERT by default -- `mode` drives everything. Add a drift-check forbidding a second table's return.
details.why: two tables that disagree right now mean an operator enabling encryption in the obvious place (`[security.luks]`) changes nothing on the running system, and the divergence widens with every edit.

title: ROCm/AMD: add `[gpu.rocm]` SSOT plus a static kfd+dri CDI fallback generator for when `amd-ctk` is missing
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- multi-vendor GPU CDI so ROCm reaches parity with the existing NVIDIA CDI plane.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-rocm-cdi-gen /path/to/mios.toml` emits schema-valid JSON (`python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(...)'`) enumerating the SSOT kfd+dri devices, and emits nothing when `[gpu.rocm].enabled=false`; the service references the generator in its fallback branch; `bash -n` clean on both; no live GPU required.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-gpu-amd.service` emits a CDI spec only `if command -v amd-ctk` (lines 21-23), and `amd-ctk` is not in the Fedora RPM repos (the unit's own comment says so) -- so ROCm containers never get `/run/cdi/amd.json` and must hand-pass `--device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri` forever, while NVIDIA has a full plane (`usr/libexec/mios/mios-cdi-detect`, `nvidia-cdi-refresh`, greenboot `wanted.d/30-nvidia-cdi.sh`). The ROCm userland is already installed (`rocm-opencl`/`rocm-hip`/`rocm-runtime`/`rocm-smi`/`rocminfo`, mios.toml:7217) but has no `[gpu.rocm]` SSOT block. Add `[gpu.rocm]` next to `[gpu]` (mios.toml:675) with `enabled`, `render_group`, `devices` (defaulting to `/dev/kfd` plus `/dev/dri/renderD*`) and `cdi_kind = "amd.com/gpu"`; add `usr/libexec/mios/mios-rocm-cdi-gen` emitting a deterministic CDI v0.6 `/run/cdi/amd.json` (one device enumerating the kfd+dri nodes with the render group) projected from that table; call it from the service's non-`amd-ctk` branch. Ship INERT (`enabled=false` -> no-op) so non-AMD hosts are unaffected.
details.why: every AMD-GPU container on MiOS today needs hand-written device flags, so ROCm workloads are not reproducible from SSOT and the documented multi-vendor GPU story is unimplemented.

title: ROCm/AMD: drift-check the CDI generator round-trip and prove `mios-gpu-amd.service` is actually reachable
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- a wired capability is gated, and a unit nothing pulls in counts as unwired.
acceptance_criteria: the new check round-trips the AMD CDI projection and passes at HEAD; a mutated `[gpu.rocm].render_group` fixture makes it red; the check confirms the service is enabled or pulled in; a negative test in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` proves it; `just drift-gate` green.

First establish whether `mios-gpu-detect` pulls it in via Wants/role; if nothing does, add the preset enable line (its `ConditionVirtualization`/`ConditionPathExists=/dev/kfd` already keep it inert). Then add a drift-check at the next free number, registered in `main()` beside the CDI checks, that (a) runs `mios-rocm-cdi-gen` against `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` into a temp file and asserts the enumerated device nodes and render group equal `[gpu.rocm]` (degrade-open when python3 is absent, mirroring `check_cephfs_ssot`), and (b) asserts `mios-gpu-amd.service` is reachable from the preset/role graph.
details.why: without this, the AMD CDI generator can drift from SSOT unnoticed, and the service that invokes it may never start on a real AMD host -- reintroducing the exact hand-passed-device situation task_1356 removed.

title: Guacamole: load the JDBC schema into the mios DB and SSOT-ify the hardcoded DB creds and guacd port
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- a shipped service is either working and SSOT-wired or explicitly removed; Guacamole becomes the former.
acceptance_criteria: the JDBC schema loads idempotently (a re-run creates nothing new); the container's DB password resolves from `[identity].default_password` and the guacd port from `[ports]` (grep proves no literal `4822` or password beyond the SSOT var in the generated Quadlet); `generate-pod-quadlets.py` re-render equals the committed files; `bash -n` and SQL parse clean; explicit-path staging only.

details.what_how: The `mios-guacamole` Quadlet (`usr/share/containers/systemd/mios-guacamole.container`) points at `POSTGRESQL_DATABASE=mios`, but `usr/share/mios/postgres/schema-init.sql` contains ZERO Guacamole tables (`grep -c guacamole_ schema-init.sql` = 0) -- the container has no `guacamole_connection`/`guacamole_user` schema and cannot authenticate, so Guacamole is a dead service today. Vendor the Guacamole PostgreSQL JDBC DDL (`001-create-schema.sql` + `002-create-admin-user.sql`) under `usr/share/mios/postgres/guacamole/` and wire it into the DB init path (a `schema-init.sql` include or a firstboot loader against the mios DB), guarded to load only when the guacamole tables are absent so it is idempotent. Project the DB password from `[identity].default_password` (mios.toml:37, "every service defaults to this credential") and add `guacd_port` to `[ports]` so the Quadlet template stops hardcoding `4822`. Regenerate via `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py` and STAGE ONLY the explicit changed files -- never a broad `git add` in this shared tree.
details.why: MiOS ships a remote-desktop gateway that cannot start a session -- an operator enabling it gets an authentication failure -- and its credentials are baked as literals outside the SSOT.

title: Guacamole: fix the desktop launcher pointing at the wrong port and gate Quadlet<->SSOT consistency
goal: E-13 Ports are allocated from SSOT, not hand-assigned -- an operator-visible surface stops disagreeing with `[ports]`.
acceptance_criteria: the launcher opens the SSOT port (no stale `8090` remains); the new check reds when the `.desktop` port and `[ports].guacamole_web` disagree; the guac Quadlet round-trip is green; a negative test flips the `.desktop` port and asserts red; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/share/applications/mios-svc-guacamole.desktop` hardcodes `http://localhost:8090/guacamole/` (Exec line 9 and Comment line 8), while SSOT says `[ports].guacamole_web = 8080` (mios.toml:7848) -- the launcher literally opens the wrong port. The generated Quadlet is correct (`${MIOS_PORT_GUACAMOLE_WEB}`, `mios-guacamole.container`:22-24), so the `.desktop` is the sole divergent surface. Repoint its Exec/Comment at the SSOT port -- ideally by projecting it through the same dotfile/theme-render path used for other surfaces, at minimum by correcting the literal -- and add a drift-check at the next free number, registered in `main()`, asserting (a) the `.desktop` URL port equals `[ports].guacamole_web` and (b) the `mios-guacamole` / `mios-guacd` Quadlets round-trip against `[containers.mios-guacamole]` / `[containers.mios-guacd]` through `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py`, guarding the task_1360 regeneration.
details.why: clicking the shipped Guacamole launcher today lands on a dead port -- a first-impression failure for any operator -- and nothing prevents the same drift returning after the task_1360 regeneration.

title: NUT: actually RUN the rendered UPS config by enabling upsd/upsmon, gated on standalone MODE
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- rendered configuration that no service consumes is unwired; NUT gets its daemons.
acceptance_criteria: the NUT daemons are enabled in the preset and no-op on the default (no-UPS) build; a drift-check (or an extension of check 56) asserts render MODE and unit-enable state agree (name set -> units enabled + `MODE=standalone`; name empty -> inert); `bash -n` clean; `just drift-gate` green; no live UPS required.

details.what_how: `automation/25-nut-render.sh` renders `/etc/ups/{nut,ups,upsd,upsmon}.conf` from `[power.ups]` (gated by check 56), but NO NUT service is ever started -- there is no `nut-server`/`upsd`/`upsmon`/`nut-monitor` line in `usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/90-mios.preset` (grepping for `ups` or `nut` returns nothing), so on a host with a real UPS the rendered `MODE=standalone` config sits dead and the box never shuts down on battery. Enable the upstream `nut-server.service` (upsd) and `nut-monitor.service` (upsmon) in the preset, each gated to no-op when NUT is inert -- a MiOS drop-in with `ConditionPathExists`/`ConditionFileNotEmpty=/etc/ups/ups.conf`, keyed off the render writing a non-empty `[name]` block (the default `[power.ups].name=""` renders `MODE=none` and an empty ups.conf). Confirm the package providing those units is in the MiOS package set, and document the service-state contract in the render script.
details.why: a MiOS host on a real UPS silently loses power protection -- the config is perfect and nothing reads it, so the machine hard-powers-off on battery exhaustion.

title: CephFS: gate every `${MIOS_CEPHFS_*}` template variable against the `[storage.cephfs]` SSOT keys
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- a template placeholder with no SSOT key behind it becomes unrepresentable.
acceptance_criteria: the check enumerates every template var and asserts both a matching `[storage.cephfs]` key and a matching substitution in the firstboot script; deleting `mount_options` from SSOT (or its substitution) makes it red; a negative test proves it; `bash -n` clean; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/systemd/home-@.mount.tmpl` and `home-@.automount.tmpl` reference `${MIOS_CEPHFS_MONITORS}`, `${MIOS_CEPHFS_TENANT_ID}`, `${MIOS_CEPHFS_KEYRING_DIR}` and `${MIOS_CEPHFS_MOUNT_OPTIONS}` (lines 6, 9, 12), which must resolve from `[storage.cephfs]` (`monitors`/`tenant_id`/`keyring_dir`/`mount_options`, mios.toml:9896) when `automation/firstboot/mios-cephfs-mount-setup.sh` instantiates them -- but nothing gates that correspondence, so a renamed or removed SSOT key silently yields a broken mount unit with an empty `What=`. Extend `check_cephfs_ssot` (`automation/38-drift-checks.sh`:1034), or add a sibling check, that greps every `${MIOS_CEPHFS_*}` token out of the two `.tmpl` files, asserts each maps to a defined `[storage.cephfs]` key via the existing env-name convention, and asserts `mios-cephfs-mount-setup.sh` substitutes each one so no un-substituted `${MIOS_CEPHFS_*}` survives its render. Static validation only -- no live ceph mount.
details.why: a silent SSOT rename produces a mount unit with an empty target -- discovered only when a user's home directory fails to mount on a real cluster.

title: mdevctl: add `[mdev]` SSOT persistent mediated-device definitions for SR-IOV VFs (explicitly NOT GPU fractioning)
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- mdevctl gains its legitimate positive wiring without weakening the architectural rejection of driver-free GPU fractioning.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-mdev-define-gen` emits deterministic mdevctl-persist config from `[mdev]` and no-ops when `enabled=false`; the output carries no vGPU/fractioning claim and the check at line 3326 stays green; `bash -n` and JSON parse clean; inert by default; no live hardware.

details.what_how: mdevctl exists in the tree ONLY as a rejection gate: `automation/38-drift-checks.sh`:3326 fails any doc claiming `mdevctl vGPU` unless marked impossible/unsupported/out-of-scope (correct -- the mios-metal architecture is whole-GPU-to-one-guest). There is no positive wiring for its legitimate use: persisting mediated devices for SR-IOV VFs and vendor-driver mdev types via `mdevctl define`, which the already-enabled `mios-sriov-init.service` sets the stage for. Add a `[mdev]` SSOT table (`enabled` default false; a list of definitions `{ parent = "<BDF>", mdev_type = "<type>", uuid = "<uuid>" }`) and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-mdev-define-gen` emitting `mdevctl define`-compatible config (the `/etc/mdevctl.d/<parent>/<uuid>` JSON mdevctl persists) projected from it, shipping INERT (`enabled=false` emits nothing). Critically: add a header comment scoping this to mediated SR-IOV/vendor devices only, leave the 3326 rejection gate fully intact, and introduce no vGPU/GPU-fractioning claim anywhere.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-mdev-define-gen` (new), `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (`[mdev]`), `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (do NOT weaken the check at 3326), `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sriov-init.service` (document the relationship)
details.why: SR-IOV VF assignments must be re-created by hand after every reboot today, and the only mention of mdevctl in the tree is a prohibition -- so the supported capability looks unsupported.

title: virt-v2v: add `[virt.v2v]` SSOT and a `mios-v2v-import` wrapper onto the local libvirt/KVM plane
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- the least-wired shipped feature gets SSOT and an entry point, or a recorded decision; this is the wiring.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-v2v-import --help` / dry-run resolves `[virt.v2v]` and prints the exact `virt-v2v` command it WOULD run (pool/network/format from SSOT) without executing; it exits 0 with a clear message when `virt-v2v` is absent; `bash -n` clean; inert by default; no live VM or conversion.

goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- a documented `[build.float]` allowlist becomes the ONLY place a legitimately-pinned build input may live.

details.what_how: ADR-0003 (SBOM-not-hardcode) says versions FLOAT and are resolved plus recorded at build, never hand-pinned in SSOT -- yet `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [build.bake_refs]` (lines 8554-8560) hand-pins `quickshell = "v0.3.0"`, `syft = "v1.19.0"`, `lookingglass = "B7"` and `surfer = "<40-hex>"`. The forthcoming NO-HARDCODE-VERSION gate (task_1368/318) must not red on these legitimate pins, so add one explicit exemption registry: a `[build.float]` table with `pinned_refs` (dotted keys under `[build.bake_refs]` intentionally pinned, each with an inline reason comment) and `exempt_globs` (repo-relative path globs whose version literals are legitimate, e.g. `automation/lib/globals.*`, `MiOS-SBOM.csv`, `usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/*`). title: Build the `mios-version-lint` NO-HARDCODE-VERSION scanner driven by the `[build.float]` allowlist
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- every inlined version literal and hand-pinned digest is mechanically detectable, so SSOT carries intent only.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 usr/libexec/mios/mios-version-lint .` exits 0 on the clean tree; injecting `RUN pip install foo==1.2.3` into a scratch tracked file makes it exit 1 citing file:line; `python3 -m py_compile` (or an equivalent syntax check) clean; allowlisted `[build.bake_refs]` pins do not trip it.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` (consumed by `check_no_hardcode`, `38-drift-checks.sh`:862) enforces the NO-HARDCODE law for DATES-in-comments only -- it does not catch hand-pinned VERSIONS, which ADR-0003 forbids. Create the sibling scanner `usr/libexec/mios/mios-version-lint` (exit 1 on violation, `MIOS_VERSION_LINT_SOFT=1` advisory mode, `sys.exit` style, matching mios-hardcode-lint's header/AI-Hint convention) that fails on three regression classes in TRACKED source: (1) a `vN.N.N` / `N.N.N` literal embedded in a download URL (`curl`/`wget`/`ADD`/`https://.../releases/download/...`); (2) an `@N.N` / `==N.N` / `~=N.N` pip pin or `@N.N.N` / `pkg@N` npm/bun pin in an install command; (3) a hand-pinned `@sha256:<64hex>` image digest in a tracked `.container`/`.image`/Containerfile/`.sh` -- SBOM records digests at build, source carries `:latest` intent. Load exemptions from `mios_toml.float_allowlist()`: skip paths matching `exempt_globs` and skip `[build.bake_refs]` values whose key is in `pinned_refs`. Keep it comment- and quote-aware like mios-hardcode-lint so a documented example is not flagged.
details.why: hand-pinned versions and digests are the exact class that produced the recurring Quadlet-digest drift and stale-download breakage, and nothing in the tree can currently find them.

title: Bake-plan integrity gate: prove the firstboot-tier eviction is correct AND complete
goal: E-16 The bake plane -- the invariant that lets a standard GitHub runner bake and publish is mechanically guaranteed, not assumed.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n` clean; `bash automation/38-drift-checks.sh check_bake_plan_integrity` green at HEAD (vllm/sglang in `firstboot.list`, absent from group lists, present in `core`); wired into `main()` next to `check_bake_plan`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check_bake_plan` (line 3672) only runs `generate-bake-plan.py --check` (lists match SSOT) -- it never proves the firstboot-tier EVICTION is semantically correct, the invariant that keeps the ~47GB vLLM+SGLang whales out of the runner bake. Add `check_bake_plan_integrity()` to `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` that loads `[build.bake].core`, `groups`, `group_members` and `firstboot_tokens` (`usr/share/mios/mios.toml` lines 8575-8619) via tomllib, reads the generated `usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/*.list` plus `firstboot.list`, then asserts: (1) every image matching a `firstboot_tokens` substring is ABSENT from every `NN-<group>.list` and PRESENT in `firstboot.list`; (2) no token-matching image is dropped entirely -- each remains in `core`; (3) the union of all group lists plus `firstboot.list` exactly equals the resolved `core` set (a true partition, no orphans or duplicates); (4) `firstboot_tokens` is non-empty iff `firstboot.list` is non-empty. `_violation` per broken invariant. Read-only, no build. Emit the next free display label.
details.why: if the eviction silently breaks, the publish bake exceeds the standard runner's disk and fails late in CI -- or worse, an evicted image is dropped from `core` entirely and a published image ships missing a service.

title: Value-parity, not just presence, for baker `MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_*` defaults
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- extend SSOT-projection coverage so a projected literal must EQUAL its SSOT source, not merely be non-empty.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n automation/38-drift-checks.sh` is clean; the gate is green at HEAD (every baker default equals SSOT); temporarily editing one baker's `:-` literal turns it red naming that baker and key; the function is wired into `main()`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check_bake_ref_defaults` (`automation/38-drift-checks.sh:3684`) only asserts baker scripts carry a NON-EMPTY `${MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_<X>:-...}` default; it never compares that literal to `[build.bake_refs]` in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml:8554-8560`, so a baker default can drift from SSOT undetected. Extend the gate (or add a sibling `check_bake_ref_parity`): `git grep` `automation/` for every `MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_<KEY>:-<lit>` default, lowercase `<KEY>` into `[build.bake_refs].<key>`, resolve the SSOT value via a `tomllib` heredoc, and `_violation` on each mismatch as `<baker>: MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_<KEY> default '<lit>' != SSOT '<ssot>'`. Keep the existing empty-default assertion intact. Same class of value-parity check 28 `check_globals_ports` already performs for ports.
details.why: A baker whose fallback ref has drifted from `[build.bake_refs]` bakes a DIFFERENT image than the SSOT declares whenever the env var is unset -- the image and the config disagree, and the gate currently blesses it.

goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the gate file audits ITSELF so a check cannot be silently shadowed, orphaned, or reported through a non-canonical path.

Then FIX the shadowing by merging/removing the redundant `check_greenboot` so the new gate is green.

title: `mios-userdb-render`: project the `account` table into systemd userdb JSON drop-ins
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- Postgres becomes the account SSOT on Linux, projected to the OS rather than hand-maintained in `/etc`.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-userdb-render` passes; a mocked-cursor dry-run emits a User Record that `python -c "import json;json.load(...)"` accepts with `userName`/`uid`/`homeDirectory` matching the fixture rows; a second run on unchanged input writes nothing.

details.what_how: Implement §3(a) of `docs/design/doc-postgresos-accounts.md` as a NEW `usr/libexec/mios/mios-userdb-render` (Python, same `get_pg_config()` + psycopg + `MIOS_TOML` gate style as `usr/libexec/mios/materialize-user-config.py`). SELECT enabled Linux-scoped rows from `account` (`WHERE enabled AND os_targets IN ('both','linux')` -- the same predicate as `mios-account-sync`'s `query_db_accounts`) and write one JSON User Record per user to `/run/userdb/<name>.user` (runtime tmpfs, since the DB is the runtime SSOT and `/usr` is immutable), following systemd.io/USER_RECORD: `userName`, `uid`, `gid`, `realName`<-display, `homeDirectory`<-home_dir, `shell`, `disposition:"regular"`; the hashed secret goes in a `.user-privileged` companion at mode 0600, NEVER plaintext. Idempotent via compare-before-write, mirroring `materialize-user-config.py:160-176`. Gate the whole run on `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED` like `automation/17-accounts-db.sh`, and fail-open (log, exit 0) when psycopg or the DB is absent so offline boot is unaffected. This is a PROJECTION only -- Postgres stays out of the login critical path per the doc's libnss-pgsql caution.
details.why: `[accounts].db_backed` ships inert today -- accounts exist in Postgres but the Linux side has no way to see them, so the DB-driven account model is a schema with no consumer.

title: Wire `mios-userdb-render` into a NOTIFY-driven unit under the db_backed gate
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the account projection re-renders on change instead of only at bake time.
acceptance_criteria: `bash -n automation/17-accounts-db.sh` passes; `systemd-analyze verify usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-userdb-render.service` reports no errors; the automation gate enables the unit only when db_backed is truthy; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Add `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-userdb-render.service` (Type=oneshot, `After=`/`Requires=mios-pgvector.service`, `ExecStartPre` pg_isready -- copy the shape of `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-account-sync.service`), plus a `.path`/timer or a small LISTEN wrapper on the `account_sync` channel the schema already emits (`notify_account_changes` trigger, `schema-init.sql:1088-1110`), so drop-ins re-render on account changes. Extend `automation/17-accounts-db.sh` to `install -m 0755` the renderer and `install -m 0644` the unit, and `systemctl enable`/`disable` it under the SAME `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED` gate the script already applies to `mios-account-sync.service` (`17-accounts-db.sh:37-46`). Note `nss-systemd` presence in the userdb NSS path in the script's log line -- do not hand-edit nsswitch beyond the existing revert logic. Stage ONLY the explicit new/edited paths.
details.why: A renderer with no unit runs never. Without the NOTIFY hookup, an account added to Postgres does not appear on the host until the next full rebuild -- which is not a usable account system.

title: Land `[accounts.lldap]` SSOT knobs + userenv alias derivation for the cross-platform LDAP face
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the cross-platform identity face gets an operator-tunable SSOT surface before any container exists to consume it.
acceptance_criteria: the TOML parses (`python -c "import tomllib,pathlib;tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('usr/share/mios/mios.toml').read_text())"`); `bash -n` passes on both userenv.sh copies; the two userenv.sh files remain byte-identical (drift check 27); `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Per §3(a)/§2 of `docs/design/doc-postgresos-accounts.md`, lldap-over-Postgres is the adopt-now cross-platform account SSOT face. Add an `[accounts.lldap]` sub-table to `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` beside the existing `[accounts]` block (`:92`): `enable=false`, `base_dn=""`, `db_schema="lldap"` (a separate schema in the SAME `mios` Postgres so Postgres stays the single SSOT), `ldap_port`, `http_port` -- all resolved-at-build/float, with NO hand-pinned image tag (SBOM law, ADR-0003). Extend the alias-derivation switch in BOTH `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` and `tools/lib/userenv.sh` (they must stay byte-identical per check 27) to emit `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_LLDAP_ENABLE`/`_BASE_DN`/`_DB_SCHEMA`/`_LDAP_PORT`/`_HTTP_PORT`, following the exact pattern at `userenv.sh:198-199` for `accounts.db_backed`. Do NOT deploy a container here -- that is task_1388's projector plus a later Quadlet task.
details.why: Without keys to float TO, any lldap work would arrive as hardcoded ports and DNs in a unit file -- a Law 7 violation created by the very task meant to unify identity.

title: `mios-lldap-seed`: project `account` rows into an lldap bootstrap so Postgres stays SSOT
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the LDAP wire protocol is a projection of the one datastore, never a second hand-maintained account store.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-lldap-seed` passes; a mocked-cursor dry-run produces bootstrap output that `json.load` (or an LDIF sanity parse) accepts, with users and groups matching the fixture rows; a disabled-gate run is a clean exit-0 no-op.

details.what_how: Add `usr/libexec/mios/mios-lldap-seed` (psycopg + `get_pg_config()` + the gate style from `materialize-user-config.py`) that reads enabled rows from `account` joined with `mios_identity.canonical_users`/`aliases` exactly as `mios-account-sync`'s `query_db_accounts` does (`mios-account-sync:63-94`) and emits lldap's bootstrap format -- its `bootstrap.json` user/group objects, or LDIF add records. title: Make `mios-account-sync` event-driven: LISTEN on `account_sync`, keep the poll as fallback
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- account changes converge on the host immediately, using the NOTIFY plumbing the schema already ships.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-account-sync` passes; a unit-level shim test with a stubbed connection shows the poll-only fallback still runs when `LISTEN` setup raises; the non-daemon single-pass branch is reachable and unchanged.

details.what_how: The schema already fires `pg_notify('account_sync', ...)` from triggers on `account` and `mios_identity.aliases` (`schema-init.sql:1088-1130`), but the daemon only POLLS every 15s (`mios-account-sync:328-342`). Upgrade the `--daemon` branch of `main()` to open a dedicated psycopg connection, `LISTEN account_sync`, and block on `conn.notifies()` with a 15s timeout that still triggers a full `sync_accounts()` pass as the safety fallback, so a missed NOTIFY or a fresh boot still converges. The LISTEN connection is ONLY the wake signal -- keep the existing `mios-pg-query`-subprocess path for the sync work itself. Preserve the state-file write-back logic (`:325-326`) and keep the `psycopg` import optional/guarded (log and fall back to pure polling if the direct connection cannot be built).
details.why: A 15s poll against Postgres runs 5,760 wasted round-trips a day and still leaves up to 15s of lag on a password or group change, while the NOTIFY triggers that would make it instant already exist and fire into nothing.

title: Generate the Windows `New-LocalUser` account manifest from the `account` table
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- the Windows account set becomes a projection of Postgres rather than hand-authored unattend XML.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-winaccounts-render` passes; a mocked-cursor dry-run emits a `json.load`-valid manifest whose fields, `is_admin` and `groups` match the fixture rows, with stable key ordering across two runs; a disabled-gate run exits 0 writing nothing.

details.what_how: Per §3(b)/§4 of `docs/design/doc-postgresos-accounts.md`, Windows has no NSS/PAM, so the honest baseline is a generated manifest a SetupComplete step consumes. Add `usr/libexec/mios/mios-winaccounts-render` (psycopg, gated on `MIOS_ACCOUNTS_DB_BACKED`) that SELECTs `WHERE enabled AND os_targets IN ('both','windows')` from `account` and writes a deterministic JSON manifest `{name, display, groups[], is_admin, password_hash?}` to a stable path (e.g. `/var/lib/mios/win-accounts.json`) which the Windows plane reads to drive `New-LocalUser`/`Add-LocalGroupMember`. This task stays inside `C:\MiOS` and emits ONLY the manifest -- do NOT edit `C:\mios-bootstrap` (autounattend/SetupComplete) or the Portal; the manifest IS the contract the other plane reads. Passwords hash-only, never plaintext.
details.why: Windows accounts are currently hand-written into autounattend XML, so the two platforms' user sets drift the moment either side changes -- and there is no artifact a gate could compare them against.

title: Allocate ids from the DB-owned `uid_alloc` sequence instead of the hardcoded 1000 gid fallback
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- ids are assigned ONCE in Postgres so every account projection reads the same number.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m py_compile usr/libexec/mios/mios-account-sync` passes; a stubbed-`mios-pg-query` unit test shows a NULL-gid row triggers exactly one `allocate_gid()` plus one write-back UPDATE and reuses the stored id on the next pass; no `1000` literal remains in the id path; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `schema-init.sql:795-807` defines `SEQUENCE uid_alloc` plus `allocate_uid()`/`allocate_gid()` precisely so ids are DB-owned, yet `mios-account-sync:180` still falls back to a hardcoded `gid = db_user["gid"] or 1000` which `useradd` at `:214-228` inherits -- silently colliding with the allocator. When a row has NULL uid/gid, allocate through the DB (`SELECT allocate_gid()` / `allocate_uid()` via `mios-pg-query`) and persist the result back onto the `account` row with an UPDATE, so Linux `useradd`, the task_1385 userdb records and the task_1390 Windows manifest all read the identical id. Keep the change additive and idempotent (allocate only when the column is NULL). Also drop the literal `1000` default from `query_db_accounts` (`:180`) -- an unresolved id is an error to log, not a magic default (Law 7 spirit).
details.why: Every account with a NULL gid currently lands on group 1000 -- so two different users collide on one group, and the three projections can each invent a different id for the same person.

title: Harden the SSOT template renderer and dispatch builder against placeholder/arg-splice injection
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- proves by test that no agent-supplied verb argument can escape shell quoting on the one path every verb dispatch takes.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 -m py_compile mios_template.py mios_dispatch.py` passes; the new adversarial tests prove every metacharacter stays quoted and unknown placeholders render empty rather than literal; no existing `test_mios_template.py` case regresses; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mios_template.py::_template_to_cmd` (sole verb command-template renderer, `_TEMPLATE_PH_RE = \{([a-zA-Z_]\w*)(?:(=|\?|!|\*)([^}]*))?\}`) already `shlex.quote`s substituted values and `mios_dispatch.py::_build_dispatch_cmd` routes verbs through it; add defense in depth without changing quoting semantics. (1) Placeholder-name allowlist: a placeholder that resolves via `_arg_with_synonyms` to nothing AND is not a declared arg for the verb must render EMPTY, never leak a literal `{name}` into the bash line -- add the guard plus an assertion/log for unknown names. (2) Regression tests feeding adversarial values (`$(id)`, `;rm -rf /`, backticks, `foo bar`, embedded newline) through `_template_to_cmd` for a representative `[verbs.*].cmd`, asserting every metacharacter lands inside a single `shlex.quote`d token. (3) Confirm the `{arg=$ENVVAR:fallback}` branch (L96-99) reads only template-author-chosen env names, with a test asserting args cannot influence WHICH env var is read.
details.where: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_template.py` (guard + log only); `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/test_mios_template.py` (adversarial cases); `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_dispatch.py::_build_dispatch_cmd` if a builder-level guard is warranted.
details.why: The renderer's safety is asserted but untested -- a future edit to the substitution loop could silently drop the `shlex.quote` and hand the agent plane arbitrary shell execution, and a leaked literal `{name}` becomes an unquoted brace in a live command line.

title: Make the short `MIOS_VLLM_*`/`MIOS_SGLANG_*` form canonical and gate the long form out
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- kills the emitted-vs-consumed dual-name split for the inference lanes so one fact carries one name.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "MIOS_AI_VLLM_\|MIOS_AI_SGLANG_" root-manifest.json` returns nothing; the new gate is green on HEAD and reds if a long canonical is reintroduced; `bash -n automation/38-drift-checks.sh` clean; userenv twins still identical; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The SSOT-to-env projection disagrees with reality: `tools/generate-names-registry.py` (`SHORT_ALIAS_PREFIX = {"ai.vllm":"MIOS_VLLM","ai.sglang":"MIOS_SGLANG"}`) and `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh::get_aliases` (L171-184) both know the short form, and EVERY real consumer reads it -- `automation/15-render-quadlets.sh` L121-122, `usr/libexec/mios/system-sync-env.sh` L155/207, the `${MIOS_VLLM_SERVED_NAME}` Quadlet Exec lines in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, `automation/38-vllm-prep.sh`'s `MIOS_VLLM_BAKE_MODEL`. Only `root-manifest.json` still records the LONG form as `proposed_canonical` (~13 entries, L1022-1099: `MIOS_AI_VLLM_SERVED_NAME`, `MIOS_AI_VLLM_GPU_UTIL`, `MIOS_AI_SGLANG_*`). Rewrite those `proposed_canonical` values to the short names produced by the generator's `_alias_for`, then add `check_vllm_name_canonical()` to `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` failing on any `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*`/`MIOS_AI_SGLANG_*` string used as an emitted or proposed-canonical name anywhere in the tree (allowlist only genuine historical audit fields). Keep `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` and `tools/lib/userenv.sh` byte-identical (drift-27).
details.where: `root-manifest.json` (the ~13 `proposed_canonical` lines only); `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` (new check + `main` wiring); `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (negative case); verify but do not diverge `tools/generate-names-registry.py`, `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh`.
details.why: With the manifest naming one canonical and every consumer reading another, key-library tooling keeps "fixing" toward a name nothing reads -- reintroducing the referenced-but-not-emitted drift class that breaks vLLM/SGLang Quadlet rendering.

title: Precompile every verb `cmd` template at catalog load; drop the per-dispatch regex parse
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- turns verb command templates into compiled, inspectable objects, which is also the precondition for build-time template validation.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 -m py_compile mios_template.py mios_dispatch.py` passes; every existing `test_mios_template.py` case passes unchanged (semantic parity); a new test asserts `compile_template(t).render(tool,args)` equals the old `_template_to_cmd` output for each placeholder form and that a repeated template returns the SAME cached object; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Today `mios_template.py::_template_to_cmd` re-runs `_TEMPLATE_PH_RE.sub` on EVERY dispatch and nothing validates placeholder-to-arg linkage. Add `compile_template(template) -> CompiledTemplate` that parses placeholders ONCE into an ordered segment list (`literal | Placeholder(name, op, rest)`) and returns a dataclass/callable; `_template_to_cmd` becomes a thin `compile_template(template).render(tool, args)` over an LRU/dict cache keyed by the template string (SSOT text is static, so the cache is safe and bounded by verb count). Precompile all `[verbs.*].cmd` / `cmd_args` / `cmd_positioned` / `cmd_pixel` / `cmd_resize` variants where `mios_dispatch.configure(verb_catalog=…)` receives the catalog, and expose `CompiledTemplate.placeholder_names` for the task_1406 gate. Preserve every placeholder semantic (`{arg}`, `{arg!}`, `{arg=default}` including `$ENV:fallback`, `{arg?FLAG}`, `{arg*}`) and the None-on-abort behavior byte for byte.
details.why: Re-parsing a regex on every dispatch burns latency on the hot agent path, and because templates are never structurally inspected a malformed `cmd` can only be discovered as a `None` render at runtime.

title: Emit a machine-readable `server.py` module-boundary manifest as the LANG-port contract
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- records the exact agent-pipe interface a future compiled port must preserve, before any code is ported.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 tools/gen-pipe-boundary-manifest.py` emits the JSON deterministically (regenerate equals committed); `python3 -m py_compile tools/gen-pipe-boundary-manifest.py` passes; the gate diffs green on HEAD and reds when a `configure()` kwarg is added without regenerating; `bash -n` clean on the shell edits; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The R7/R13 extractions (task_1395..task_1400) are turning `server.py` into `mios_pipe/**` modules each with a `configure()` DI seam, but nothing records WHAT each module exposes or which server-owned symbols it depends on. Add `tools/gen-pipe-boundary-manifest.py` that AST-walks `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/**/*.py` and, for each module defining `configure(**kwargs)`, records module path, the `configure` keyword names (its injected dependencies), and the public (non-underscore) symbols `server.py` re-imports from it; emit a deterministic `usr/share/mios/pipe-boundaries.manifest.json`. Add a regenerate-and-diff check `check_pipe_boundaries()` to `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` that fails when the committed manifest is stale. Inventory and enforcement ONLY -- port no code.
details.why: Without a written boundary contract, the eventual Rust/Go rewrite has to re-derive the dependency graph by reading 9k lines of Python, and any drift between the seams and the port is undetectable.

title: Run the drift-gate negative self-test harness in CI on every PR
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- makes CI prove the gates can still FAIL, not merely that they pass.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml'))"` parses clean; the new step invokes `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`; a local `bash tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` exits 0 with `git status` clean afterward; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `just drift-gate` (Justfile L99-102) runs BOTH `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` AND `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (the 16-case inject/assert/restore harness whose `main()` calls `test_version_ssot` … `test_containerfile_pinned_clones`), but the CI `drift-gate` job in `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` runs only `lint-shell.sh`, `38-ssot-lint.sh`, the agent-pipe tests, docgen, and `38-drift-checks.sh` -- the negative harness never runs in CI. Add a step named "Drift-gate negative self-tests (drift-gate-negatives.sh)" to the `drift-gate` job, immediately AFTER the "AI-plane source drift checks" step: `run: bash ./tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`. The harness restores every mutated file byte for byte before exit (no residue) and needs only shellcheck (already installed earlier in the job) and python3 (present on ubuntu-24.04). Keep it in the source-only `drift-gate` job so it fails fast before the bake.
details.why: A refactor that neuters a check -- makes it stop biting while still exiting 0 -- sails through CI today, so the whole enforcement plane can go quietly toothless with a green badge.
