## task_1409 -- Run the drift-gate negative self-test harness in CI on every PR (WS-TESTDOC | P1 | S) **[DONE]**
**Goal:** E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- makes CI prove the gates can still FAIL, not merely that they pass.
**What+How:** `just drift-gate` (Justfile L99-102) runs BOTH `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` AND `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (the 16-case inject/assert/restore harness whose `main()` calls `test_version_ssot` … `test_containerfile_pinned_clones`), but the CI `drift-gate` job in `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` runs only `lint-shell.sh`, `38-ssot-lint.sh`, the agent-pipe tests, docgen, and `38-drift-checks.sh` -- the negative harness never runs in CI. Add a step named "Drift-gate negative self-tests (drift-gate-negatives.sh)" to the `drift-gate` job, immediately AFTER the "AI-plane source drift checks" step: `run: bash ./tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`. The harness restores every mutated file byte for byte before exit (no residue) and needs only shellcheck (already installed earlier in the job) and python3 (present on ubuntu-24.04). Keep it in the source-only `drift-gate` job so it fails fast before the bake.
**Where:** `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` (drift-gate job, new step after 38-drift-checks.sh); `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (invoked, unchanged).
**Done When:** `python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml'))"` parses clean; the new step invokes `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`; a local `bash tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` exits 0 with `git status` clean afterward; `just drift-gate` green.
**Why:** A refactor that neuters a check -- makes it stop biting while still exiting 0 -- sails through CI today, so the whole enforcement plane can go quietly toothless with a green badge.
**Dep:** none.
**Who:** you (bash + GitHub Actions).

title: Close the shellcheck error-level coverage hole: lint EVERY shell dir, not three
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- extends the shell lint from a sampled subset to the whole shell surface, permanently.
acceptance_criteria: `bash automation/lint-shell.sh` error-lints the installation/tests/lib scripts too and exits 0 (all clean or explicitly disabled); `bash -n automation/lint-shell.sh` and `bash -n tests/test-lint-shell-coverage.sh` parse clean; the coverage self-test passes and FAILS if a dir glob is removed; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/lint-shell.sh` (L36-58) builds its error-level `files` list from ONLY `automation/*.sh`, `tools/*.sh`, and shebang-matched `usr/libexec/mios/mios-*`. That leaves `installation/*.sh` (mios-install.sh, mios-common.sh), `tests/*.sh`, `automation/tests/*.sh`, `automation/support/*.sh`, `automation/lib/*.sh`, `tools/lib/*.sh` and `usr/lib/mios/*.sh` (userenv.sh) never error-linted repo-wide -- they are reached only by the warning-level modified-files pass (L71-97), i.e. only when touched. Extend the collection loop with those globs, guarding each entry with `[ -f "$f" ]` and applying the same `^#\!.*(bash|sh)` shebang filter already used for libexec to extensionless files. Add `tests/test-lint-shell-coverage.sh` that greps `lint-shell.sh` and asserts each named dir appears in a collection glob, wired into the negative harness or a small check so coverage cannot be silently re-narrowed. Fix every NEW error-level finding the widened net surfaces, or record it as an inline `# shellcheck disable=` with a reason.
details.why: The install front door and the test harness -- the scripts that run on operator hardware and that gate the tree -- are exactly the ones no error-level lint has ever seen.

title: Negative tests for the bake-projection gates: check_bake_plan + check_bake_ref_defaults
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- proves the two bake-projection gates actually bite before the publish bake relies on them.
acceptance_criteria: `bash tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` runs both new cases green (each injected violation caught, each restore returning the gate to pass); `bash -n` clean; `git status` clean after the run; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Both gates ship with no negative case (`main()` in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` covers bake_budget/bake_tokens but not these): `check_bake_plan` (38-drift-checks.sh:3672) runs `python3 tools/generate-bake-plan.py --check` and _violations when `usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/*.list` are STALE versus mios.toml; `check_bake_ref_defaults` (line 3684) git-greps `MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_[A-Z0-9_]+:-\}` under `automation/` and _violations on any empty bake-ref default. Add `test_bake_plan` (append a bogus image line to `usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/03-extra.list`, assert nonzero, restore byte for byte, assert pass) and `test_bake_ref_defaults` (append `: "${MIOS_BUILD_BAKE_REFS_ZZZ:-}"` to a TRACKED `automation/*.sh` so the working-tree git-grep sees it, assert nonzero, restore, assert pass), both following the exact inject/assert-fail/restore/assert-pass shape of `test_version_ssot` (L23-42) including the `MIOS_THEME_ROOT`/`MIOS_TOML_ROOT` env prefix. details.where: `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (new `test_bake_plan`, `test_bake_ref_defaults` + `main()` calls); fixtures `usr/lib/mios/bake/plan.d/03-extra.list` and a tracked `automation` script, each mutated then restored.
details.why: A stale bake plan or an empty bake-ref default is a publish-breaking class, and today nothing proves those two gates would catch it rather than pass vacuously.

title: Negative tests for the security/mini SSOT-projection gates: check_clevis_luks + check_metal_vfio
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- proves the two generator-backed security projections fail on a broken SSOT instead of passing vacuously.
acceptance_criteria: both cases run green -- the malformed SSOT makes each gate exit nonzero and restore returns each to pass; `bash -n` clean; `git status` clean after the run; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check_clevis_luks` (38-drift-checks.sh:4004, "(67)") runs `usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen <mios.toml>` and _fails unless the output contains `CLEVIS_LUKS_ENABLED=`; `check_metal_vfio` (line 4020, "(68)") runs `usr/libexec/mios/mios-metal-vfio-gen <mios.toml>` and _fails unless the output contains `MIOS_METAL_ENABLED=` -- neither has a negative test. Add `test_clevis_luks` and `test_metal_vfio` that inject via a MALFORMED SSOT: create a temp toml fixture missing the `[security]`/`[mini]` table (or empty), invoke the check with `MIOS_TOML_ROOT` pointed at it, assert nonzero, then remove the fixture and assert the check re-passes against the real mios.toml. If a generator emits its marker key regardless of the missing table, instead inject by sed-breaking the marker `echo` line on a working COPY invoked through an overridden PATH -- and document whichever injection actually flips the gate red. Follow `test_router_parity` (line 298) for the generator-based pattern; register both in `main()`.
details.where: `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (new `test_clevis_luks`, `test_metal_vfio` + `main()` calls); `usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen` and `mios-metal-vfio-gen` (invoked, unchanged); a temp toml fixture created then removed.
details.why: These gates guard disk-encryption key binding and the VFIO passthrough projection; a check that only ever asserts a substring can pass on a generator that has stopped reading SSOT at all, shipping an unbound LUKS or a mis-bound GPU.

title: Negative tests for check_hyprland_conf_heredoc + check_target_languages
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- covers the desktop-config projection gate and the Law 14 language gate with proof-of-failure cases.
acceptance_criteria: both cases run green, each injected violation caught and each restore returning the gate to pass; `bash -n` clean; `git status` clean after the run; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check_hyprland_conf_heredoc` (38-drift-checks.sh:3848, "(50)") diffs `usr/share/mios/hyprland/hyprland.conf` against the heredoc embedded in `automation/54-bake-hyprland.sh` and _violations on drift; `check_target_languages` (line 3641, Law 14 TARGET-LANGUAGES) also has no negative case. Add `test_hyprland_heredoc` (append `# INJECTED-DRIFT` to `usr/share/mios/hyprland/hyprland.conf`, assert `check_hyprland_conf_heredoc` exits nonzero, restore byte for byte, assert pass) and `test_target_languages` (read the function body to learn its actual rule, then inject exactly what it forbids -- e.g. a disallowed-language source file dropped into a scanned dir or a forbidden extension -- assert nonzero, remove, assert pass). Mirror `test_version_ssot`'s inject/fail/restore/pass shape and its `MIOS_THEME_ROOT`/`MIOS_TOML_ROOT` env prefix; register both in `main()`.
details.where: `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (new `test_hyprland_heredoc`, `test_target_languages` + `main()` calls); `usr/share/mios/hyprland/hyprland.conf` (mutated then restored); a scanned language-dir fixture (created then removed).
details.why: The hyprland heredoc is a hand-duplicated copy that drifts by construction, and Law 14 is only as real as the check enforcing it -- an unfailable language gate means new C#/Batch/Go can land unnoticed.

title: Ratchet gate: every dispatched drift-check must have a negative case (shrink-only allowlist)
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- makes negative-test coverage self-enforcing so the gap can never silently reopen.
acceptance_criteria: `bash automation/38-drift-checks.sh check_negative_coverage` is green at HEAD; adding a new `check_foo` to `main()` without a negative case and without an allowlist entry FAILS; removing a still-uncovered allowlist entry FAILS; the negative case flips it red then restores; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` covers roughly 16 of the ~75 `check_*` functions dispatched from `automation/38-drift-checks.sh` `main()` (L~4224-4292) and nothing enforces the ratio -- new gates land untested, which is exactly why task_1411..task_1415 had to exist. Add `check_negative_coverage` to 38-drift-checks.sh that (a) extracts the dispatched check-name list from `main()` (the `check_[a-z_]+` calls between `check_dead_lane` and the final `echo` divider), (b) extracts the covered set from `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` (the `bash .../38-drift-checks.sh <name>` invocations inside each `test_*`), and (c) FAILS when a dispatched check that is not on an explicit `[testing.negative_coverage_exempt]` allowlist in mios.toml has no negative case -- a ratchet where the exempt list may only shrink. Seed the allowlist with today's genuinely untestable (warn-only/environmental) checks so HEAD is green, register the check in `main()`, and add a negative case for IT to the harness.
details.why: Coverage added by hand decays the moment attention moves on -- without a ratchet, the 16-of-75 gap quietly regrows and the enforcement plane's own trustworthiness becomes unmeasurable.

title: SSOT-drive the smoke-test component manifest from mios.toml plus a parity drift-gate
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- makes the smoke component list a Law 8 projection of SSOT so a rename fails the source gate, not a late boot.
acceptance_criteria: `bash automation/38-drift-checks.sh check_smoke_manifest` green at HEAD; listing a non-existent path in `[testing.smoke_components]` fails the gate; grep confirms no hardcoded shim list remains in `tests/bake-smoke.sh`; the negative case flips red then restores; `bash -n` and `python3 -m py_compile` clean on touched files; `just drift-gate` green.

title: ADR-0012: float-latest / no-hand-pinned-versions, generalizing ADR-0003 to every artifact class
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- turns the operator's float-latest principle into an accepted, cross-linked decision so its scattered enforcement has one authority to cite.
acceptance_criteria: every frontmatter key is filled with real laws (within the mios.toml `[laws]` 1..13 range) and real ssot_keys; the README table lists ADR-0012 with matching status/laws; a Markdown render shows all 8 body sections; References cites ADR-0003 without restating the digest mechanics; if `tools/adr-index.py` exists at implementation time, `python3 tools/adr-index.py --check` is green.

details.what_how: ADR-0003 (`usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0003-sbom-not-hardcode.md`) decided container-image digests are build-resolved SBOM data and explicitly leaves "model checksums, package version-hashes … as PLANNED follow-up"; the broader principle -- nothing hand-pinned, everything floats latest, resolved at build and recorded in SBOM -- is not itself a decision, and its enforcement is scattered (`check_containerfile_pinned_clones` "(71)" wanting git clones pinned to a REF; WS-MIOSSYS/WS-RELTOP newest-packages-tagged-at-build; the firstboot tier carrying `:latest` intent). Write `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0012-float-latest-no-hand-pinned-versions.md` following the README file format EXACTLY (two-line AI-hint header, YAML frontmatter, Status/Context/Decision/Rationale/Alternatives/Consequences/Implementation/References). Frame it as GENERALIZING ADR-0003 from container digests to RPM/package versions, model weights, git-clone refs and base-image tags, and reconcile the apparent tension: SSOT carries floating version INTENT (`:latest`, newest `MIOS_<X>_VERSION`), the BUILD resolves+verifies+records the concrete version to SBOM, and reproducibility = baked manifest + SBOM, never a hand-pin. Frontmatter `laws: [7, 8, 12]` (all <=13 so the roadmap/ADR law checks accept), `ssot_keys` from real keys (`image.sidecars`, `build.bake`, `build.bake_groups`, `ai.bake_models`), `related_ws: [WS-SBOM, WS-MIOSSYS, WS-RELTOP]`, `supersedes: []`; leave ADR-0003's `superseded_by: []` UNCHANGED and cross-link in References instead. Add the row to the README "The record" table.
details.why: With no accepted decision behind float-latest, each surface argues the pinning question locally -- one check demands pinned clone refs while the operator directive demands floating tags, and there is nothing to point at to settle it.

title: ADR-0013: deploy-surface consolidation behind `installation/mios-install`
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- records the landed single-dispatcher architecture as an immutable decision instead of tribal knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: all frontmatter keys filled with real laws (<=13) and real ssot_keys; the body has all 8 sections; it explicitly scopes to the AGY `installation/` surface and defers MiOS-Cat/Portal to ADR-0008 with no mios-bootstrap edits proposed; the README table lists ADR-0013; if `tools/adr-index.py` exists, `--check` is green.

details.what_how: The AGY-side consolidation is real and landed -- `installation/mios-install.{sh,ps1,bat}` is a pure DISPATCHER whose `usage()` lists targets `live|xbox|fedora|bootc|oci|seed|flash|build|update|config`, whose `resolve_*` functions build each entrypoint's argv/env and exec it, over the shared contract in `installation/mios-common.{sh,ps1}` (the UNIFY.md campaign) -- but no ADR records it, so "one front door resolving to N deployment types, never rewriting the underlying entrypoints" is undocumented. Write `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0013-deploy-surface-consolidation.md` per the README format EXACTLY. Decision: `installation/mios-install` is the single Linux/Windows install surface that RESOLVES a chosen target to an existing entrypoint (`build-mios.sh`, `mios-update`, `cat/MiOS-Cat.sh`, …) via the shared common-lib contract, with `--dry-run` plan output and gated target-matrix parity (cite the AGY-owned checks). Scope to the AGY tree ONLY: describe, do not propose changes to, the MiOS-Cat/Get-MiOS/Portal bootstrap side -- that is ADR-0008's domain; cross-link both. Frontmatter `laws: [1, 7, 8, 9]`, real `ssot_keys` (verbs, ports, any `[install]`/`[cat]` keys the dispatcher reads), `related_ws: [WS-INSTALL, WS-CONFIG]`, References cross-linking ADR-0008 and ADR-0009. Add the README "The record" row.
details.where: new `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0013-deploy-surface-consolidation.md`; `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/README.md` ("The record" row); cites `installation/mios-install.sh`, `installation/mios-common.{sh,ps1}`, `installation/UNIFY.md` (referenced, not modified).
details.why: An undocumented consolidation gets re-fragmented: the next contributor adds a fourth parallel install script because nothing states that the dispatcher is the only front door and that entrypoints are resolved, never rewritten.

title: ADR-0014: the bare-metal leg, `bootc install to-disk --transport oci`
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- names and scopes the missing blank-hardware, fully-offline install path as a decision before code is written for it.
acceptance_criteria: all frontmatter keys filled with real laws (<=13) and real ssot_keys; `status: proposed`; the body has all 8 sections and names the three bootc-install legs plus the `--transport oci` offline requirement; the README table lists ADR-0014; if `tools/adr-index.py` exists, `--check` is green.

details.what_how: The bare-metal leg is the least-done deploy path and is undocumented: `automation/build-mios.sh` (~L517) offers only `bootc install to-existing-root --source-imgref localhost/mios:latest` (converts an ALREADY-running host in place), and `installation/mios-install.sh`'s `bootc` target (`resolve_bootc`, L228) does only `switch` (a no-op unless the host already booted bootc) or `upgrade` (delegating to `mios-update`) -- there is NO fresh-disk `bootc install to-disk` and NO offline `--transport oci` path onto blank hardware, the gap the FOSS-upstream memo names. Write `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0014-bootc-install-bare-metal-leg.md` per the README format EXACTLY. Decision: adopt `bootc install to-disk` (and `to-filesystem` for the kickstart path) sourcing the image via `--transport oci`/`oci-archive` from the MiOS-Data OCI tar so a blank machine installs the SAME image offline -- distinguishing the three legs (to-existing-root = convert, to-disk = blank disk, to-filesystem = anaconda/kickstart `%post`) and the offline-transport requirement. Mark `status: proposed` (implementation PLANNED). Frontmatter `laws: [3, 4, 12]`, real `ssot_keys` (`image.sidecars`, `build.bake`, and the ventoy/kickstart keys `check_deploy_plane` reads), `related_ws: [WS-CAT, WS-MDRIVE]`, References cross-linking ADR-0005 and ADR-0008. Add the README "The record" row.
details.where: new `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/0014-bootc-install-bare-metal-leg.md`; `usr/share/doc/mios/adr/README.md` ("The record" row); cites `automation/build-mios.sh`, `installation/mios-install.sh`, `usr/share/mios/ventoy/mios-kickstart.cfg` (referenced, not modified).
details.why: Today the only "install" MiOS can perform on blank hardware installs plain Fedora, and with the gap unwritten it keeps being mistaken for a bug in the media rather than a whole missing leg.

title: Record the testdoc/deploy work as ROADMAP workstreams and regenerate the index/rollup/ToC
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- makes the roadmap reflect the work that exists so an arriving agent can pick up a workstream cold.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 tools/roadmap-index.py --check` exits 0 (index/rollup/ToC match the frontmatter); both new WS sections carry every frontmatter key with real laws (<=13), real ssot_keys and valid adr refs; `bash automation/38-drift-checks.sh check_roadmap_index` green; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: ROADMAP.md's generated blocks -- `<!-- ROADMAP_ROLLUP_START -->` (Done/Active/Proposed/Blocked counts), `<!-- ROADMAP_INDEX_START -->` (per-theme WS list), `<!-- ROADMAP_TOC_START -->` -- are produced by `tools/roadmap-index.py` from each `## WS-*` section's KEP-style frontmatter, and none of this session's testdoc/deploy work is recorded. Add two WS sections with full frontmatter (`id, title, theme, status, priority, laws[], ssot_keys[], adr[], deps[], acceptance`) using existing WS blocks as the template: `WS-TESTDOC` (drift-gate negative coverage in CI, shellcheck coverage widening, bake-smoke harness; `adr: []`; `laws: [7, 8]`) and `WS-DEPLOY` (theme "Deployment & Sovereignty" -- deploy-surface consolidation plus the bootc-install bare-metal leg; `adr: [13, 14]` referencing task_1420/370; `laws: [1, 3, 4, 12]`). NOTE: `tools/roadmap-index.py` (~L204) currently rejects any `law > 13`, so keep every WS `laws[]` entry <=13 until that ceiling is de-hardcoded.
details.where: `ROADMAP.md` (new WS-TESTDOC + WS-DEPLOY sections and the regenerated INDEX/ROLLUP/TOC blocks); `tools/roadmap-index.py` (invoked, unchanged).
details.why: Work that is not on the roadmap is invisible to the next agent, who re-derives or duplicates it -- and a hand-edited rollup that no longer matches the frontmatter reds `check_roadmap_index`.

title: Vendor the REAL k3s binary at LATEST with sha verification and install.sh
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- replaces a stub with a latest-resolved, sha-verified, SBOM-recorded artifact so the k3s stack bakes offline with no hand-pin.

title: Split the monolithic build.sh RUN into resumable checkpointed layers  (WS-GHSELF | **P1** | L)
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image, and can a stock runner hold it -- makes a bake survivable on ordinary hardware and ordinary interruptions.
acceptance_criteria: a reboot part-way through a build resumes from the last completed RUN layer instead of restarting at stage 1.

details.what_how: `STEP 17/25` currently runs all ~65 stages of `automation/build.sh` inside ONE Containerfile `RUN`, so a mid-bake reboot discards 1-2h of work. Split that into a few checkpointed `RUN` layers along natural stage boundaries (e.g. overlay+packages | services+render | bake+finalize), keeping the numeric stage ordering intact, so podman's layer cache resumes at the last completed checkpoint.
details.why: every interrupted publish attempt today costs a full rebuild, which is the single largest tax on both the local publish loop and the GitHub runner.

title: Implement the sha256 verification TODO in mios-models-firstboot
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- closes an integrity hole in the one component that writes model weights to disk.
acceptance_criteria: a deliberately corrupted download is rejected and retried, and never lands under its final filename.

details.what_how: Replace the `# In real scenario we'd check sha256 here` comment in `usr/libexec/mios/mios-models-firstboot` with a real digest check: hash each downloaded GGUF, compare against `[ai.firstboot_models].sha256`, and only then perform the rename into place. On mismatch, discard and retry; degrade-open when no expected sha is declared.
details.why: an unverified GGUF from a network fetch is loaded straight into the inference lane — a truncated or substituted file is installed silently today.

title: Audit and harden the coderun sandbox now that code_mode ships enabled  (WS-CODEMODE | **P1** | L)
goal: E-24 Autonomy guardrails: the agent plane cannot starve its own host -- makes shipping code-execution-on defensible instead of hopeful.
acceptance_criteria: a deliberately hostile snippet cannot reach the network, the host filesystem, or elevated capabilities, and the threat model is written down.

details.what_how: `code_mode.enable` now defaults true, so audit the coderun sandbox against each control and fix every gap found: rootless execution, `no-new-privileges`, dropped capabilities, read-only rootfs, network denied unless the request AND `[code_mode].allow_net` AND deploy context agree, a seccomp profile, and memory/pid/wall-time limits. Record the resulting threat model alongside the config.
details.why: with code_mode on by default, any prompt-injected snippet inherits whatever the sandbox fails to deny — this is the security backstop for the whole agent plane.

title: Collapse the install entry points to one shim-less `.bat` and add a global `mios mon` service tracker
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- every target reaches the single guided `mios-install` dispatcher instead of a fan of forwarder scripts.
acceptance_criteria: exactly one install entry point remains, `mios mon` lists every mios-* unit, check-86 (installer-family-roles) is green, and `grep` for the deleted shims finds no orphaned references.

details.what_how: Reduce the `installation/` entry points to ONE `.bat` that is not a shim but the real Windows entry, handing directly into the guided installer; delete the pure-forwarder scripts it replaces. Add a `mios mon` verb to `usr/bin/mios` that tracks ALL `mios-*` functions and services globally (one monitor surface, not per-service commands). Deletions must not break drift-check 86 (installer-family-roles), which asserts each installer file still fills a declared role, nor the LAYERS documentation bundle that references those filenames.
details.why: Multiple near-identical entry points mean an operator can start an install down a path that skips prereq resolution or elevation, and every fix has to be made N times.

title: Number drift-gate checks inline with the scripts under one global 0-99 system
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one globally-identifiable number per pipeline element so OCI layer = stage = step = check.
acceptance_criteria: a single numbering scheme spans scripts, stages and checks; gate output shows a check's number matching the stage it guards; inserting a new check leaves existing numbers unchanged.

details.what_how: The pipeline currently runs four independent counters: `automation/NN-*.sh` script prefixes, drift-check `(N)` ordinals, build stages, and OCI layers. Unify them onto the same 0-99 scheme so a check carries the number of the stage it guards, and update the `[NN-name]` log labels emitted by `build.sh` and `98-drift-checks.sh` to print that one number. The scheme must be renumber-immune: inserting a check must not shift the identity of unrelated ones.
details.why: With four counters, a red "(57)" in the log cannot be traced to the build stage that produced the drift without reading the source, which slows every gate failure triage.

title: Prototype the compiled-template system that generates twin implementations from one source
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- structure is generated and validated, so hand-maintained twins cannot diverge.
acceptance_criteria: one twin pair is produced entirely from a single template source, and hand-editing a generated output is detected as drift.

title: Ratchet shellcheck to a repo-wide warning-level CI gate
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- shellcheck is a real CI gate rather than source-directive comments.
acceptance_criteria: a newly-added script carrying a shellcheck warning fails CI, and the recorded baseline cannot grow.

details.what_how: The drift-gate lints only MODIFIED scripts at warning level today. Extend `automation/lint-shell.sh` and the CI job to scan the whole repo at warning level with a grandfathered baseline of existing warnings, so pre-existing noise is recorded once and any NEW warning fails. The baseline count only ever goes down.
details.why: Only touched files are checked now, so an untouched script can carry quoting and word-splitting bugs indefinitely and no gate has an opinion.

title: Rotate the exposed GitHub PAT and move publish auth to a secret store  (WS-SEC | **P0** | M)
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- publish credentials are scoped, stored and revocable rather than plaintext on disk.
acceptance_criteria: the old PAT is revoked and returns 401, no on-disk file contains a token, and a publish succeeds reading the scoped token from the secret store.

details.what_how: A classic PAT was pasted in-session and used to authenticate `gh` and the publish. Rotate it (operator action), then purge every on-disk copy -- the VM's `/root/ghtok`, any log capturing it -- and code the plumbing so `pub.sh` reads a FINE-GRAINED token from a secret store via `secrets.env` and `mios.toml [security]`, never from a plaintext file path.
details.why: A live classic PAT with broad scope sits in a plaintext file on a VM and in session history; anyone who reads it can push to the published image ref.

title: Prove the cosign policy signs on publish and the install path verifies
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the signature chain is closed end to end, not merely configured.
acceptance_criteria: installing a tampered image is BLOCKED with a signature-verification failure, and an untampered image installs.

details.what_how: Verify that `automation/49-cosign-policy.sh` actually produces a signature on the published image, and that the install path performs `cosign verify` against the policy before it deploys. details.why: A signing step that is never verified on the consuming side provides no protection at all, only the appearance of one.

title: Gate SBOM completeness so every baked artifact carries a resolved version
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the SBOM plus the baked manifest ARE the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: the SBOM covers 100% of baked artifacts and the gate fails when a newly-baked binary is added without an SBOM entry.

details.what_how: Add a check that walks the baked binaries, venvs and vendored assets and asserts each appears in `MiOS-SBOM.csv` with a resolved version or digest, failing the build on a missing row. This is the consuming half of WS-LATEST: floating a ref to `:latest` is only safe if the resolved value is recorded here.
details.why: With `:latest` intent everywhere, an SBOM with holes means the image cannot be reproduced or audited for a CVE at all.

title: Wire `[accounts].db_backed` to Linux userdb and a Windows baseline
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- accounts are declared once in SSOT and projected per platform.
acceptance_criteria: one account declared in SSOT produces a valid systemd userdb JSON record on Linux AND a Windows baseline account definition, from a single run of `mios-account-sync`.

details.what_how: `[accounts].db_backed` currently ships inert. Assemble the FOSS-brick model documented in `docs/design/doc-postgresos-accounts.md`: a systemd userdb JSON projection for Linux, lldap-over-Postgres as the cross-platform SSOT face, and `New-LocalUser` via autounattend/SetupComplete for the Windows baseline (which has no NSS/PAM). details.why: A flag that reads as a feature but does nothing is worse than an absent one; operators define accounts twice, per platform, by hand.

title: Extend `mios-ssot-regen` to regenerate ALL SSOT projections in one command
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one command re-projects everything the gate checks.
acceptance_criteria: one `mios-ssot-regen` run regenerates all 8 projections and the full drift-gate is green immediately afterwards, with Quadlet `@sha256` pins intact.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ssot-regen` currently regenerates only the 2 AI manifests. Extend it to invoke the remaining drift-gate generators -- `mios-registry`, `generate-bake-plan`, `roadmap-index`, `generate-blade-dropins`, `generate-egress-firewall`, `generate-pod-quadlets` -- so a single run re-projects all 8. details.why: Contributors have to know and run six generators in the right environment; missing one is the recurring red-gate class, and getting pod-quadlets wrong strips the digest pins.

title: Publish a machine-readable publish-status file beside the publish log so state survives reboots
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image, and can a stock runner hold it -- the resumable publish must be observable across a WSL idle/reboot cycle, not reconstructed by scraping a text log.
acceptance_criteria: `cat /mnt/c/mios-publish-status.json | jq .state` returns the live publish state after a host reboot, and `mios mon` renders publish stage/digest without reading the log file.

details.what_how: `pub.sh` currently only appends to `/mnt/c/mios-publish-build.log`. Add a status writer that emits `/mnt/c/mios-publish-status.json` with the five fields the operator actually needs — `state`, `stage`, resolved-version, image digest, `last_error` — updated at each stage transition, and teach the `mios mon` backend to read that JSON instead of tailing the log. Both copies of `pub.sh` (the `/root` one and the repo copy) must write the same schema.
details.where: `pub.sh` (the `/root` copy AND the repo copy), the `mios mon` backend.
details.why: Today publish state is only recoverable by eyeballing a growing log, and a reboot mid-publish leaves the operator unable to tell whether the bake resumed, stalled, or already pushed a digest.

title: Reorder mios-sys Containerfile RUN steps static-first to stop cache-busting
goal: E-17 Shared-base consolidation: shrink the sidecar fleet to two lineages -- the shared base rebuilds cheaply so a standard runner can hold the bake.
acceptance_criteria: the layer order places static installs before volatile copies, and a rebuild after a source-only edit reuses cache through the package layers instead of rerunning them.

details.what_how: Sort the RUN steps in `usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile` (and the corresponding region of the root `Containerfile`) by change-frequency: the most-static binaries and package installs come FIRST, immediately after the git-to-root overlay, with volatile per-commit content last. This follows the operator directive "core/stationary componentry FIRST" and means a source-only change invalidates only the tail layers.
details.why: With volatile layers early, every trivial commit busts the whole cache and re-runs the heavy package installs, pushing the bake past what a standard runner can finish.

title: `mios-env-snapshot`: the ground-truth capture for every lossless refactor  (WS-UNIFY | **P0** | S)
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- provides the measuring instrument without which no namespace-collapse step can be proven lossless.

title: `check_resolved_env_lossless`: gate the resolved env against a committed baseline  (WS-UNIFY | **P0** | M)
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- turns the losslessness invariant into a mechanical check so the 2523-key collapse cannot lose a value in passing.
acceptance_criteria: the check is green on the current tree and the negative test proves it goes red when a resolved value is injected/changed.

title: Wire the lossless gate into CI and a pre-commit hook
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- a check that only runs when someone remembers to run it is not enforcement; this makes the lossless invariant unavoidable at both commit and merge time.
acceptance_criteria: a deliberately value-changing commit is rejected by the local hook AND fails the CI job -- both legs demonstrated, not just one.

details.what_how: Add `check_resolved_env_lossless` to the CI workflow so no PR merges with a changed resolved env, and install a git pre-commit hook under `.githooks/` that runs the same check locally so the failure is caught before the commit exists rather than after the push.
details.why: GUP spans hundreds of tasks; relying on the author to remember one manual command guarantees that the one forgotten run is the one that drops a key.

**Goal:** E-09 One value, one name -- takes the measured duplication list to zero.

title: Reconcile mismatched `[image.sidecars]` version/tag pairs BEFORE deriving  (WS-UNIFY | **P1** | M)
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- version keys derive from image-ref tags, which is only lossless if tag and version already agree.
acceptance_criteria: for every sidecar, `X_version` equals the tag of `X`, so a subsequent derive produces a byte-identical env.

details.what_how: Find every `[image.sidecars]` entry where `X_version` disagrees with the tag of the ref `X` (the known case: `cuda_version = latest` against a `:cuda` ref). For each, decide which side is the truth -- normally the ref tag -- and set `X_version` to match, or correct the ref if the ref is the wrong one.
details.why: Deriving on top of a mismatch turns a silent pre-existing inconsistency into a visible value change in the lossless diff, which either blocks Phase 2 or gets waved through with a baseline bump that hides a real bug.

title: Resolver twin A: derive `MIOS_X_VERSION` from the image ref (`mios_toml.py`)  (WS-UNIFY | **P1** | M)
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- makes the image ref the single source for its own version, one of the named GUP derivations.
acceptance_criteria: with the `_version` keys still present in `mios.toml`, the env diff is empty -- proving the derived value matches the declared one exactly.

details.what_how: In the `image.sidecars` handler, when a non-`_version` key `X` holds a full image ref, additionally emit `MIOS_<X>_VERSION` set to the tag of that ref, while keeping `MIOS_<X>_IMAGE` as-is. Turn the explicit `_version` key handling into a no-op so the keys can be deleted in task_1547 without changing behavior.
details.why: Until the version derives, a sidecar bump requires editing two keys, and the pair drifts the first time only one of them is touched (the cuda case is that bug, already live).

title: Compose `[build.bake].core` from `[image.sidecars]` plus a `local_builds` list  (WS-UNIFY | **P1** | M)
goal: E-16 The bake plane -- the core allow-list becomes a generated view of the image declarations instead of a hand-maintained second copy of every sidecar ref.
acceptance_criteria: no sidecar ref literal remains in `[build.bake]`, and both the env diff and the bake-plan diff are clean against the pre-change baseline.

title: Rewire the seven double-baked services onto their derived image, one service per task
goal: E-17 Shared-base consolidation -- shrink the ~18-image sidecar fleet onto shared lineages so a standard runner can bake and publish.
acceptance_criteria: each of the seven services starts from the single derived image, its upstream ref no longer appears in the bake plan, and `podman system df` shows the local store shrunk after the set lands.

details.what_how: One task each for adguard(503), forgejo(504), k3s(505), open-webui(506), jaeger(507), matchbox(508), searxng(509), plus a verification task(510). Per service: point its Quadlet at the mios-sys/derived image, remove the now-redundant upstream ref from the `03-extra` bake set in `plan.d/`, and confirm the unit still starts under its existing `User=`/`Group=`/`Delegate=` (runtime Model A is unchanged — only the image collapses). 510 verifies the whole set together.
details.why: baking both the upstream image and the derived one doubles pull time and store size and is a direct cause of the bake exceeding standard-runner capacity.

goal: E-16 The bake plane -- a stock runner can hold the bake, and a restart resumes rather than restarts.

title: Collapse the Windows/Linux install shims into one dispatcher and prove both repos ship it byte-identical
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- one guided entry that both installs MiOS and opens the Portal, with no redundant elevation, fetch or redirector left in the chain.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-install --dry-run` succeeds on every target from either repo's checkout, the .sh/.ps1 parity drift-check is green, and the deleted shim files no longer exist in either tree.

details.what_how: (633) rewrite the `.bat` as a name-stable, logic-free arg-forwarder into the canonical `.ps1`; (634) promote `mios mon` from a local alias to a global verb; (635) add the missing `Get-MiOS -Action Install/Configure` handoff so the `irm | iex` web door hands INTO the guided installer instead of orphaning MiOS-Cat; (636) assert mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git carry byte-identical copies of the shared installer surface (Law 15 DOUBLE-REPO); (637) delete the redirectors that are pure duplicate logic; (638) emit family/role markers so a route knows which target it is serving; (639) an installer smoke run per route; (640) the operator-facing install doc.
details.why: today an operator can enter through several files with divergent elevation/prereq/TOML-resolution logic, the web door dead-ends before the installer, and every fix must be hand-copied into a second repo where it silently rots.

title: One global 0-99 numbering so OCI layer = stage = step = drift-check, renumber-immune
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one numbering system across scripts, stages and checks so a log line, a build layer and a gate id all name the same thing.

details.what_how: (641) one progress counter in `build.sh` rather than per-script counts; (642) `check_pipeline_numbering` as a regression gate plus its negative test; (643) renumber-immune check labels so inserting a check does not rewrite 100 others; (644) publish the OCI-layer = stage = step = check map; (645) tag every log line with its number; (646) the numbering doc; (647) migrate the legacy check numbers onto the SSOT ordinal (the 149 colliding `(NN)` labels deleted); (648) verify the inline runtime display. `generate-gate-index.py` is the ONE real label parser and must be updated in lockstep with any label change.
details.why: without it every inserted stage renumbers unrelated checks, log lines cannot be traced back to the check that emitted them, and the gate index drifts from the scripts it indexes.

title: Systemically fix the three failure classes that broke the 0.3.0 publish bake

acceptance_criteria: the snapshot is byte-identical across the locale x HOME matrix, `check_resolved_env_lossless` and check-45 are green in both CI locale jobs, and a red prints its diff.

details.what_how: (749) pin HOME/XDG/LC_ALL/LANG/TZ and the user+host TOML layers to fixed nonexistent paths in `mios-env-snapshot`, excluding self-referential meta-keys, and add a header contract; (750) a sentinel running the snapshot under >=3 locales x >=3 HOMEs asserting byte-identical output; (751) gate that `env-baseline.txt` is regenerated whenever `referenced_names.txt` changes (pre-commit + CI); (752) a leak sentinel asserting no resolved value embeds the tree root, `$HOME`, hostname or uid; (753) make `check_resolved_env_lossless` print the ACTUAL diff even on the negative path (stop `>/dev/null`); (754) a `mios-env-baseline --regen` helper plus documented `MIOS_ENV_BASELINE_BUMP=1`; (755) decide the referenced_names -> empty-emit policy for the `MIOS_A2A_*`/`MIOS_CAT_LIVE_CHAT_*` class; (756-757) a baseline header and a CI matrix running the check in both C and en_US.UTF-8; (758-760) generate the two byte-identical `userenv.sh` from ONE source (killing check-27's manual copy-sync), run check-45 twin-equivalence under `env -i`, and emit `names.generated.txt` + `referenced_names.txt` from one invocation behind one gate; (761) the resolver-hermeticity ADR; (762) a pre-commit hook regenerating both on any resolver/SSOT change.
details.why: the gate that protects every GUP step currently goes red for caller locale, HOME and stale referenced-names rather than for real drift -- and prints nothing, so the red is undebuggable.

title: Derive every sidecar version from its image tag and delete the standalone X_version keys
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- a version is declared once (in the image ref) and derived everywhere else, ending the k3s-in-35-places class.
acceptance_criteria: no `X_version` key remains in SSOT, `mios-env-snapshot` shows every `MIOS_X_VERSION` unchanged, and a single-ref k3s bump propagates to Quadlets, bake list and docs with the gate green.

details.what_how: (763) enumerate every `[image.sidecars]` `X_version` against `tag(X)` into a reconcile worklist and commit the analysis; (764) fix the INCONSISTENT pairs first (e.g. `cuda_version` vs the `:cuda` tag) so derive == old; (765-778) one task per sidecar (adguard, cuda, sglang, vllm, k3s, postgres, pgvector, searxng, valkey, guacamole, guacd, open-webui, otelcol, hermes/sys) making the resolver derive `MIOS_X_VERSION=tag(MIOS_X_IMAGE)`, deleting the standalone key, and lossless-verifying the value is unchanged; (779) land the tag-extraction rule identically in `mios_toml.py` `get_aliases`, both `userenv.sh` twins and `check-resolver-twin.py`; (780-783) delete all `X_version` keys, gate `check_no_duplicate_value_key`, make the 19 `_VERSION=latest` keys derive from a `:latest` ref, and stop `[build.bake].core` re-listing sidecar refs; (784-785) regenerate Quadlet `Image=` from the canonical `MIOS_*_IMAGE` (never de-digesting; stage explicit paths) and regenerate `03-extra.list`; (786) sign-off by bumping k3s in ONE place and watching every surface update.
details.why: the same version currently lives in the tag AND a sibling key AND the bake list AND the Quadlets, so a bump updates some of them and the fleet runs a mix.

title: Collapse the measured alias bloat: one value carried by many names
goal: E-09 One value, one name -- the duplication measured in `env-baseline` (values under >=3 keys) collapses to one canonical name plus a documented compat leg.
acceptance_criteria: `check_no_duplicate_value_key` is green over all value classes, and the env diff shows ONLY the intended key drops with every surviving value byte-identical.

details.what_how: (787) COLOR vs COLORS -- pick canonical, repoint consumers, drop the other; (788) collapse the 6-name embed-model fanout (`MIOS_PG_EMB_MODEL`/`PG_EMBED_MODEL`/`PGVECTOR_EMB_MODEL`/`PGVECTOR_EMBED_MODEL`/`AI_EMBED_MODEL`/`VERB_EMBED_MODEL` == nomic-embed-text); (789) separate true model aliases (`MIOS_AI_MODEL`==`MIOS_MODEL`, the 8-way granite fanout) from distinct configurable facts and collapse only the true dupes; (790) derive the 6 `nodes.local.*_ENDPOINT` from one; (791) collapse the ANSI singular/plural pair; (792) allowlist the mios-find launcher aliases as INTENTIONAL many-to-one; (793) audit `MIOS_A2O_*` vs `MIOS_FRONTIER_*`; (794) extend `check_no_duplicate_value_key` to non-version values with that allowlist; (795) resolve the task_1554 pgvector/pg double-alias; (796-799) per-family collapse (portal, agents, nodes, lanes); (800) sign-off.
details.why: the same fact under six names means six places to edit and five chances to leave a stale value that some consumer still reads.

title: Actually build and BOOT every deploy artifact in CI, not just plan it  (WS-DEPLOY-REAL | P1/P2 | L)
goal: E-20 The bootc-native install legs -- a blank machine installs the real immutable MiOS fully offline, proven by a booting artifact rather than a document.
acceptance_criteria: each CI job uploads its artifact AND its boot log shows the installed system is bootc-managed MiOS (not plain Fedora), with the per-format gate green.

details.what_how: (801-802) build a BIB Anaconda ISO from the PUBLISHED image in CI, upload it, and boot it headless in QEMU asserting Anaconda reaches the `ostreecontainer` stage; (803) `bootc install to-disk` into a QEMU raw disk OFFLINE from an oci-archive with a first-boot assert; (804) qcow2 and vhdx artifacts built and booted; (805) the Secure Boot chain shim->GRUB->signed-UKI with MOK enrollment under OVMF with SB ON; (806) a Ventoy USB image (ISO + oci-archive + loopback.cfg-from-SSOT) booting from USB in QEMU; (807) the Windows/Xbox leg (autounattend + SetupComplete `New-LocalUser` baseline); (808) pin the kickstart `ostreecontainer` source to the published digest offline; (809) the MiOS-Cat.sh <-> build-mios.sh FULL-FOLD with the shims deleted; (810) the missing bare-metal leg via `bootc install --transport oci`; (811-817) per-format boot-assert (raw/qcow2/vhdx/iso/oci-archive/ventoy/win-iso); (818) one USB, all formats, sign-off.
details.why: the deploy plane is the least-finished area: the USB machinery works but installs plain Fedora, the bare-metal leg has no `tools/install.sh` at all, and nothing today proves an artifact boots.

title: Wire every shipped-but-inert runtime capability from SSOT, or document the deferral  (WS-RUNTIME-WIRE | P2/P3 | L)
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- close the doc-vs-SSOT gap so nothing ships as silent dead weight.
acceptance_criteria: for each capability either a drift-check asserts its SSOT wiring and a smoke exercises it, or a recorded decision states why it is deferred -- with no capability left unclassified.

details.what_how: one task per capability MiOS already bakes but does not drive: (819) greenboot health-checks defined from SSOT and gated; (820) clevis/LUKS auto-unlock from `[security]`; (821) chrony NTP; (822) the ROCm/venus GPU plane wired or documented-deferred (venus != CUDA); (823) decide ceph -- wire or sunset alongside gluster; (824) mdevctl vGPU; (825) the freeipa / lldap-over-Postgres accounts SSOT face; (826) NUT UPS; (827) guacamole/guacd wired plus a smoke; (828) virt-v2v import; (829) clarify signed-UKI vs MOK (MOK != UKI) and wire it; (830) audit that every stateful dir lives on `/var` so it survives a bootc update; (831-833) three further features; (834) sign-off that every shipped binary is wired-from-SSOT or explicitly deferred with a reason.
details.why: the image carries greenboot, clevis, chrony, ROCm, ceph, mdevctl, freeipa, NUT, guacamole and virt-v2v that no config path reaches, so operators believe they have protections that are not running.

title: Security follow-through: the exposed PAT is still live  (WS-SEC2 | P0/P2 | M)
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- every declared control is actually enforced and gated, starting with the credential that is currently valid.
acceptance_criteria: gitleaks returns clean over the full history, the rotated credential is confirmed revoked, `cosign verify` gates the publish, and every privileged unit's caps are justified in SSOT.

details.what_how: (835, P0) rotate the exposed PAT (`ghp_…` present in git history) and move credentials to a secret store -- operator action, tracked to completion; (836) scan the full history with gitleaks and rotate anything else found; (837) cosign sign the published ghcr image and gate on `cosign verify`; (838) SBOM completeness -- every bound image and vendored asset carries digest + sha; (839) fapolicyd trust for the coderun-sandbox plus an agent-codegen rules audit; (840) the egress firewall from an SSOT allowlist using nft (no firewalld); (841) least-privilege each of the 10 privileged root Quadlets under Law 10; (842) sign-off.
details.where: git history, `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[security]`/`[security.privileged_quadlets]`, the rendered Quadlets, CI publish workflow
details.why: a working token in a readable history is an active compromise path, and an unsigned image plus unbounded egress means a tampered artifact would be indistinguishable from a real one.

title: Build the tooling that MEASURES duplication and gates it permanently
goal: E-09 One value, one name -- measure before collapsing, so the dedup campaign is driven by data rather than guesses.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-dup-report` runs and its committed TSV is refreshed by `mios-ssot-regen`, both new checks are green with negative tests, and the baseline key count is recorded.

details.what_how: (856) build `mios-dup-report` that groups the resolved env by VALUE, lists every value carried by >=2 keys, classifies each group {true-alias | distinct-configurable-fact | intentional-many-to-one} and emits a TSV; (857) a cross-surface literal scanner finding every version/ref/port/path/color/model literal in NON-SSOT files (docs, `mios.html`, `knowledge-graph.json`, SBOM, scripts) that equals an SSOT value; (858) extend `check_no_duplicate_value_key` beyond versions to all value classes with an explicit documented allowlist; (859) add `check_no_hardcoded_ssot_literal` (GUP Phase 4 enforcement); (860) enumerate every resolver rule (`get_aliases` plus the 3 emitters) that emits >=2 names for one dotted path, tabled with consumer counts -- the STRUCTURAL dupe source; (861) negative tests ratcheting check-77; (862) commit `value-dup-report.tsv` refreshed by `mios-ssot-regen` and gated; (863) the tracking doc with the measured baseline key count and target; (864) a referenced-but-empty audit deciding keep-vs-drop per key.
details.why: without a measurement the collapse is guesswork -- names get dropped that still have consumers, and new dupes reappear with nothing to catch them.

title: Create the `mios-build` orchestrator crate and expose a `miosd build` seam that wraps (not replaces) build.sh
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- gives every later phase port ONE stable compiled entrypoint so the strangler-fig migration has a facade to grow behind.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build --release` in `src/mios-rs` yields a miosd exposing `miosd build`; that command drives the existing 74-phase loop to the same exit code as `bash automation/build.sh`; `just drift-gate` stays green; no phase behavior changed.

title: Unify the two Rust workspaces so the Containerfile builds and ships EVERY native crate
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- makes native-first dispatch real: a binary that is referenced must actually exist in the image.
acceptance_criteria: Every native crate appears in a workspace `members` list; a clean `cargo build --release` builds them all with zero warnings; `mios-bake-plan`/`mios-ssot-lint`/`mios-aiplane-lint` land under `/usr/libexec/mios` in the image; the bake log shows 85-bake-plan.sh and 98-drift-checks.sh hitting the native binary, not the python fallback.

details.what_how: The Containerfile rust-builder stage only `COPY src/mios-rs` + `cargo build --release`, shipping just `/usr/libexec/mios/miosd`. Add the four orphan crates to `members`, then either fold `tools/native` into the `src/mios-rs` workspace or add a second `COPY tools/native` + `cargo build --release` stage installing the release binaries into `/usr/libexec/mios/`. Stage explicit paths only (never `git add -A`; AGY shares the tree).
details.where: `tools/native/Cargo.toml, src/mios-rs/Cargo.toml, Containerfile (rust-builder stage), automation/85-bake-plan.sh, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (lines 1539/4871 reference tools/native/target/release binaries)`

title: Record golden masters (trycmd + insta) of current build-phase output before any phase is ported
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the parity oracle that lets fragile untested bash be refactored without silently changing generated bytes.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-build` runs the golden suite; each snapshot matches the byte output of the corresponding current bash/python phase on the fixture; `cargo insta test` is green; a deliberately divergent port fails loudly with a diff.

Capture from the CURRENT bash/python phases so the recorded bytes are the oracle every port must reproduce. Commit fixtures + snapshots and document the `cargo insta review` accept flow.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/mios-build/tests/ (new), tests/fixtures/mios.toml (new golden input), automation/{34,35,42,43,75,76,85}-*.sh (sources of current output), usr/share/mios/mios.toml (real SSOT shape reference)`

title: Replace build.sh's grep-blob phase policy with a typed `[build.phases]` registry projected from SSOT
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- turns phase selection and fatality from substring matching into typed data every phase port routes through.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd build --plan` emits the same ordered phase list and fatal/non-fatal classification build.sh computes today (golden-diff); a substring collision (e.g. a second `35-` script) can no longer misclassify a phase; both repos carry the identical `[build.phases]` table.

details.what_how: build.sh gates phases with three fragile mechanisms: the `[0-9][0-9]-*.sh` glob (or `build_phases.json`), the `CONTAINERFILE_SCRIPTS` skip string, and the `NON_FATAL_SCRIPTS` blob — the last two matched by `grep -qF`, the exact ordinal/substring coupling flagged as TD-7. Define a typed `[build.phases]` table in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (ordinal, script, `fatal:bool`, `apply_class`), have `mios-build` deserialize it into a `Vec<Phase>` driving selection + fatal/non-fatal policy, and reduce build.sh to a thin shim that asks `miosd build --plan` for the ordered list. Keep the literal blobs as a `${...:-}` fallback until the registry is drift-gated equal. Mirror the table into mios-bootstrap per Law 15.
details.where: `automation/build.sh (lines 223-250 CONTAINERFILE_SCRIPTS/NON_FATAL_SCRIPTS, 258-275 selection loop), usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([build.phases] new), src/mios-rs/mios-build/, C:/mios-bootstrap mios.toml mirror`
details.why: A correctness-critical dispatch matched by substring means renaming a phase silently flips whether its failure aborts the build — a build that "succeeds" while a phase died.

title: Make the image build reproducible: derive SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the git commit and pass --rewrite-timestamp
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- reproducible bit-for-bit builds as the strongest provenance record behind the baked manifest.
acceptance_criteria: Two back-to-back local builds of the same commit produce byte-identical file timestamps in the layers; `MIOS_BUILT` equals the commit time; the build still passes `bootc container lint`.

details.what_how: The bake (`automation/build-mios.sh` → podman/buildah build over the Containerfile) sets no `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, so layer and file mtimes vary per build, and `automation/88-finalize.sh` bakes a wall-clock `MIOS_BUILT=$(date -u ...)` into `/usr/share/mios/version`. Compute the epoch deterministically from the `$ROOT` git tree commit time (`git -C $ROOT log -1 --format=%ct`) in build-mios.sh, pass `--source-date-epoch` + `--rewrite-timestamp` to the build, and thread the same epoch into 88-finalize.sh so `MIOS_BUILT` is the commit time. Key off the commit rather than wall-clock precisely because build.sh already does `git reset --hard HEAD` before drift-checks, making the commit the stable reference.
details.where: `automation/build-mios.sh (podman/buildah build invocation), automation/88-finalize.sh (MIOS_BUILT line 42), Containerfile, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (build job env)`
details.why: Wall-clock mtimes make every rebuild a different artifact, so no rebuild-and-compare gate can ever exist and "reproducible" stays an aspiration rather than a checkable claim.

title: Add a rebuild-and-compare-digest gate that fails when two builds of one commit diverge
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- converts reproducibility from a property that should hold into an enforced, continuously verified invariant.
acceptance_criteria: The gate rebuilds and compares; an intentionally injected wall-clock file makes it fail and names the offending path; a clean tree passes; the job is documented as scheduled to bound runner cost.

details.what_how: With the deterministic epoch landed, add a CI job (scheduled/manual trigger given runner cost) that builds the image twice from the same commit and asserts identical manifest digests — or, cheaper, compares a normalized `syft`/file-listing hash of the two rootfs. Wire it as a fitness function alongside the existing drift-gate ordering in `mios-ci.yml`. Emit a miette-style report naming the FIRST divergent path so a non-reproducible file (embedded hostname, build path, random ordering) is immediately actionable rather than a bare digest mismatch.
details.where: `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (new job after build), automation/build-mios.sh, src/mios-rs/mios-build/ (compare helper), automation/90-generate-sbom.sh (reuse syft output)`
details.why: Reproducibility silently rots — one new phase embedding a timestamp or hostname undoes task_1605 with nothing to notice.

title: Gate the bake on `cargo fmt --check` + `clippy -D warnings` across both Rust workspaces
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- gives the compiled plane the shellcheck-equivalent it never had, so Rust is trustworthy enough to subsume bash.
acceptance_criteria: CI fails on any unformatted file or clippy warning in either workspace; the restriction lints reject `unwrap`/`panic`/`todo` in shipped binaries; the gate runs in the drift-gate job ahead of the 17-minute bake.

details.what_how: The `mios-ci.yml` drift-gate job installs shellcheck but runs zero Rust quality gates, so the growing native surface (`miosd`, `tools/native/*`) has no style or lint enforcement. Add `cargo fmt --all --check` and `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` steps to the drift-gate job (which runs BEFORE `build`), for both the `src/mios-rs` and `tools/native` workspaces. Curate targeted restriction lints per crate root — `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::panic, clippy::todo)]` — to harden system verbs against panics, rather than blanket-enabling the whole restriction group.
details.where: `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (drift-gate job, after 'Install shellcheck' line 59), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (crate attrs), tools/native/*/src/main.rs`
details.why: Moving off bash buys nothing if the replacement panics at runtime on an unwrap; without the gate, the compiled tier is less checked than the shell it replaces.

title: Build a typed figment-based `mios-config` resolver crate deserializing mios.toml into structs
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the resolver core: ONE typed engine behind SSOT-operator-defined, replacing three parallel string-munging resolvers.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-config` deserializes the real `mios.toml` into typed structs; a malformed value yields a miette span diagnostic naming the line; the crate builds warning-clean and is unit-tested; all three legacy resolvers remain untouched and parallel in this task.

details.what_how: Collapse the three parallel resolvers — `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` (601 lines), the `tools/lib/userenv.sh` + `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` twins (325 lines each), and `automation/lib/globals.ps1` — into one `mios-config` crate using `figment` (defaults→TOML→env→CLI precedence) to deserialize `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` into typed structs (Ports, Colors, Sidecars, Services, Kargs, Compliance…). The struct IS the schema; deserialization fails loudly with miette diagnostics pointing at the offending line/span. The `MIOS_*` env projection becomes serialization FROM the typed model, feeding the zero-hardcodes campaign (ports/paths/colors stop being hand-parsed). Ship it as a library consumed by both `mios-build` and the future verb dispatcher; leave the shell/python resolvers live in parallel until parity is gated.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/mios-config/ (new crate), usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, tools/lib/userenv.sh, usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh, automation/lib/globals.ps1, usr/share/mios/mios.toml, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check_userenv_parity line 1757)`
details.why: Three hand-rolled resolvers over one file is TD-3's core: a wrong value silently breaks a Quadlet or a boot karg with no type error anywhere — and every projection downstream inherits the mis-parse.

title: Demote both userenv.sh twins to shims over `miosd resolve --shell` and PROVE parity with proptest
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- retires the hand-maintained shell resolver twins and mechanizes the Law-13 parity check into a differential proof.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd resolve --shell` output diffs identically against sourcing userenv.sh across the whole proptest corpus; both twins are shims with literal fallback; `check_userenv_parity` passes against the native emitter; both repos updated (Law 15).

details.what_how: Add `miosd resolve --shell` emitting `KEY=VAL` export lines from the `mios-config` typed model, then rewrite `tools/lib/userenv.sh` and `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` as thin shims doing `eval "$(miosd resolve --shell)"` with the current manual tuples retained as a `${...:-}` fallback. Prove byte-equivalence with a `proptest` differential test: generate random-but-valid `mios.toml` documents, feed BOTH the legacy shell resolver and `miosd resolve --shell`, and assert the emitted `MIOS_*` key set and values are identical, auto-shrinking to a minimal failing document. This also reconciles the short-vs-long key mismatch (`MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` emitted vs `MIOS_VLLM_*` consumed) recorded in the unified-key-library memo.
details.why: Two hand-maintained resolver copies with no generator binding them WILL diverge, and a spot-check cannot show they agree on inputs nobody thought to try.

title: Port 35-render-ports.sh (awk stack_id offset) to `miosd render-ports` behind a shim
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the first end-to-end proof of the strangler loop on a small leaf phase with tricky arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd render-ports` writes an `install.env` `MIOS_PORT_*` block byte-identical to the current awk on the fixture (including the stack_id offset and the 53 exclusion); 35-render-ports.sh is a shim; the golden test is green; the awk is deleted only after parity is confirmed.

details.what_how: `35-render-ports.sh` extracts `[ports]` from mios.toml with a hand-rolled awk block, applies the `stack_id*10000` offset to every numeric value EXCEPT literal 53, uppercases keys, and appends `MIOS_PORT_*` to `/etc/mios/install.env` after a `sed -i '/^MIOS_PORT_/d'`. Reimplement as `miosd render-ports` reading the typed Ports struct from `mios-config`, replicating the offset math and the port-53 carve-out exactly. Demote the bash to a shim calling the binary, keeping the awk as a `command -v miosd ||` fallback. Gate byte-parity of the emitted `install.env` block against the golden snapshot before deleting the awk.
details.why: The 53 carve-out is exactly the kind of detail a rewrite drops — proving it here validates the port/parity/demote loop before it is applied to riskier phases.

goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- kills the recurring quadlet-digest-drift class at its source by making Quadlet generation a compiled, diff-gated projection.

title: Finish the mios-bake-plan native cutover and DELETE the python fallback in 85-bake-plan.sh
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- proves the strangler's final "delete the legacy slice" step on a case that is already ported and already matching.
acceptance_criteria: 85-bake-plan.sh invokes only the native binary; `tools/generate-bake-plan.py` no longer exists; `mios-bake-plan --check` gates `plan.d` in CI; the bake log shows the native path; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-bake-plan` already implements the full generator with `--check` byte-parity (writes `plan.d/*.list`, `firstboot.list`, `bound-images.tsv`, validates core/firstboot membership). `85-bake-plan.sh` dispatches native-first, but the binary is not built in the bake (see the workspace-unify task), so it silently falls to `tools/generate-bake-plan.py`. Once the binary ships: add a parity CI step asserting `mios-bake-plan --check` == committed `plan.d`, remove the `elif ... python3 tools/generate-bake-plan.py` branch from 85-bake-plan.sh, and delete `tools/generate-bake-plan.py` (282 lines) with explicit-path staging. Wire `mios-bake-plan --check` into the drift gate as the plan.d gate.
details.why: Two generators for the bake plan means the one that actually runs is decided by build accident — and 282 lines of duplicate python keep drifting from the Rust that supposedly replaced them.

title: Port generate-cosign-policy.py + 49-cosign-policy.sh to `miosd cosign-policy` and pin the LEGACY sigstore attachment format
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- hardens the OS plane's highest-leverage boot-integrity control against the silent-verify-failure class.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd cosign-policy` emits a `policy.json` byte-identical to the python's and jq-clean; the policy uses `matchRepository` sigstoreSigned with the legacy attachment format documented and pinned; the `.py` is removed post-parity; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `49-cosign-policy.sh` installs cosign (v2.x-pinned), TUF roots and `policy.json`; `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py` (64 lines) generates the sigstoreSigned policy. Port policy generation to `miosd cosign-policy` over a typed `[security.cosign]` model emitting the same jq-parse-clean `policy.json`. While there, close the two boot-integrity gaps from the research: target the LEGACY sigstore attachment format (cosign v3's new bundle format is undiscoverable by containers-image/rpm-ostree, giving a silent upgrade-verify failure), and keep enforcement in the on-disk `policy.json` because `bootc upgrade` has no `--enforce-container-sigpolicy`. Demote the `.py` behind the binary, keep the cosign-install bash as a thin shim, golden-diff `policy.json`.
details.why: If the signature format silently stops being discoverable, `bootc upgrade` verifies nothing while appearing to succeed — the whole signed-image chain becomes decorative.

title: Port the hardening service-enable family (51-hardening.sh + siblings) to `miosd harden` over an SSOT unit roster
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- makes the security-critical enabled-unit set typed SSOT data rather than ln-loops scattered across four phases.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd harden` creates the identical `.wants` symlink set and config permissions as the current bash on a fixture rootfs; the enabled-unit list lives in SSOT; 51-hardening.sh is a shim delegating external-tool calls; the golden test is green.

details.what_how: `51-hardening.sh` symlinks usbguard/auditd/fapolicyd into `multi-user.target.wants`, chmods the usbguard/fapolicyd configs, runs `fagenrules`/`fapolicyd-cli`, and materializes `clevis-luks.env` via `mios-clevis-luks-gen`. Sibling phases (38-selinux, 40-fapolicyd-trust, 78-greenboot) repeat the same "if unit exists, `ln -sf` into `.wants`" pattern. Reimplement the service-enable plus config-permission logic as `miosd harden` driven by a typed `[security.enable_units]`/privileged roster in SSOT, so the enabled set is data. Preserve degrade-open (missing unit → skip). Demote 51 to a shim that still invokes the genuinely-external tool calls (fagenrules, clevis); golden-diff the created symlink set.
details.why: A security service that quietly fails to be enabled — because its `ln -sf` sits in a phase nobody diffs — ships an image that only looks hardened.

goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- removes TD-3's hand-rolled-parsing risk from the code path that decides what actually gets installed.

title: Replace 88-finalize.sh's os-release `sed` loop with a typed `miosd finalize-osrelease` version projector
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one compiled owner of the single-source version projection, so the OS identity fields stop being a hand-written sed list.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd finalize-osrelease` rewrites all seven os-release fields and writes the version file identically to the sed block on a fixture os-release, drift-check 42 passes, the systemctl calls remain shell, and the golden test is green.

details.what_how: 88-finalize.sh currently re-projects the one SSOT version onto every version-bearing field of `/usr/lib/os-release` (VERSION, VERSION_ID, BUILD_ID, IMAGE_VERSION, OSTREE_VERSION, PRETTY_NAME, CPE_NAME) with `sed -i` (lines 46-59) and writes `/usr/share/mios/version` (lines 39-44). Move that rewrite into a `miosd finalize-osrelease` subcommand that takes the version from the typed config model / VERSION file so the field list is code, not a sed loop; drift-check 42 keeps os-release equal to SSOT. Leave `systemctl preset-all` / `set-default` in shell. Demote the sed block to a shim call and golden-diff the produced os-release against the fixture.
details.where: `automation/88-finalize.sh (lines 46-59 os-release sed, 39-44 version file), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (finalize-osrelease), usr/lib/os-release, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check 42)`
details.why: Today the OS identity fields are re-derived by a fragile sed loop; a missed or mis-anchored pattern silently ships an image whose os-release disagrees with SSOT, and the version-unification (TD-2) work has no compiled field list to build on.

title: Port the firstboot-token bound-images binding from 01-system-files-overlay.sh into `miosd overlay-bind-images`
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image, and can a stock runner hold it -- keep the multi-GB firstboot whales out of bootc's deploy-time pull so offline USB deploy stays viable.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd overlay-bind-images` produces an identical `bound-images.d` symlink set on a fixture (firstboot whales excluded, `.gitkeep` stripped, symlinks only), the tar stages remain shell, degrade-open still holds, and the golden test is green.

details.what_how: `automation/01-system-files-overlay.sh` (270 lines) symlinks every Quadlet into `/usr/lib/bootc/bound-images.d` EXCEPT those whose `Image=` substring-matches a `firstboot_tokens` entry (the GPU whales, ~47GB, deliberately evicted from the bake). It parses tokens with `grep|sed` and does the `Image=` match with sed+glob loops, then strips `.gitkeep`. Port ONLY that binding block (lines 184-227) to a `miosd overlay-bind-images` subcommand driven by the typed firstboot-token list, reusing `mios-bake-plan`'s existing `is_firstboot`/token logic rather than adding a second parser; leave the tar overlay stages in shell. Preserve degrade-open (unreadable tokens -> bind everything) and the symlinks-only invariant (`bootc install` rejects a regular file there). Golden-diff the created symlink set against a fixture Quadlet dir.
details.where: `automation/01-system-files-overlay.sh (LBI block lines 184-227), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (overlay-bind-images), tools/native/mios-bake-plan/src/main.rs (is_firstboot reuse), usr/lib/bootc/bound-images.d/`
details.why: A single mis-matched substring binds a firstboot whale and makes bootc pull ~47GB at install time, which breaks offline USB deploy outright — high-consequence matching logic currently living in a duplicate `grep|sed` parser that can drift from `mios-bake-plan`'s.

title: Port 90-generate-sbom.sh to `miosd sbom` and publish the SBOM as a signed cosign attestation
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- promote the SBOM from an in-tree file to verifiable OCI provenance attached to the published digest.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd sbom` reproduces the same CycloneDX + SPDX artifacts and still exits 0 with syft or egress missing, CI attaches the SBOM as a cosign attestation on the image digest, and `cosign verify-attestation --type spdx` succeeds against a published image.

details.what_how: `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` is degrade-open (it never fails the build) and drives syft to emit CycloneDX + SPDX into `/usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom`. Port the orchestration — syft-present check, SSOT-pinned version resolution, exclude globs, version labeling — into a `miosd sbom` subcommand that always exits 0, keeping syft itself as the external scanner the binary invokes. Then extend the publish leg with `cosign attest --type spdx` / `--type cyclonedx` against the pushed image digest, next to the existing keyless-sign step (mios-ci.yml ~line 451), so downstream bootc hosts and scanners can `cosign verify-attestation` instead of reading a file inside the image. Demote the .sh to a shim; the SBOM bytes stay identical.
details.where: `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh, src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (sbom), .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (cosign attest step near the keyless-sign step line 451), usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/`
details.why: An SBOM that only exists inside the image proves nothing to a consumer verifying the pulled ref; without an attestation the ADR-0003 provenance loop stays open and no puller can check what they actually received.

title: Give greenboot real required.d health-checks (Hermes /v1 + core Quadlets) backed by `miosd healthcheck`
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- make boot-counted rollback actually detect a broken update instead of rubber-stamping it.
acceptance_criteria: `required.d` contains a Hermes + core-Quadlet health-check backed by `miosd healthcheck`, a simulated Hermes-down marks the boot red and exercises the rollback path in a unit test or harness, 78-greenboot.sh stays thin enable/chmod, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `automation/78-greenboot.sh` only symlinks greenboot units and chmods scripts under `/etc/greenboot/check/{required,wanted}.d` — the checks themselves are minimal, so a signed-but-broken publish rolls a fleet forward with no auto-recovery. Author real `required.d` checks asserting the MiOS SLAs: the canonical Hermes endpoint responds on `/v1` (degrade-open via `${MIOS_PORT_HERMES:-8642}`, per the AI-endpoint canon), core Quadlets are active, and drift-critical services are up. Implement the check logic as a compiled `miosd healthcheck` that the greenboot script calls, so it is typed and unit-testable, keeping 78-greenboot.sh as thin enable/chmod shell. Note the greenboot-rs (F43) migration in a comment for the follow-on.
details.where: `automation/78-greenboot.sh, /etc/greenboot/check/required.d/ (new checks), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (healthcheck), usr/share/mios/mios.toml (canonical ports for the SLA set)`
details.why: Hollow greenboot checks defeat the entire boot-counted rollback promise: signing, UKI and composefs are worthless if a broken update boots "green" and the fleet has no way back.

title: Port the oscap severity gate (86-oscap-compliance.sh + mios-oscap-gate) into one `miosd compliance-gate`
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- collapse an inline-python config read plus a separate python verdict gate into a single typed compliance path.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd compliance-gate` reproduces the disabled no-op and, on a fixture ARF, the same at/above-severity verdict as mios-oscap-gate, the datastream resolution matches, 86 is a thin shim invoking oscap plus the binary, and the golden tests are green.

details.what_how: `automation/86-oscap-compliance.sh` reads `[compliance]` through an inline `python3` tomllib helper (`_toml_get`, lines 22-38), locates the SSG datastream from the scap-security-guide RPM, runs `oscap xccdf eval`, then hands the verdict to `usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscap-gate`, which counts FAILED rules at or above a severity. Port the config read, datastream resolution and verdict orchestration into `miosd compliance-gate` over the typed `[compliance]` struct, keeping `oscap` itself as the external scanner; preserve DEFAULT-OFF degrade-open (`enabled != true` -> exit 0) and fail-closed once opted in. Fold the mios-oscap-gate ARF parsing into the binary. Golden-test both the disabled no-op and a fixture-ARF verdict.
details.why: Compliance posture is currently decided by an inline python tomllib blob in a shell phase plus a second python parser — two fragile pieces that can disagree about whether a build is compliant, and neither is testable without a full oscap run.
