title: Declare a `[build.phases].deps` DAG in SSOT and run independent phases concurrently in `mios-build`
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- let the compiled orchestrator own ordering and concurrency, which is the concrete payoff of moving build policy out of bash.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd build` runs the independent bake-builder phases concurrently, a fixture build's rootfs and phase logs match the sequential golden, fatal/non-fatal policy is honored from the registry, and wall time on the bake-builder band drops measurably.

details.what_how: `automation/build.sh` runs every phase strictly sequentially by ordinal, yet the bake builders 65-bake-hyprland, 66-bake-quickshell, 67-bake-surfer, 68-bake-kvmfr and 69-bake-lookingglass-client have no interdependencies and dominate wall time. Add a `deps` field to the `[build.phases]` registry in mios.toml, build the DAG in `mios-build`, and execute independent phases on a bounded worker pool while keeping log output deterministic (buffer per-phase output, flush in ordinal order) so the golden phase-output snapshots still hold. Take fatal/non-fatal policy from the registry, and gate correctness by asserting the resulting rootfs is identical to a sequential build over a fixture subset. Mirror the SSOT change into the C:/mios-bootstrap tree.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([build.phases].deps), src/mios-rs/mios-build/ (DAG scheduler), automation/build.sh (delegates ordering to miosd), automation/{65,66,67,68,69}-*.sh (independent leaves), C:/mios-bootstrap mirror`
details.why: Every build pays the full serial cost of the five heaviest GPU/UI builders, and the ordering rules that would allow otherwise live nowhere a machine can read them — so the build stays slow and phase order stays an implicit property of filenames.

title: Move build.sh's ASCII progress UI into `mios-build` and report phase failures as miette diagnostics
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one typed console/diagnostic surface for the orchestrator instead of duplicated framing math and an opaque failure blob.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd build` renders the framed progress UI byte-compatible with today's build.sh output under snapshot test, a phase failure prints a miette diagnostic carrying phase name and step-log path, library errors are thiserror enums, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: build.sh carries roughly 150 lines of hand-rolled ASCII framing (`_pad`, `_hline`, `_row`, `_progress_bar`, `_step_header`, `_step_result`, `_fail_report`, `_warn_report`, `_final_summary`, lines 32-178). Move the console UI into a `mios-build` ui module so progress renders in one place, and adopt `miette` for phase failures: a failing phase returns a `miette::Result` whose diagnostic names the phase, the exit code and the step-log path with help text. Use `thiserror` enums for internal errors so the drift-gates can match on variants. Preserve the exact framed output operators read today behind a compatibility snapshot test.
details.where: `automation/build.sh (UI helpers lines 32-178, fail/warn reports 135-163), src/mios-rs/mios-build/ (ui module), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (miette::Result main), src/mios-rs/mios-build/tests/ (UI format snapshot)`
details.why: A failing build currently emits a grep-assembled FAILURE LOG that names no log path and no cause, so every failure costs an operator a manual hunt — and the framing math is duplicated across nine shell helpers that drift from the real output.

title: Replace build.sh's git-reset + reproject dance with `miosd drift --prepare` keyed on $ROOT/$CTX
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- remove the incomplete-tree false-drift class that repeatedly reddens the gate during the OCI bake.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd drift --prepare` reprojects the three gitignored SSOT files unconditionally from mios.toml, drift-checks 92/93/95 pass in both the incomplete-tree bake and the pristine-checkout CI job, build.sh invokes it as a single step, and nothing depends on `git reset` succeeding.

details.what_how: Before running 98-drift-checks, build.sh performs a delicate sequence (lines 440-473): `git config safe.directory`, `git reset --hard HEAD`, then an UNCONDITIONAL re-projection of three gitignored SSOT files via `tools/generate-ipa-enroll-env.py`, `tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py` and `tools/generate-cockpit-conf.py` — unconditional because inside the OCI bake the copied `.git` is an INCOMPLETE work tree where `git rev-parse`/`reset` are unreliable, and gating the reproject on git left checks 92/93/95 failing the bake. Port this pre-drift orchestration into `miosd drift --prepare`, keying off `$ROOT`/`$CTX` (the inverse-polarity fix) rather than git state, and reproject the three files deterministically from mios.toml. build.sh calls it as one thin step; once the native render-uki-cmdline / cockpit / ipa generators exist, call those directly.
details.why: This exact sequence is a documented, recurring bake failure: when git misbehaves in the incomplete work tree the projections are stale and the gate reports drift that does not exist, burning full bake cycles on a phantom.

title: Land the shared thiserror/miette error model with mios.toml span diagnostics before the phase ports
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one error surface every ported phase inherits, so the compiled tier is a UX upgrade over bash rather than a lateral move.
acceptance_criteria: mios-config and mios-build expose thiserror enums wrapped by miette, a malformed mios.toml value produces a diagnostic highlighting the exact line/span with help text, miosd's main returns `miette::Result`, unit tests assert the diagnostic against a bad fixture, and builds are warning-clean.

details.what_how: Define `thiserror` enums in `mios-config` and `mios-build` for the internal/library layer (parse error, missing key, type mismatch) and wrap them into `miette` diagnostics at the CLI boundary, so a bad `[colors]`, port or karg value in mios.toml is reported AT its line/span with actionable help — computing spans from byte offsets, not char counts, so UTF-8 content points at the right place. Return `miette::Result` from miosd's `main`. This is the natural error surface for the figment resolver and gives the drift-gates programmatically-matchable variants instead of string matching. Land it EARLY so subsequent phase ports inherit it rather than each inventing ad-hoc error strings.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/mios-config/src/ (error module), src/mios-rs/mios-build/src/ (error module), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs (miette::Result), usr/share/mios/mios.toml (the source spans point into)`
details.why: Every port that lands before this invents its own error strings, and retrofitting a shared model across a dozen crates later costs far more than defining it once — meanwhile operators keep getting bash-grade opaque messages from compiled code.

title: Port 99-postcheck.sh's 19 build-abort invariants to a native `miosd postcheck` fitness-function suite
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- move the last line of defense that aborts insecure images into typed, testable code keyed to the `[laws]` numbering SSOT.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd postcheck` reproduces all 19 checks with byte-identical pass/fail output against golden fixtures, 99-postcheck.sh is under 15 lines, a deliberately-broken invariant still aborts the build, and `cargo test` plus `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: `automation/99-postcheck.sh` (810 lines) runs the 19 numbered build-time invariants that ABORT the bake: OpenSSH >= 9.6 (#1), Cockpit posture (#2/#6), karg schema (#3), NVIDIA-toolkit version (#5), WSL2 wsl.conf parity (#7), sysusers fixed-UID (#8, via `_sysusers_effective`/`_gid_in_etc_group`), tmpfiles no-`/var/run` (#9), `systemd-analyze verify` (#10), `systemd-tmpfiles --dry-run` (#11), Law 5 UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS (#12), Law 6 UNPRIVILEGED-QUADLETS (#13), Law 3 BOUND-IMAGES (#14), the task_39 benchmark (#15), Law 10 BARE-SAFE-ENV (#16), Law 11 SECRETS-NEVER-IN-ENV (#17), BOUND-IMAGES-RESOLVE (#18). Re-implement each as a typed check under a `miosd postcheck` subcommand returning miette diagnostics, keyed to the same `[laws]` numbering, and reduce 99-postcheck.sh to a thin shim that execs it (keeping degrade-open only where the original had it). Prove byte-parity of the emitted `mios_ok`/`die` lines against golden captures BEFORE deleting any bash check body.
details.why: This is the largest untargeted build phase and the only thing standing between a broken invariant and a published insecure image; leaving 810 lines of bash as the final gate while everything around it hardens is the biggest coverage hole in the domain.

title: Collapse the Law checks duplicated across 99-postcheck and 98-drift-checks into one native mios-laws module

title: Build a record/replay host-tool sandbox (podman, semanage, nvidia-ctk, systemd-analyze) so phases are characterizable offline
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- supply the hermetic seam that makes byte-parity provable before any security-sensitive shell script is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: a recorded fixture set exists for the host tools each ported phase invokes, `cargo test` runs all phase characterization tests offline on both Windows and Linux runners with no podman/semanage present, and a replay mismatch fails the test.

details.what_how: Most phases shell out to host tools that cannot run in CI or on Windows: 38-selinux calls `restorecon`/`semanage import`, 25-26 call `nvidia-ctk`, 99-postcheck calls `systemd-analyze verify`, `systemd-tmpfiles --dry-run` and `sshd -V`, and the bakes call podman. The golden-capture harness records phase OUTPUT but cannot re-run these hermetically. Build a native record/replay shim layer — a PATH-shadow directory of recording wrappers plus a fixtures store — that captures every external invocation and response during one real build and replays them deterministically, so ported miosd subcommands can be exercised under `cargo test` with zero host dependencies. Wire it into the existing trycmd/insta harness.
details.why: Without a hermetic host-tool seam, the golden harness cannot verify parity for exactly the phases that touch SELinux, GPU CDI, systemd and podman — so the most security-sensitive strangler-fig cutovers are blocked or would have to land unverified.

title: Establish the strangler-fig control plane: a per-phase MIOS_NATIVE toggle plus a cutover-order ADR
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- make the native/bash cutover reversible per phase so the port lands incrementally instead of as a big bang.
acceptance_criteria: `MIOS_NATIVE=1` in CI runs every already-ported phase natively while `0` runs bash, both producing byte-identical images, the ADR and tracking table exist in both repos, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: build.sh enumerates phases via a `[0-9][0-9]-*.sh` glob plus a hand-ordered list and `CONTAINERFILE_SCRIPTS` special cases (L223+), and there is no way to run native and bash side by side during the multi-phase port. Add one control surface: each shimmed phase checks `${MIOS_NATIVE_<PHASE>:-${MIOS_NATIVE:-0}}` and either execs the miosd subcommand or runs the legacy bash body, using the standard `${VAR:-LIT}` degrade pattern. Ship ADR-0013 declaring the dependency order (error model -> config resolver -> shared libs -> host-tool sandbox -> renderers -> postcheck -> orchestrator) plus a ROADMAP tracking table, landed in both mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: Dozens of queued phase-port tasks have no agreed order and no A/B switch, so any single port that regresses the image can only be diagnosed by reverting the commit — and without the ADR the ports will land in an order that breaks their own dependencies.

title: Pin and checksum the network-fetch bakes (66-quickshell, 68-kvmfr, 69-lookingglass, 73-model-prep) through `miosd fetch-verify`
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- close the four unpinned upstream fetches that make the image non-reproducible and the digest-compare gate unusable.
acceptance_criteria: each bake fetches a pinned ref and verifies a recorded checksum, a tampered or moved source fails the build, two independent builds fetch identical bytes, the SBOM records the resolved refs, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: These bakes pull live sources at build time: `66-bake-quickshell.sh` does `git clone ${MIOS_URL_QUICKSHELL:-...}` plus cmake, `68-bake-kvmfr.sh` and `69-bake-lookingglass-client.sh` git-clone plus cmake/make, and `73-model-prep.sh` `curl -fL`s a HuggingFace resolve GGUF. None pins a commit or tag and none verifies a checksum. Add a `miosd fetch-verify` helper that resolves each source URL to a pinned ref/commit and validates a SHA — recorded in the SBOM per ADR-0003, never hand-pinned in SSOT — failing closed on mismatch, and route all four bakes through it while keeping the `${URL:-LIT}` fallbacks.
details.why: Four phases clone or curl a moving upstream with no verification, so today's image cannot be rebuilt to the same bytes and a compromised upstream would be baked in silently — the rebuild-and-compare-digest gate can never pass until this is fixed.

title: Make the 72-hermes-agent shared Python venv reproducible with hash-locked, fully-offline wheels
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- close the largest unpinned dependency surface in the bake and honor Law 12 BAKE-NOT-FETCH.
acceptance_criteria: the venv installs only from vendored wheels with `--require-hashes` and no network access, two builds produce an identical package set recorded in the SBOM, the venv contents are digest-stable, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `automation/72-hermes-agent.sh` (684 lines) builds the shared agent venv at `/usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv` (Hermes, opencode) via pip — a large, network-dependent, unpinned install that brushes Law 12. Convert it to a hash-locked, fully offline install: generate a pinned `requirements.lock` used with `--require-hashes` against vendored wheels under `usr/share/mios/vendored/`, and have a miosd verb (or the mios-build orchestrator) drive the deterministic install and record the resolved package set into the SBOM. Keep phase 72 thin around the locked install.
details.why: An unpinned pip resolve means the AI plane's dependency set differs between any two builds and a compromised PyPI package lands with no signal — it is simultaneously the biggest reproducibility hole and the biggest supply-chain hole in the bake.

title: Finish the 97-ssot-lint cutover to the existing mios-ssot-lint crate and ship it from the Containerfile
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- retire a bash validator whose native replacement already exists but is never built or run.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-ssot-lint` produces byte-identical findings against the 97-ssot-lint.sh golden, the Containerfile builds and ships the crate, 97-ssot-lint.sh is a shim, and `cargo test` plus the drift-gate are green.

title: Route build-mios.ps1 through a cross-compiled `miosd resolve` and stop dot-sourcing globals.ps1
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- collapse the third hand-maintained resolver so Windows and Linux builds read values from one native implementation.
acceptance_criteria: build-mios.ps1 obtains all MIOS_* values from the native binary on Windows with output matching today's globals.ps1 values, CI produces a cross-compiled miosd artifact, twin-equivalence stays green through the transition, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/globals.ps1` (220 lines, `Resolve-MiosVersion` plus the MIOS_* constant registry) is the THIRD resolver — a hand-maintained PowerShell twin of globals.sh/userenv.sh held in sync only by the twin-equivalence drift-check. Once `miosd resolve --shell` exists, cross-compile miosd for `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and have `build-mios.ps1` source its variables from `miosd resolve --format ps` (or JSON) instead of dot-sourcing globals.ps1. Keep globals.ps1 as a fallback that the drift-check continues to pin until parity is proven, and produce the cross-compiled artifact in CI.
details.why: The shell-shim work leaves the PowerShell twin standing, so every new SSOT key must still be hand-added in a third place; until Windows runs the same binary, the parallel-resolver duplication is only two-thirds solved.

title: Build miosd as a static musl binary so one artifact runs at build, in-image, and in the firstboot-tier
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one immutable image whose compiled tools are context-independent, so the same binary serves the builder, the runtime and the stripped firstboot-tier.
acceptance_criteria: `ldd /usr/libexec/mios/miosd` reports "not a dynamic executable"; the binary executes on the base image and in a distroless/firstboot context; image size does not regress; `cargo test` and `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: The Containerfile currently builds miosd under `FROM docker.io/library/rust:slim` (glibc) and copies `/miosd` into `/usr/libexec/mios/miosd`, which couples the binary to the builder's libc. Retarget the rust-builder stage at `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`, pin a rustls/no-openssl feature set in `src/mios-rs/Cargo.toml` so nothing links OpenSSL, and add the musl target install + `--target` flag to the builder stage and to the CI job that compiles it.
details.why: miosd is becoming the executor for postcheck and the renderers while the firstboot-tier deliberately evicts the vLLM/SGLang whales; a glibc-dynamic binary can fail to load in exactly that shrunk tier, and cannot be reused as a host build tool on any other base.

title: Build mios-toml-core: one figment-based typed layered mios.toml resolver crate with a --shell emitter
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the compiled resolver core that makes SSOT-operator-defined a single typed engine instead of three hand-synced twins.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-toml-core --shell` diffs byte-identical against `source tools/lib/userenv.sh && env | grep ^MIOS_ | sort` for the vendor SSOT; a malformed value yields a miette diagnostic with the correct byte-span; `cargo test` green; the crate is a workspace member.

details.what_how: Create lib+bin crate `tools/native/mios-toml-core` that deserializes the vendor < host < user mios.toml overlay (the exact layering `tools/lib/userenv.sh` and `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` implement) into typed structs via figment (Toml + Env providers with defined precedence), with miette/thiserror diagnostics pointing AT the offending line/span for a bad `[colors]`/`[ports]` value. Expose `mios-toml-core --shell` emitting the exact sorted `MIOS_*` KEY=value projection userenv.sh produces — canonical `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` long form plus the short `MIOS_VLLM_*` aliases consumers actually read — so it drops in behind the existing shell seam. Keep userenv.sh as a strangler-façade fallback until byte-parity is drift-gated; type the canonical ports in `[security.nohc_allowlist]` so the zero-hardcodes campaign has a schema to lint against.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-toml-core/ (new), tools/native/Cargo.toml, tools/lib/userenv.sh + usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh (kept as fallback), usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py (kept as fallback)`
details.why: Three parallel resolvers (mios_toml.py, the userenv.sh twins, globals.ps1) held together only by twin-equivalence testing is the duplication the operator flagged; every divergence between them silently mints wrong values into Quadlets and install.env.

title: Stand up the golden-master parity harness (trycmd + insta) that every libexec port must pass
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the characterization safety net that makes strangler-fig deletion of a bash tool provably safe.

Wire `cargo test -p langx-golden` and a `just golden-capture` / `just golden-verify` pair so every later port asserts byte-for-byte equivalence against the captured legacy output. details.why: The 144 libexec bash tools have no unit tests at all; without recorded golden output, every port is an unverifiable rewrite and the first regression ships silently into a bootc image that fleets pull.

title: Add a proptest differential oracle proving mios-toml-core == userenv.sh over random mios.toml
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the proptest differential oracle that mechanizes the Global-Unification-Plan lossless-diff invariant.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-toml-core` runs >=1000 proptest cases with zero key/value divergence vs userenv.sh; a seeded intentional bug (drop one short alias) shrinks to a minimal reproducing mios.toml; the suite runs in CI before the main drift gate.

details.what_how: Add a proptest suite under `tools/native/mios-toml-core/tests/` that generates random-but-valid mios.toml documents (varying `[ports].*`, `[colors].*`, `[ai].*`, `[pgvector].*`, and section presence/absence), feeds each to BOTH the legacy resolver (`source tools/lib/userenv.sh`) and `mios-toml-core --shell`, and asserts the emitted `MIOS_*` key SET and every value are identical, auto-shrinking to a minimal failing document on divergence. Treat the bash resolver as the oracle for the duration of the migration; promote any divergence found into a fixture in the golden harness. This is also where the short-vs-long alias reconciliation (`MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` vs `MIOS_VLLM_*`) is proven rather than asserted.
details.why: Example-based tests miss the edge-case value divergences that matter — one wrong resolved value silently breaks a Quadlet, which is precisely the recurring SSOT-projection drift class the gate keeps catching after the fact.

title: Add cargo fmt/clippy -Dwarnings plus cargo-deny/cargo-audit as native quality drift-gates
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the shellcheck-equivalent the Rust plane never had, plus a supply-chain story for the compiled tier.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` and `cargo deny check` pass on the repo; both new checks appear in the generated gate index and fail on an injected `unwrap()`/`panic!` or a banned-license crate; the negatives-before-main ordering is preserved.

details.what_how: Add `check_native_lint` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` running `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` (RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings) with curated restriction lints — `clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::panic`, `clippy::todo` denied in system verbs — and `check_native_supplychain` running cargo-deny (license allow-list, banned/duplicate crates, advisories) and cargo-audit against the committed `tools/native/Cargo.lock`. Place both AFTER the negatives job and BEFORE the main gate, mirroring the existing NO-HARDCODE / pod-quadlets ordering, and degrade-open when cargo is absent. Author `tools/native/deny.toml` with the FOSS-aligned license allow-list; if a law row is added, register it in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [laws]`.
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check_native_lint + check_native_supplychain), tools/native/deny.toml (new), usr/share/mios/mios.toml [laws] numbering if a law row is added`
details.why: The tech-debt map records that MiOS has no shellcheck CI at all; as code moves to Rust, a panic or an unvetted transitive dependency would ship into the image with nothing checking it, and `Cargo.lock` would be a reproducibility SSOT nobody audits.

title: Add a monotonic bash-tool ratchet drift-check over usr/libexec/mios
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- turn "minimize loose scripts" into an enforced fitness function that can only move one direction.
acceptance_criteria: the check prints live count vs ceiling and passes at baseline; adding one new bash tool under `usr/libexec/mios` makes it fail; each later port lowers the ceiling by one with the gate staying green; per Law 15 the SSOT key is mirrored in mios-bootstrap.git if that repo carries the surface.

details.what_how: Add `check_libexec_bash_ratchet` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` counting executables under `usr/libexec/mios` whose shebang is bash/sh (145 at measurement) and failing if the count EXCEEDS a ceiling recorded in a new `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [langx].libexec_bash_ceiling` key. Print the live count and remaining budget, degrade-open when git/awk is unavailable, and follow the soft->hard ratchet convention already used by `check_hint_coverage`. Seed the ceiling at the measured baseline; each port task's PR decrements it by one. Regenerate the gate index via `tools/generate-gate-index.py`.
details.why: Without a ratchet, the campaign is reversible by accident: a single new hand-written bash tool erases a port's progress with nothing flagging it, and the 145-script surface never provably shrinks.

title: Build mios-verb-dispatcher to replace the eval-bearing verb routing seam
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the strangler seam where the verb NAME is the stable façade and compiled ports slot in behind it unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: every verb in KNOWN_VERBS resolves through mios-verb-dispatcher to the identical exec target (golden snapshot passes); a fuzzed or hostile arg cannot reach `eval` or an unlisted command; `mios build`, `mios theme` and `mios sync-env` behave byte-identically; `cargo test` green.

details.what_how: Author a Rust `mios-verb-dispatcher` binary implementing a hardened dispatch table (assoc-array/case equivalent, no string-built commands) covering the verbs routed by the `KNOWN_VERBS` dict in `usr/bin/mios` and the `mios()` shell function in `etc/profile.d/mios-verbs.sh` — build, dash, config, theme, sync-env, env, vfio, tune and the rest. Route BOTH callers through the one binary so old and new coexist; agent-supplied args become an explicit allowlisted verb lookup, structurally removing the 9 eval-on-agent-args sites the tech-debt map flags. Keep the existing Python/shell dispatch as fallback until a golden snapshot of `mios help` plus each verb's exec target proves the two tables identical.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-verb-dispatcher/ (new), usr/bin/mios (KNOWN_VERBS -> delegate), etc/profile.d/mios-verbs.sh (route through binary), tools/native/Cargo.toml`
details.why: Verb arguments arrive from an untrusted agent boundary and today reach `eval` in nine places — a command-injection surface sitting in the OS's primary CLI, and the one seam that must be stable before any verb body can be ported.

title: Add the [migration] SSOT toggle for oxidizr-style per-verb Rust/bash opt-out and rollback
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- rollback as a first-class deliverable so adopting a compiled verb never risks the bake.

details.why: Without a per-verb switch, every port is an all-or-nothing commit: a regression discovered after the bake requires reverting and rebuilding the whole image instead of changing one SSOT value.

title: Port mios-resolve-latest to a Rust OCI-digest + SBOM recorder that reads refs from SSOT
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- digest capture becomes build-resolved provenance instead of an in-code ref list plus a fallback literal.

details.what_how: Reimplement `usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolve-latest` — `resolve_ref` shelling to skopeo/podman for `{{.Digest}}` on the floating `:latest` refs, then dedup-appending `ref,tag,digest,container_image,date` to `MiOS-SBOM.csv` — as a Rust binary that reads the ref list FROM the SSOT (`[image.sidecars]` / plan.d) rather than the hardcoded refs array in the bash, shelling out only for the network step. Demote the bash to a shim and prove the appended CSV line byte-identical via the golden harness against a mocked digest.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolve-latest (-> shim), tools/native/ (new crate or mios-bake-plan subcommand), MiOS-SBOM.csv (output), usr/share/mios/mios.toml (ref source)`
details.why: The bash hardcodes both the sidecar ref list and a fallback sha256 literal, so adding a sidecar to SSOT silently fails to appear in the SBOM and a stale pinned digest can be recorded as provenance.

title: Port mios-sync-theme to a native theme-surface renderer driven by mios-toml-core
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- theme surfaces born FROM `[colors]` SSOT by a compiled renderer rather than an embedded python heredoc.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust renderer writes byte-identical `theme.json` + `mios-theme.css` versus the bash for the vendor palette; `--check` prints without writing; drift-check 25 (theme SSOT projection) is green; golden test green.

details.what_how: Reimplement `usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme` — the embedded python heredoc that reads `[colors]`, `[theme]` and `[theme.font]` through mios_toml, resolves the `_SEMANTIC` palette, and writes `/etc/mios/theme/theme.json` plus `mios-theme.css` — as a Rust renderer driven by mios-toml-core, keeping the `--check` dry-run and the optional `--apply-home` hand-off. Codegen the CSS and JSON deterministically from the typed palette so no surface is hand-authored twice. Leave the downstream `mios-theme-render` / `mios-dotfiles-render` / `mios-generate-icons` chaining shelled out for now; demote only the resolver body, and prove both outputs byte-identical via the golden harness.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme (-> shim), tools/native/ (theme subcommand of mios-toml-core or a new crate), /etc/mios/theme/ (outputs), usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sync-theme.service`
details.why: An embedded python heredoc inside a bash tool is untestable and unlintable, and it is the single point where every theme surface is derived — a silent divergence there puts drift-check 25 red across the whole desktop.

title: Port the greenboot AI-plane required health check to a static Rust binary
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- greenboot health coverage that is memory-safe and cannot false-fail a fleet into rollback.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust check returns the identical exit code to the bash for the all-up, one-down, unit-disabled and port-unresolved fixtures; a non-zero exit still triggers greenboot rollback; the golden trycmd fixtures are green.

details.what_how: Reimplement `usr/lib/greenboot/check/required.d/40-mios-ai-plane.sh` — `check_service` with the `systemctl is-enabled` guard, `_tcp_up` via bounded connect, `_http_up` treating <500 as up, ports read from `/etc/mios/install.env` (`MIOS_PORT_AGENT_PIPE`, `LLM_LIGHT`, `PGVECTOR`), and skip-not-guess on an unresolved port — as a small static Rust binary that takes ports from mios-toml-core and probes mios-agent-pipe, mios-llm-light and mios-pgvector. Preserve the degrade-open and bounded-retry semantics EXACTLY: a config-bridge glitch must never roll the OS back. Demote the `.sh` to a shim exec-ing the binary.
details.why: This check decides whether a freshly-upgraded host keeps its new image or rolls back; a shell probe that mis-parses an unresolved port can roll an entire fleet back on a false negative, and greenboot itself is moving to Rust for bootc.

goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- one audited health-check crate so every critical service has a real check and a rollback path.

goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- remove the string-spliced SQL injection surface from the OS's database CLI.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust `mios-db` produces identical stdout and exit codes for `--config get/set/show`, `--owui`, `--embed` and the no-flag error versus the bash on fixtures; SQL values are bound, not concatenated, with the sed-escape path gone; golden tests green; the ratchet ceiling is decremented.

Demote `mios-db` to a shim; keep the three-backend routing contract and the 0/1/2 exit codes. Golden-test the `--config get/set` SQL and the mode-dispatch error messages.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-db (-> shim), tools/native/ (new mios-db crate), usr/libexec/mios/mios-pg-query (parameterized backend, unchanged)`
details.why: Quoting SQL by `sed`-escaping single quotes is a known-broken defense — one crafted config value written through `mios-db --config set` reaches the database as statement text, in a tool that holds the credentials for the agent datastore.

**Goal:** E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one memory-safe diagnostic entry point for agents and operators, with no embedded python.
**What+How:** Reimplement `usr/libexec/mios/mios-doctor` — the ok/fail/warn/info probes for sudo grants, mount-namespace escapability, podman `additionalimagestores` permissions, hermes session state, OWUI registration and the primary services, with ports resolved from install.env — as `miosd doctor`, reusing the greenboot probe helpers and mios-toml-core for ports. Keep the grep-able `── ── ──` section headers byte-stable so existing agent investigation flows keep parsing. Demote `mios-doctor` to a shim and snapshot the section structure plus exit code via trycmd.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-doctor (-> shim), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/ (doctor module) or tools/native/, /etc/mios/install.env (input)`
**Done When:** `miosd doctor` emits the same section headers and pass/fail verdicts as the bash on a fixture host; the exit code matches; the embedded `python3 -c` probes are gone; golden trycmd green; ratchet decremented.
**Why:** mios-doctor is the structured replacement for throwaway diagnostic scripts, but its embedded python heredocs make it unlintable and dependent on a python that the firstboot-tier may not carry — so the one tool used when things are broken is itself fragile.
**Dep:** task_1653 -- Build mios-toml-core, the figment-based typed layered resolver crate

title: Absorb mios-ssot-regen orchestration into a miosd ssot-regen subcommand with real exit aggregation
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- `mios-ssot-regen` becomes a trustworthy regenerator whose failures are visible.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd ssot-regen` regenerates the same ai/v1 manifests plus roadmap and gate indices with byte-identical output versus the bash, but exits non-zero if any generator fails (no silent `|| true`); drift-gate green; ratchet decremented.

details.what_how: Reimplement `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ssot-regen` — which sets `MIOS_TOML`, `MIOS_AGENT_PIPE_DIR`, `MIOS_VERB_MANIFEST` and `MIOS_CAPS_OUT`, then runs `mios-ai-manifest-gen`, `mios-ai-capabilities-gen`, `tools/roadmap-index.py`, `tools/generate-gate-index.py` and `tools/mios-dup-report` — as a `miosd ssot-regen` subcommand that sequences the same generators with typed env from mios-toml-core and aggregates exit codes properly, dropping the `|| true` that currently swallows every failure. Leave the individual generators unchanged and still invoked; demote the bash to a shim.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ssot-regen (-> shim), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/ (ssot-regen module), tools/roadmap-index.py + tools/generate-gate-index.py + tools/mios-dup-report (invoked)`
details.why: A generator can fail today and the orchestrator still reports success, so a broken projection is committed and only surfaces later as a red drift-gate with no clue which generator produced it.

title: Port hermes-worker-firstboot to a small idempotent Rust unit binary (the firstboot port template)
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- establish the reusable idempotent-unit template on the smallest firstboot before the big ones.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust binary reproduces hermes-worker-firstboot's side effects and exit code idempotently (a second run no-ops); the `.service` invokes it unchanged; degrade-open is verified (a non-zero step never aborts boot); golden test green; ratchet decremented.

details.what_how: Port `usr/libexec/mios/hermes-worker-firstboot` (43 lines; the atomic + retried + idempotent firstboot pattern for the hermes worker) to a small Rust binary invoked unchanged by `hermes-worker-firstboot.service`. goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- harden the release-topology plane where admin credentials and tokens are handled.

title: Port mios-ai-firstboot to an idempotent sentinel-gated Rust provisioner (bash kept as fallback)
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- make the hottest firstboot in the tree memory-safe without ever wedging a boot.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust provisioner writes the sentinel under the identical all-pieces-present condition, seeds the venv offline from the OCI image byte-for-byte, and returns 0 (degrade-open) on any partial failure exactly like the bash; the `.timer` re-fire no-ops once complete; golden fixtures green; parity confirmed before the shim body is deleted.

details.what_how: Port `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-firstboot` (696 lines: the agent venv build via `automation/72-hermes-agent.sh`, the BROKEN-VENV cleanup, the OFFLINE OCI-image venv seed via a podman tar-pipe, the llama.cpp GGUF fetch, the WSL persistence symlinks, and the `/var/lib/mios/.ai-firstboot-done` sentinel written ONLY when every piece is in place) to a Rust binary via the firstboot template. Preserve the `set +eu` degrade-open semantics EXACTLY, the timer-owned retry (`ConditionPathExists=!sentinel`), and every idempotence guard. Keep the bash as fallback behind `[migration]` until the sentinel-writing conditions and all observable side effects are proven identical on fixtures; only then delete the body.
details.why: This is where the operator-reported "outages / must deploy every time" failures lived — a premature sentinel write leaves the AI plane permanently half-provisioned because the timer never retries, and 696 lines of `set +eu` shell is the least verifiable place in the boot path.

title: Extract the hermes config-YAML renderer out of the 1916-line mios-hermes-firstboot into a `mios-toml-core hermes-config` subcommand
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- moves the single largest firstboot bash mass onto the compiled tier by porting its pure SSOT-projection slice first (strangler-fig), so no shell is deleted before byte-parity is proven.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-firstboot` regenerates `~/.hermes/config.yaml` and `/var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml` from `mios.toml [ai]` on every boot. Add a `hermes-config` subcommand to the `mios-toml-core` crate that deserializes `[ai]` into a typed struct and serializes both YAML files deterministically. Leave the service-restart/orchestration steps in bash for a later slice. details.why: 1916 lines of boot-critical bash re-derive AI config from SSOT on every boot with no test; a silent render bug there ships a broken Hermes config to every host, and the mass keeps growing while it stays in shell.

goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- retires an opaque packed-zipapp artifact (neither loose script nor hardened binary) from the image.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust dashboard renders `--dash`/`--mini` snapshots matching the zipapp's framed output on a fixture with ports driven from SSOT; the zipapp artifact no longer exists in the built image; `mios dash` / `mios mini` are unchanged for the operator; the golden test is green.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-09 (M8, operator rulings R1/R2): superseded by the M8 tmux desktop. title: Port mios-build-driver to a `miosd build` orchestrator behind the verb dispatcher
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- puts the hottest verb backend, the `mios build` pipeline driver, under a compiled orchestrator that owns step order and gating explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd build` drives the same pipeline step order, writes an identical `/etc/mios/install.env` identity block, and resumes idempotently like the bash on a dev build; the 66 NN-*.sh steps are byte-unchanged; the side-by-side diff is clean; the ratchet is decremented once the shim is the only bash left.

title: Port mios-hardcode-lint to Rust and anchor the allowlist regexes that spuriously exempt real port literals
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- restores the NO-HARDCODE (Law 7) gate's actual coverage by fixing the allowlist bug that lets `:8080`/`:8033` slip through.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust linter reports an identical violation set to the Python on the fixture repo for the date-in-comment / date-in-string / header-risk / port-IP classes, EXCEPT that previously-mis-exempted ports are now flagged; `MIOS_HARDCODE_LINT_SOFT=1` remains advisory; the drift-gate is green after the newly-surfaced violations are floated; Law 15 mirrored in mios-bootstrap.git.

details.what_how: Reimplement `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` (Python: `_date_in_comment_py`/`_date_in_string_py` tokenize+AST scans, `_check_ports_ips_py`, `_header_risk` BOM/shebang rules, `scan`, `_load_allowlist` reading `[security.nohc_allowlist].exempt_files`/`exempt_patterns`) as a Rust tool folded into `mios-ssot-lint`, with a real tokenizer/AST-aware pass and, critically, ANCHORED allowlist regexes so canonical ports are no longer matched as substrings and exempted. Preserve `MIOS_HARDCODE_LINT_SOFT` advisory mode and the exact violation categories and exit codes. Demote the Python to a shim; golden-test the violation set against a fixture repo covering each class.
details.why: The unanchored allowlist silently exempts hardcoded canonical ports, so the NO-HARDCODE law reports green while real violations accumulate; the scanner is also hot Python on the drift-check path.

goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- eliminates the single largest loose-script liability in usr/libexec/mios.

details.what_how: Port `capability-audit.sh`, which backs the `mios assess` verb in KNOWN_VERBS, to a `miosd assess` subcommand that enumerates hardware/system capabilities through native `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev` reads and structured command output instead of long awk/grep chains, taking thresholds and config from `mios-toml-core`. title: Add `check_langx_shim_retirement`: a rust-defaulted verb may not keep a fat bash body
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- makes the strangler-fig "delete the slice once rerouted" step a machine-enforced fitness function instead of a convention.
acceptance_criteria: the check passes on the current tree, fails when a rust-defaulted verb still has a fat bash body, and fails when a retired tool reappears carrying logic; the generated gate index lists it; Law 15 mirrored in mios-bootstrap.git.

details.what_how: Add `check_langx_shim_retirement` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh`. For every tool whose `[migration]` toggle default has flipped to `"rust"`, assert (a) a passing golden-parity fixture exists and (b) the bash file is either a <=15-line pure-exec shim or deleted, failing when a full bash body coexists with a rust-defaulted verb (the oxidizr gap-free-window rule). Also flag any bash tool ported to Rust that still carries live logic behind its shim. Record retired tools in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [langx].retired` so the list is append-only. Degrade open when git/cargo are absent; keep negatives-before-main gate ordering.
details.why: Without it, a verb defaulted to Rust can silently keep a divergent bash body that a rollback or a `[migration]` flip re-activates, so the two implementations drift apart unnoticed and the ratchet never actually falls.

title: Fold the usr/bin/hermes launcher into the verb dispatcher
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- removes a standalone bash launcher by keeping venv-binary resolution in one audited place.
acceptance_criteria: `hermes <subcommand>` passes argv through byte-identically and the not-installed path prints the same guidance with exit 127 as the bash; `usr/bin/hermes` is a shim; golden test green; ratchet decremented.

details.what_how: `usr/bin/hermes` is a 39-line bash wrapper that exec's `/usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv/bin/hermes` after an existence check. Move its logic (venv-binary resolution plus the helpful not-installed error) into `mios-verb-dispatcher` as the `hermes` entry, reducing `usr/bin/hermes` to a one-line shim or a dispatcher symlink. Keep the exec-through-to-the-upstream-CLI contract identical. Golden-test both the not-installed error path and argv passthrough.
details.why: Venv-path resolution duplicated outside the dispatcher means a venv layout change has to be fixed in two places, and this file counts against the loose-script surface for no benefit.

title: Extend the Containerfile rust-builder to build the tools/native workspace and COPY every release binary into /usr/libexec/mios
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the enabler that makes any Rust port actually ship inside the bootc image.
acceptance_criteria: `podman build` produces an image containing `/usr/libexec/mios/<bin>` for every declared native crate; a new drift-check asserts each declared binary exists and is executable in the built layer; the bake is green.

details.what_how: The Containerfile rust-builder stage (lines 40-70) only runs `cargo build --release` on `src/mios-rs` and COPYs a single `/miosd` into the image. The `tools/native` crates (`mios-ssot-lint`, `mios-bake-plan`, `mios-aiplane-lint`, `mios-drift-runner`, `mios-version-check`, `mios-wallpaperd`, `generate-names-registry`) and every newly-ported libexec binary never reach the running image; they are only built ad hoc on the host at drift-check time (`98-drift-checks.sh:4880` runs `cargo build --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml`). Add a second builder stage that builds the `tools/native` workspace with the same registry and target cache mounts, then COPY each `target/release/<bin>` into `/usr/libexec/mios/`.
details.why: Every port is inert today: the compiled artifact is not in the image, so a ported tool cannot be verified end-to-end and the running system keeps executing the bash it was supposed to replace.

title: Consolidate the two divergent Cargo workspaces (src/mios-rs/miosd + tools/native) under one root with shared workspace.dependencies
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- one consolidated workspace with a single pinned Cargo.lock as the reproducibility SSOT for the whole native tier.
acceptance_criteria: one workspace root builds miosd and every native crate against a single `Cargo.lock`; shared deps are declared exactly once; `cargo test` and the drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: Two independent workspaces with two `Cargo.lock` files exist today: `src/mios-rs` (miosd, `drift.rs`/`main.rs`) and `tools/native` (the lint/plan/walk crates), each with its own edition/version and dependency graph. The workspace-repair work only adopts orphans WITHIN `tools/native` and leaves this split untouched, so miosd and the ported libexec binaries can never build or version-sync together. Pick one authoritative workspace root (or a virtual manifest including both trees), hoist edition/version and the common deps (clap, figment, serde) into `[workspace.dependencies]`, and unify to a single lockfile so one `cargo build --release` yields miosd plus all native crates.
details.why: Two workspaces double the build, cache and lint surface, let miosd's dependency versions drift from the native tier, and block both the single-stage Containerfile build and a workspace-wide version-sync gate.

title: Generalize the version-sync drift-check to walk every Cargo workspace member instead of a hardcoded 3-path list
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- closes a gate that is currently blind to most crates, including miosd.
acceptance_criteria: setting any crate, including miosd or a newly-added port crate, to a non-SSOT version makes the check fail; the check is green on a correct tree.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` (~lines 3629-3636) enforces crate `version` == SSOT version over a HARDCODED list of exactly three manifests: `tools/native/Cargo.toml`, `mios-version-check/Cargo.toml`, `mios-wallpaperd/Cargo.toml`. It silently misses `src/mios-rs/miosd/Cargo.toml` and every crate a port adds, so a mismatched crate version passes. Replace the fixed `for _toml in ...` loop with a `cargo metadata --format-version=1` walk (or a `git ls-files '**/Cargo.toml'` walk) that checks the `version` of every workspace member against the `mios.toml` SSOT version.
details.why: A hand-maintained manifest list rots as ports add crates, so the exact gate meant to catch version drift is the thing carrying the drift; miosd's version is unchecked today.

title: Enroll native /usr/libexec/mios binaries into fapolicyd file-trust so ComposeFS execution is not denied
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- keeps application whitelisting intact while the libexec fleet turns into non-rpm binaries.
acceptance_criteria: the fapolicyd trust db lists every native `/usr/libexec/mios` binary; a boot smoke-test executes each one with no fapolicyd denial; the drift-check fails when a binary is missing from the trust drop-in; gate green.

details.what_how: `automation/40-fapolicyd-trust.sh` sets `trust = file,rpmdb` for application whitelisting on ComposeFS. Binaries COPY'd in by the Containerfile (miosd today, every port tomorrow) are not in the rpmdb, so they depend on the `file` trust backend and will be DENIED at exec unless explicitly enrolled in the fapolicyd trust db. Add a build phase that enumerates ELF binaries under `/usr/libexec/mios` and writes a generated fapolicyd trust drop-in (`fapolicyd-cli --file add` or a `trust.d` file, with fs-verity), plus a drift-check asserting every native libexec binary is trusted.
details.why: A ported binary that fapolicyd blocks is strictly worse than the bash it replaced -- it fails closed at exec on exactly the hardened installs MiOS targets, and nothing today would catch it before boot.

title: Preserve AI-hint discoverability for compiled ports via an out-of-band sidecar registry
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- extends the AI-hint header convention to artifacts that have no shell header, so Law 16 conformance and AI-hint coverage survive compilation.
acceptance_criteria: a ported binary whose bash source has been deleted keeps checks 5 and 46 green and still appears in the generated AI manifest; the sidecar registry is the SSOT for that tool's hint metadata.

details.what_how: Every libexec bash tool carries `# AI-hint:` / `# AI-related:` / `# AI-functions:` headers consumed by `mios-ai-tag` (the taggability SSOT), `mios-ai-hint-coverage` (98-drift-checks check 5 ratchet), `check-template-conformance` (Law 16 / check 46) and `automation/manifest.json` (119 `full_content` entries via `tools/generate-ai-manifest.py`). A compiled binary has no such header, so deleting a ported bash tool regresses AI-hint coverage AND template conformance and drops the tool from the AI manifest/index. Define a sidecar registry (e.g. `usr/share/mios/aihints/<tool>.toml` or a `mios.toml [aihints]` block carrying hint/related/functions) and teach `mios-ai-tag`, `mios-ai-hint-coverage` and `check-template-conformance` to treat a binary with a registered sidecar as tagged.
details.why: The AI plane discovers tools by header metadata, so each completed port would silently shrink agent capability and redden two already-green gates -- which in practice blocks deleting the bash at all.

title: Migrate the 70 systemd ExecStart references onto ported binaries with prefixes intact, gated by an ExecStart-resolves drift-check
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- lets ports land without converting soft-fail provisioners into boot blockers.
acceptance_criteria: the drift-check fails on any dangling or non-executable ExecStart libexec path; all 70 units resolve after porting; ported units keep identical paths and `-`/`+` prefixes; gate green.

details.what_how: 70 units under `usr/lib/systemd/system` invoke `/usr/libexec/mios/*` (verified: `mios-adguard-firstboot`, `mios-ai-firstboot`, `mios-cdi-detect`, `bootc-switch-from-build.sh`, `ceph-bootstrap.sh`, and others), many carrying load-bearing prefixes: `-` (degrade-open, Law 12), `+` (full privilege), `@`, plus ExecStartPre/Post ordering. A port must land its binary at the SAME `/usr/libexec/mios/<name>` path as a drop-in replacement and keep every prefix. Audit each ported unit for prefix preservation and add a drift-check that every `ExecStart*=/usr/libexec/mios/...` token resolves to an existing, executable path in the built tree.
details.why: A path rename or a dropped `-` prefix during a port silently turns a degrade-open provisioner into a boot-blocking one, and the tree has no gate today that even asserts an ExecStart target exists.

title: Port the WSL early-boot bootstrap family (wsl-early, wsl-init, mios-wslg-env-import, wsl-theme-bridge.sh) to a `miosd wsl` subcommand
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- hardens the pre-sysinit namespace/device shell on the cross-platform WSL leg.
acceptance_criteria: the `mios-wsl-*` units invoke the `miosd wsl` subcommands; characterization tests match the bash on mounts, device nodes, `wsl.conf` content and the subnet fix; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `wsl-firstboot` is already targeted, but the rest of the boot-critical WSL2 chain is not: `wsl-early` (`mios-wsl-early.service`, pre-sysinit) marks `/` rshared and mknods `/dev/net/tun` + `/dev/fuse` for cockpit and rootless podman; `wsl-init` (`mios-wsl-init.service`) enforces `/etc/wsl.conf` integrity, maps WSLg X11 sockets and de-conflicts the podman/WSL2 IP subnet; plus `mios-wslg-env-import` and `wsl-theme-bridge.sh`. Fold them into `miosd wsl {early,init,wslg-env,theme-bridge}` using idempotent mount/mknod syscalls and real wsl.conf parsing, keeping the bash as a degrade-open fallback shim until byte-parity is proven.
details.why: This runs before sysinit and is the least-tested provisioner class in the tree; a partial failure leaves podman and cockpit broken on the Windows leg with no diagnostic.

**Goal:** E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- hardens the pre-sysinit namespace/device shell on the cross-platform WSL leg.
**What+How:** `wsl-firstboot` is already targeted, but the rest of the boot-critical WSL2 chain is not: `wsl-early` (`mios-wsl-early.service`, pre-sysinit) marks `/` rshared and mknods `/dev/net/tun` + `/dev/fuse` for cockpit and rootless podman; `wsl-init` (`mios-wsl-init.service`) enforces `/etc/wsl.conf` integrity, maps WSLg X11 sockets and de-conflicts the podman/WSL2 IP subnet; plus `mios-wslg-env-import` and `wsl-theme-bridge.sh`. Fold them into `miosd wsl {early,init,wslg-env,theme-bridge}` using idempotent mount/mknod syscalls and real wsl.conf parsing, keeping the bash as a degrade-open fallback shim until byte-parity is proven.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/{wsl-early,wsl-init,mios-wslg-env-import,wsl-theme-bridge.sh}, src/mios-rs/miosd, usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-wsl-early.service, usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-wsl-init.service`
**Done When:** the `mios-wsl-*` units invoke the `miosd wsl` subcommands; characterization tests match the bash on mounts, device nodes, `wsl.conf` content and the subnet fix; drift-gate green.
**Why:** This runs before sysinit and is the least-tested provisioner class in the tree; a partial failure leaves podman and cockpit broken on the Windows leg with no diagnostic.
**Dep:** Stand up the golden-master parity harness (trycmd + insta) for libexec verb ports

title: Port the GPU/CDI detection + passthrough family (gpu-detect, gpu-pv-detect, mios-cdi-detect, mios-gpu-passthrough, mios-sriov-init) to a `miosd gpu` subcommand
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- puts the boot-time hardware enumerators that gate all containerized GPU access on tested PCI/sysfs parsing.
acceptance_criteria: `/run/cdi` output is byte-identical vs the bash across golden multi-vendor sysfs fixtures; the two units invoke `miosd gpu`; gate green.

details.what_how: Distinct from the `vfio-*.sh` work: these are the enumerators feeding the container GPU plane. `mios-cdi-detect` (293 lines) detects NVIDIA/AMD/Intel and writes `/run/cdi` specs before `nvidia-cdi-refresh.service`; `gpu-detect` toggles the nvidia blacklist and `GSK_RENDERER` based on virt status; `mios-gpu-passthrough`, `mios-sriov-init` and `gpu-pv-detect` complete the set (units `mios-cdi-detect.service`, `mios-gpu-detect.service`, and `50-gpu-passthrough.conf`). Port to `miosd gpu {detect,cdi,passthrough,sriov}` with robust `/sys/bus/pci` parsing and structured CDI YAML emission.
details.why: Multi-vendor sysfs/PCI text-parsing in shell decides whether containers see a GPU at all; a misparse silently disables acceleration for the whole AI plane or breaks passthrough, and there are no fixtures proving otherwise.

title: Port the atomic bootc/OCI-delta swap family to a transactional `miosd bootc-apply` subcommand
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- gives the highest-blast-radius operation in the tree a compiled, transactional implementation with explicit rollback.
acceptance_criteria: characterization tests cover sentinel present/absent/corrupt and an interrupted swap; the operation is idempotent and rolls back on failure; the units invoke `miosd bootc-apply`; gate green.

details.what_how: `bootc-switch-from-build.sh` parses a `last_build.txt` sentinel and runs `bootc switch` to the freshly-built local image, driven by `mios-bootc-switch.path` + `mios-bootc-switch.service`; `mios-oci-delta-service.sh` with `mios-oci-delta-apply.service` performs the edge-delta OS swap; `mios-stage-oci-archive` stages the archive. Port to `miosd bootc-apply` with strict sentinel validation (present / absent / corrupt), transactional pre-checks and explicit rollback, keeping the bash as a fallback only until parity is proven.
details.why: A partial or interrupted swap driven by string-parsing shell can leave the host unbootable -- the difference between a self-updating machine and a brick -- with no test asserting the corrupt-sentinel path.

title: Port the security-enrollment tools (mios-enroll-secure-boot, mios-clevis-luks-gen, mios-keyring-autounlock, selinux-init) to fail-closed Rust binaries
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- makes the fail-closed contract on Secure Boot, LUKS and SELinux explicit and testable instead of implicit in shell exit codes.
acceptance_criteria: each replacement matches the bash on golden fixtures, provably exits non-zero when its security assertion fails, and emits an audit trail entry; gate green.

details.what_how: These untargeted bash tools sit on the security path: `mios-enroll-secure-boot` enrolls the akmods MOK via `mokutil` so signed NVIDIA/ZFS kmods load under Secure Boot; `mios-clevis-luks-gen` binds LUKS via clevis; `mios-keyring-autounlock` handles keyring autounlock; `selinux-init` initializes SELinux. Unlike the degrade-open provisioners, silent failure here weakens Secure Boot or disk encryption. Port each to a small static Rust binary that FAILS CLOSED on its security assertion (non-zero exit, audit-logged) rather than degrading open, with characterization tests over `mokutil`/clevis fixtures.
details.why: Today a failed MOK enrollment or LUKS bind can exit 0 through shell fallthrough, so a host boots believing it is protected when it is not, and no test distinguishes the two.

title: Port the eight-tool mios-flatpak-* lifecycle family to a native JSON-envelope binary
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- stabilizes the agent-facing JSON envelope shape by generating it from typed structs instead of hand-written bash.
acceptance_criteria: JSON-envelope output is byte-parity with the bash under insta snapshots across search/install/upgrade/run and the error path; the init and install units invoke the native binary; gate green.

details.what_how: The flatpaks-manage port covers only `flatpaks-manage.sh` + `flatpak-launch`; the real per-app install/override plane is the `mios-flatpak-*` family: `mios-flatpak` (a 286-line agent-facing JSON-envelope CLI with search/install/upgrade/run) plus `-init` and `-install` (units `mios-flatpak-init.service`, `mios-flatpak-install.service`), `-preflight`, `-overrides-apply`, `-icon-sanitize` and `-beta-migrate`. details.why: Agent tool-calling parses that exact envelope, and a hand-built bash JSON emitter breaks it on any unescaped app name or error string -- on a path invoked per app launch, so it is hot as well as brittle.

title: Port the root-as-git-tree machinery (git-root-init.sh, mios-sync-to-root, verify-root.sh) to a `miosd root` subcommand
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- gives the "/ IS $ROOT" self-updating-tree design compiled guarantees on the code that mutates the live system root.
acceptance_criteria: the mutable-vs-immutable gate is preserved and covered by a test that fails if sync is attempted against an immutable root; `miosd root verify` exits non-zero on an integrity mismatch; the units invoke miosd; characterization tests pass; gate green.

details.what_how: `verify-root.sh` is an early-boot composefs/ostree integrity check (`mios-verify-root.service`, basic.target); `git-root-init.sh` initializes the deployed `/` as a git working tree of the local repo; `mios-sync-to-root` applies the war-room ext4 replica LIVE onto the system root, gated to mutable MiOS-DEV roots only and never to an immutable bootc/ostree root. Port to `miosd root {verify,git-init,sync}`, preserving the mutable/immutable gate exactly and making verify fail closed. Keep the bash as a fallback until parity is proven.
details.why: A gating regression in `mios-sync-to-root` would write onto an immutable bootc root, and a soft-failing `verify-root` lets a tampered composefs boot unnoticed -- both under the code that underpins the self-updating tree.

title: Collapse the three build-if-missing firstboot bash scripts into one SSOT-driven `miosd build-if-missing` provisioner
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one compiled, sentinel-gated provisioner replaces triplicated shell so the image's firstboot path is code, not copy-paste.
acceptance_criteria: one Rust build-if-missing provisioner drives all three container builds from mios.toml specs; the run is sentinel-gated, idempotent and degrade-open; bash retained as fallback; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Three uncovered bash firstboots implement the identical pattern -- probe whether a podman image exists, `podman build` it when missing, degrade-open on failure: `mios-agents-firstboot.sh` (A2O super-container, invoked as ExecStartPre), `mios-forgejo-runner-firstboot.sh` (register-once runner token), `mios-webtools-firstboot.sh` (crawl4ai + firecrawl stack). Replace all three with one parameterized `miosd build-if-missing <spec>` subcommand in `src/mios-rs/miosd` that reads its image build specs from `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, so the sentinel/retry/idempotency/degrade-open logic exists exactly once. Repoint each `*.service` unit at the Rust subcommand and keep the bash scripts as an explicit fallback until parity holds.
details.why: Three independently-drifting copies of the same build-if-missing shell mean a retry or idempotency fix lands in one and rots in the other two, and a firstboot that is not idempotent re-builds images on every boot.

title: Build a hermetic fake-root / recorded-invocation harness that proves side-effectful firstboot ports match bash
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- no stateful script is deleted until its port is proven to issue the same external commands and filesystem writes.
acceptance_criteria: every firstboot/provisioner port carries a recorded-invocation characterization test matching bash's external-command sequence and FS effects; the tests run under `cargo test` and in CI; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The trycmd+insta golden-master harness verifies stdout/exit for read-only verbs only; the firstboot orchestrators (mios-ai-firstboot, the hermes/libvirtd/forge/webtools/agents provisioners, bootc-apply) mutate the filesystem and shell out to `podman`/`systemctl`/`bootc`/`mokutil`, so stdout proves nothing about them. Add a new test-support crate under `tools/native` that stands up a tempdir fake root plus PATH-shimmed fake `podman`/`systemctl`/`bootc`/`flatpak` binaries which RECORD their argv to a log. Tests under `src/mios-rs/miosd/tests` then assert a port emits the identical ordered external-command sequence and the identical FS effects as the bash original. Wire it into `cargo test` and the CI job.
details.where: `tools/native (new test-support crate), src/mios-rs/miosd/tests, usr/libexec/mios firstboot family`
details.why: Stateful ports are the riskiest and least covered surface in the campaign -- without an invocation-recording oracle a Rust firstboot can silently skip a `podman build` or write to the wrong path and ship undetected.

title: Regenerate the AI manifest/catalog after each shim retirement and gate on tracked build cruft
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the agent plane's view of the tree stays truthful as bash tools are retired.
acceptance_criteria: manifest and catalog are regenerated with retired entries removed; `git ls-files usr/libexec/mios` shows no `*.bak`/`*.retrytest*`/`__pycache__`; the new drift-check fails when one is reintroduced; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/manifest.json` embeds `full_content` for 119 script entries and is produced by `tools/generate-ai-manifest.py`; retiring a ported bash tool leaves a stale `full_content` entry the AI plane keeps serving, and the `materialize-build-catalog.py` / `mios-codebase-index` indexes go stale alongside it. The tree already proves this cleanup is not happening: `usr/libexec/mios/57-mios-sys-build.sh.retrytest.bak`, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-metal-vfio-gen.bak` and committed `__pycache__` are all tracked. Add a mandatory post-retirement regeneration step (run `generate-ai-manifest.py` + reindex, staging explicit paths -- never `git add -A`, which strips digest pins) and add a check in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that fails on any tracked `*.bak`, `*.retrytest*` or `__pycache__` under `usr/libexec/mios`.
details.why: A manifest full of ghost source content actively misleads the agent plane into editing files that no longer exist, and the .bak/pyc files already in the tree show the cleanup step does not exist today.

title: Co-port the build-observability companions (status, tail, log-copy, blade) with the mios-build-driver orchestrator
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the build plane and its readers move together so no bash/Rust seam forms over the shared sentinels.

details.what_how: `mios-build-driver` is already targeted for port, but its companion surface is not: `mios-build-status` and `mios-build-tail` read and stream build state, `copy-build-log.sh` is the ExecStart of the copy-build-log service and persists the log, and `mios-blade` is the related build UI helper. Fold them into the miosd build orchestrator as `miosd build {status,tail,log-copy}` subcommands sharing the driver's state model, and repoint the units at miosd.
details.why: Porting the writer while leaving the readers in bash splits one sentinel/log format across two languages, and the first format change silently breaks `mios-build-status` mid-build.

title: Package the 122 libexec Python tools as an installable `mios_tools` module, killing the 52 sys.path hacks
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- an importable package boundary is the strangler-fig façade every later typing, test and Rust-port task lands into.
acceptance_criteria: `python -m build` produces a wheel and `pip install` exposes `import mios_tools.config` with NO `sys.path.insert`; the 3 shared modules import cleanly as `mios_tools.*`; `just drift-gate` green; changes staged by explicit path (no `git add -A`).

details.what_how: There is NO `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py` anywhere in the tree (verified), and 52 files under `usr/libexec/mios` do `sys.path.insert(0, '.../usr/lib/mios')` to reach the shared resolver. Create `usr/lib/mios/pyproject.toml` declaring a PEP 621 `mios_tools` package (hatchling/setuptools backend) owning `mios_toml.py`, `mios_env.py` and `mios_db_config.py` as importable submodules, and register the extensionless hyphenated tools (`mios-a2a-discover`, `mios-ai-tag`, `mios-hardcode-lint`, ...) as `[project.scripts]` console entry-points, e.g. `mios-a2a-discover -> mios_tools.a2a_discover:main`. Strangler-fig: land the package + entry-points FIRST while the tools stay at their current paths (the build installs the wheel into the image site-packages), then flip each tool body to `from mios_tools import config` in follow-ups. Keep each current path as a thin `runpy.run_module('mios_tools.<x>')` launcher until parity is proven, then delete the loose script.
details.where: `usr/lib/mios/pyproject.toml (new), usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_env.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_db_config.py, usr/libexec/mios/* (122 python tools), automation/*.sh (install phase)`
details.why: 52 fragile `sys.path.insert` calls and the SourceFileLoader workarounds they force break on any file move, and without importable modules there is nothing for mypy, pytest coverage or a typed model layer to attach to.

title: Capture every SSOT `--check` projector's stdout/stderr/exit in a trycmd golden-master harness before any Rust port
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- a recorded parity oracle exists before a single security projector is rewritten.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-projector-golden` passes against committed fixtures for >=6 projectors; snapshots include exit code plus full stdout/stderr; the harness runs inside `just drift-gate`; fixtures are byte-frozen with an accept workflow documented.

details.what_how: `generate-cosign-policy.py`, `generate-uki-cmdline.py`, `generate-egress-firewall.py`, `generate-pod-quadlets.py`, `generate-names-registry.py` and `compile-templates.py` all expose a deterministic `--check` drift mode (verified: each diffs its generated artifact against the tracked file and exits 1 on drift). Before porting ANY of them, add a Rust `trycmd` crate at `tools/native/mios-projector-golden/` that runs each current `.py` against a frozen fixture `mios.toml` and records stdout + stderr + exit code into committed `.trycmd`/`.md` snapshots. Capture BOTH modes: the generate mode (the emitted file bytes) and the `--check` mode (the diff/OK message). Add `cargo test -p mios-projector-golden` to the `Justfile` drift-gate recipe (~line 81) and document the trycmd/insta accept workflow in the crate README.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-projector-golden/ (new crate), tools/generate-cosign-policy.py, tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py, tools/generate-egress-firewall.py, tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py, tools/generate-names-registry.py, tools/compile-templates.py, Justfile (drift-gate recipe ~line 81)`
details.why: Without a recorded oracle, a Rust rewrite of a projector that emits `policy.json` or the kernel cmdline can diverge byte-wise and nobody will notice until a boot-integrity control silently stops enforcing.

title: Consolidate the 8 tools/native crates into ONE cargo workspace with a committed Cargo.lock and cargo-deny/audit gates
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- one workspace, one lockfile, one clippy/audit posture that every Rust port inherits.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build --workspace` builds all 8 crates from `tools/native/`; `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` pass and run in CI; `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` is clean; exactly one `Cargo.lock` is committed; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/native/Cargo.toml` declares a workspace with only 3 members (`mios-drift-runner`, `mios-version-check`, `mios-wallpaperd`), yet 5 more crate directories exist and build out-of-tree: `generate-names-registry`, `mios-aiplane-lint`, `mios-bake-plan`, `mios-ssot-lint`, `mios-ssot-walk` (verified by ls). Add all 8 as workspace members so they share one `Cargo.lock` and one target dir. Add `tools/native/deny.toml` covering the advisories DB, a license allow-list matching the FOSS posture, and banned/duplicate-crate rules; wire `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` as new drift-gate steps in the `Justfile` and `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml`. Commit `Cargo.lock` as a reproducibility SSOT (SBOM-not-hardcode: dependency digests recorded at build, not hand-pinned). Add `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` alongside.
details.why: Five compiled tools currently build outside the workspace with no shared lockfile, no clippy, and no advisory scanning -- the bash they replace at least had shellcheck, so today's ports are less vetted than the scripts.

title: Eliminate the os.system() command-injection sites in mios-models and mios-v2v-import
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the shell-injection surface is removed from the OS-plane tool fleet.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -r 'os.system(' usr/libexec/mios` returns nothing; both tools invoke subprocess with an argv list; behavior is unchanged whether the target binary is present or absent; the drift-gate fails on any reintroduced `os.system`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Two injection surfaces are confirmed: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-models:46` runs `os.system(f"python3 {fb}")`, interpolating a path into a shell string, and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-v2v-import:88` runs `os.system(cmd_str)` on a fully string-built virt-v2v command. Replace both with `subprocess.run([...], check=...)` passing an argv LIST so no value is re-parsed by `/bin/sh`: `mios-models` becomes `subprocess.run([sys.executable, fb], ...)`, and `mios-v2v-import` builds its command as a list from the start rather than joining a string. Preserve degrade-open behavior (`mios-v2v-import` already guards with `shutil.which('virt-v2v')`). Add a ruff/grep drift-check banning `os.system(` under `usr/libexec/mios`.
details.why: `os.system` on an f-string or joined command is textbook shell injection in a tool that runs with OS-plane privilege -- a filename containing `;` is arbitrary code execution today, and the fix is a few lines.

title: Harden sqlite identifier interpolation in the CLIs behind a validated table allowlist
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the residual SQL-injection surface the parameterized-postgres gate does not cover is closed.
acceptance_criteria: every identifier splice passes through `safe_ident()` with regex + allowlist validation; a malformed table name raises before `execute()`; `test_mios_cli_sqlsafety.py` gains a rejection case; the drift-gate fails on a new raw f-string identifier; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: f-string interpolation of table names into SQL is confirmed at `usr/libexec/mios/mios-cache-clear:176` (`DELETE FROM {t}`), `mios-owui-apply-knowledge:143` (`PRAGMA table_info({table})`) and `:214` (`SELECT 1 FROM {tbl}`), and `mios-owui-bootstrap-admin:313` (a dynamic column list spliced into an INSERT). sqlite cannot bind identifiers, so wrap each splice in a strict validator: assert the identifier matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` AND is a member of an explicit allowlist derived from the known schema, raising a typed error before it ever reaches `execute()`. Add a shared `mios_tools.sql.safe_ident()` helper (after packaging) so all four sites use one validated path, and extend the existing `check_cli_sql_safety` gate (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh` ~line 685, with `test_mios_cli_sqlsafety.py` present) to fail on any new unvalidated f-string identifier reaching `execute()`.
details.why: These four call sites are the only remaining path where an attacker-influenced string reaches SQL unvalidated, and the existing gate does not see them, so the class can grow unnoticed.

title: Wire the already-written Rust generate-names-registry into the build and check 30; demote the .py to a toggled fallback, then delete it
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the first real cutover demonstrates the strangler-fig + SSOT-toggle + byte-parity playbook.
acceptance_criteria: check 30 invokes the Rust binary; Rust and `.py` outputs are proven byte-identical on the current tree; flipping one `[migration] use_rust_verbs` value rolls back to the `.py`; `just drift-gate` green; the `.py` deleted or shimmed with the change staged by explicit path.

details.what_how: A Rust port ALREADY exists at `tools/native/generate-names-registry/src/main.rs` (6115 bytes, references check 30), but the drift-gate at `automation/98-drift-checks.sh:2103+` still invokes `tools/generate-names-registry.py` (164 lines) -- the compiled implementation is dead code. Cut over in four steps: (1) add the crate to the consolidated workspace and build it into the image; (2) run BOTH implementations against the current tree and assert `usr/share/mios/names.generated.txt` and `usr/share/mios/referenced_names.txt` come out byte-identical; (3) flip check 30 to call the Rust binary with the `.py` retained as a `--fallback` behind a new SSOT toggle `mios.toml [migration] use_rust_verbs`; (4) after a clean window, delete `tools/generate-names-registry.py`. Mirror the SSOT surface change in BOTH repos (Law 15).
details.why: A finished Rust binary sits unused while the gate runs the Python it was written to replace -- so the campaign carries maintenance cost for two implementations and has proven neither the toggle nor the parity workflow that 20 later ports depend on.
