title: Replace `eval "$@"` on agent-controlled args in mios-ai-clear/reset/launch/window with hardened dispatch (TD-1)
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the eval-on-agent-args injection surface is gone from the verb library.
acceptance_criteria: no `eval` on agent- or user-derived strings remains in the four verbs; launch dispatch uses shlex plus array exec; the drift-gate fails on a new `eval` in a libexec verb; existing launch behavior is held by a characterization test; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The TD-1 eval-on-input sites are confirmed: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-clear:65` `eval "$@"`, `mios-ai-reset:91` `eval "$@"`, `mios-launch:507` `eval exec "$_hit_cmd"` (the file already carries a TD-1 note at :721 recommending shlex.split), and `mios-window:386` `eval "$(python3 - ...)"`. Replace each string-eval with a safe form: the `run()` helpers in `mios-ai-clear`/`mios-ai-reset` invoke the argv array directly (`"$@"`) instead of `eval "$@"`; `mios-launch` tokenizes the launch field with shlex and execs the resulting array; `mios-window` has its python helper emit a NUL-separated array the shell reads without eval. Where a command genuinely must be data-driven, use an explicit `case`/associative-array dispatch table of allowed verbs. Add a drift-check banning bare `eval ` in `usr/libexec/mios` verbs, allowlisting any proven-safe residual.
details.why: Agent-supplied arguments are an explicitly untrusted boundary, and `eval` on them is the Gemini-CLI-class remote-code-execution bug -- a crafted tool argument today runs arbitrary shell as the verb's user.

title: Replace the SourceFileLoader dynamic-import hacks with clean `mios_tools.*` package imports
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- runtime code-loading-by-file-path disappears once the tools are importable modules.
acceptance_criteria: no `SourceFileLoader` or `spec_from_loader` remains in the three tools (test_*.py fixtures may keep theirs); they import siblings via `mios_tools.*`; the tag-coverage and a2a tests still pass; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Because the hyphenated tools are not importable, three files load siblings via `importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader` (verified): `check-template-conformance:25` loads `mios-ai-tag`, `mios-a2a-discover:27`/`:67` loads `mios-a2a-mdns`, and `mios-ai-hint-coverage:56` loads `mios-ai-tag`. Once the `mios_tools` package lands (entry-points give underscore module names), rewrite these to `from mios_tools import ai_tag` / `from mios_tools import a2a_mdns` and delete the SourceFileLoader plus `sys.path.insert` scaffolding. Behavior is unchanged -- the tagger and the mDNS browse helper become ordinary package attributes.
details.why: Loading code by hardcoded file path breaks the moment a tool is renamed or ported, and it is a dynamic-exec smell that ruff's S rules will flag -- the packaging work makes it entirely unnecessary.

title: Fold mios_toml.py, mios_env.py and mios_db_config.py into one typed `mios_tools.config` surface
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the shared resolver becomes one facade, the seam the typed-model and compiled-resolver work plugs into.
acceptance_criteria: `from mios_tools import config` exposes the union API; the three legacy modules are re-export shims or removed with consumers updated; `check-resolver-twin.py` still passes; `just drift-gate` green; SSOT twin surfaces mirrored in both repos (Law 15).

details.what_how: The three shared modules (`usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` 601 lines, `mios_env.py` an 18-line strip_empty helper, `mios_db_config.py`) are imported ad-hoc by 43+ tools. After packaging, merge them behind one `mios_tools.config` facade exposing `load_merged`/`load_vendor`/`section`/`colors`/`layer_paths` (from mios_toml) plus `strip_empty_mios_env` (from mios_env) plus the DB-config accessor, so callers write `from mios_tools import config` once. Keep the three files as thin re-export shims (`from mios_tools.config import *`) during migration so no consumer breaks, update consumers in batches, then delete the shims. This is a pure re-home with no behavior change -- assert that by keeping `tools/check-resolver-twin.py` green, which proves twin-equivalence with `userenv.sh` still holds.
details.where: `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_env.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_db_config.py, usr/lib/mios/mios_tools/config.py (new), tools/check-resolver-twin.py, usr/libexec/mios/* (43 importers)`

title: Introduce pydantic v2 typed models for the mios.toml sections the tools consume, replacing raw dict .get() plumbing
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the SSOT schema becomes code, so a mistyped key fails loudly instead of projecting a wrong value.
acceptance_criteria: `MiosConfig` models cover >=6 sections; `config.load_typed()` round-trips the shipped `mios.toml` without error and raises on a deliberately malformed fixture; >=3 consumers are off raw `.get()`; mypy is clean on the models; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mios_toml.load_merged()` returns an untyped dict and consumers chain `.get()` into it (e.g. `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py` does `data.get('security',{}).get('sigstore',{})`; `seed-db-config.py` does the same for env+toml plumbing; dozens more). Define pydantic v2 `BaseModel`s in `usr/lib/mios/mios_tools/models.py` for the high-traffic sections first -- `[security.sigstore]`, `[ports]`, `[colors]`, `[ai.vllm]`/`[ai.sglang]`, `[templates]`, `[migration]` -- with real types (ports as int, colors as validated hex, `[security.nohc_allowlist]` typed). Add `config.load_typed() -> MiosConfig` that deserializes the merged overlay and raises on any shape/type error. Migrate the projectors and `seed-db-config.py` to the typed accessor incrementally, leaving raw `load_merged()` available as a fallback until every consumer is converted.
details.why: Chained `.get()` turns a renamed or mistyped SSOT key into a silent default that flows straight into a Quadlet or `policy.json` -- the failure appears as a misconfigured running system, not as an error.

title: Add a mypy --strict drift-gate seeded on the resolver, models and projectors
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the Python that stays Python gets a type guarantee on the SSOT-critical modules.
acceptance_criteria: `mypy` runs in CI and `just drift-gate` over the strict include-set with zero errors; the resolver public API is fully annotated; a newly-added untyped function in an in-scope module fails the gate; the include-list ships with a documented shrink plan.

details.what_how: No mypy config exists. Add `[tool.mypy]` to the new pyproject with `strict = true` and run `mypy` as a drift-gate step over a curated, growing include-list starting with `mios_tools/config.py`, `mios_tools/models.py` and the SSOT projectors (`tools/generate-*.py`) -- the smallest, most safety-critical modules. Use per-module `ignore_errors` overrides for the untyped long tail so the gate lands green, then advance the strict frontier module-by-module (strangler-fig for types). Fully annotate the resolver's public API (`load_merged`/`section`/`colors` return types) so downstream callers are checked too.
details.why: The modules that decide what gets projected into `policy.json`, the kernel cmdline and the Quadlets are exactly where a wrong type silently corrupts an SSOT projection, and today nothing checks them.

goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness: negative self-tests, coverage, doc integrity -- every test that exists actually runs, and coverage only goes up.

title: Port generate-uki-cmdline.py to Rust with byte-parity on the signed kernel cmdline
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the kernel-cmdline projector becomes compiled code without changing a byte of the signed UKI payload.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust binary reproduces `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline` byte-identically and its `--check` diff format matches; trycmd goldens pass; the UKI render step calls Rust with the `.py` fallback toggle; `just drift-gate` green; `.py` demoted or deleted with explicit staging.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py` (59 lines) flattens the `usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml` drop-ins (sorted, each with a `kargs` list array) into `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline`, and its `--check` mode emits a unified diff on drift. Port to a workspace crate `mios-uki-cmdline`: glob and sort the kargs.d TOMLs, concatenate the `kargs` arrays with a single space and a trailing newline (match the `.py`'s `' '.join(...).strip()+'\n'` exactly), and reproduce the `[drift]` diff output format for `--check`. Use miette for parse errors keyed to the offending fragment. Prove against the trycmd golden, demote the `.py` behind `[migration] use_rust_verbs`, then delete. The cmdline carries `enforcing=1` and LUKS args baked into the signed UKI, so parity is safety-critical.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-uki-cmdline/ (new crate), tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py, usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml, usr/lib/kernel/cmdline, automation/76-uki-render.sh, usr/share/mios/mios.toml [migration]`
details.why: The cmdline is embedded in the signed UKI and cannot be edited at boot -- a dropped or reordered karg ships a system that boots permissive or without LUKS args, and only a reinstall fixes it.

title: Port generate-pod-quadlets.py to Rust to kill the quadlet-digest-drift class at the generator root
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the largest projector becomes reproducible compiled output, making the recurring digest-drift failure structurally impossible.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust generator emits every Quadlet unit type byte-identical to the `.py`, proven per-type against goldens; `check_pod_quadlets` passes with Rust as the generator and `.py` as fallback; regenerating after a broad stage no longer strips pins; `just drift-gate` green; `.py` demoted or deleted with explicit staging.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py` (504 lines) generates the pod/container/network/volume Quadlets with `@sha256` pins from `mios.toml [pods.*]` and is the drift subject of `check_pod_quadlets` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh` ~lines 881-900). Port to a workspace crate `mios-pod-quadlets` consuming a typed `[pods]` model and emitting each unit deterministically (stable key ordering, exact whitespace) so the artifact is reproducible rather than hand-staged -- directly attacking the recurring "a broad `git add` strips the `@sha256` pins" failure, per SBOM-not-hardcode (digests resolved and recorded at build). Match the current `--check` drift behavior. Because it is the largest projector, port incrementally: emit ONE unit type (`.network`) in Rust and diff against the `.py`, expand type-by-type behind `[migration] use_rust_verbs`, keep the `.py` as fallback until every unit type reaches byte-parity, then delete.
details.why: Quadlet-digest drift is a documented recurring outage in this tree -- the pod-quadlets check goes red, someone re-stages pins by hand, and it happens again next commit; generating-not-authoring ends the cycle.

title: Extend the 800-line module ceiling from agent-pipe to a tree-wide Python drift-gate
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the module-cohesion ceiling becomes a ratcheting fitness function across all 122 tools instead of one subtree.
acceptance_criteria: the ceiling check covers all tracked Python tree-wide; the 6 current offenders are grandfathered by explicit SSOT entry; adding a new 801-line `.py` fails the gate; `just drift-gate` green; the SSOT allowlist mirrored in both repos (Law 15).

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh:6014-6033` enforces the <=800-line ceiling ONLY for `agent-pipe`/`mios_pipe` modules. Generalize the check to scan ALL tracked `.py` plus python-shebang tools under `usr/libexec/mios`, `usr/lib/mios` and `tools/`, failing on any file over 800 lines. Seed a grandfathered allowlist in SSOT (`mios.toml [debt.module_ceiling_grandfathered]`) naming today's known offenders -- `mios-daemon` (3371), `mios-dotfiles-render` (1239), `mios-computer-use` (1113), `mios-skills` (991), `MiOS-Mon.py` (911), `mios-mcp-server` (759) -- so the gate lands green while forbidding NEW oversized modules, then shrink the allowlist as the split tasks land.
details.why: Outside agent-pipe nothing stops a new 3000-line tool from landing, so the debt this campaign is paying down regrows in the 122-tool surface faster than it is removed.

title: Split mios-daemon (3371 lines) into cohesive sub-800-line modules behind a stable entry-point
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- the worst module-cohesion offender is decomposed so typing and coverage can reach the most operationally critical tool.
acceptance_criteria: no `mios_tools.daemon` module exceeds 800 lines; the three daemon tests plus find-ranker pass unchanged; `mios-daemon` behaves identically under a characterization test of the start/gate-eval path; the daemon grandfather entry is deleted from SSOT; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-daemon` is 3371 lines -- 4x the ceiling and by far the largest Python tool. Decompose it into a `mios_tools.daemon` package with cohesive submodules along its existing seams (scheduling/gate-eval, launch-claim, postcheck, refusal-handling -- each already has a dedicated test: `test_mios_daemon_launchclaim.py`, `test_mios_daemon_postcheck.py`, `test_mios_daemon_refusal.py`). Keep `mios-daemon` as a thin entry-point that imports and wires the submodules so CLI behavior is unchanged. Strangler-fig: extract one responsibility at a time, keeping the three daemon tests green after each extraction, and remove the grandfather entry only once every submodule is <=800 lines.
details.why: A 3371-line untyped daemon is unreviewable and untestable as a unit, mypy and coverage cannot usefully reach it, and it is the tool whose failure most directly stalls the autonomous plane.

title: Prove the shell and Python mios.toml resolvers equivalent with a shrinking proptest differential oracle
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- gives the resolver collapse the randomized differential oracle that makes a compiled single implementation provably safe.
acceptance_criteria: The test generates >=100 random valid `mios.toml` documents and both resolvers produce identical `MIOS_*` projections (or the shrunk case is fixed); the harness runs inside `just drift-gate`; a deliberately divergent key mapping planted in one resolver is caught and reported; the gate is green on the current tree.

details.what_how: `tools/check-resolver-twin.py` (173 lines) only spot-checks `mios_toml.py` against `userenv.sh` on the one shipped `mios.toml`. Replace that with a differential property harness (Rust proptest crate `tools/native/mios-resolver-parity/`, or hypothesis inside the existing checker) that GENERATES random-but-valid layered documents — vendor<host<user, empty-string-does-not-override, drop-in fragments — runs BOTH resolvers on each, and asserts the emitted `MIOS_*` key set and values are byte-identical, auto-shrinking any divergence to a minimal failing document. Wire the harness as a drift-gate check next to the existing twin check (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh` ~L3191). The known short-vs-long key mismatch (`MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` emitted vs `MIOS_VLLM_*` consumed) should surface as a concrete failing generated case, not a hand-noticed one.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-resolver-parity/ (new crate) or tools/check-resolver-twin.py (extend), usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh, tools/lib/userenv.sh, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (line ~3191)`
details.why: Today equivalence of the three parallel resolvers rests on one hand-written spot check over a single file, so any collapse-to-one-implementation is a leap of faith — a randomized oracle is the missing safety proof and also mechanizes the GUP lossless-diff invariant.

title: Split mios-dotfiles-render (1239) and mios-computer-use (1113) below the module ceiling
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- shrinks the module-ceiling grandfather list toward zero so the tools become typeable and testable.

details.what_how: Two libexec tools exceed the 800-line ceiling: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render` (1239) and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-computer-use` (1113). details.why: After mios-daemon these are the two largest ceiling offenders, and while they stay monolithic the ceiling gate is permanently softened by a grandfather list that never shrinks.

title: Route every tool through the shared resolver, deleting the ~13 re-rolled `try tomllib/except tomli` + hardcoded-layer copies
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- finishes the consolidation `mios_toml.py` was created for, so one resolver semantics holds everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -r 'import tomli' usr/libexec/mios tools` matches only `mios_tools/config`; every consumer resolves `mios.toml` solely through the shared resolver; a deliberately reintroduced local tomli fallback fails the new drift-gate check; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `mios_toml.py`'s own docstring says it exists to collapse ~13 independently re-rolled `try: import tomllib / except: import tomli` + `deep_merge` + hardcoded-layer-path blocks — yet those blocks are still inline in consumers (verified in `generate-cosign-policy.py`, `generate-uki-cmdline.py`, `seed-db-config.py`, and `compile-templates.py`'s fallback). Sweep `usr/libexec/mios` and `tools/` for the local tomllib/tomli try-import plus ad-hoc `mios.toml` path resolution and replace each with `from mios_tools import config` (or the packaged `mios_toml`). Tools already slated for a Rust port need no change. Then add a drift-gate check forbidding a local `import tomli` fallback anywhere outside `mios_tools.config`.
details.why: A dozen divergent copies of the layer-resolution boilerplate means a fix to vendor<host<user semantics lands in one place and silently misses the other twelve — the exact drift the shared resolver was supposed to end.

title: Give the migrated Rust projectors a miette/thiserror typed-diagnostic error surface pointing at mios.toml spans
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- makes every compiled verb report SSOT errors identically, as compiler-grade diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Each ported projector depends on `mios-diagnostics` and returns `miette::Result`; a malformed `[security.sigstore]` or `[pods]` value produces a spanned diagnostic naming the offending `mios.toml` line; a trycmd fixture pins the diagnostic format; `cargo test` and `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: As projectors move to Rust (cosign-policy, uki-cmdline, egress-firewall, pod-quadlets, index-gen, config-gen), standardize their error handling: library-internal errors become `thiserror` enums the drift-gates can match on programmatically, and each `main` returns `miette::Result` so a bad value in `mios.toml` prints with source span, label and help text. Add a shared crate `tools/native/mios-diagnostics/` providing the `SourceSpan` helper that maps a failing `[section].key` back to its line and BYTE range in the merged TOML (byte offsets, not char counts, so UTF-8 highlights correctly), and have every ported tool depend on it. Lock the output shape with a trycmd fixture that feeds a deliberately malformed `mios.toml`.
details.where: `tools/native/mios-diagnostics/ (new crate), tools/native/mios-cosign-policy/, tools/native/mios-uki-cmdline/, tools/native/mios-egress-firewall/, tools/native/mios-pod-quadlets/, usr/share/mios/mios.toml`
details.why: Without a shared span-mapper each ported tool invents its own error text, and an operator who mistypes a port value gets an opaque traceback instead of "this value is invalid, here, try X" — losing the main UX dividend of compiling the tier.

title: Eliminate the shell=True recipe-template command-injection in mios-os-recipe
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- closes the last argument-injection execution sink in the libexec Python surface.
acceptance_criteria: No `shell=True` remains in `mios-os-recipe`; the injection characterization test proves metacharacters in params are inert; ruff/bandit S602/S604 report clean on the file; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-os-recipe` builds `cmd` from `_expand(template, params)` — params sourced from spec/agent input — and runs it through `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, ...)` at ~L194, a template-injection sink the separate os.system task (mios-models / mios-v2v-import) does not cover. Rewrite to a `shlex`-tokenized argv list with no shell, splitting the WSL/binfmt `.exe` exec path out explicitly (the `appendWindowsPath=false` rationale in the L186-192 comment is satisfied by passing the absolute `/mnt/c/...` path as argv[0]), and validate param interpolation against an allowlist of declared placeholder keys. Keep the existing timeout and degrade-open `TimeoutExpired`/`Exception` fallbacks intact. Add a characterization test asserting a param containing `; rm -rf` arrives as one literal argv element.
details.why: This is the only surviving `shell=True` in the entire libexec Python surface and it interpolates agent-controllable recipe params — a live remote-code-execution path reachable from the agent dispatch chain today.

title: Replace predictable /tmp temp-file paths with tempfile mkstemp/mkdtemp and gate literal-/tmp
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- removes a local-escalation hazard and adds the gate that keeps it removed.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -r '/tmp/' usr/libexec/mios --include='*.py'` excluding tests returns empty; the ruff S108 gate is active and green; oscap-scan writes under a 0700 `mkdtemp`; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Three Python tools write fixed, world-predictable temp paths: `mios-finetune-dataset` (`/tmp/mios-finetune-smoke.jsonl`, L413), `oscap-scan.py` (`/tmp/tailoring.xml`, L92) and `MiOS-Mon.py` (`/tmp/mios-cat-install.log`, L553) — symlink/TOCTOU-prone, and the oscap scan runs privileged. Replace each with `tempfile.mkstemp` / `NamedTemporaryFile(dir=...)` or an `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`-anchored path, cleaning up on exit; oscap specifically should write inside a 0700 `mkdtemp`. Then enable flake8-bandit/ruff `S108` (hardcoded-tmp) in the Python drift-gate so regressions are blocked, allowlisting only the `test_*.py` fixtures that legitimately embed `/tmp` string literals.
details.why: A privileged compliance scanner writing to a guessable `/tmp` filename is a symlink-attack primitive an unprivileged local user can exploit, and nothing else in the campaign touches temp-file safety.

title: Pin requires-python and add a Python 3.14 forward-compat drift-gate
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- ends the unmanaged 3.13/3.14 interpreter straddle by making the version a gated fact.
acceptance_criteria: `requires-python` is pinned to the bake's interpreter; the `-W error` import-smoke of all 122 tools passes on 3.14; CI produces no cpython-313 artifacts; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: No `pyproject.toml` / `requires-python` exists anywhere in the repo, yet the committed tree carries bytecode from BOTH cpython-313 and cpython-314 (mixed `__pycache__` tags) while MEMORY records 3.14 as the real CI path. Add `requires-python = ">=3.14"` to the new `mios_tools` pyproject so the floor is declared, then add a compat check to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that import- and exec-smokes every libexec tool under `python3.14 -W error::DeprecationWarning`, surfacing removed-stdlib and deprecation breakage before ship. Pin the gate to the exact interpreter the bake uses so the 313/314 ambiguity cannot recur.
details.where: `new pyproject.toml (requires-python); automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new compat check); resolves mixed usr/libexec/mios/__pycache__ tags`
details.why: With zero declared version floor a stdlib removal in the next interpreter breaks the bake with no warning, and the mypy task pins types while nothing pins the interpreter those types are checked against.

title: Standardize CLI argument parsing across the 27 argparse-less tools with a --help/--version contract test
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- gives a third of the runtime tools an actual, testable CLI contract.
acceptance_criteria: All 27 tools use the shared scaffold; every entry-point passes the `--help`/`--version` contract test; goldens capture the usage strings; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: 27 libexec Python tools hand-roll `sys.argv` with no argparse/click/typer — `mios-dotfiles-render`, `mios-os-control`, `mios-pg-query`, `mios-registry`, `mios-sync-toml`, `mios-template-engine`, `mios-theme-render`, `mios-toml-get`, `mios-account-sync`, `mios-cephfs-provision` and the rest — so flags are inconsistent, there is no `--help` or `--version`, and positional parsing is brittle. Add a shared argparse-based CLI scaffold in `mios_tools` (uniform `--help`, `--version` read from package metadata, `--json` for the tools that already emit JSON) and convert all 27 onto it. Add a contract smoke-test asserting every packaged entry-point exits 0 with non-empty usage on `--help`, feeding the same trycmd/golden harness the projectors use.
details.where: `the 27 argparse-less tools under usr/libexec/mios/ (mios-dotfiles-render, mios-os-control, mios-pg-query, mios-registry, mios-sync-toml, mios-template-engine, mios-theme-render, mios-toml-get, mios-account-sync, mios-cephfs-provision, ...)`
details.why: The trycmd work only characterizes `--check` projectors, so these 27 hand-rolled parsers have no baseline at all — they cannot be safely packaged, ported, or refactored, and each behaves differently for the operator.

title: Build a golden characterization harness for the non-projector runtime tools before the refactors touch them
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- supplies the byte-parity safety net every strangler-fig demotion is supposed to prove itself against.

title: Introduce a stable mios-generate dispatch so the drift-gate stops hardcoding python3 tools/generate-*.py
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- decouples the gate from projector implementation language so ports become atomic.
acceptance_criteria: The gate and build invoke `mios-generate <name>` rather than raw `python3 generate-*.py`; swapping a projector's backing implementation requires no gate edit; every projector `--check` gate passes through the dispatcher; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` invokes each projector as a literal `MIOS_DRIFT_ROOT=$ROOT python3 $ROOT/tools/generate-X.py` (see `_gen_diag` L109-116 and the per-check calls at L149/881/912/935/3850), so every Rust port must hand-edit the gate and a half-ported gate can call the wrong implementation. Add a thin packaged console-script dispatcher `usr/libexec/mios/mios-generate <name> [--check]` that resolves name -> implementation (Python today, the Rust binary after each port) behind one stable contract, and repoint both the gate call sites and the build phases that regenerate projectors onto it.
details.where: `new usr/libexec/mios/mios-generate dispatcher; automation/98-drift-checks.sh (_gen_diag L109-116 + call sites); build phases that regenerate projectors`
details.why: Without this indirection each of the ~8 Rust-port tasks must patch `98-drift-checks.sh` itself, and a mid-port language straddle can leave the gate validating the old implementation while the build ships the new one.

title: Convert the drift-gate's degrade-open python3/tool skips into hard failures for security and law checks
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- closes the fail-open hole that lets security and law checks pass by being un-runnable.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs with `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`; removing the interpreter or `mios_tools` turns the security/law checks RED rather than skipped; benign optional checks still degrade-open; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` fails OPEN when `python3` or a tool is missing: `_require_python3` (L193-198) only records a violation under `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS`, and several security/law checks print `WARNING ... skipping` and then PASS (node+manifest L267-268, AI-hint coverage L398-399, names-registry L2080). Once `mios_tools` is an installed package, make the Python toolchain a hard build and gate dependency: default `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1` in CI, and reclassify the security/law-tier skips (SSOT projection, RBAC, egress, cosign) from WARNING-pass to violation when their toolchain is absent, leaving benign optional checks degrade-open.
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (_require_python3 L193-198; WARNING-skip sites L267-268, L398-399, L2080)`
details.why: A security gate that silently passes when its runtime is missing enforces nothing — the whole Python-hardening campaign is void if the gate policing it can be no-op'd by an absent interpreter in one CI image change.

Once the proptest differential parity proves agreement, make the packaged `mios_toml.py` EMIT `tools/lib/userenv.sh` and `automation/lib/globals.ps1`, converting check 27 from a hand-sync twin comparison into a regenerate-and-diff projector check, and regenerating the committed byte-copy rather than copying it. goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- gives the agent-pipe a real harness with coverage, the prerequisite for parity testing every migration slice.

title: Introduce pydantic wire-schema models for the FastAPI request/response bodies
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- puts typed wire schemas under the agent-pipe HTTP boundary ahead of the server.py decomposition.
acceptance_criteria: The two pilot handlers accept typed models; a malformed body returns 422 naming the field; `test_server_import.py` and the surface-parity gate stay green; the schemas package has a sibling test.

details.what_how: `server.py` handles bodies as raw dicts (`body = await request.json()` at L1743 and L5309, across 451 route-definition sites) with NO pydantic anywhere (verified: zero `BaseModel` imports). Create a `mios_pipe/schemas/` package with pydantic v2 models for the core wire contracts — chat-completions request/response, embeddings, the `/v1/dispatch` envelope, `/v1/agents/directory` — mirroring the OpenAI shapes already proxied. Convert the two `await request.json()` handlers (`lora_load` L1735, `v1_agents_directory` L5309) to typed params as the pilot slice and leave the other routes raw behind the same paths so typed and untyped coexist. Validation failures return 422 with field locations; set `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')` so unmodeled fields still pass through (degrade-open).
details.why: Raw-dict bodies at the HTTP boundary let a wrong-typed value travel deep into dispatch before failing (or worse, succeed with the wrong meaning), and there is no shared substrate for the per-cluster pydantic tasks until these models exist.

title: Add a typed exception hierarchy + operator-facing config diagnostics
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- replaces silently-swallowed SSOT failures with typed, spanned, gate-matchable diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed `[colors]` value raises a typed `MiosConfigError` naming the section/key with a span; absence of an optional section still returns `{}` degrade-open; a sibling test covers both paths.

details.what_how: Config and resolver failures in `mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` currently do `log.warning(...); out = {}` and swallow (the `_toml_section` except block ~L40), so a malformed `mios.toml` degrades silently to defaults with no pointer to the offending line. Define `mios_pipe/errors.py` as a typed exception tree — `MiosConfigError`, `MiosVerbError`, `MiosDispatchError` (the thiserror analogue) — plus a diagnostic renderer that reports the offending section/key with a BYTE-offset span (not char count, for correct UTF-8 highlighting) and actionable help text (the miette analogue). Wire it into `_toml_section` and `_cfg_num` so a bad `[colors]` or port value raises a typed spanned diagnostic drift-gates can match programmatically, while genuinely optional sections still degrade-open.
details.why: An operator who mistypes one SSOT value today gets a silently-defaulted system and a buried warning line — the worst failure mode in a config-projected OS, since the wrong behavior looks like correct behavior.

title: Kill the eval-on-agent-args launcher path in mios-launch/mios-window (TD-1)
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- eliminates the named TD-1 eval-injection surface from the verb library and gates its return.
acceptance_criteria: Neither file evals an agent-derived string; launcher behavior is verified against a golden of prior launch commands; the no-eval gate is green and RED against a deliberately planted eval; the `[laws]` entry is mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-launch` L507 still runs `eval exec "$_hit_cmd" '"$@"'` on an agent-resolved launch string (L721 even carries a stale `TD-1: Replace unsafe eval with shlex split` TODO), and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-window` L386 evals python-heredoc output — both argument-level injection boundaries reachable from the agent-pipe dispatch chokepoint `mios_dispatch.dispatch_mios_verb`. Replace each eval with a `shlex.split`-parsed argv array exec or an explicit case-based dispatch table keyed by the resolved verb, rejecting any token the SSOT `[verbs.*]` catalog did not declare. Add a `check_no_eval_on_args` drift-gate scanning `usr/libexec/mios/*` for `eval ` applied to agent-derived variables (allowlisting reviewed-safe sites), register it as candidate Law 14, and mirror the `[laws]` entry in BOTH repos per Law 15.
details.why: `eval` on agent-controlled arguments is direct remote-code-execution surface (cf. the Gemini-CLI eval-injection CVE) reached straight from the dispatch chokepoint, and the system's own rule is that agent input is never authorization.

title: Port jsonsalvage `loads_lenient` to a pyo3 crate proven by differential proptest
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- establishes the pyo3 strangler + differential-parity pattern the rest of the port campaign copies.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test` differential proptest shows Rust == Python for all generated inputs, the toggle switches implementations at runtime, `test_mios_jsonsalvage.py` is green under BOTH toggle states, and the crate is a workspace member staged explicitly.

details.what_how: `mios_pipe/routing/jsonsalvage.py`'s `loads_lenient` is pure and dependency-free (`re` + `json` only) and is the tool-loop rescue path used by `mios_dispatch` and `routing/toolexec`. Create `tools/native/mios-jsonsalvage` (added to `tools/native/Cargo.toml` `members`) exposing a pyo3 `loads_lenient`; reduce the Python module to a thin shim importing the compiled function, retaining today's body as a degrade-open fallback. title: Remove blocking subprocess.run from async handlers and lint the class shut
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- removes a live event-loop stall from the /v1 front door every agent request traverses.
acceptance_criteria: the three ceph probes run non-blocking, the AST lint reports zero `subprocess.run` inside `async def` and fails on a planted one, health endpoints return byte-identical bodies (golden parity), and the timeout resolves from env.

details.what_how: `server.py` calls blocking `subprocess.run(..., timeout=5)` inside async request paths — the ceph health/df probes at lines 1661, 1715 and 1722 stall the loop for up to 5s under load. Replace them with `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` + `await proc.communicate()` (the non-blocking pattern already present at line 3513) wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for`, or offload via `asyncio.to_thread`. Audit the whole file for `subprocess.run` and other blocking I/O inside `async def`, and add an AST-based `check_no_blocking_in_async` drift-lint. Float the timeout as `${MIOS_CEPH_PROBE_TIMEOUT:-5}` (SSOT with literal fallback).
details.why: One blocking call head-of-lines every concurrent request on the AI front door — this is measurable latency today, not cosmetics.

title: Route every outbound call through the pooled httpx client and gate ad-hoc clients out
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- makes connection pooling structural rather than a convention one code path already ignores.
acceptance_criteria: no `httpx.AsyncClient(` remains outside `_get_client`, the gate rejects a planted ad-hoc client, and planner requests reuse the pool with unchanged behavior.

details.what_how: `server.py` maintains a shared `_client: httpx.AsyncClient` via `_get_client` (line 1792), yet the planner path opens a FRESH `async with httpx.AsyncClient(...)` per call (line 4518; the line-1809 comment already flags the connect/teardown-per-write cost). Repoint the planner and any other per-call client through `_get_client()`, and add a `check_no_adhoc_httpx_client` drift-gate forbidding `httpx.AsyncClient(` anywhere outside the `_get_client` factory (factory allowlisted). Preserve degrade-open: fall back to a per-call client only when the shared pool is unset.
details.why: Every planner call currently pays a TCP connect and teardown on a hot outbound path that already has a pool sitting unused.

title: Derive the DCI act schema from a pydantic model instead of a hand-written dict
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- puts the deliberation layer's structured-output contract under a typed schema that cannot drift from its vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: dci.py is mypy-strict clean, the pydantic-generated schema is byte-identical to the golden of `_DCI_ACT_SCHEMA`, and `test_mios_dci.py` plus the server-free boundary gate stay green.

details.what_how: `mios_pipe/routing/dci.py` (733 lines) declares the DCI epistemic-act vocabulary as raw dicts (`_DCI_ACTS`, `_DCI_ACT_SCHEMA`, `_DCI_ACT_NAMES`) driving structured output, with `test_mios_dci.py` pinning the 14-act/6-family contract. Add full type hints (mypy-strict clean) and replace the hand-written `_DCI_ACT_SCHEMA` with a pydantic model whose `.model_json_schema()` REGENERATES the existing schema, asserted byte-identical against a golden of today's schema so the wire contract is untouched. Keep the `configure()` DI seam and the one-way server-free boundary (98-drift-checks check 6) intact.
details.why: Acts and schema are maintained separately today, so adding an act can silently produce a schema the model is never told about.

title: Replace kernel/config's ad-hoc readers with a typed settings model proven byte-equal to userenv.sh
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- collapses one of the three parallel resolvers into a typed schema and mechanizes the lossless-diff gate.
acceptance_criteria: the typed resolver's `MIOS_*` projection is byte-identical to userenv.sh across the corpus, the module is mypy-strict clean, the no-raw-`MIOS_TOML` gate (check 51) is still green, and new keys exist in both repos.

title: Generate the AI manifest from SSOT via a pydantic model
goal: E-09 One value, one name: the full de-duplication campaign -- stops the agent's advertised identity being authored a second time alongside the config it describes.

title: Property-test the council diversity/arbiter/blades invariants
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- proves the fail-closed and degrade-open invariants of the pure policy cluster instead of asserting them in comments.
acceptance_criteria: the three invariants hold under hypothesis for all generated inputs, the modules are mypy-strict clean, and the existing council tests plus the boundary gate are green.

details.what_how: The cluster is pure geometry/policy: `mios_pipe/routing/council_diversity.py` (212 lines; `select_diverse`, `should_bypass`, `medoid_index` over 768-d cosine), `mios_pipe/access/arbiter.py` (69 lines; deterministic `decide()` with deny-list/allow-list/tier-ceiling), `mios_pipe/scheduler/blades.py` (173 lines; SSOT blade capacity). Add full type hints plus hypothesis property tests encoding each stated invariant: `select_diverse` always returns a subset with pairwise similarity below threshold; `arbiter.decide` is FAIL-CLOSED for an unknown tier (ranks above the top); `blade_vram_budget` degrades open to the local scalar for an unknown blade. Keep all three server-free (one-way boundary) and their default-OFF byte-parity.
details.why: arbiter is a second-opinion security gate; example-based tests can pass while an unknown tier quietly ranks BELOW the ceiling and is allowed.

title: Type-harden the access security gates with a verdict golden and taint property tests
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- hardens the taint/HITL/quarantine boundary between agent input and the broker without touching its name-keyed contract.
acceptance_criteria: the `(verb,tier,taint)` verdict golden is unchanged, the three property invariants hold under hypothesis, the modules are mypy-strict clean, dispatch tests are green, and no symbol was renamed.

details.what_how: The access cluster is imported directly and name-keyed by `mios_dispatch`: `mios_pipe/access/policy.py` (445 lines; `_hitl_block_reason`, `_dispatch_pdp_reason`, `_dispatch_quota_reason`), `mios_pipe/access/firewall.py` (179; `_classify_verb_taint`, `_session_is_tainted`, `_is_external_url`), `mios_pipe/access/quarantine.py` (167; the CaMeL dual-context gate). BEFORE touching types, capture current verdicts for a matrix of `(verb, tier, taint)` as a characterization golden and assert unchanged. Then add full type hints and hypothesis property tests for the security invariants: a tainted session NEVER auto-allows a high-privilege verb; `_is_external_url` classification is TOTAL (no input returns None); the quarantine gate is a strict superset of the HITL gate. Rename nothing.
details.why: These untyped gates are the last thing standing between model-supplied input and host command execution, and nothing currently proves a tainted session cannot reach a privileged verb.

title: Harden mios_codemode, the model-controlled code-execution surface
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- makes the highest-risk agent path sandbox-mandatory and degrade-CLOSED, and moves it into the governed package.
acceptance_criteria: codemode lives under `mios_pipe` with a sibling test, every exec path is sandbox-wrapped, the no-eval/exec-of-model-output lint is green and fails on a planted violation, and degrade-closed is verified.

details.what_how: `mios_codemode.py` (230 lines, still an un-migrated top-level module) is the `code_mode` execution branch reached from the tool loop (`routing/toolexec.py` `_exec_tool_calls`). Migrate it to `mios_pipe/routing/codemode.py` (satisfying the modular-boundary and sibling-test gates), add full type hints, and harden it: enforce the `mios-sandbox` wrapper on EVERY execution path, forbid `eval`/`exec` of model output (asserted by a targeted drift-lint), and add a characterization test of sandbox-profile selection. Gate any behavior change behind a `[migration]` toggle; degrade CLOSED — refuse to run — when the sandbox is unavailable.
details.why: Executing model-authored code is the most dangerous verb path in MiOS, and today nothing mechanically guarantees it is sandboxed or that it refuses to run unsandboxed.

goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- hardens the fitness-function generator every server.py split task depends on, so the parity gate emits signal rather than noise.

title: Sandbox conductor.py: replace create_subprocess_shell with exec+StepSpec and Jinja2 Template with SandboxedEnvironment
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- removes the last model-reachable shell/template injection surface in agent-pipe, distinct from the mios_codemode path already covered.
acceptance_criteria: no `create_subprocess_shell` or bare `jinja2.Template` remains anywhere in agent-pipe (new drift-gate grep negative added), `StepSpec` rejects a free-form `cmd`, the injection proptest is green, and `pytest` + `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: `mios_pipe/routing/conductor.py` (89 lines, imported by `server.py`) executes `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(args.get('cmd',''), ...)` on a model-supplied shell string inside `run_step()`, and builds the workflow via unsandboxed `jinja2.Template(template_str).render(**params)` (server-side template injection). Replace the shell call with `create_subprocess_exec` over an argv list validated by a pydantic `StepSpec` (action enum + `argv: list[str]`, no free-form `cmd` field), swap the raw Template for `jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment` with autoescape, allowlist the permitted actions, and route non-shell actions through the existing verb broker instead of today's `Mock executed` stub. Add negative/injection tests proving a `$(...)` or `;rm` payload can no longer spawn a shell, plus a drift-gate grep that fails on any reintroduction.
details.why: Any prompt that reaches the conductor today can run arbitrary shell on the host as the agent-pipe user; this is the sharpest remaining RCE-class hazard in the AI plane and nothing else in the queue closes it.

title: Delete the global `os.environ = _StrippedEnviron` monkeypatch; strip quotes at read via a typed accessor
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- removes a process-global singleton mutation that silently undercuts the typed-config effort across the whole agent-pipe.
acceptance_criteria: the `os.environ =` assignment no longer exists (drift-gate grep negative added), env reads go through the typed accessor, a parity golden shows identical resolved values against the current stripped mapping, and mypy + pytest are green.

details.what_how: `server.py` lines 67-89 define `class _StrippedEnviron(collections.abc.MutableMapping)` and then run `os.environ = _StrippedEnviron(os.environ)` at import time, replacing the process environment mapping for every imported module and every child process just to strip surrounding quotes on read. Delete both the reassignment and the class. Add a typed `env_str(key, default) -> str` helper in `mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` beside the typed settings model that strips quotes at the single read site and preserves `${VAR:-LIT}` fallback semantics, then route the `MIOS_*` reads through it. Characterize with a golden that resolves the same values pre/post for a fixed env fixture.
details.why: Every module and subprocess inherits a mutated environment mapping with async/thread-surprising behavior, `os.environ` cannot be statically typed, and any typed settings model built on top of it is built on sand.

title: Add one fast-fail `just agent-pipe-check` gate DAG and wire it into the drift-gate and CI
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- gives the Python plane one ordered entrypoint so its gates run in a defined sequence rather than ad hoc.
acceptance_criteria: `just agent-pipe-check` runs the four gates in fail-fast order, a new drift-check invokes it and degrades open without the venv, the CI job exists, and the aggregate is green.

details.what_how: The campaign introduces several independent Python gates (mypy, pytest + coverage floor, ruff, the 800-line ceiling) with no single ordered entrypoint; `Justfile`/`justfile` and `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` already carry scattered agent-pipe checks (~lines 424-870). Add a `just agent-pipe-check` recipe that runs in fast-fail cost order: `ruff check` -> `mypy --strict` -> `pytest -q` with the coverage floor -> the module-ceiling scan, all scoped to `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe`. Add one `check_*` function in 98-drift-checks.sh that shells the recipe and degrades open when `/usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv` is absent (mirroring the unit's `ConditionPathExists` pattern), and register the corresponding CI job.
details.where: `Justfile, justfile, automation/98-drift-checks.sh, .github/workflows (or the repo CI entrypoint that runs the drift gate)`
details.why: Without one ordered target the per-tool gates run inconsistently between local and CI, so a contributor can land code that passes locally and fails the bake, and the WS-DEBT tasks have no defined sequencing backbone.

title: Add a ruff lint + format drift-gate over the 123-module agent-pipe Python tree
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- gives Python the lint/format/async-antipattern gate that Rust already has via clippy/rustfmt.

Add a `[tool.ruff]` section to the agent-pipe `pyproject.toml` with a curated ruleset -- pyflakes `F`, pycodestyle `E`, bugbear `B`, the `ASYNC` rules for the async service, isort `I` -- plus `ruff format --check`. goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- puts typed schemas and invariants under the GPU admission logic that gates every AI route.

details.what_how: `mios_pipe/scheduler/` is ~2493 lines across admission, batch, bench, evict, preempt (643), sched, slo, stress and vram with near-zero return-type coverage and no owning task (blades belongs to the council task and is excluded here). Add full type hints plus pydantic models for `VramBudget`, `AdmissionDecision`, `PreemptPlan` and `SloTarget`, and property-test the VRAM-fit and preemption math with hypothesis over three invariants: admission never over-commits a `VramBudget`, preemption is monotonic in priority, and evict never drops a pinned lane. details.why: An over-commit or non-monotonic preemption bug in this cluster strands the GPU for every lane at once, and today nothing -- no type, no test, no invariant -- would catch it before an operator's box wedges.

title: Type and golden the identity cluster (crl/principal/reputation) signing, revocation and scoring
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- pins the trust root that the A2A federation plane consults on every inbound agent card.
acceptance_criteria: `mypy --strict` is clean over `identity/`, the signature/CRL/reputation golden vectors are byte-stable, revoked and expired principals fail closed with typed errors, sibling tests exist, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `mios_pipe/identity/{crl,principal,reputation}.py` (~432 lines) implements principal identity, certificate revocation and reputation scoring feeding a2a/agentcard verification, but is untyped and untested. Add type hints plus pydantic models for `Principal`, `CRLEntry` and `ReputationScore`; add typed errors for revoked, expired and unknown principals wired into the typed exception hierarchy; and add deterministic golden vectors using a fixed test keypair proving signature verification, CRL membership and reputation aggregation are stable. Ensure the revoked and expired paths fail closed rather than degrading open.
details.why: A regression that made verification pass for a revoked principal would be invisible today, and it would admit an untrusted federated peer into the agent plane.

title: Register the 5 orphaned native crates as workspace members and add a fmt/clippy build-gate
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- makes the Rust plane actually buildable and lint-gated so every downstream compiled-resolver task is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: `members[]` lists all 8 crate dirs; `cargo build --workspace` is green; `check_native_workspace_clean` is in the dispatch array and passes `just drift-gate`; `check_ssot_lint_equivalence` no longer depends on `|| true` to hide a missing build target.

details.what_how: `tools/native/Cargo.toml` declares `members = [mios-drift-runner, mios-version-check, mios-wallpaperd]` only, yet `mios-ssot-walk`, `mios-ssot-lint`, `generate-names-registry`, `mios-aiplane-lint` and `mios-bake-plan` each set `version.workspace = true` (verified by grep), which requires membership -- so they are orphaned and `cargo build -p mios-ssot-lint` inside `check_ssot_lint_equivalence` (98-drift-checks.sh ~line 4880) fails and is swallowed by `|| true`, silently skipping the twin gate. Add all five crate directories to `members[]`, run `cargo build --workspace --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml` to confirm they compile as members, then add a new drift-check `check_native_workspace_clean` running `cargo fmt --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml --check` plus `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, registered in the `check_*` dispatch list.
details.why: The crate WS-RESOLVER must extend does not compile as a workspace member and the ssot-lint twin gate is a silent no-op today, so the tree reports green on a check that never ran.

title: Promote mios-ssot-walk from a 12-line stub to the typed SSOT of the section-partition constants
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- single-sources the sets that decide which keys are emitted, so the Rust and Python resolvers cannot disagree about the namespace.
acceptance_criteria: lib.rs exports the three reconciled constant arrays plus predicates; `cargo test -p mios-ssot-walk` includes the mios_toml.py set-equality test; the `meta/laws` stub list no longer exists; the crate compiles under `-Dwarnings`.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-ssot-walk/src/lib.rs` currently exports only `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS = ["meta","laws"]`, which DIVERGES from the authoritative Python sets in `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` (`EXCLUDED_SECTIONS = {containers,verbs,recipes,packages,dotfiles,btop,theme,install_phases,messages}`; `WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD = {ai,image,bootstrap,profile,sandbox,security}`; `WALK_EMIT_KEEP` = 21 names). Replace the stub with three `pub const &[&str]` arrays mirroring the Python sets verbatim plus `is_excluded` / `is_mostly_dead` / `is_emit_keep` predicates, and add a test that regex-extracts the Python literals from mios_toml.py and asserts set-equality token-for-token. Keep the Python sets as the temporary source of truth the test reads FROM, so this lands non-behaviorally and fails loudly if either side is edited alone.
details.why: The crate designated as the compiled resolver library ships partition sets that contradict the real resolver, so every function ported on top of it would emit the wrong key set from day one.

title: Port tier/layer discovery (layer_paths + _frags + _tier_dirs) into mios-resolver
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- reproduces the vendor<host<user precedence contract in the compiled resolver byte-for-byte.
acceptance_criteria: `layers::resolve()` returns an identical ordered path vector to `mios_toml.layer_paths()` across 4 fixtures (no mios.d, vendor-only fragment, all-tier fragments, env-overridden root); `cargo test -p mios-resolver` green including the Windows-normalization case.

details.what_how: Reimplement `mios_toml.py` `_tier_dirs()`, `_frags()` and `layer_paths()` (lines 43-87) in Rust: honor the same env overrides (`MIOS_TOML_ROOT`, `MIOS_VENDOR_TOML`/`MIOS_TOML`, `MIOS_HOST_TOML`, `MIOS_USER_TOML`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, the `*_TOML_D` fragment dirs), the `/usr/lib/mios/mios.d` vendor-fragment location (Law 1 USR-OVER-ETC), and lexical-by-basename ordering within a tier with tier-major precedence. Reproduce the Windows path normalization the userenv.sh heredoc performs (the `/c/... -> c:/...` regex at userenv.sh lines 126-135) so CI on Windows resolves identically. Add characterization tests that build a temp tree of monolith + mios.d fragments and assert the returned `Vec<PathBuf>` ordering matches a golden list captured from the current Python `layer_paths()` on the same fixture.
details.why: If tier ordering or fragment discovery differs by even one entry, every value the compiled resolver emits can come from the wrong layer, and a host override would silently stop applying.

title: Port deep_merge overlay semantics (empty-string-never-overrides) with golden unit tests
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- moves the subtlest overlay invariant out of two hand-maintained twins into one tested function.
acceptance_criteria: `merge::deep_merge` matches the Python result on all 6 golden fixtures including the empty-string-shadow case; a small property test confirms merge is associative over the layer order; `cargo test -p mios-resolver` green.

details.what_how: Reimplement the overlay rule shared by `mios_toml.py` `deep_merge()` (lines 89-99) and its byte-parity copy in the userenv.sh heredoc (lines 146-153): recursive table merge, non-empty scalars and lists overwrite, and the critical rule that an empty string NEVER overrides a non-empty lower-layer value. Implement over `toml::Value` (or figment's `Dict`) rather than the typed struct so unknown/free-form tables such as `[env]` survive the merge. Capture golden fixtures by running the Python `deep_merge` on ~6 layered inputs (empty-string shadowing, list replace-not-append, nested `[ai.vllm]` override, absent-layer no-op) and assert structural equality. Library function only -- not yet wired to emit.
details.why: The empty-string rule is duplicated in two twins and easy to break; a wrong merge silently writes a wrong value into a rendered Quadlet with no error anywhere.

title: Port get_aliases() -- the ~50-branch alias map -- as a data-driven table with a differential test vs Python
goal: E-09 One value, one name: the full de-duplication campaign -- consolidates the COMPAT-ALIAS logic that is currently forked across three implementations into one proven table.
acceptance_criteria: `aliases::for_path` matches `mios_toml.get_aliases` for 100% of paths in the real SSOT (differential test green); every multi-alias/extend branch (`identity.*`, `locale.*`, `ports.*`, `image.sidecars.*`, `services.webtools.*`) is covered; `cargo test` green.

details.what_how: `mios_toml.py` `get_aliases()` (lines 224-557) is the single largest divergence risk: ~50 prefix/exact-match branches mapping dotted paths to legacy `MIOS_*` aliases (`ai.vllm.* -> MIOS_VLLM_*`, `identity.username -> [MIOS_USER, MIOS_DEFAULT_USER]`, `portal.*`, `a2a.*`, the `image.sidecars.*` version-split, the `services.webtools` special cases, `bootstrap.dev_vm.*`), and `generate-names-registry/src/main.rs` already re-implements a SUBSET as `alias_for` -- a third copy. Encode the full map in Rust as an ordered match (or a table of `(matcher, emitter)` closures) preserving branch order and the multi-alias `extend` cases. Add a differential test that iterates EVERY dotted path from the real merged mios.toml, calls the Python `get_aliases` via subprocess and the Rust function, and asserts identical alias vectors. Do NOT retire the Python -- it remains the oracle.
details.why: This map is already forked three ways, and a single mismatched alias silently breaks whichever consumer reads the short name -- a failure that shows up as a missing env var at runtime, not as a build error.

goal: E-13 Ports are allocated from SSOT, not hand-assigned -- makes the compiled resolver the engine that floats every port out of `[ports]` on both platform twins.
acceptance_criteria: port dual-alias emission matches Python for all `[ports]` keys including the guacamole canon and stack offset; the test flags any globals.ps1 `MIOS_PORT_*` with no backing `[ports].<key>`; `cargo test` green.

Cross-check against the two static allowlists that must stay in sync: the `_ssot_lint_ports_dummy` array at `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` lines 312-325 and the `MIOS_PORT_*` fallback block in `automation/lib/globals.ps1` lines 95-113 (drift-gated by check 28). details.why: globals.ps1 still hardcodes a `MIOS_PORT_*` fallback block, so a Windows-side port can exist with no SSOT key and no one finds out until check 28 goes red or a service binds the wrong port.

title: Port the WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD / WALK_EMIT_KEEP canonical-emit gating
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- reproduces the suppression rule that keeps the exported namespace at ~2523 keys instead of tens of thousands.
acceptance_criteria: canonical-key emission matches Python for the real SSOT including every MOSTLY_DEAD-suppressed and EMIT_KEEP-retained case; the constants are sourced from `mios-ssot-walk` with no redeclaration; `cargo test` green.

details.what_how: Reimplement the emit-suppression the userenv.sh heredoc applies (lines 209-213) using the sets single-sourced in `mios-ssot-walk`: for a walked path whose top section is in `WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD` (ai, image, bootstrap, profile, sandbox, security), the section-generic canonical `MIOS_<PATH>` is SUPPRESSED unless it appears in `WALK_EMIT_KEEP` (the 21 names such as `MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT`, `MIOS_IMAGE_REF`); legacy aliases from `get_aliases` are still emitted regardless. Golden-test that the set of canonical `MIOS_*` keys emitted for the real SSOT equals the Python `exports_map` canonical key set (aliases handled separately).
details.why: Get this gate wrong and the compiled resolver either floods the environment with thousands of dead keys or drops a key like `MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT` that live consumers read -- either way the lossless env-snapshot diff fails.

goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- delivers the byte-identical export stream that lets userenv.sh be demoted to a shim losslessly.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-resolver --emit=shell` stdout is byte-identical to the mios-env-snapshot capture of the current userenv.sh on the vendor SSOT (`env -i`, `HOME=/nonexistent`, `LC_ALL=C`); shlex-quote parity is unit-tested including values with spaces, quotes and `$`; `cargo test` green.

details.what_how: Reimplement the final serialization steps of the userenv.sh heredoc: the `[env]` table emitted verbatim in sorted order (lines 221-226), the `referenced_names.txt` passthrough that emits `export V="${V:-}"` for names not already set (lines 231-240), and the shell-safe `export NAME=<shlex.quote(value)>` line format (lines 228-229). Implement shlex.quote equivalently (POSIX single-quote escaping) so the bytes match exactly. Golden-test the full stdout against a captured snapshot of `source usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh; env | grep ^MIOS_ | sort` produced by `mios-env-snapshot` under the same `env -i` / `LC_ALL=C` isolation.
details.why: 22 consumers source userenv.sh today; without proven byte-identical output there is no safe way to swap the emitter, and a single quoting difference would break a sourcing script at boot.

title: Decide and implement the mios_db_config authoritative-overlay boundary for the Rust resolver
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the compiled resolver reproduces every branch of the Python resolver, including the DB overlay, or scopes it out on the record.
acceptance_criteria: On the default (DB-inert) path mios-resolver output is byte-identical to Python; the DB-authoritative path merges the same overlay; a test proves default-path equivalence with the hook absent; the chosen boundary is documented in the crate.

details.what_how: `mios_toml.py`'s `load_merged`/`get`/`colors` each consult `mios_db_config.is_db_authoritative()` and deep-merge a DB-sourced config on top (lines 128-136, 170-179, 204-212). Choose one: (a) port a Rust client reading the same DB config through the pg loopback-in-pod path used by `mios-pg-query`, or (b) scope it out for v1 by having mios-resolver shell to the existing Python hook only when `is_db_authoritative()` is true, documented as the one retained subprocess boundary. Since `db_backed` ships inert, prefer (b): add a `--db-overlay` opt-in that invokes the Python hook and merges its JSON. Add a test asserting default-path output is identical whether or not the hook is compiled in.
details.why: The DB overlay is a live branch in all three public entry points — ignoring it silently breaks parity the moment `db_backed` is wired, and an undocumented omission makes the strangler slice dishonest.

title: Cut userenv.sh over to `mios-resolver --emit=shell` with the Python heredoc as fallback
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the first strangler cutover: the shell façade is unchanged while the compiled binary takes over behind it.

details.what_how: Wire the ported pipeline into `mios-resolver --emit=shell` so it produces the exact `export ...` stream. Then replace the embedded Python heredoc in `tools/lib/userenv.sh` (`_mios_load_unified`, lines 86-249) with `if command -v mios-resolver; then eval "$(mios-resolver --emit=shell)"; else <existing heredoc as FALLBACK>; fi`, leaving the pgvector bind post-step (lines 258-261) and the legacy-file compat block (lines 267-309) untouched. Because the file is byte-mirrored to `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` (check_userenv_parity, check 27) and staged into mios-bootstrap.git, apply the identical edit to both copies and mirror in both repos (Law 15).

title: Generate automation/lib/globals.ps1 from the resolver and delete its ~200 hand-maintained literals
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface -- the duplicated mios.toml resolvers collapse to ONE generated PowerShell module derived from SSOT.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh render of globals.ps1 produces zero diff against the committed file (check 130 `check_globals_generated` green); ports/colors/images derive from mios.toml so checks 28/52 are satisfied by generation rather than hand-editing.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/globals.ps1` is the divergent third resolver: ~200 hand-maintained `if($env:X){...}else{'literal'}` fallbacks for USERS/UIDs/PORTS/URLS/IMAGES/COLORS/UNITS (lines 36-221), kept aligned to mios.toml only by drift-checks 28 (ports) and 52 (images). Emit a PS module assigning `$script:MIOS_* = if($env:MIOS_*){...}else{'<SSOT-resolved value>'}` for exactly the keys globals.ps1 defines today, retaining only genuinely PS-host-specific bits (`Resolve-MiosVersion` fallback, Windows APPDATA/USERPROFILE paths at lines 164-166). Regenerate and stage the exact paths (never `git add -A`). LANDED DIFFERENTLY AND BETTER: there is no `.generated` sidecar — `automation/lib/globals.ps1` IS the generated artefact (same filename, so every dot-sourcing consumer is untouched), rendered in full by `tools/render-globals.py` from the SSOT resolver (~2000 constants, zero hand-written literals, no shim indirection), gated by check 130 `check_globals_generated` which byte-compares against a fresh render; generation runs through the Python resolver (`mios_toml`) rather than the not-yet-installed binary, with the emit logic mirrored in `emit_ps.rs` for when it is.
details.why: globals.ps1 was the only resolver not derived from mios.toml, so Windows values drifted from SSOT by default and two drift-checks existed solely to police that divergence.

title: Demote mios_toml.py's public API to a signature-preserving shim over `mios-resolver --emit=json`
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the widest-imported resolver surface reroutes through the compiled crate without a flag day.
acceptance_criteria: A unit test comparing both modes across the real SSOT shows every public function byte-identical; `MIOS_RESOLVER_NATIVE=0` forces pure-Python; the importer count is unchanged; `just drift-gate` and the agent-pipe tests are green.

details.what_how: Add `mios-resolver --emit=json` producing the merged config plus the full resolved `MIOS_*` map. Rewrite the PUBLIC functions of `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` (`load_merged`, `load_vendor`, `get`, `section`, `colors`, `get_aliases`, `walk`, `process_val`) to subprocess the binary and parse JSON when present, falling back to the existing pure-Python implementation when absent, preserving exact signatures so the ~13 importers and the agent-pipe tree need no edits. Keep `clear_cache()` semantics. Gate behind an `MIOS_RESOLVER_NATIVE=0` kill-switch. Ensure the userenv.sh fallback heredoc, which imports this module, can never recurse back into the binary.
details.why: Thirteen importers plus the whole agent-pipe tree depend on these signatures; without a shim the Python plane either stays on a second resolver forever or requires a simultaneous rewrite of every caller.

title: Emit /etc/mios/install.env from the resolver and reduce mios-sync-env to a wrapper
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- one typed serializer produces the derived env consumed fleet-wide, retiring a second quoting codepath.
acceptance_criteria: Binary-produced install.env is byte-identical to current `mios-sync-env` output on the vendor SSOT including secret eviction and bare quoting; `mios-sync-env --dry-run` output is unchanged; the fallback path works with the binary absent.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/system-sync-env.sh` (`mios-sync-env`) sources userenv.sh to regenerate `/etc/mios/install.env` in a strict BARE `KEY=value` form simultaneously safe for systemd `EnvironmentFile=`, `bash source` and `podman --env-file` (documented in its header). Add `mios-resolver --emit=install-env` applying the identical rules — evict `$`-bearing and whitespace values, emit no quotes — and the same secret-eviction policy the script enforces. Demote `generate_env()` to call the binary when present, keeping the sourcing path as fallback. Golden-test the emitter byte-for-byte against current script output on the vendor SSOT.
details.why: install.env is parsed by three mutually incompatible parsers; keeping a second hand-written serializer alive is a standing source of quoting bugs that break systemd units and podman at once.

title: Add a proptest differential gate proving mios-resolver == mios_toml.py == userenv.sh on random valid mios.toml
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- proptest differential oracles make the three-resolver equivalence a property, not a handful of examples.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-resolver differential` runs N proptest cases with all three resolvers agreeing, or shrinks and reports the minimal divergence; a new drift-check runs it in CI; generated `ai.vllm` inputs exercise the short-vs-long alias reconciliation (`MIOS_VLLM_*` vs `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*`).

details.what_how: Build a proptest generator emitting random-but-valid mios.toml documents sampling real sections and keys with type-correct values (`[ports]` ints including 53 and stack_id, `[colors]` hexes, `[ai.vllm]`/`[ai.sglang]` tables, `[image.sidecars]` `name:tag`, `[env]` free-form, bools, lists). For each document run all three resolvers — `mios-resolver --emit=json`, the mios_toml.py export reconstruction (reuse `tools/check-resolver-twin.py`'s `toml_vars` builder), and `source userenv.sh; env | grep ^MIOS_` — and assert the resolved key/value SETS are identical, letting proptest auto-shrink to a minimal failing document. title: Register the resolver-equivalence checks as first-class entries in mios-drift-runner
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the checks migrate into native `miosd` Rust so the gate stops being fragile bash.
acceptance_criteria: mios-drift-runner exposes resolver-shell/ps/install-env/names equivalence checks; runner and bash gate report the same pass/fail on the current tree; the runner is documented as the migration target for these checks.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-drift-runner/src/main.rs` is the Rust drift infrastructure coexisting with bash `98-drift-checks.sh`. Add the resolver parity and generation-equivalence checks (shell, PS, install-env, names) as first-class runner entries so they execute without the bash harness, mirroring how `mios-ssot-lint` is invoked: each shells to `mios-resolver --emit=<surface>` and diffs the committed artifact, reporting through the runner's existing result type. Keep the bash `check_*` functions authoritative until the runner is proven at parity by running both in CI and comparing pass/fail.
details.why: Every new check added only to the 6000-line bash gate deepens the dependency this epic exists to remove, and the native runner has no resolver coverage to prove itself against.

title: Route mios-env-snapshot through mios-resolver while keeping the lossless baseline byte-identical
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the compiled resolver becomes the source of the very lossless-diff baseline the GUP gates against.
acceptance_criteria: mios-env-snapshot output is byte-identical whether it sources userenv.sh or calls mios-resolver (empty diff); `check_resolved_env_lossless` green; the fallback still works with the binary absent.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot` resolves the full layered SSOT under `env -i`/`LC_ALL=C` and sorts `MIOS_*` for the lossless-diff gate, feeding `check_resolved_env_lossless` via `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py`. Point it at `mios-resolver --emit=shell` when the binary is present, falling back to sourcing userenv.sh, preserving the exact isolation (`HOME=/nonexistent`, XDG pins, the `MIOS_ROOT`/`MIOS_TOML` meta-key exclusion grep). Since the gate compares before/after snapshots this must be a no-op diff; confirm the closure emitter still reports the same emitted count.
details.why: If the oracle for losslessness keeps resolving through bash while consumers move to the binary, the GUP gate stops measuring what actually ships.

title: Characterize every PowerShell entry point against the generated globals module
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface -- the Windows leg of the strangler completes with the dot-source façade unchanged for every consumer.
acceptance_criteria: Each PS entry point's captured `MIOS_*` dump diffs empty before vs after the demotion; no consumer references a removed globals.ps1 internal; the Windows drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: After the generated globals module exists, verify the PS consumers that dot-source `automation/lib/globals.ps1` — `build-mios.ps1`, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscontrol-server.ps1` and any other `. globals.ps1` site found by grep — still see identical `$script:MIOS_*` values. title: Collapse the userenv.sh byte-mirror to one canonical shim and shrink or retire check 27
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the payoff of the cutover: two hand-maintained bash copies and the gate policing them both disappear.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical userenv.sh shim is installed at build with no hand-maintained byte-mirror, or check_userenv_parity is reduced to the shim; the build install path is verified; the change is mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: `check_userenv_parity` (check 27, 98-drift-checks.sh ~1757) exists solely because `tools/lib/userenv.sh` is byte-mirrored to `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` (`59-tools.sh` installs the former to the latter). Once both are the same thin `eval "$(mios-resolver --emit=shell)"` shim, install ONE canonical copy from a single source — have `59-tools.sh` install `tools/lib/userenv.sh` and delete the committed `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` — or keep both and shrink the parity check to the shim. Update the drift-check accordingly, stage exact paths, and mirror in mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15).
details.why: Once the logic lives in the binary, maintaining two byte-identical bash files plus a check to police them is pure carrying cost that also makes every future edit a two-repo, two-file operation.

title: Delete the embedded Python heredoc from userenv.sh once the parity gates are green
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the strangler's final deletion: the legacy slice is removed only after its replacement is mechanically proven.
acceptance_criteria: userenv.sh embeds no Python resolver; sourcing it with the binary present gives an identical env (snapshot diff empty); the missing-binary path errors loudly; shell-equivalence and differential gates green; mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: Once `mios-resolver --emit=shell` is drift-gated byte-identical, the differential proptest is green, and the binary is guaranteed present in the built image (cargo-built and installed by an automation phase), remove the ~160-line Python heredoc (`_mios_load_unified` body, lines 86-249) from userenv.sh, leaving only the `eval "$(mios-resolver --emit=shell)"` invocation plus the pgvector post-step and legacy-file compat. Make a missing binary a hard error rather than silently resolving nothing — fail-closed for the resolver, degrade-open only for optional overlays. Mirror to both repos.
details.where: `tools/lib/userenv.sh, usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh (mios-bootstrap.git mirror), automation phase that installs the binary`
details.why: A retained fallback that silently resolves an older, divergent view of SSOT is worse than an error — and leaving it forever means the duplication this campaign removed is only ever half-removed.

title: Add an oxidizr-style [migration] SSOT table for per-surface Rust/bash resolver selection

title: Gate the new crate dependency surface with cargo-deny and cargo-audit
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- the compiled tier gets the supply-chain story bash never needed, mirroring the OS-plane cosign gates.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` run in CI as drift-checks; deny.toml encodes the license allow-list; a planted advisory or banned crate fails the gate; Cargo.lock is committed and referenced by the SBOM step.

details.what_how: The resolver crate pulls figment/toml/serde/miette/thiserror/proptest — a dependency surface bash never had. Commit a `deny.toml` encoding the license allow-list (operationalizing the FOSS posture), banned- and duplicate-crate rules, and RustSec advisory policy, then wire `cargo deny --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml check` and `cargo audit` as new drift-checks alongside the existing NO-HARDCODE/pod-quadlets gates, honoring the negatives-before-main-gate ordering. `tools/native/Cargo.lock` (already committed) becomes the reproducibility SSOT feeding SBOM-not-hardcode. Keep the checks soft while the tools are missing in CI, then flip them gating.
details.why: Every crate added to the resolver is unreviewed third-party code shipped into the bootc image with no advisory or license check between it and the operator's machine.

acceptance_criteria: A malformed `[colors]`/`[ports]`/`[image.sidecars]` value produces a miette diagnostic with a correct byte-offset span into the offending layer file plus actionable help; a fixture covers each case; `mios-resolver --check-parse` exits nonzero with the report.

details.what_how: Use the thiserror/miette scaffolding from the crate skeleton: when figment deserialization or a domain validation fails — a non-hex `[colors]` value, a non-integer `[ports].x`, a malformed `[image.sidecars]` `name:tag` — attach a miette source span (byte offsets, not char counts, so UTF-8 highlights correctly) into the specific mios.toml LAYER file and emit a diagnostic with help text naming the offending SSOT key. Return `miette::Result` from `main` so `mios-resolver --check-parse` prints the highlighted report. Add malformed fixtures asserting the diagnostic names the right `[sect].key` and points at the right layer path.
details.why: Today a typo in a layered mios.toml surfaces as an unattributed resolver failure, and the operator has to bisect three layer files by hand to find which one they broke.
