title: Add a cargo xtask for cross-platform build+install+regen, replacing scattered raw-cargo invocations
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- one consolidated, shell-free workspace surface builds and regenerates everything the compiled tier owns.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo xtask build-resolver` compiles and installs mios-resolver on both Linux and Windows; `cargo xtask regen` reproduces every generated artifact with no diff; the ad-hoc `cargo build -p` calls in drift-checks route through the xtask; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Drift-checks and build phases invoke `cargo build --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml -p <crate>` ad hoc today (e.g. `check_ssot_lint_equivalence`). Add an xtask crate at `tools/native/xtask`, invoked through a `.cargo/config.toml` alias, with a type-checked `build-resolver` task that compiles mios-resolver in release mode and installs it to the image path the automation phase expects plus the Windows path the PS surface expects, and a `regen` task that runs every `--emit=*` generator and stages the exact output files. Repoint the relevant automation phase and drift-checks at the xtask instead of raw cargo.
details.where: `tools/native/xtask/ (new), tools/native/.cargo/config.toml (new), automation/59-tools.sh (or the native-build phase), automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
details.why: Scattered raw-cargo glue is where the two build scripts diverge and where a Windows path silently differs from a Linux one — the exact hazard the launcher-unification work exists to remove.

title: Author the unified-resolver ADR and populate the WS-RESOLVER roadmap section
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- the three-resolvers-to-one decision is recorded and cross-linked so an arriving agent picks the campaign up cold.
acceptance_criteria: The ADR is merged describing the unified resolver, cutover order, rollback toggle and parity gates; ROADMAP.md's WS-RESOLVER section lists the tasks and cross-links the relevant ADRs and Laws; the superseded checks are named.

details.what_how: Write an ADR (next number after ADR-0012) recording the decision to collapse the three parallel resolvers (mios_toml.py, the userenv.sh twins, globals.ps1) into the compiled mios-resolver crate with figment layered providers; the strangler-fig cutover ORDER (shell -> PS -> python -> install.env -> names); the oxidizr `[migration]` toggle rollback model; and the parity/differential fitness functions that gate it. Populate the barely-there WS-RESOLVER section of `ROADMAP.md` with this task set, cross-linking ADR-0011 (languages), ADR-0003 (SBOM-not-hardcode) and Laws 13/15, and naming checks 27/28/45/52 as the duplication being eliminated.
details.why: Without the record, the rationale for retiring four long-standing drift-checks lives only in this batch, and the next agent re-adds the resolver duplication it removed.

title: Generate automation/lib/globals.sh from the resolver and extend checks 28/52 to the shell twin
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the build-time shell resolver derives its ports/images/URLs from the single declaration instead of carrying its own.
acceptance_criteria: globals.sh is reproduced byte-identically by a fresh render; checks 28/52 assert the generated shell module against mios.toml `[ports]`/`[image]`; the firewall phases still resolve their ports; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/globals.sh` (292 lines) is the shell sibling of globals.ps1 and a FOURTH hardcoded resolver the task list ignored: it is dot-sourced in the pre-userenv bootstrap context by `automation/44-firewall-ports.sh`, `45-firewall.sh`, `46-sshd-port.sh` and `automation/lib/common.sh`, carrying its own `MIOS_PORT_*`/image/URL literals. Generate it from the resolver so the `${VAR:-LIT}` fallbacks come from SSOT, and extend `check_globals_ports` and `check_globals_image_parity` (98-drift-checks.sh ~1829/~1894), which already gate both globals files, to assert the generated shell module. LANDED DIFFERENTLY AND BETTER: `automation/lib/globals.sh` IS the generated artefact (no `.generated` sidecar, no shim), rendered by the same `tools/render-globals.py` pass as its PowerShell sibling so the two cannot diverge; checks 28 and 52 still pass because the renderer deliberately emits `: "${VAR:=value}"` and bare `else { <digits> }`, the exact shapes those gates parse; values carrying `}` or a quote fall back to `[ -n "${VAR+x}" ] ||`, and `.gitattributes` EOLs (`*.sh` LF, `*.ps1` CRLF) are honoured per file.
details.why: The PowerShell-only migration left the resolver the build-time firewall phases actually use unmigrated, so the duplication the operator flagged would only half-collapse and the build could open ports SSOT never declared.

title: Route agent-pipe kernel/config.py's re-rolled TOML readers through the resolver shim
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement -- the largest duplicate resolver, sitting in the hottest request path, is folded into the shared one.
acceptance_criteria: config.py has no private `deep_merge`/tomllib read path; server.py's imported surface diffs zero; agent-pipe tests and the drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` independently re-rolls the layered read (`_toml_section`, `_cfg_num`, `_dispatch_toml`/`_DISPATCH_TOML` with a lazy `import tomllib` around line 523) instead of calling `mios_toml.load_merged` — one of the ~13 independently re-rolled tomllib copies the crate exists to collapse. `gateway-agent/server.py` re-imports these names verbatim on the hot request path, and the one-way boundary enforced by check 6 must stay intact. Add characterization tests capturing current `[section]`/`[dispatch]` resolution, then replace the readers with calls into the mios_toml shim (which fronts the crate), preserving the module-level constant surface byte-for-byte.
details.why: Fronting only the mios_toml public API leaves agent-pipe resolving SSOT its own way, so the AI plane can read a different config than the rest of the OS on the same host.

title: Reconcile the generated workspace member list and gate generated-vs-committed Cargo.toml
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- one consolidated Cargo workspace whose membership is generator-owned and gated, not hand-edited.
acceptance_criteria: Generator members equal committed members including mios-resolver and mios-drift-runner; the new drift-check fails on any regen diff; the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `tools/native/Cargo.toml` is GENERATED by `tools/generate-cargo-manifests.py`, yet the committed file lists 3 members (mios-drift-runner, mios-version-check, mios-wallpaperd) while the generator emits a DIFFERENT 7-member literal that OMITS mios-drift-runner — so any hand-registered crate is clobbered on the next regen. Add mios-resolver, the 5 orphaned crates and mios-drift-runner to the generator's member list, and add a drift-check (e.g. `check_cargo_manifest_generated`) asserting that regenerating `tools/native/Cargo.toml` yields zero diff against the committed file, staging explicit paths.
details.why: Crates registered by hand are silently reverted on the next regeneration, and the generator currently drops mios-drift-runner entirely — a live drift no gate catches.

title: Add a bake phase that compiles the native workspace and installs mios-resolver into the image
goal: E-16 The bake plane -- the compiled resolver is actually PRESENT in every published image, so the shims have something to delegate to.
acceptance_criteria: The bake installs `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolver`; consumers use it when present and fall back when absent; bake-green and drift-gate green.

details.what_how: No automation phase compiles Rust into the bootc image today — only `98-drift-checks.sh` references cargo — and native tools ship as prebuilt binaries while `85-bake-plan.sh` selects native -> `tools/native/target/release` -> python at runtime (lines 23-33). Add `automation/NN-native-build.sh` running `cargo build --release` for the workspace and installing mios-resolver and its siblings to `/usr/libexec/mios` during bake, staging explicit paths, and wire userenv.sh and the globals surfaces to prefer the installed binary and degrade-open to the retained bash/python resolver when it is absent, mirroring the mios-bake-plan fallback pattern.
details.where: `new automation/NN-native-build.sh, automation/85-bake-plan.sh (degrade pattern to mirror), usr/libexec/mios/`
details.why: Every migration in this workstream terminates at a binary nothing currently builds into the image — without this phase the crate is unreachable at runtime and every shim permanently takes its legacy branch.

title: Port the post-resolve derived transforms (loopback-bool bind address and composed *_URL defaults) into mios-resolver
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one compiled resolver emits the COMPLETE env projection, including the values the Python resolver never produced, so no shell post-processing survives the port.
acceptance_criteria: the crate emits `MIOS_PG_BIND_ADDR` and every composed `*_URL` byte-identical to today's shell/PowerShell post-load steps, and the differential test against the captured output is green.

details.what_how: `process_val()` only covers stack_offset / port!=53 / bool / CSV, so the values computed AFTER the python resolver are invisible to it: `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh:258-261` maps `[pgvector].listen_loopback` (bool) to `MIOS_PG_BIND_ADDR` = 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0, and `automation/lib/globals.ps1:116-132` plus `automation/lib/globals.sh` compose the `*_URL` defaults (e.g. `http://localhost:$MIOS_PORT_HERMES/v1`, the pgvector DSN) from already-resolved port values. Model both classes as typed derived-value rules inside the `mios-resolver` crate — a bool→address rule and a port→URL composition rule — so the single binary emits them, and keep the degrade-open fallbacks (loopback-safe bind address, localhost URLs) when the source key is absent.
details.why: A naive port ships a resolver that silently drops the pgvector bind hardening (exposing the DB on 0.0.0.0) and every service URL, breaking Quadlets and firstboot with no gate red to warn anyone.

title: Port float_allowlist() / [build.float] into mios-resolver and repoint mios-version-lint off mios_toml
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- the `[build.float]` allowlist stays the ONE place a legitimately-pinned build input may live, and its enforcing lint keeps working after the resolver is demoted to a shim.
acceptance_criteria: the crate and the shim both expose `float_allowlist`, `mios-version-lint` reads it via the shim, and both the version-lint check and `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: `mios_toml.float_allowlist()` (`usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py:218-222`) resolves the `[build.float]` table from the vendor-only view and has exactly one real consumer, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-version-lint` — it is a PUBLIC resolver API that the shim-demotion tasks never enumerate. Add an equivalent accessor to the `mios-resolver` crate, expose it through the Python shim passthrough so the call signature is unchanged, and repoint `mios-version-lint` to read the allowlist via the shim/binary rather than importing `mios_toml` directly.
details.why: Today the demotion plan would remove a public entry point that a live gate depends on, so the version-lint gate goes red (or worse, silently allows a hand-pinned version) the moment the shim lands.

title: Rebind the R-subset-of-E var-closure gate (check 37) and the names.generated.txt emitter set to the resolver crate output
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the 767-to-~240 key minification keeps its safety net when the resolver it measures becomes a binary.
acceptance_criteria: check 37 collects the emitted set via the crate/shim and computes an identical closure result, `names.generated.txt` is crate-generated, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py:emitted_set()` shells out to the `userenv.sh` resolver to collect every emitted `MIOS_*` name — that set is the whole basis of check 37 (referenced-set must be a subset of emitted-set) — and its `EMITTER_SUFFIXES` list enumerates `userenv.sh`, `tools/lib/userenv.sh`, `system-sync-env.sh` and `names.generated.txt` as emitters-not-consumers. Once the shims delegate to the binary, repoint `emitted_set()` at the shim/binary so it still captures the FULL emitted set, add the resolver binary path to `EMITTER_SUFFIXES`, and make `usr/share/mios/names.generated.txt` a crate-generated artifact.
details.why: If the shim's emitted set differs by even one name the closure gate either false-fails and blocks every merge, or false-passes and orphans a consumer referencing a variable nothing emits.

title: Repoint the referenced_names staleness gate at the Rust generator and delete tools/generate-names-registry.py
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- one generator owns the alias map, ending the three-way fork behind the names registry.
acceptance_criteria: the staleness check invokes the native generator, `tools/generate-names-registry.py` no longer exists in the tree (deletion staged), `referenced_names.txt` and `names.generated.txt` regenerate byte-identical, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: The referenced_names/names staleness check in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` (~lines 2093-2141) regenerates the registry using the PYTHON `tools/generate-names-registry.py`, while a Rust `generate-names-registry` crate already exists and `mios_toml.get_aliases` carries a third copy of the alias map. After the crate owns `get_aliases`, switch the staleness check to invoke the native generator (or the resolver binary directly), then delete `tools/generate-names-registry.py`, staging the explicit paths rather than a broad `git add`.
details.why: Retiring the Rust crate's forked `alias_for` while leaving the Python generator alive keeps the fork the gate ACTUALLY runs, so the alias map can still drift between three implementations.

title: Implement MSYS/Windows drive-letter path normalization in mios-resolver matching userenv.sh normalize_path
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the lossless env-snapshot baseline holds byte-identically whether it is captured on the Windows host or the Linux CI runner.
acceptance_criteria: the crate emits identical normalized layer paths on win32 and linux, the unit test covers all three input forms, and the env-snapshot lossless gate is green cross-host.

details.what_how: The `userenv.sh` heredoc normalizes `/c/...` to `C:/...` on win32 (lines 126-135) and `automation/lib/globals.ps1` resolves the Windows-side layer paths; the crate must reproduce that or layer paths diverge by host. Add a `normalize_path` equivalent in `mios-resolver`, gated on `target_os` or an explicit flag rather than inferred from the input string, and cover it with a unit test over `/c/`-style MSYS inputs, `C:\` drive-letter inputs and plain POSIX inputs.
details.why: The GUP lossless-diff gate deliberately normalizes root paths; a crate that skips MSYS drive-letter normalization fails env-snapshot parity the first time it is driven from the Windows `build-mios.ps1` path.

title: Build the golden characterization corpus of layered mios.toml overlays capturing all three resolvers' current output
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the strangler-fig rule that byte-parity is PROVEN before any shell is deleted gets the captured pre-migration baseline it currently lacks.
acceptance_criteria: the fixtures and their captured baselines are committed (staged explicitly), `cargo test` consumes them, and every downstream golden/proptest/insta gate references this corpus rather than inventing its own.

details.what_how: Every byte-identical / insta / proptest gate task in this campaign assumes committed baselines exist; none do. Curate fixture overlays covering the real layering cases — vendor-only, vendor+host, +user, +`mios.d` fragments, an `[env]` verbatim table, and db-authoritative — and capture the CURRENT output of `mios_toml.py`, `userenv.sh` and `globals.{ps1,sh}` for each via `usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot` into committed fixture files under the crate's `tests/fixtures/`. This becomes the one shared characterization corpus every migration and gate task diffs against.
details.why: Without a captured pre-migration baseline every equivalence claim in the resolver port is unfalsifiable — "byte-identical" has nothing to be identical TO, so a regression ships green.

title: Mirror the resolver shim and binary into mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the compiled resolver lands in BOTH publishing repos at once, so the installer never runs a stale forked copy.
acceptance_criteria: the bootstrap repo carries the identical shim and binary/build recipe, a parity check or manifest asserts the two repos match, and both trees drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `userenv.sh`, `/etc/mios/install.env` and the alias/name surfaces are shared SSOT that the bootstrap installer depends on, and `mios-bootstrap.git` ships its own copies of the resolver. Law 15 DOUBLE-REPO-TRIPLE-CHECK requires shared SSOT surfaces to update byte-identically in both trees, so land the demoted shim plus the resolver binary (or its build recipe) in `mios-bootstrap.git` as well, and add a cross-repo parity assertion — a manifest of shared files with hashes, or a check that compares the two copies.
details.where: `mios.git usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh + tools/lib/userenv.sh, mios.git install.env producers, mios-bootstrap.git resolver copies`
details.why: Migrating only `mios.git` leaves the bootstrap installer resolving config with a stale fork — the exact cross-repo divergence Law 15 exists to prevent, and it surfaces as a mis-installed system, not a red gate.

title: Reconcile the two divergent EXCLUDED_SECTIONS semantics into one typed model in mios-ssot-walk
goal: E-10 One canonical name -- one confusable name stops standing for two different rules, so the walk's exclusion semantics are explicit and gated.
acceptance_criteria: the crate exposes both exclusion sets as named typed constants, the differential test asserting Python-set == crate emission-exclusion passes, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py:591` excludes `{containers, verbs, recipes, packages, dotfiles, btop, theme, install_phases, messages}` at WALK time (i.e. these sections are not emitted into the env), while `tools/native/mios-ssot-walk/src/lib.rs` excludes `{meta, laws}` for names-registry section-partitioning — two different sets serving two different roles under one name. Encode BOTH in the crate as distinct named typed constants (emission-exclusion vs partition-exclusion) so each consumer selects the right one, and add a differential test asserting `mios_toml.EXCLUDED_SECTIONS` equals the crate's emission-exclusion constant.
details.why: The section-partition promotion task moves `meta`/`laws` and would conflate the two sets; a single merged constant makes the walk start emitting `containers`/`verbs` into the environment, polluting every consumer's env with structured tables.

title: Add a bootstrap-ordering degrade-open guard so resolver consumers survive before the binary is installed
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the shim degrades open, so replacing a sourced bash resolver with a binary can never brick a login shell or firstboot.
acceptance_criteria: sourcing the shim with the binary absent degrades to the bash path with no error, the firstboot smoke test passes on a binary-less image, and the drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `etc/profile.d/mios-env.sh` sources `userenv.sh` on every login, and the firstboot producers (`usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-firstboot`, `forge-firstboot.sh`, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-firstboot`) source `/etc/mios/install.env` — all in early-boot or pre-bake windows where `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolver` may legitimately not exist yet. Make the shim's binary-selection fall back to the retained bash/python path when the binary is absent, never fatal under `set -e`, and make that fallback INDEPENDENT of the `[migration]` toggle (the toggle expresses preference, not availability). Add a smoke test that a fresh image with no resolver binary still resolves the env.
details.why: The `[migration]` toggle picks a resolver but does not cover the chicken-and-egg where the binary is simply not there yet; a degrade-closed shim bricks every login shell and every firstboot unit on the first boot of a new image.

title: Establish the mios-drift lib crate + Check-trait harness in miosd, absorbing mios-drift-runner
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the seam that lets 123 bash checks become native `miosd` checks without the gate ever going dark.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build -p miosd` yields `miosd drift-check --root <tree>` running the two seeded checks through the Registry, `miosd drift-check --list` prints their ids and descriptions, `mios-drift-runner` delegates to miosd with bash reachable only via `MIOS_DRIFT_LEGACY=1`, and `just drift-gate` is still green.

details.what_how: Create `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift/mod.rs` defining a `Check` trait (`fn id(&self)->&str`, `fn describe(&self)->&str`, `fn run(&self,ctx:&DriftCtx)->Verdict`), a `Registry` Vec, and `DriftCtx{root, soft, in_image, git_ok, incomplete_tree}`. Port the harness scaffolding from `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` lines 56-93 and 6198-6210 — `MIOS_DRIFT_CHECK_ROOT` resolution, `MIOS_DRIFT_CHECK_SOFT`, the `_violation` counter — and crucially the in-image skip semantics at lines 6180-6187 (`CTX` set OR `$ROOT == /tmp/build` implies in_image; non-empty `git ls-files --deleted` implies incomplete_tree) so ported checks skip identically. Move the two existing checks in `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs` (SSOT-parse and `check_backfill_coverage`) into the registry as the first `Check` impls, then rewrite `tools/native/mios-drift-runner/src/main.rs` (today a pure `bash 98-drift-checks.sh` shim, lines 15-30) to exec `miosd drift-check`, keeping the bash exec path reachable behind `MIOS_DRIFT_LEGACY=1`.
details.why: Without a façade that encodes the exact ROOT/soft/CTX skip semantics, every family port re-implements them slightly differently and the gate starts skipping (or failing) in the bake where nobody is watching.

title: Build the bash-vs-Rust golden-master + differential parity harness for drift checks
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- no bash check is deleted until its Rust twin is proven to red and green in exactly the same situations.
acceptance_criteria: `bash tests/drift-parity.sh` exits 0 with every co-defined id agreeing bash-vs-Rust on the clean tree and on its negative fixture, `cargo insta test` and the trycmd fixture pass, and the parity harness runs as a `just drift-gate` step.

title: Add the [migration] SSOT toggle with oxidizr-style per-family Rust/bash opt-out and rollback
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- rollback is a first-class deliverable: any ported family reverts by flipping one operator-visible SSOT value, never a build revert.
acceptance_criteria: setting `[migration].drift_families.ports = "bash"` makes `miosd drift-check` run the bash ports family and `"rust"` runs the Rust one, the parity harness is green under both settings, `[migration]` is byte-identical in both repos, and `check_law_enforcers` / gate-index are unaffected.

details.what_how: Add a `[migration]` table to `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` with `use_rust_drift = true` and a per-family map `drift_families.<family> = "rust"|"bash"` (defaulting to rust once a family passes parity). Teach `miosd drift-check` to read it through the resolver and, per family, run either the Rust `Check` or the still-present bash `check_*` function — since sourcing `98-drift-checks.sh` is not side-effect-safe, add a `--only <fn>` dispatch shim inside the bash file that runs one named check. Both implementations keep shipping. Mirror the `[migration]` block into the bootstrap repo per Law 15 (both CIs consume it) and keep the literal default (`${...:-rust}`) so a missing key degrades to Rust.
details.why: Without a per-family switch, a single bad port can only be undone by reverting the build, which means a red gate blocks the whole tree while the fix is written.

title: Make the gate-index / gate-registry / negatives-ratchet meta-gates hybrid-aware
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one global numbering system spans bash and Rust checks so the ordinal SSOT survives the migration.
acceptance_criteria: after moving a check to Rust and deleting its bash function, `check_gate_registry`, `check_gate_index` and `check_negative_test_coverage` stay green, `drift-gate-index.tsv` remains dense 1..N with the Rust check present, and both repos hold the identical index.

details.what_how: Three self-referential gates assume every check is a bash function registered in `main()`: `check_gate_registry` (lines 4620-4691, parses `check_*(){` definitions against `main()` calls 1:1), `check_gate_index` (line 4917, runs `tools/generate-gate-index.py --check` to regenerate `drift-gate-index.tsv`), and `check_negative_test_coverage` (lines 4769-4852, requires a `test_*` per listed check in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`). Porting a check to Rust deletes its bash function and false-fails all three. Extend `tools/generate-gate-index.py` to merge the bash `main()` registration with `miosd drift-check --list` (id + description) into ONE dense 1..N ordinal SSOT, and update the three checks to consume that union so a Rust-only check keeps its ordinal and still requires a negative test. `drift-gate-index.tsv` is a shared SSOT surface, so mirror the regenerated file into the bootstrap repo (Law 15).
details.why: Until the meta-gates span the hybrid population, the very FIRST port turns the gate red and blocks every subsequent migration task in the workstream.

goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one compiled engine backs ~20 projection checks instead of 20 near-identical bash blobs.

MIOS_ROOT=$ROOT python3 gen --check`, and `check_egress_firewall` lines 918-925, render-to-tmp then `diff -q`). details.why: Porting 20 projection checks one-by-one without this shared runner re-implements the clean-env isolation 20 times, and any copy that gets it wrong reproduces the recurring quadlet-digest false-drift.

title: Port check_names_registry onto the existing generate-names-registry Rust crate
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the strangler pattern is proven end-to-end (build native tool, prove byte-parity, delete the script) on a low-risk check.

title: Build a figment-based Rust resolver and differential-test it against the userenv.sh/mios_toml.py twins
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- one typed resolver replaces the three parallel string-munging resolvers that TD-3 and the GUP both point at.
acceptance_criteria: the proptest differential test passes for 1000+ random configs (Rust == both twins), the six Rust checks match bash verdicts on clean tree and negatives, the twins remain reachable behind the toggle, and the `check_userenv_parity` port is unblocked.

details.what_how: Create a `mios-resolver` crate deserializing `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` into typed structs via `figment` (defaults -> vendor TOML -> vendor.d -> host -> host.d -> user, matching the layering exercised by `check_resolver_twin_parity` lines 3145-3165) and emitting the `MIOS_*` projection FROM the typed model. Port `check_resolver_twin_equivalence` (line 3181, today `tools/check-resolver-twin.py`), `check_resolver_twin_parity` (3132), `check_resolved_env_lossless` (6061), `check_raw_toml_readers` (735), `check_value_aliases` (6205, the `reference/value-aliases.tsv` derive/delete/keep-distinct decisions) and `check_no_duplicate_value_key` (6097). Add a `proptest` differential oracle generating random-but-valid `mios.toml` documents, running BOTH twins and the Rust resolver, and asserting the emitted key/value set is identical (shrinking divergences automatically). Keep the twins as fallback until parity is drift-gated, and return `miette::Result` so a bad `[colors]` entry or port points at the offending line.
details.why: Three hand-written resolvers must agree by discipline alone; when they silently disagree the wrong value reaches a Quadlet and the failure shows up as a broken service, not a red gate.

**Goal:** E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- co-locates the Law-14/16 conformance fitness function with the scaffolder that generates the files it judges.
**What+How:** Port `check_template_conformance` (:3202, today a delegate to `usr/libexec/mios/check-template-conformance`), `check_templates_compilation` (:3458), `check_verb_templates` (:5608) and `check_verb_backends` (:1776) into `drift/templates.rs`, reading `[templates.<type>]` and `[verbs.*]` from `mios.toml`. Follow the existing delegate pattern (`check_hint_coverage -> mios-ai-hint-coverage`) but enforce the required AI-hint headers and template markers natively instead of shelling Python, emitting byte-offset spans with `miette` labels that point at the offending line. Wire it against the `miosd scaffold` stub (`main.rs:46`) so authoring and validation live in one binary. Prove parity, delete bash funcs, re-register.
**Where:** `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift/templates.rs, usr/libexec/mios/check-template-conformance, automation/98-drift-checks.sh, usr/share/mios/mios.toml, usr/share/mios/reference/drift-gate-index.tsv`
**Done When:** The four Rust checks match bash verdicts on a clean tree and negatives; a non-conformant file produces a miette report labelling the exact offending byte range; bash funcs deleted; index dense.
**Why:** Conformance failures today report only a filename, so an author must bisect the template by hand — and the validator lives in a different language from the scaffolder that must satisfy it.
**Dep:** A1 regen runner, INFRA-5 hybrid registry

title: Port the hardcode-lint family and fix the unanchored-allowlist bug that exempts real port literals
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- restores the zero-hardcodes gate to actually catching the `:80xx` literals it currently waves through.
acceptance_criteria: The Rust family matches bash on a clean tree EXCEPT the documented spuriously-exempted literals, which are now flagged or floated; a unit test asserts `:8080` is no longer blanket-exempt; bash funcs deleted; index dense.

details.what_how: Port `check_no_hardcode` (:978, delegate to `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint`), `check_no_hardcode_version` (:998, `mios-version-lint`), `check_no_hardcoded_ssot_literal` (:6255), `check_canonical_bools` (:2485) and `check_fluff_tokens` (:3386) into `drift/hardcode.rs`. Reimplement the lint natively over `[security.nohc_allowlist]` (see `mios-hardcode-lint::_load_list` line 270) and FIX the known bug: allowlist entries match UNANCHORED today, so `:8080`, `:8033` and friends are silently exempted anywhere they appear. Anchor every allowlist pattern (full-token or `^...$` regex). Golden-capture the current buggy verdict set first, port with the fix, then show the diff is confined to the enumerated spuriously-exempted literals. Delete the bash funcs and retire the Python lints behind the migration toggle.
details.why: A live hazard, not cleanup: the unanchored allowlist silently defeats the entire zero-hardcodes campaign, so ports the operator believes are floating are in fact frozen in code and no gate says so.

title: Port the bare-port-literal / container-ports checks onto the typed ports model
goal: E-13 Ports are allocated from SSOT, not hand-assigned -- grounds port enforcement in the derived `[ports.categories]` model instead of a string allowlist.
acceptance_criteria: The three Rust checks match bash verdicts on a clean tree and negatives with the canonical set resolved from the typed model (no literal allowlist consulted); bash funcs deleted; index dense.

details.what_how: Port `check_container_ports` (:1390), `check_bootstrap_ports_drift` (:1468) and `check_no_bare_port_literals` (:1622) into `drift/ports.rs`, resolving the canonical port set from the typed `[ports.*]` / `[network]` model exposed by the D2 resolver crate — so a legitimate derived default such as `:11441` is recognised STRUCTURALLY rather than by matching an allowlist string. title: Port the DB->TOML materialize round-trip check (the 320-line embedded-Python blob) to Rust
goal: E-23 DB-driven configuration and vector recall -- makes the lossless TOML->DB->TOML round-trip oracle a typed, reviewable check instead of Python-inside-bash.
acceptance_criteria: The Rust round-trip check matches the bash verdict on a clean tree and reds on the mutated-verb-field fixture exactly as bash does; the bash function and its 320-line heredoc are gone from `98-drift-checks.sh`; index dense.

details.what_how: Port `check_drift_projection` (:2157-2482, gate check 31): 320 lines of embedded Python that mock psycopg (`MockCursor`/`MockConnection`), exec `seed-db-config.py` then `materialize-config-toml.py`, and assert the round-trip is lossless for the ports/ai/routing/pgvector/a2a/mcp/observability/sandbox/security/agent_passport/agent_pipe scopes, `routing.domains` and `verbs`, under the field-normalization rules at :2446-2470. Choose per parity feasibility between (a) reimplementing the mock-psycopg round-trip in Rust by parsing the SQL the two scripts emit, or (b) a strangler intermediate that runs the two scripts under a thin Rust-provided mock shim and diffs through the typed resolver. Validate on a clean tree AND on a deliberately-drifted verb-field fixture before deleting the bash function and its heredoc.
details.why: This is the single largest Python-in-bash blob in the gate; it is effectively unreviewable, and one wrong normalization rule would let real DB drift pass unnoticed while everyone reads the gate as green.

The equivalence check has a required negative — carry it forward until the twin is gone.
details.why: Two implementations of the same lint means every Quadlet-wiring rule must be edited twice and a whole extra check exists solely to police the duplication — cost with no product value.

title: Adopt miette+thiserror typed diagnostics across every ported drift check
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- gate failures become compiler-grade, actionable diagnostics pointing at the offending SSOT line.
acceptance_criteria: A bad `[colors]` or port value produces a miette diagnostic labelling the correct byte span; every existing greppable prefix still appears in output; `cargo test` insta diagnostic snapshots pass; the parity harness shows no verdict regression.

details.what_how: Retrofit the ported `Check` impls to return `miette::Result`: internal errors as `thiserror` enums the negatives harness can match on, user-facing failures as `miette` reports with source-span labels and help text pointing AT the offending `mios.toml` line/token. Spans must use BYTE offsets, not char counts, so UTF-8 content highlights correctly. Provide a shared `miette::SourceSpan` helper in `drift/diag.rs` mapping a `[section].key` to its byte range in `mios.toml`. Preserve the existing machine-greppable prefixes (`[98-drift-checks][diff]`, `[gate-registry-drift]`, etc.) by carrying them as miette `code`/`help` so downstream greps and `drift-gate-index.tsv` description capture keep working unchanged.
details.why: Bash emits an opaque one-line failure string, so an operator hitting a bad SSOT value has to hand-bisect `mios.toml` — and downstream tooling that greps those prefixes would break the moment the runner changes without this contract preserved.

title: Cut the default drift runner over to Rust and delete the retired bash families
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- `miosd drift-check` becomes the single source of drift truth, retiring `98-drift-checks.sh`.
acceptance_criteria: `just drift-gate` and both CIs invoke `miosd drift-check` as the authoritative gate; all 123 check verdicts are reproduced by Rust under the parity harness; `98-drift-checks.sh` is deleted or shimmed; `drift-gate-index.tsv` is dense and byte-identical across both repos; the rollback flip is documented.

details.what_how: Once all 28 family ports are parity-green under the toggle, flip `[migration].use_rust_drift` and the `drift_families.*` defaults to `rust` in `mios.toml`, mirrored into the bootstrap repo (Law 15 DOUBLE-REPO-TRIPLE-CHECK); repoint the Justfile `drift-gate` step (Justfile:100) and both CI workflows from `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh` to `miosd drift-check`; delete the now-empty `98-drift-checks.sh` or reduce it to a `MIOS_DRIFT_LEGACY=1` shim, including its `main()` registration. Regenerate `drift-gate-index.tsv` from the pure-Rust `--list` and confirm it is dense 1..N and byte-identical in both repos. Document an oxidizr-style one-flip rollback (`use_rust_drift=false`) for one release before final deletion. Stage every path explicitly — never `git add -A`, AGY shares the tree — and land via a real `git merge --no-ff`.

title: Replicate the gitignored-projection-absent skip and in-loop vs post-loop ordering semantics in the Rust runner
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- encodes the vacuous-PASS ordering invariant every ported projection check depends on, so the Rust gate cannot abort a bake.
acceptance_criteria: The Rust runner returns vacuous-PASS for absent gitignored projections and absent `/etc` overlays identically to bash; a test that removes ipa-enroll.env, cmdline and cockpit.conf passes; no false-fail when invoked pre-reprojection or against an incomplete in-image tree.

details.what_how: `automation/build.sh` documents that 98's projection checks — uki-cmdline (check 93), ipa-enroll (92), cockpit (95) — MUST vacuously PASS when their gitignored derived files (`etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env`, `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline`, `etc/cockpit/cockpit.conf`) are ABSENT at `$ROOT`, because the gate runs BEFORE the post-loop SSOT re-projection. A naive Rust port treating absent-target as FAIL aborts the bake. Encode `target absent -> skip`, the `/etc`-overlay-usually-absent semantics (`SCAN_DIRS` guarded by `-d`, ~line 84) and the CTX/ROOT in-image incomplete-tree skip as ONE shared `DriftContext` primitive consumed by every projection `Check`. Prove it with a characterization test that deletes those three files and asserts PASS.
details.why: This exact false-fail bankrupts the bake — it is the documented failure recorded in build.sh and in the drift-gate-local-verify notes; getting it wrong makes every ported projection check a build-breaker rather than a gate.

title: Make regen-and-diff snapshot/restore crash-safe and port `tests/drift-gate-readonly.sh` onto the binary
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- preserves the gate's read-only promise under the compiled runner, on a tree AGY edits concurrently.
acceptance_criteria: Rust regen-and-diff checks restore the tree byte-for-byte even under an injected panic; the drift-gate-readonly self-test passes against the binary; `git status` is clean after a full run with a forced failure; the `[diff]` evidence contract is byte-preserved.

details.what_how: 98's `_emit_projection_evidence` (~line 96) snapshots each target on a failing projection check, re-runs the generator IN WRITE MODE onto disk, diffs, then RESTORES the tree byte-for-byte — netting read-only. The Rust port must make that restore panic-safe via an RAII `Drop` guard so a mid-render panic or SIGINT cannot leave a mutated working tree. Port `tests/drift-gate-readonly.sh` to run against the binary and assert `git status` is clean after a full run INCLUDING a forced failure, and preserve the machine-greppable `[98-drift-checks][diff]` evidence prefix that downstream tooling greps.
details.why: The whole gate's read-only promise rests on this one restore path, and C:\MiOS is shared with AGY — a non-crash-safe port leaves phantom diffs in a tree another agent is concurrently committing.

title: Make the Rust drift runner Windows-native and drop the bash + python3 shim so the gate runs git-bash-free on win32
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the gate becomes runnable on the primary dev host without a POSIX emulation layer.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd drift-check` runs on win32 with neither bash/git-bash nor python3 available and yields verdicts byte-identical to the bash gate on the same tree; path and EOL normalization are verified by test; `mios-drift-runner` no longer shells out to bash.

details.what_how: `98-drift-checks.sh` opens with a `python3`->`python` fallback shim (~lines 62-72) and is otherwise pure bash, so on the win32 dev host it runs only under git-bash — and `mios-drift-runner` today merely shells `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh`. Make `miosd drift-check` the genuine cross-platform entrypoint: no bash, no `python3` in PATH, with CRLF and backslash-safe path handling (relevant because `check_impossible_eol_regressions` and the CRLF hazards live in this surface). Normalize separators and line endings inside the runner, remove the shell-out from `mios-drift-runner`, and differential-test git-bash vs native execution to prove identical verdicts.
details.why: The repo is developed on Windows with PowerShell primary while the entire gate is bash-only, so the conscience of the tree is flaky-to-untestable on the machine where the code is actually written.

title: Bless the Rust drift plane in Law 14 and regenerate the gate's own AI-hint self-reference as check families migrate
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- keeps the gate GREEN on its own artifacts while its checks move from bash to native `miosd`.
acceptance_criteria: New drift `.rs` files pass `check_target_languages`; the `AI-functions:` header and `mios-ai-hint-coverage` name no retired bash functions; `check_hint_coverage` is green after each family retires; mios.toml is byte-identical in mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git.

details.what_how: `check_target_languages` (automation/98-drift-checks.sh ~3814) enforces Law 14 (Rust is the native tier; `grandfathered_cs` may only shrink) and `check_hint_coverage` (~396) parses the `AI-functions:` header on line 4 that enumerates 98's `check_*` functions. Every family that moves to `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/checks/*.rs` and deletes its bash function invalidates that self-reference, so the gate flags ITSELF. Add/extend `[laws.target_languages]` in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` to bless the `.rs` drift plane, teach `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-hint-coverage` and the `AI-functions:` header to reflect the relocated checks, and re-run both after each strangler step. Mirror the shared mios.toml surface into mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15).
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check_target_languages ~3814, AI-functions header line 4, check_hint_coverage ~396), usr/share/mios/mios.toml [laws.target_languages], usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-hint-coverage`
details.why: Porting a gate that lints its own languages and headers is self-referential -- ignore it and the migration red-fails on the very files it just produced, blocking every downstream port mid-flight.

title: Model shellcheck and python-lint as a typed ExternalLinter check that survives cutover -- never delete them
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- no lint coverage is lost for the bash/python surface that legitimately remains after the Rust cutover.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd` runs shellcheck and py-compile through a typed ExternalLinter check with verdict parity vs bash; both degrade-open on a host lacking the tool; neither is removed by the final cutover; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check_shellcheck` (~4082, wrapping automation/lint-shell.sh) and `check_python_lint` (~4693, wrapping automation/lint-python.sh + py-compile) are not portable to Rust: they invoke external tools over the REMAINING bash/python code. Give the miosd check harness an `ExternalLinter` check variant that shells out to the tool, degrades-open when it is absent (matching today's WARNING/skip verdict), and stays registered in the dispatch set through and after cutover. Add an explicit exemption so the "delete retired bash families" sweep cannot remove these two.
details.why: A naive port-then-delete plan silently drops shell and python lint coverage over thousands of surviving lines -- exactly the regression class the rubric marks automatic P0.

title: Port the GUP value-unification trio to Rust, with root-path normalization baked into the env snapshot
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- the losslessness invariant that gates every namespace-collapse step runs natively and stops false-failing in CI.

details.what_how: Three checks drive the GUP and all consume `usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot`: `check_value_aliases` (~6255) asserts derive/delete pairs in `reference/value-aliases.tsv` resolve EQUAL while keep-distinct pairs resolve DIFFERENT (false-friends such as `MIOS_PGVECTOR_USER` vs `MIOS_PG_USER`); `check_no_duplicate_value_key` (~6097) flags the ~79 duplicate-value keys; `check_resolved_env_lossless` (~6061) diffs the snapshot against `reference/env-baseline.txt`. title: Port the resolver-discipline lints: check_raw_toml_readers + check_verb_backends
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- nothing may bypass the single resolver, and every declared verb must have a real backend.
acceptance_criteria: Rust flags raw `MIOS_TOML`/mios.toml readers in agent-pipe and verbs with a missing backend, byte-parity vs bash, honoring `test_*` exemptions; negatives green.

details.what_how: `check_raw_toml_readers` (~735) scans `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/**.py` and flags any module reading `os.environ['MIOS_TOML']` directly or hardcoding an `open()` of mios.toml, enforcing rule B11 (all reads go through `mios_toml.load_merged()`/`load_vendor()`); `check_verb_backends` (~1776) parses `mios.toml [verbs.*]` and asserts each declared backend actually exists on disk. Port both to Rust -- a regex/AST-lite scan for the raw-reader anti-pattern and a TOML walk for backend existence -- preserving the `test_*` exemptions.
details.why: B11 is the guardrail that keeps the new Rust resolver the ONLY config entrypoint; unported, agent-pipe modules silently reacquire private config paths and the SSOT stops being single.

title: Port the network-fetch degrade-open and retired-technology regression guards to Rust

details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check_curl_retry ~4177, check_vendor_urls ~3102, check_impossible_eol_regressions ~3478, check_vendored_assets_non_stub ~6038), SCAN_DIRS, mios.toml, usr/share/mios/vendored`

title: Unify the template placeholder vocabulary into one SSOT-declared token set
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- one token vocabulary so every generator renders the same templates identically.
acceptance_criteria: No template file contains an undeclared `{{token}}`; `mios new <type> <name>` for every registered type emits zero residual `{{...}}`; the new drift-check fails when an undeclared placeholder is introduced; the table is byte-identical in both repos.

details.what_how: Three consumers disagree on placeholders: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-new` `render_template()` substitutes `{{name}},{{PascalName}},{{id}},{{title}},{{status}},{{date}},{{description}},{{image}},{{uid}},{{gid}},{{theme}},{{priority}},{{task_title}},{{task_id}}`; `usr/libexec/mios/mios-template-engine` `render_template()` substitutes only `{{filename}},{{path}},{{description}},{{date}}` -- tokens that do not appear in the templates, so it leaves `{{name}}` unrendered; `tools/compile-templates.py` `MOCK_VALS` is a third partial set. Add a canonical `[templates.placeholders]` table (token -> description/mock-value) to `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, point all three consumers at it, and extend the `check_templates_compilation` region (automation/98-drift-checks.sh:3458) to assert every `{{token}}` literal in `usr/share/mios/templates/` is declared and that scaffolding leaves zero `{{...}}` residue. Mirror the table into mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15).
details.why: The orphan engine is silently broken (wrong placeholder scheme) and the three schemes drift independently, so scaffolded files ship with literal `{{name}}` in them -- and porting any consumer to Rust would bake the divergence in.

goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- Law 16's enforcer becomes compiled, with the Python retained as a one-flag rollback.

details.what_how: Create `tools/native/mios-template-conform` (toml 0.8 + regex, matching the miosd/mios-ssot-lint dependency style) reproducing `usr/libexec/mios/check-template-conformance`: read `[templates.*]` from mios.toml, compile each `match` regex, walk the tree porting `mios-ai-tag.walk`'s ignore rules, verify `required_header` via the AI-hint header, verify `required_markers`, honor `usr/share/mios/templates/conformance-grandfathered.list`, and enforce the `[ai_tag].max_unconforming=0` ceiling. title: Self-consistency gate: every registered template must scaffold to a conforming file
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- the templates themselves become ground truth, verified round-trip.
acceptance_criteria: Every template round-trips to a conforming file; deliberately corrupting one template (removing its AI-hint or a required marker) fails the gate; the negative test asserts that failure.

details.what_how: Add a meta-check that, for each key in `[templates.*]`, scaffolds a mock file (via `miosd scaffold`/`mios-new`) into a temp dir and pipes it through the conformance checker, delivering the ROADMAP acceptance "a template that can't produce a conformant file fails the build." Implement it either as an extension of `check_templates_compilation` (98-drift-checks.sh:3458) or as a dedicated `check_template_self_conformance`, degrading-open when python3/cargo are missing (mirroring the SOFT-skip at check_template_conformance:3203). Add a negative in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` proving that dropping a template's AI-hint header turns the gate red.
details.why: A template can otherwise drift into producing non-conforming files that the scaffolder then propagates fleet-wide, with the conformance gate blaming the generated files instead of the template.

title: Split the one-size quadlet template into per-kind scaffolds (.container/.pod/.network/.volume)
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- every Quadlet kind is born conformant instead of born broken.
acceptance_criteria: Scaffolding each Quadlet kind produces a syntactically valid unit with the correct section header; all four pass the round-trip compiler; all four registered and mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: `[templates.quadlet].match` (mios.toml:11437) claims `.container|.pod|.network|.volume|.image`, but the single `usr/share/mios/templates/quadlet` body is a `.container` skeleton, so `mios new quadlet foo.network` emits an invalid unit. title: Make the grandfather list a monotonic, never-grow ratchet
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- makes de-grandfathering permanent progress rather than a reversible win.
acceptance_criteria: Appending any new line to the grandfather list turns the gate RED; removing lines passes; the recorded ceiling decreases as each ratchet tranche lands.

details.what_how: Today nothing stops a new non-conforming file from being papered over by APPENDING it to `usr/share/mios/templates/conformance-grandfathered.list` instead of conforming it. Add a drift-check that the list's line count never exceeds a ceiling recorded in `mios.toml` (e.g. `[ai_tag].grandfather_ceiling`) -- or, when git is available, that the list is a strict subset of its `git HEAD` version -- so the exemption set can only shrink. Wire it as its own numbered check in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` and add a negative test in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` asserting that appending a line fails.
details.why: A ratchet with no pawl is just a suggestion -- without monotonicity the two de-grandfathering tranches get silently undone by the next author who finds appending easier than conforming.

title: Emit miette-style spanned diagnostics from the Rust conformance checker
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- cashes in the compiled-checker port as a real operator-UX upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: A non-conforming file yields a spanned, help-annotated diagnostic on stderr while the machine-parseable summary line is unchanged; internal errors are matchable `thiserror` variants; golden snapshots updated and green.

details.what_how: The Python checker prints opaque lines like `path: Missing AI-hint header (required by systemd-unit)` with no location. In the `mios-template-conform` crate, model internal errors as `thiserror` enums and render operator-facing failures with `miette`: point the diagnostic at the exact byte span (the first non-comment line for a missing header, or where the missing marker was expected), using byte offsets so UTF-8 highlighting is correct, with help text (`run \`mios new <type>\`` / `add \`# AI-hint:\`` / `add an [Install] section`). Keep the one-line summary format that the drift-gate greps for byte-identical so the golden CLI snapshots still match -- the rich report goes to stderr only.
details.why: Today an author gets a path and a vague noun and has to hunt the offending line by hand; that friction is why people reach for the grandfather list instead of fixing the file.

title: Add the TD-8 doc-metric re-derivation drift-check
goal: E-02 Technical-debt retirement: the TD-1..TD-8 register -- closes TD-8 so documented line-count claims are derived, not asserted.
acceptance_criteria: An over-claimed line-count metric turns the gate RED; corrected claims pass; the `server.py` "~26k" claim is fixed and now gated.

title: Commit Cargo.lock as reproducibility SSOT and add a cargo-deny/audit supply-chain gate
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- gives the growing Rust tier the dependency-integrity gate bash never had.
acceptance_criteria: `Cargo.lock` is committed; `cargo deny check` + `cargo audit` run as a gate, green on the clean tree and RED on a banned-license or advisory-flagged dep; the gate SOFT-skips when the tools are not installed.

details.what_how: This campaign adds Rust crates (`mios-template-conform`, `mios-template-compile`) and folds in orphan crates, expanding the dependency surface. Commit `tools/native/Cargo.lock` (and `src/mios-rs`'s lock) as a reproducibility SSOT per SBOM-not-hardcode/ADR-0003, author `tools/native/deny.toml` (license allow-list operationalizing the FOSS posture, plus advisory and duplicate/banned-crate rules), and add a `check_supply_chain` drift-check running `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit`, SOFT-skipping when the tools are absent (degrade-open like the other cargo gates). Stage `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` with explicit paths.
details.why: Every crate added right now widens an unaudited transitive dependency surface with no lockfile in the tree -- so builds are not reproducible and a known-vulnerable or non-FOSS dep can land unnoticed.

title: Harden the templates-dir walk so a stray __pycache__ cannot false-RED the gate
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- removes an intermittent false-RED that undermines trust in the Law 16 gate.
acceptance_criteria: Planting `usr/share/mios/templates/__pycache__/x.pyc` leaves `check_templates_compilation` green; `mios new` help lists only real kinds; the characterization test and `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: `tools/compile-templates.py` `main()` does `for fn in sorted(os.listdir(templates_dir))` and marks any name absent from `[templates.*]` as "Not registered", so a working-tree `usr/share/mios/templates/__pycache__/` (gitignored at .gitignore:766-767 but present on disk during a build or a local drift-run) turns `check_templates_compilation` (Check 59) falsely RED. The same naive `listdir` in `usr/libexec/mios/mios-template-engine` `list_templates()` (which filters only `.list`) also pollutes the `mios new` kind menu. Guard both to iterate only regular files whose name is a registered template key, skipping directories and names starting with `.` or `__`. Add a characterization test that plants a `__pycache__` dir and asserts Check 59 stays green.
details.why: This is the documented "stale `__pycache__` pollution fakes SSOT drift" local-verify hazard biting a second gate -- a RED that depends on whether someone ran Python recently trains people to ignore the gate.

title: Scope the over-broad [templates.*] match regexes and add a shared vendored/generated exclude
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- fixes the root cause of the 430-line grandfather list before any ratchet is attempted.
acceptance_criteria: `check-template-conformance`'s `checked_count` drops to MiOS-owned files only; `conformance-grandfathered.list` shrinks after re-derivation; the both-repo parity check and `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: In mios.toml, `[templates.json-schema].match=^[\w./-]+\.json$` claims EVERY json in the repo (package.json, tsconfig, SBOM manifests, generated files); `[templates.typescript]` `\.ts$`, `[templates.toml-config]` `\.toml$` and `[templates.powershell]` `\.ps1$` are equally unscoped. Anchor each `match` to MiOS-owned directories (`^usr/share/mios/`, `^tools/`, etc.) and add a shared `[templates].exclude` glob list (`target/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`, `web_dist/`, `__pycache__/`, `.git/`, `vendor/`) consumed by `usr/libexec/mios/check-template-conformance` -- its walk already skips some via `mios-ai-tag` `SKIP_DIR` (mios-ai-tag:51) but the MATCH still claims them. Mirror the `[templates.*]` edits across mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: Unscoped patterns are why the grandfather list is enormous and why vendored/generated artifacts get conformance-claimed as MiOS source -- de-grandfathering without scoping first just conforms files MiOS does not own.

title: Declare explicit template match precedence and detect ambiguous multi-matches
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- makes type resolution deterministic so no file is validated as the wrong language.
acceptance_criteria: Every tracked file maps deterministically to exactly one winning template; a planted conflicting-comment double-match turns the gate RED; scaffolder and checker agree on the winner; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check-template-conformance` compiles `[templates.*]` into a list and `break`s at the FIRST dict-order match (check-template-conformance:87-99), so precedence is implicit insertion order and language-ambiguous: the extensionless Python tool `usr/libexec/mios/mios-new` matches `[templates.bash-tool]` (`^usr/libexec/mios/mios-[\w-]+$`) BEFORE `[templates.python-tool]`, and `automation/NN-x.sh` matches `automation-step`, `bash` and `bash-verb` with conflicting `comment` styles. Add an explicit `priority` field (or most-specific-wins resolution) to `[templates.*]` plus a lint that FAILS when one file satisfies two templates whose `comment` or `required_markers` disagree, and make `mios-new`/the scaffolder resolve the winner identically to the checker.
details.why: A Python tool is currently being validated as bash; the moment the patterns are scoped or reordered the mislabels move, silently changing which files are checked against which syntax.

title: Make the Law-16 conformance gate fail-closed in CI instead of silently no-op'ing
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- turns Law 16 from an asserted law into an actually-enforced one on every runner.
acceptance_criteria: Removing `mios-ai-tag` or `python3` in a CI-flagged run turns the gate RED rather than green; interactive runs still degrade-open; `just drift-gate` is green with tooling present.

details.what_how: `check-template-conformance` `main()` returns 0 with only a stderr warning when `mios-ai-tag` is absent (lines 46-49), and `98-drift-checks.sh:check_template_conformance()` (~3202-3206) SOFT-skips (`return 0`) when `python3` or the tool is missing -- so the entire Law 16 gate reports green while enforcing nothing. Because the checker is python3-only yet Law 16 is `applies_to="both"` (mios.toml:723), Windows CI never enforces it at all. Add a strict mode keyed on `CI`/`MIOS_STRICT` converting these soft-skips into hard failures (missing tagger or interpreter => non-zero), keeping degrade-open only for interactive runtime, and assert the tagger is importable before declaring PASS.
details.why: A Law-level gate that passes while enforcing nothing is worse than no gate -- right now Law 16 has effectively zero enforcement on Windows and on any runner missing the tagger, and the dashboard says green.

title: Extend the golden compiler to validate every registered type and fail-closed on missing validators
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- makes the round-trip compiler a real validator rather than a decorative pass.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered type is either validated or explicitly allowlisted-as-unvalidated with a recorded reason; a deliberately broken rust/systemd-unit/quadlet template turns Check 59 RED; toml/yaml with a missing parser fails closed under CI; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `tools/compile-templates.py` `compile_template()` validates only python/json/toml/yaml/bash and returns `None` (unconditional PASS) for rust, typescript, powershell, systemd-unit, quadlet, adr, markdown-doc, roadmap*, and drift-check -- so most types are never compiled. It also skips bash validation entirely on Windows (`if os.name != 'nt'`, line 80) and lets TOML/YAML pass silently when `tomllib`/`pyyaml` import fails (lines 57-62, 67-70): FALSE GREEN. Add real validators (`systemd-analyze verify` / a podman quadlet dry-parse where present, a syn/tree-sitter parse for rust+ts, a structural required-marker parse for adr/markdown/roadmap) and make an unavailable validator a HARD skip only under a documented allowlist, never a silent pass. This validation coverage must survive the later Rust port of the compiler.
details.where: `tools/compile-templates.py, usr/share/mios/templates/ (rust, typescript, powershell, systemd-unit, quadlet, adr, markdown-doc)`
details.why: The "golden round-trip compiler" green-lights the majority of template types without parsing them, and silently passes on Windows or without pyyaml -- so the compiled and structured types the campaign cares most about are the ones least checked.

title: Meta-lint the [templates.*] schema and enforce templates-dir <-> registry bijection
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- guarantees the registry and the directory cannot half-land out of sync.
acceptance_criteria: A `[templates.X]` with no matching file, a template file with no registry entry, a non-compiling or unanchored `match`, or a bad `comment` enum each turn the gate RED; both-repo parity green; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Nothing validates the `[templates.*]` table itself: that each `match` compiles as a regex and is anchored `^...$`, that `comment` is one of {hash,slash,md}, that `required_markers` is a list, and that the mapping is a full bijection -- every registered type has a file in `usr/share/mios/templates/` AND every file has a registered type. `compile-templates.py` checks only the file->cfg direction (flagging unregistered files, lines 106-108); the cfg->file direction and field validity are unchecked, so a half-landed cargo-manifest/systemd-timer/quadlet-split entry ships silently until scaffold time. Add `check_template_registry` (or fold it into compile-templates) covering field-schema plus bijection, mirrored per Law 15 in both repos.
details.why: The registry and the directory are two hand-maintained halves that diverge silently, and the incoming cargo-manifest/systemd-timer/quadlet-split additions are precisely the half-landed edits this bijection catches at commit time instead of at `mios new` time.

title: Hoist mios-new's hardcoded scaffold defaults (ADR next-id, drift-check id, roadmap-ws enums) into SSOT
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- puts the scaffolder's default VALUES under operator-defined SSOT instead of frozen in code.
acceptance_criteria: `mios new adr foo` assigns the true next sequential id; enum defaults resolve from `[templates.*]` with literal fallback; a golden fixture pins the computed output; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-new` freezes literals that go stale: `get_dest_path()` prefixes new ADRs with `0012-` (line 64) though ADRs already run past 0011, and `render_template()` hardcodes drift-check `{{id}}=99`, adr `{{status}}=accepted`, and roadmap-ws `{{theme}}='OS-Image & Build'`/`{{priority}}=P2`/`{{status}}=proposed`/`{{task_id}}=999`. title: Enforce shebang/LF-only/exec-bit for script templates and fix templates' self-referential AI-related
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- extends conformance from substring markers to the physical file properties bootc actually depends on.
acceptance_criteria: A CRLF, shebang-less, or non-executable script of a registered type turns the gate RED; scaffolded files carry an `AI-related` pointing at themselves; golden fixtures updated; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `check-template-conformance` checks only for an AI-hint header and substring markers; it never verifies a script's shebang, line endings, or exec bit -- even though `mios-new` writes `newline='\n'` + `chmod 0o755` (mios-new:186-193) while `mios-template-engine` prepends a shebang only when `AI-hint:` is absent (mios-template-engine:37-43), an inconsistency. Separately, the shipped templates set `AI-related` to the TEMPLATE's own path (e.g. `usr/share/mios/templates/python-tool` line 3 points at `/usr/share/mios/templates/python-tool`), so every scaffold inherits a wrong `AI-related`. Extend conformance for bash/python/powershell types to require a first-line shebang, LF-only endings, and (on bootc) the exec bit; and rewrite the templates so the scaffolder emits an `AI-related` pointing at the produced file.
details.why: LF/shebang/exec-bit are load-bearing on bootc and completely unenforced, and the self-referential `AI-related` means every scaffold ships a header pointing at the wrong file -- which the AI-tagger and every downstream agent then trust.

title: Reconcile Law-16 enforced_by to name both template gates and supply the missing compile-gate negative test
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- closes the law-to-check registry gap so Law 16's metadata matches its real enforcers.
acceptance_criteria: Law 16's `enforced_by` names both checks; a broken-template negative test drives Check 59 RED and is registered so `check_negative_test_coverage` is satisfied; both-repo parity green; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: mios.toml Law 16 (line 723) declares `enforced_by="98-drift-checks.sh:check_template_conformance"`, omitting `check_templates_compilation` (Check 59), which is wired into the run at 98-drift-checks.sh:6336 and also enforces the one-template rule. Separately, `check_template_conformance` is listed in `[testing.negative_coverage_exempt]` (mios.toml:11513) but `check_templates_compilation` is NOT, so the negative-coverage gate expects a negative test for it that does not exist. Add `check_templates_compilation` to Law 16's `enforced_by` string and author the negatives entry (a deliberately invalid template must turn Check 59 RED). Mirror the mios.toml edits across mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: A real Law 16 enforcer is invisible to the law's own metadata and to negative-coverage accounting, so the governance registry misreports what is enforced -- and an expected-but-absent negative test is an accounting hole that hides a missing eval.

title: Gate that generated=true templates are byte-reproducible from their generator
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- makes the `generated=true` claim verified rather than asserted.
acceptance_criteria: Editing a `generated=true` template so it diverges from generator output turns the gate RED; regenerating restores green; the quadlet-split scaffolds are covered.

details.what_how: `[templates.quadlet]` is `generated=true` (mios.toml:11441) -- produced by a generator, not hand-edited -- yet nothing verifies the shipped `usr/share/mios/templates/quadlet` matches what its generator would emit; this is the same drift class as the recurring "broad `git add` strips `@sha256` from generated Quadlets" hazard. Add a check (extending `tools/compile-templates.py` or a dedicated gate) that, for every `[templates.X]` with `generated=true`, re-running its generator yields byte-identical output and goes RED on divergence. This also gives the incoming `.container`/`.pod`/`.network`/`.volume` split a home as verified generated artifacts rather than hand-maintained files.
details.why: `generated=true` is currently an honor-system label -- one hand-edit or one broad `git add` desyncs a generated template from its source of truth, and the tree keeps shipping the stale copy.

title: Add `just template-gate`: run the toolchain in strangler-fig order with a no-delete-before-parity guard
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- encodes the port ordering so no fallback shim is deleted before its replacement is proven.
acceptance_criteria: `just template-gate` runs the four stages in order and is wired into CI; deleting a python producer without a green byte-parity fixture fails the guard; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: The template work has hard ordering constraints the individual tasks do not encode: golden fixtures + workspace membership + fmt/clippy must land BEFORE the Rust ports; vocab/routing SSOT unification BEFORE `miosd scaffold`; and no python producer (`mios-new`, `mios-template-engine`, `check-template-conformance`, `tools/compile-templates.py`) may be DELETED until the Rust binary passes ALL golden fixtures byte-for-byte. Add a `just template-gate` target (and matching CI job) running compile-templates -> scaffold-every-registered-type -> check-template-conformance -> cross-repo parity in dependency order as ONE gate, plus a guard that FAILS if any listed python producer is removed while its golden-parity test is not green.
details.where: `justfile (or Justfile), .github/workflows or automation CI entry, tools/compile-templates.py, usr/libexec/mios/{mios-new,check-template-conformance}`
details.why: Without one ordered gate and a delete guard, a port can remove the working fallback before the Rust replacement is proven -- and scaffolding breaks for everyone with no obvious culprit.

title: Add a PowerShell AST parse-gate to CI (the single highest-value PS gate)
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the 36 PowerShell scripts pass a real parse gate in CI.
acceptance_criteria: `lint-powershell.sh` exists and is invoked by both CI workflows and the build.sh drift phase; deliberately breaking any `.ps1` syntax fails the gate; a `check_powershell_parse` drift-check is registered; `bash automation/lint-powershell.sh` returns 0 on a clean tree and non-zero on an injected parse error; changes staged with explicit paths.

details.what_how: `build-mios.ps1` was unparseable for ~70 commits undetected because no PS parse check runs in CI. `audit_all.ps1` (lines 12-20) ALREADY implements the correct check via `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile` but is never invoked by `mios-ci.yml` (its drift-gate job, .github/workflows/mios-ci.yml lines 59-127, runs only lint-shell.sh/lint-python.sh/97-ssot-lint.sh/98-drift-checks.sh). Create `automation/lint-powershell.sh` mirroring `lint-shell.sh`'s structure (SCRIPT_DIR/ROOT resolve, degrade-open exit 2 when pwsh is absent, best-effort pwsh self-provision via apt/dnf) that globs every tracked `*.ps1` and runs `pwsh -NoProfile -Command` calling `Parser::ParseFile`, failing on any parse error. Wire it as a new step in BOTH `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` (drift-gate job, before 98-drift-checks) and `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml`, and add a `check_powershell_parse` function to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` so `just drift-gate` gates it locally too.
details.why: A syntactically dead build script survived ~70 commits because nothing parsed it -- the parser logic already exists in-repo, so the only thing standing between MiOS and that whole bug class was wiring.

title: Add a PSScriptAnalyzer static-analysis gate with a curated ruleset
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- gives PowerShell the clippy-equivalent lint tier the Rust and shell planes have.
acceptance_criteria: `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer` runs in both CI workflows against the committed settings file; injecting an `Invoke-Expression` on untrusted input fails the gate; the clean tree passes at the chosen severities; settings file and runner staged explicitly.

details.what_how: MiOS has NO PowerShell static analysis (grepping for `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer`/`PSScriptAnalyzer` across the tree finds only doc mentions). Add `automation/lint-ps-analyzer.sh` that ensures the PSScriptAnalyzer module (`Install-Module -Scope CurrentUser` best-effort, degrade-open like `lint-shell.sh`) then runs `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Recurse -Settings automation/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` over all tracked `*.ps1`, failing on Error-severity findings. Author `automation/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` as the curated ruleset (enable `PSAvoidUsingInvokeExpression`, `PSAvoidUsingPlainTextForPassword`, `PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments`, `PSAvoidAssignmentToAutomaticVariable`, `PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions`; style rules start Warning-only to keep the tree green, security rules at Error). Wire the step into `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` and `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml` after the parse-gate.
details.why: A parse-gate only proves a script parses -- `Invoke-Expression` injection, automatic-variable clobber and plaintext secrets all parse perfectly, and MiOS has 36 PS scripts with zero coverage for them.

title: Extract the duplicated mios.toml resolver into one shared PowerShell module
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- collapses the duplicated PS TOML resolvers to ONE implementation matching mios_toml.py's layer order.
acceptance_criteria: `MiOS.Toml.psm1` holds the single shared reader; both caller scripts import it with no inlined duplicate functions; a test script proves `[ports].ssh`, `[desktop].theme` and `[ai].vllm_port` resolve byte-identically before and after; the parse-gate stays green.

details.what_how: `Resolve-MiosTomlText` + `Get-MiosTomlValue` are copy-pasted into BOTH `build-mios.ps1` (lines 95 and 138) and `Get-MiOS.ps1` (lines 401 and 438) -- a third parallel resolver alongside `mios_toml.py` and `userenv.sh`. Extract the canonical regex-based reader into `automation/lib/MiOS.Toml.psm1` (or fold it into `installation/mios-common.ps1`'s existing `Get-MiosSsotValue` at line 30, itself a fourth partial copy) and replace all call sites with an `Import-Module`/dot-source of the single implementation. Keep behavior byte-identical: FIRST capture the current `Get-MiosTomlValue` output for a spread of `[section].key` lookups from `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` as golden fixtures, then prove the extracted module reproduces them exactly. This is the strangler seam that later lets a compiled resolver (`tools/native`) back the whole PS config surface.
details.why: Four parallel copies of the TOML regex already cost a real bug -- the UTF-8 PUA glyph fix landed in `build-mios.ps1` and never reached `Get-MiOS.ps1`, so the two entry points read the same SSOT differently.

title: Collapse the two same-named Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1 into one SSOT-floated proxy and delete the retired ollama port literals
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- one canonical implementation per PowerShell capability, with no second copy carrying stale constants.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n '11434\|11435\|11450'` over both files returns nothing; only one file contains a real implementation and the other is a verified forwarding shim; every port resolves from `MIOS_PORT_*` with a literal fallback; the PS parse-gate and `just drift-gate` are green; both repos carry the change.

details.what_how: Two DIFFERENT scripts ship under the name `Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1`: the 118-line `usr/libexec/mios/` copy floats every port through its `_MiosPort` helper off `MIOS_PORT_*` with literal fallbacks, while the 47-line `usr/share/mios/windows/` copy hardcodes retired ollama ports 11434/11435 and the 11450 AI-node Tailscale v4tov6 bridge. Fold the tailnet-bridge behavior into the floated libexec implementation (an `-AiNode` switch or a `MIOS_PORT_LLM_LIGHT`-driven v4tov6 branch) so ONE hardened script serves both the LAN-NIC and Tailscale cases; demote the `usr/share/mios/windows/` file to a thin shim that dot-sources/invokes the canonical one, keeping the `98-drift-checks.sh` allowlist entry at ~line 1665 valid. Strip 11434/11435/11450 entirely — they are retired by the /v1-only purge. Mirror into mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: Two different bodies under one filename is exactly the duplication smell the operator flagged — a caller cannot know which behavior it gets — and the retired ollama ports are live hardcodes violating both the zero-hardcodes and /v1-only campaigns.

title: Stop clobbering the `$args` automatic variable and put every hardened .ps1 under Set-StrictMode
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the loose-script surface gets the cheapest available bug-class elimination before it is ported.
acceptance_criteria: No script assigns to `$args`/`$input`/`$_`; every hardened script opens with StrictMode + `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`; `Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer` reports zero `PSAvoidAssignmentToAutomaticVariable`; all edited scripts still dot-source and parse clean; edits staged per explicit path.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1` assigns `$args = @('-NoProfile',...)` in its self-elevate block (~line 20), overwriting PowerShell's automatic `$args` — a latent argument-forwarding bug and a `PSAvoidAssignmentToAutomaticVariable` violation. Rename that local to `$psArgs`, then sweep every .ps1 with `grep -nE '\$args\s*='` for the same pattern. Add `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` plus `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` to the ~15 `windows/*.ps1` and `libexec/*.ps1` that set neither (`mios-window-foreground.ps1`, `mios-uia-dump.ps1`, `mios-tailscale-serve.ps1`, …), using `installation/mios-common.ps1` lines 11-12 as the model. Guard adoption by running the parse-gate plus a smoke dot-source of each edited file so nothing trips on newly-strict undefined-variable access.
details.why: Silent `$args` clobbering breaks argument forwarding at the elevation boundary (the user's flags simply vanish), and without StrictMode a typo'd variable reads as empty instead of failing, so provisioning scripts "succeed" while doing nothing.
