title: Extract the four-times-duplicated mios.toml resolver into one shared PowerShell module
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the PowerShell config plane reads SSOT through exactly one resolver, the seam a compiled resolver later slots into.

title: Strangler-decompose the 11k-line build-mios.ps1 into a MiOS.Build module behind a stable shim
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the Windows build monolith becomes testable, per-slice-hardenable modules without changing its CLI contract.
acceptance_criteria: `build-mios.ps1` is under ~1500 lines and imports the extracted modules; every extracted function has a passing Pester characterization test; a full build path still completes on MiOS-DEV; parse-gate + PSScriptAnalyzer + drift-gate green; each slice visible as a real `--no-ff` merge in both repos.

details.what_how: `build-mios.ps1` is 11011 lines / 92 functions spanning dashboard rendering (`Show-Dashboard` 1155, `Start-Phase` 1444), WSL/podman provisioning (`New-BuilderDistro` 2804, `Set-PodmanMachineStorageOn` 2463), build/export (`Invoke-WslBuild` 4942, `Export-WslTar` 5072, `Invoke-BibBuild` 5135) and branding/launcher install (`Install-WindowsBranding` 6032, `Install-MiosLauncher` 6532). Extract cohesive groups into `automation/lib/MiOS.Build/*.psm1` (Dashboard, Provision, Bake, Branding), reducing `build-mios.ps1` to a thin orchestrator that imports and dispatches; the top-level entrypoint name and CLI stay stable so old and new coexist. Characterize each group with Pester golden tests (invoke `-WhatIf`/dry-run where possible) BEFORE deleting the inline copy. Land each sub-module as its own `git merge --no-ff`, mirrored to mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: An 11k-line monolith stayed silently broken for 70 commits because nothing could parse or test it; until it is split, no piece of the Windows build can be individually verified, ported or compiled.

title: Strangler-decompose the 420KB Get-MiOS.ps1 web entrypoint into a MiOS.Install module
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the `irm|iex` front door shrinks to a bootstrap loader while its behavior stays byte-frozen.
acceptance_criteria: `Get-MiOS.ps1` is a thin loader importing the extracted modules; an `irm|iex` install still completes end-to-end on a clean Windows host; every extracted group has a passing Pester test; parse/analyzer/drift gates green; slices merged `--no-ff` in both repos.

details.what_how: `Get-MiOS.ps1` is 7193 lines / 65 functions / 420847 bytes and mixes the agreement gate (`Show-MiOSAgreement` 642, `Invoke-MiOSAgreementGate` 732), Windows tool install (`Install-MiOSWindowsTerminal` 1577, `Install-MiOSPwsh7` 1620, `Install-MiOSGeistFont` 1685), terminal theming (`Install-MiOSTerminalProfile` 1974), the live dashboard (`Show-MiosDashboard` 3913) and the `mios-*` verb wrappers (`mios-build` 4433 … `mios` 4747). Extract these into `automation/lib/MiOS.Install/*.psm1` (Agreement, WinTools, Theme, Dashboard, Verbs) and shrink `Get-MiOS.ps1` to a bootstrap that fetches deps then imports them, preserving the exact `irm|iex` contract as the stable facade. Golden-master the agreement-gate text and the verb-dispatch table before moving them; delete each inline copy only once its Pester parity test passes. Mirror to mios-bootstrap.git — this file is a shared SSOT surface (Law 15).
details.why: A 420KB script delivered over the wire and executed unread is both unmaintainable and a supply-chain liability — nobody can review what a user just piped into their shell — and per-slice hardening/compilation is impossible while it is one blob.

title: Build the Pester v5 + golden-master parity harness that every PowerShell port depends on
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- the PowerShell plane gets the shellcheck-equivalent oracle it never had, so refactors are provable rather than hopeful.
acceptance_criteria: The Pester suite runs in CI on both forges; golden snapshots exist for the TOML resolver, env projection, palette and oscontrol dispatch; deliberately mutating any of those outputs turns the suite red; the runner exits 0 with a skip notice when Pester is unavailable; fixtures and runner staged by explicit path.

details.what_how: Create `tests/powershell/` with a Pester v5 project, a `golden-fixtures/` dir and a runner `tests/powershell/run-pester.sh` that degrades open when pwsh/Pester are absent (the `lint-shell.sh` pattern). Seed it by capturing the CURRENT observable output of the behavioral functions as golden masters: `Get-MiosTomlValue` over a table of `[section].key` inputs, the `automation/lib/globals.ps1` `MIOS_*` env projection (dot-source and dump all `$script:MIOS_*`), `Get-MiosPalette` RGB tuples, and the `mios-oscontrol-server` route dispatch for canned request bodies. details.why: Every downstream decomposition and compile-port names this harness as its dependency; without a characterization oracle, each refactor of an untested 10k-line script is an uncontrolled behavior change shipped to operators.

title: Port mios-oscontrol-server.ps1 to a compiled .NET executor behind an SSOT-toggled shim
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the highest-risk network surface on Windows moves from loose script to type-checked compiled code, reversibly.
acceptance_criteria: The compiled binary serves every documented route with responses byte-identical to the captured fixtures; the .ps1 contains only shim logic; flipping the single `[migration]` key rolls back to the PS body; parse-gate green; the new key exists in both repos.

details.what_how: `mios-oscontrol-server.ps1` is a 1375-line / 28-function `System.Net.HttpListener` server exposing 20+ OS-control routes (`/launch`, `/window/move|resize|focus|state`, `/input/type|click|key-combo`, `/screenshot`, `/windows`) over Win32 P/Invoke. Port it to a compiled .NET executable reusing the `src/mios-launch.cs` precedent (which already P/Invokes `SetWindowPos`/`EnumWindows`), producing `src/mios-oscontrol/` built the same way `automation/support/deploy-tooling-live.sh` ships source-only tools. Strangler: keep the .ps1 as a thin shim that launches the binary when present and falls back to the PS body otherwise, gated by an SSOT toggle `mios.toml [migration] use_compiled_oscontrol` (oxidizr-style non-destructive opt-out). Capture every route's JSON response from the current PS server as golden fixtures and prove byte-parity BEFORE defaulting the toggle on.
details.why: An HttpListener that accepts keystroke, click and process-launch requests is the exact injection-prone boundary that must not be a loose script — a parse error or an unquoted string there is remote code execution on the interactive desktop.

title: Converge the four hand-rolled Win32 P/Invoke PS scripts onto the compiled src/mios-launch.cs
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- one compiled binary owns Win32 window control; the scripts become shims.
acceptance_criteria: One binary provides foreground/move/resize/dump; `grep -n 'Add-Type'` finds no P/Invoke block in the four scripts; golden fixtures confirm identical output; Linux callers are unchanged; parse/analyzer gates green; mirrored per Law 15.

Extend `mios-launch.cs` into a subcommand-driven executable (`foreground`/`move`/`resize`/`dump`/`click`), demote each PS script to a thin shim that shells the binary, and keep the Linux-side callers (`/usr/libexec/mios/mios-pc-control`, `mios-windows`, `mios-window-active`) invoking the same names. Capture each PS verb's current stdout/JSON as golden fixtures, port, prove parity, then delete the inline `Add-Type` P/Invoke blocks. Verify the compile path matches how `automation/support/deploy-tooling-live.sh` deploys source-only tools.
details.why: Four independent copies of the same unsafe interop surface drift apart and each carries its own marshalling bugs; a single compiled implementation removes both the divergence and three quarters of the memory-unsafe code.

title: Consolidate the five copies of UAC self-elevation into one hardened Invoke-MiosSelfElevate
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- one audited privilege-escalation path instead of five subtly different ones.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one elevation implementation remains; the other four scripts dot-source and call it; the Pester parity test passes for quoted/spaced arguments; parse/analyzer gates green; mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: The `IsInRole(Administrator)` + `Start-Process -Verb RunAs` block is copy-pasted at least five times: `installation/mios-common.ps1` `Invoke-MiosSelfElevate` (line 130, the intended canonical one), `preflight.ps1` (top), `usr/libexec/mios/Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1` (~17-22), `usr/share/mios/windows/mios-oscontrol-server.ps1` `-Install` path (105-112), and `mios-fix-wslg.ps1` — each differing in arg quoting, `PSCommandPath` handling and the `$args` clobber. Make `Invoke-MiosSelfElevate` the single hardened implementation (printf-`%q`-style argument escaping, no automatic-variable clobber, the existing NONINTERACTIVE guard) and replace the other four with a dot-source plus call. Characterize with a Pester test asserting the constructed elevated relaunch command line is byte-identical across all callers for a fixed argument set, including args containing spaces and quotes.
details.why: Five divergent RunAs builders means five chances of unescaped argument injection into an elevated process, and a fix applied to one copy leaves the other four exploitable.

title: Centralize scheduled-task registration (and the WindowsApps-alias avoidance) in one helper
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- one place resolves the interpreter path, so a known-fatal bug can only be fixed once.
acceptance_criteria: All four installers call `Register-MiosScheduledTask` and none resolves an interpreter inline; a Pester assertion proves the resolved path never contains `\WindowsApps\`; parse/analyzer gates green; the helper exists in both repos.

details.what_how: Scheduled-task registration is reimplemented in `mios-wsl-keepalive.ps1` (116), `mios-wsl-session-task.ps1` (56), `mios-oscontrol-server.ps1 -Install` (105-120) and `mios-igpu-server.ps1 -Install` — each independently re-solving the concrete interpreter path to avoid the unresolvable pwsh MSIX `WindowsApps` alias that yields `0x80070002` (a lesson documented in oscontrol lines 114-120), then building the action/trigger/principal and registering. Extract one `Register-MiosScheduledTask` helper into `automation/lib/MiOS.Win.psm1` (or `mios-common.ps1`) owning interpreter resolution, the hidden-window argline and the elevated principal, and refactor all four callers onto it. Golden-master the resolved interpreter path plus argline per task so the alias avoidance cannot silently regress.
details.why: The MSIX-alias bug already broke task registration once; with four copies, the next Windows change breaks it in the three nobody remembered to patch, and the tasks fail at boot with an opaque 0x80070002.

title: Project the PowerShell VT-console palette from mios.toml [colors] instead of four hardcoded RGB copies
goal: E-09 One value, one name: the full de-duplication campaign -- every hex is declared once in SSOT and derived everywhere, on the Windows side too.
acceptance_criteria: One PS module resolves the palette from `[colors]`; the four hardcoded RGB blocks are gone; editing a hex in `mios.toml` changes the PowerShell console output with no code edit; the drift-check goes red if the PS palette diverges from `[colors]`; parse-gate green; mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: The console palette is redefined in at least four PS places: `automation/lib/globals.ps1` `MIOS_COLOR_*` (lines 209-220), `installation/mios-common.ps1` `Get-MiosPalette` + `C`/`B`/`Rule`/`Write-MiosLine` (60-119), `Get-MiOS.ps1` `Get-MiosPalette` (1407) and `build-mios.ps1` — all hardcoding the same Hokusai RGBs while the Linux side already derives them via `mios-theme-render` under drift-check 25. Extend drift-check 25 (or add a sibling check) to assert the PS palette matches `[colors]`.
details.where: `automation/lib/globals.ps1 (209-220), installation/mios-common.ps1 (60-119), Get-MiOS.ps1 (1407), build-mios.ps1, automation/lib/MiOS.Console.psm1 (new), usr/share/mios/mios.toml [colors], automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check 25)`
details.why: Today an operator retheming `mios.toml` gets a Linux desktop in the new colors and a Windows console still painted in the old ones — the theme SSOT is silently false on half the product.

title: Float the remaining port/CIDR literals in windows/*.ps1 and extend the port drift-check to cover them
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- the last unscanned PowerShell blind spot gets a key to float to and a gate to keep it floated.
acceptance_criteria: Every `windows/*.ps1` port resolves from SSOT with a literal fallback; introducing a new raw port literal into any .ps1 turns check 28 red; intentional fixed values appear anchored in `[security.nohc_allowlist]`; parse/drift gates green; SSOT keys mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: `98-drift-checks.sh` check 28 (lines ~1852-1888) already gates `automation/lib/globals.ps1` port defaults against `mios.toml [ports]`, but does not scan the `windows/*.ps1` helpers, several of which still carry raw literals: `mios-oscontrol-server.ps1`'s `fwRemote` CIDRs (line 92) and its 11437 default, `mios-ai-node.ps1`'s 11450, `mios-tailscale-serve.ps1`'s served-port list and the `usr/share` Setup-proxy ports. Refactor each to resolve from `MIOS_PORT_*`/`mios.toml` with the current literal as a `${VAR:-LIT}` fallback (oscontrol lines 83-85 already model this), and extend the check-28 function to also scan `windows/*.ps1` for un-floated port literals against `[ports]`, recording legitimately-fixed values in `mios.toml [security.nohc_allowlist]` — anchored, to avoid the known `mios-hardcode-lint` UNANCHORED-allowlist bug that spuriously exempts real `:80xx` hits.
details.why: An operator who moves a port in `mios.toml` today gets a half-moved system — the Windows helpers keep talking to the old number — and retired ports keep reappearing because nothing scans that directory.

title: Add a Law-15 byte-parity drift-check for the PS files shared by mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- Law 15 becomes a machine-checked fitness function instead of a manual promise that has already been broken.
acceptance_criteria: The check compares SHA256 across both repos and fails on mismatch; it WARN-skips cleanly when the sibling tree is missing; appending a byte to one copy locally trips it; the roster lives in `mios.toml` and exists in both repos.

details.what_how: `build-mios.ps1`, `Get-MiOS.ps1`, `automation/lib/globals.ps1` and `installation/mios-common.ps1` ship in BOTH repos and must stay byte-identical under Law 15 (DOUBLE-REPO-TRIPLE-CHECK), yet nothing enforces it and the two `build-mios.ps1` have already diverged. Add a `check_ps_repo_parity` function to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that, when a sibling mios-bootstrap checkout is resolvable (via `MIOS_BOOTSTRAP_DIR` or a known path), computes and compares SHA256 of each enrolled file across both trees and fails on divergence, degrading open with a WARN when the sibling tree is absent (the existing optional-check convention). Declare the enrolled roster in `mios.toml` as `[law15.shared_ps_surfaces]` so the file list is SSOT-defined rather than hardcoded inside the check.
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh, usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([law15.shared_ps_surfaces] new), build-mios.ps1, Get-MiOS.ps1, automation/lib/globals.ps1, installation/mios-common.ps1`
details.why: Undetected divergence between the two published copies means an `irm|iex` user and a repo user get different installers from the same version tag — which is how the two `build-mios.ps1` silently drifted apart before.

title: Make the tracked powershell/profile.ps1 the sole profile source and stop embedding a heredoc copy
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- one file owns the shipped PowerShell profile; the installer copies rather than regenerates.
acceptance_criteria: The installer function contains no full profile body — only the redirector block; the deployed profile hashes equal to tracked `powershell/profile.ps1`; a Pester test asserts that byte-identity; parse-gate green; mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: `powershell/profile.ps1` (1078 lines) is the declared SSOT for the MiOS profile (oh-my-posh/fastfetch/PSReadLine self-heal), but `Get-MiOS.ps1`'s `Install-MiOSPowerShellProfile` (~line 3613) writes a thin `C:\` redirector AND embeds a full profile body inline — a second 1000-line copy free to drift from the tracked file. Reduce `Install-MiOSPowerShellProfile` to emitting ONLY the marker-delimited redirector block (`# >>> MiOS oh-my-posh init >>>`) that dot-sources `powershell/profile.ps1`, and have the installer COPY the tracked file to `M:\MiOS\powershell\` verbatim instead of regenerating it. Golden-master the redirector block and assert the deployed profile is byte-identical to the tracked source.
details.why: Two 1000-line copies of the same profile guarantee drift, so a fix committed to the tracked file never reaches installed machines and the two Windows hosts behave differently for no visible reason.

title: Harden mios-pipeline.ps1 as the FULL-FOLD orchestrator with StrictMode and phase characterization tests
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- the named single Windows orchestrator becomes a safe facade the monoliths can be migrated behind.
acceptance_criteria: The script runs under StrictMode with validated phase params; the Pester dry-run test pins the 11-phase order and the dispatch table and fails if either changes; `run-pipeline.ps1` still drives it non-interactively; parse/analyzer/drift gates green; mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: `mios-pipeline.ps1` (415 lines) is the canonical linear 11-phase Windows orchestrator that its own `.SYNOPSIS` declares as the replacement for the historical `build-mios.ps1` + `install.ps1` + `Get-MiOS.ps1` + `preflight.ps1` tangle, and `run-pipeline.ps1` (3 lines) already drives it non-interactively. Harden it: add `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest`, give the phase functions (`Invoke-PhaseStage`/`DevDistro`/`Overlay`/`Account`/`Install`/`Smoketest`) typed params with `[ValidateSet]`, make `Invoke-LegacyScript`'s fall-through to `build-mios.ps1` explicit and logged rather than implicit, and add a Pester test exercising each phase in `-DryRun`/`-NoPrompt` mode that asserts the phase ORDER and the legacy-script dispatch table. That makes it able to absorb `build-mios.ps1`'s logic incrementally as that monolith is modularized.
details.why: The FULL-FOLD names this file as the one orchestrator, but migrating four monoliths behind an untested, non-strict 415-line facade would move the tangle rather than remove it.

title: Harden the live mios-oscontrol-server.ps1 request boundary: input validation, launch allowlist, source scope
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- the still-shipping PS server stops being exploitable before the compiled port defaults on.
acceptance_criteria: The server rejects non-allowlisted launch targets, over-length type payloads and off-tailnet source addresses at the request layer; no request field flows into `Invoke-Expression` or an unquoted command; the malicious-input Pester suite passes; parse/analyzer gates green; mirrored per Law 15.

details.what_how: Until the compiled port lands, the live server accepts `POST /input/type` (`Invoke-TypeText` 779), `/input/key-combo` (`Invoke-KeyCombo` 929) and `/launch` (`Invoke-LaunchAndVerify` 1038) — an untrusted boundary that drives real keystrokes and process launches. Harden it in place: validate the app name in `Resolve-LaunchTarget` (1007) against an allowlist instead of a free `Start-Process`; cap `/input/type` payload length; enforce the tailnet/WSL source scope (100.64.0.0/10 + 172.16/12) in `Read-JsonBody`/request handling rather than relying on the firewall-only `fwRemote` rule at line 92; and confirm no request field reaches `Invoke-Expression` or an unquoted command string. Add Pester tests feeding malicious bodies — path traversal, oversized payloads, non-allowlisted app names, off-tailnet source — asserting each is rejected.
details.why: Anything that reaches this port today can launch arbitrary processes and synthesize keystrokes on the logged-in desktop, and the only current control is a firewall rule that a compromised LAN or misconfigured interface bypasses.

title: Unify the two divergent bootstrap repo-fetch paths into one integrity-checked, SSOT-sourced function
goal: E-21 One deploy front door: flatten every install path -- one repo fetch to one canonical checkout, with the clone source operator-defined.
acceptance_criteria: One function backs both call sites with git+zip fallback and sentinel verification; a failed/partial fetch fails loudly on both paths; the repo URL and dir resolve from `mios.toml [bootstrap]` with literal fallback; parse/analyzer gates green; the shared function is in both repos.

details.what_how: Bootstrap fetching exists twice with different semantics: `Get-MiOS.ps1`'s `Ensure-MiosBootstrapRepo` (line 115 — `git clone --depth 1` then a `codeload.github.com` zip fallback with TLS12 + `Expand-Archive`) and `installation/mios-common.ps1`'s `Ensure-MiosRepo` (line 150 — git only, exits on failure). Unify into one hardened `Ensure-MiosBootstrapRepo` in `mios-common.ps1`: git-first with the zip fallback, explicit TLS, and a post-fetch integrity check that the expected sentinel file exists (no silent success); have `Get-MiOS.ps1` call it. Float the repo URL and target dir from `mios.toml [bootstrap]` — `build-mios.ps1` already reads `bootstrap.mios_repo`/`bootstrap_repo` at lines 349-351 — with the current literals as fallbacks.
details.why: One path exits on failure and the other continues silently, so a bare-Windows install can proceed on an empty or half-extracted checkout and fail later with an unrelated error — and the clone source is hardcoded where an operator cannot redirect it.

title: Authenticode-sign the shipped Windows .ps1 from an SSOT-defined cert and verify it in a gate
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the Windows script plane gets an execution-integrity story to match Linux fapolicyd/UKI.
acceptance_criteria: The build signs the shipped .ps1 from the SSOT cert and skips cleanly when the key is unset; the verification check reports valid-signature-or-allowlisted for every shipped script; the cert path appears only in `mios.toml`; drift-gate green; keys in both repos.

details.what_how: The Windows-delivered scripts (`Get-MiOS.ps1`, `build-mios.ps1`, `bootstrap.ps1`, `usr/share/mios/windows/*.ps1`) ship unsigned and run under `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, so nothing attests what executes. Add a build-time `Set-AuthenticodeSignature` step whose operator signing cert is defined in `mios.toml [security]` and projected — never hardcoded, mirroring the MOK-cert-from-SSOT pattern — plus a verification gate using `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` status that runs on the Windows host and as a drift-check confirming every shipped script either carries a valid signature block or is explicitly allowlisted. Keep signing opt-in: degrade open when no cert is configured so unsigned dev builds still work.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/windows/*.ps1, Get-MiOS.ps1, build-mios.ps1, bootstrap.ps1, usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([security] signing cert key), automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
details.why: Today an operator pipes unsigned scripts into an elevated shell with policy bypassed, so a tampered mirror or MITM is undetectable — the Linux half of the same product refuses to run unattested code.

title: Provision pwsh + .NET SDK in the build/CI so the PowerShell and C# gates can actually execute
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- the runtime root of the whole PowerShell gate tree, without which every PS gate silently no-ops.

title: Replace the two committed Windows .exe binaries with a reproducible source build plus an SBOM gate
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- no opaque artifact ships without a build-recorded provenance chain (ADR-0003).
acceptance_criteria: `MiosServiceTool.exe` is produced from source in CI with its provenance in the SBOM; the drift-check fails when a tracked .exe has no reproducible source build or diverges from a fresh compile; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: `git ls-files` shows exactly two prebuilt binaries tracked in the tree — `usr/share/mios/windows/MiOS-iGPU-Server.exe` and `MiosServiceTool.exe` (PE32 Mono/.NET, 8192 bytes each) — with no source-build step anywhere (no `csc`/`dotnet build` in `automation/`), so neither can be verified against `MiosServiceTool.cs`. Add a build phase that compiles `MiosServiceTool.exe` from `usr/share/mios/windows/MiosServiceTool.cs` in CI (and locates/compiles the iGPU-server source, or records its absence), writes the compiler and source digest into the baked SBOM, and verifies the artifact byte-wise/functionally. Then stop committing the .exe, or gate that a committed .exe must match a fresh build. Incrementally: keep the committed binary as fallback until the built one proves parity, then delete it and gate. Stage only explicit paths.
details.why: `MiosServiceTool.exe` is load-bearing — it is the run-hidden wrapper behind every WSL scheduled task — yet nobody can prove the shipped bytes came from the committed .cs, which is an unverifiable supply-chain surface and a direct ADR-0003 violation.

title: Route every PowerShell secret prompt and secret file through one hardened Read-MiosSecret (kill the plaintext %TEMP% credential file)
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- collapses four ad-hoc credential-capture implementations into one hardened, gated helper so the Windows entry plane stops leaking secrets to disk.
acceptance_criteria: No tracked PS script writes a secret to a plaintext `%TEMP%` file; every secret prompt calls `Read-MiosSecret`; the new gate FAILS on a synthetic plaintext-secret write and PASSES on the cleaned tree; paste-capture is covered by a test.

details.what_how: `config/bootstrap/bootstrap.ps1` writes credentials in plaintext to `$env:TEMP\mios-secrets.env` (its `SecretsFile`) and carries a hand-rolled `Read-Secret`; `tools/fix-token-input.ps1` documents a broken `[Console]::ReadKey` masking loop that `Read-Host -MaskInput` already solves; `Get-MiOS.ps1` and `mios-build-local.ps1` each roll their own token capture. Write ONE `Read-MiosSecret` helper (SecureString in memory, `ConvertFrom-SecureString`/DPAPI if anything must persist, ACL'd to the invoking user, scrubbed on exit, never a world-readable `%TEMP%` path) in the shared `installation/mios-common.ps1` contract. Strangler-fig: land the helper, migrate call sites one at a time keeping the current prompt text byte-parity, then delete the ad-hoc loops and the plaintext temp path. Add a drift-check grepping for `mios-secrets.env` and for `Read-Host` without `-MaskInput` in secret contexts.
details.why: Today a real GHCR/API credential lands unencrypted in a world-readable temp directory on every operator box that runs bootstrap, and the duplicated masking loop is already known-broken for pasted tokens -- a live security defect, not a hygiene item.

title: Port the Windows computer-use surface (mios-pc-control.ps1 + mios-uia-dump.ps1) to a compiled binary
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- moves the largest remaining PowerShell-as-program surface onto the compiled tier so the agent's GUI control path is typed and tested (Law 14 TARGET-LANGUAGES).
acceptance_criteria: A compiled executor replaces both scripts; golden-master tests show byte-identical JSON for every subcommand including the `type` read-back reason codes; the .ps1 files are thin shims (or deleted) with shim parity proven; `cargo`/`dotnet test` and the drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: `mios-pc-control.ps1` is a 440-line Win32 P/Invoke computer-use surface (`SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event`/SendKeys/screenshot/`EnumWindows` plus a UI-Automation read-back `type` verifier), and `mios-uia-dump.ps1` is its 110-line UIA tree dumper; both are distinct from the window-launch/positioning in `mios-launch.cs` and from the oscontrol HTTP server. Port both into ONE compiled C#/.NET (or windows-rs) executor invoked by the Linux helper `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-pc-control`, preserving the strict SendKeys read-back verification (the anti-"LIAR" logic at lines 112-196) and the JSON envelopes verbatim. Strangler-fig: build the binary emitting byte-identical JSON, characterize every subcommand (screenshot/click/type/key/key-combo/window-*/screen-layout) against golden outputs, demote the .ps1 to a thin shim, then delete.
details.why: 550 lines of untested P/Invoke drive every GUI action the agent takes on Windows; without a golden oracle any reimplementation silently changes click/type semantics, and the read-back verifier that catches "the agent lied about typing" is exactly the logic a blind rewrite would break.

title: Unify WSL2 distro-name resolution behind Resolve-MiosDistro and gate the 'podman-MiOS-DEV' literal
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- removes a 16-file cross-cutting hardcode by lifting an existing generative resolver into the shared globals module.
acceptance_criteria: `Resolve-MiosDistro` is the single source of the distro name; the new drift-check FAILS on any new hardcoded `podman-MiOS-DEV` outside the allowlist; every migrated script still resolves the distro after the post-bootstrap rename `podman-MiOS-DEV -> MiOS-DEV` (registry match wins).

details.what_how: The literal `podman-MiOS-DEV` is hardcoded across 16 tracked `*.ps1` (mios-fix-wslg, mios-tailscale-serve, mios-wsl-keepalive, mios-wsl-session-task, Update-MiOSStartMenuShortcuts, mios-cloud-build, mios-windows-export, Reinstall-MiOSDEV, refresh-flatpak-shortcuts, Uninstall-MiOS, bootstrap.ps1, build-mios.ps1, Get-MiOS.ps1, powershell/profile.ps1, automation/mios-build-builder.ps1), while `mios-claude-mcp-setup.ps1` ALREADY resolves it generatively from `HKCU\...\Lxss` (preferring a distro whose name matches `MiOS`, else the default distro). Lift that registry resolver into `automation/lib/globals.ps1` as `Resolve-MiosDistro` with a `${MIOS_WSL_DISTRO:-podman-MiOS-DEV}` SSOT fallback, replace the literals script-by-script keeping the literal only as last-resort default, and add a drift-check banning a bare `podman-MiOS-DEV` outside the resolver plus its allowlist.
details.why: The post-bootstrap rename already breaks the literal, so 16 scripts silently target a distro that no longer exists -- and the generative fix is sitting unused in one file while the other 15 hardcode.

title: Sweep the ad-hoc regex TOML parsers onto the shared resolver and reconcile their conflicting port/color fallbacks
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- makes ONE resolver with ONE ordered layer-search list the only way a PowerShell script may read mios.toml (Law 8 SSOT-PROJECTION).
acceptance_criteria: No PS script parses mios.toml with its own regex; all read via the shared resolver over one layer-path list; the conflicting port/color fallbacks match `[ports]`/`[colors]`; drift-check 28 (or a sibling) covers these files, not just `globals.ps1`.

details.what_how: Beyond `globals.ps1` there are independent hand-rolled TOML readers that search DIFFERENT candidate paths with DIVERGENT fallbacks: `Set-MiOSWallpaper.ps1`'s `Get-ColorsFromToml` (layers `~/.config/mios`, `C:\ProgramData\MiOS`, `C:\Windows\Web\MiOS`), `Heal-MiOSLocalhostForwarding.ps1`'s `Get-MiosPort` (layers `M:\etc\mios`, `M:\usr\share\mios`, `C:\mios-bootstrap`; fallbacks open_webui=8033, cockpit=8090, searxng=8899, hermes_dashboard=8119), and `mios-tailscale-serve.ps1`'s baked `$SERVICES` table (open-webui=3030, cockpit=9090, searxng=8888, hermes-dash=9119) -- the same lanes resolve to CONFLICTING ports across scripts. Migrate every consumer onto the shared `globals.ps1` resolver with one ordered layer list, delete the ad-hoc parsers, reconcile the per-key `${...:-LIT}` fallbacks to `[ports]`/`[colors]`, and add a gate banning any `^\[section\]`-style regex TOML parsing in `*.ps1` outside the resolver.
details.why: Two MiOS scripts on the same host currently resolve DIFFERENT values for the same lane (cockpit 8090 vs 9090, searxng 8899 vs 8888) -- a live correctness drift that the globals-only check cannot see, so healing and serve-publishing target the wrong ports.

title: Establish an SSOT owned-artifact registry and gate install/uninstall symmetry
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- binds every host artifact MiOS creates on Windows to the uninstaller by construction, so create-sites can never outrun removal.
acceptance_criteria: One owned-artifact list exists in SSOT; the drift-check FAILS when a create-site produces an artifact `Uninstall-MiOS.ps1` does not remove; `Uninstall-MiOS.ps1 -WhatIf` enumerates every current task/service/firewall/registry/shortcut artifact.

details.what_how: MiOS PS scripts create host artifacts across many files -- scheduled tasks `MiOS-Autostart` and `MiOS-Resume-Bootstrap` (build-mios.ps1/Get-MiOS.ps1), `MiOS-WSL-KeepAlive`, `MiOS-WSL-Session`, the `MiOS-iGPU-Server` service+task, firewall rule `MiOS - igpu-llm ($Port/tcp)`, netsh portproxy maps, `HKLM\SOFTWARE\MiOS` + `\Wallpaper`, and Start-menu `.lnk` files -- but `Uninstall-MiOS.ps1` removes only a subset (distros, portproxy, some services), so each new create-site orphans silently. Declare an SSOT list of MiOS-owned artifact identifiers (task names, service names, firewall DisplayNames, registry roots, shortcut folders) in `mios.toml` and drive BOTH `Uninstall-MiOS.ps1` and a drift-check from it: the gate greps `Register-ScheduledTask`/`New-Service`/`New-NetFirewallRule`/`Set-ItemProperty` create-sites and fails if any produced identifier is outside the uninstall coverage set. Preserve Uninstall's dry-run default and KEEP-list safety.
details.why: Uninstalling MiOS today leaves live scheduled tasks, a running service and open firewall rules behind on the operator's machine, and the 6+ create-sites have no mechanical link to the uninstaller, so the gap widens with every new script.

title: Consolidate the three Start-Menu shortcut + icon generators into one hardened module
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- deletes triplicated WSLg icon/.lnk logic so the flatpak-shortcut workaround exists in exactly one place.
acceptance_criteria: One shortcut/icon module backs all three entry points; generated `.lnk` fields are byte-identical to the golden pre-refactor output; the icon-conversion and `.desktop` enumeration code exists exactly once; the PowerShell gate is green.

details.what_how: Three scripts re-implement overlapping WSL-flatpak Start-Menu `.lnk`/icon generation: `usr/libexec/mios/Update-MiOSStartMenuShortcuts.ps1` (438 lines: `resolve_icon`, `Convert-PngToIco`, `Clear-WindowsIconCache`), `tools/refresh-flatpak-shortcuts.ps1` (130 lines), and `usr/share/mios/ventoy/autorun/mios-stage-icons.ps1` (139 lines, icon staging). Extract ONE shared module covering icon resolve/convert, `wslg.exe` `.lnk` emission, `.desktop` enumeration and icon-cache clearing, and reduce the three entry points to thin wrappers. Strangler-fig: land the module, port `Update-MiOSStartMenuShortcuts` first with golden `.lnk` parity on Target/Arguments/WindowStyle/IconLocation, then fold the other two and delete the duplicated bodies.
details.why: The same fragile WSLg workaround is maintained in three copies, so a fix to icon resolution or cache clearing lands in one and silently rots in the other two -- the operator has already hit "apps not populating natively" repeatedly for this reason.

title: Consolidate the Windows OCI export/convert plane into a MiOS.Export module with characterization tests
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- de-duplicates the registry-auth and image-conversion logic that two self-described complementary scripts each carry.
acceptance_criteria: WSL-export, VHDX-convert and GHCR-fetch logic lives once in the shared module used by both scripts; `Set-StrictMode` is on in both; characterization tests cover the full target matrix; both scripts pass PSScriptAnalyzer and the AST parse gate.

details.what_how: `mios-cloud-build.ps1` (338 lines, BIB-via-podman) and `mios-windows-export.ps1` (421 lines, self-described "Complement to mios-cloud-build.ps1") duplicate the WSL-tarball export, VHDX conversion, and GHCR layer pull/auth paths (`Get-GhcrToken`, `Resolve-ImageRef`, `Save-ImageLayers`), and both re-declare `Write-Step`/`Write-Ok`/`Write-Warn`/`Write-Bad`. Extract the shared conversion + registry-fetch functions into a `MiOS.Export` module (reusing the shared logging module), enable `Set-StrictMode`, and add characterization tests asserting the produced manifest/target matrix (qcow2/raw/vhdx/wsl/iso) against golden fixtures without needing a real image. Strangler-fig: module first, migrate each script behind it proving identical CLI and output, then delete the duplicated function bodies.

title: Disambiguate the two bootstrap.ps1 entry points and normalize the GitHub repo slug casing
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- gives the `irm | iex` web door one unambiguous filename and one canonical slug, mirrored in both repos per Law 15.
acceptance_criteria: No two tracked scripts are named `bootstrap.ps1` with divergent purpose; every GitHub slug uses one canonical casing; the canonical web entry is Law-15 mirrored in both repos; a gate flags mixed-case `mios`/`mios-bootstrap` slugs.

details.what_how: Two unrelated scripts share the filename `bootstrap.ps1`: the root one (99 lines, the `curl`/`iex` web entry for the dev VM, shipping with a UTF-8 BOM) and `config/bootstrap/bootstrap.ps1` (240 lines, an env/secrets provisioner with `Read-Secret`/`Import-EnvFile` and a PrivateInstaller pointing at `install.ps1`). The one-liners also disagree on slug casing: root uses `mios-dev/mios-bootstrap`, config uses `MiOS-DEV/MiOS-bootstrap`, the private installer uses `MiOS-DEV/mios`. Rename one (e.g. `config/bootstrap/provision-env.ps1`), normalize every `raw.githubusercontent` slug to the canonical lowercase `org/repo`, mirror the canonical entry surface in BOTH mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15, and keep the working one-liner URLs as literals through the migration.
details.why: An operator (or an agent) fetching "bootstrap.ps1" can land on the secrets provisioner instead of the web entry, and three casings of the same slug make the `irm | iex` door fail non-deterministically depending on which one-liner was copied.

title: Add an encoding/BOM + line-ending normalization gate for shipped .ps1 files
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface: parse-gate, deduplicate, compile -- adds the byte-level policy gate that the AST parse-gate and the Authenticode gate each assume but neither enforces.
acceptance_criteria: The drift-check FAILS on any shipped `.ps1` violating the encoding/EOL policy; `bootstrap.ps1`'s BOM is resolved per policy; the `.bom-bak` file no longer exists in the tree; the gate is green on main.

details.what_how: BOM handling has already bitten this tree: the root `bootstrap.ps1` ships with a UTF-8 BOM, a `Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1.bom-bak` artifact is TRACKED (and explicitly skipped in the `98-drift-checks.sh` list around line 1665), and `build-mios.ps1` carries multiple hand-written BOM workarounds because PS 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` emits a BOM. Add a drift-check enforcing ONE policy for shipped `*.ps1` (UTF-8, a defined BOM rule, LF or CRLF applied consistently), normalize the existing files to it, and prune the `.bom-bak` artifact. This complements the AST parse-gate (which proves parseability, not encoding) and the Authenticode gate (signatures die on silent BOM/EOL rewrites).
details.why: BOM/EOL drift has already produced a committed backup artifact, a permanent drift-check skip, and scattered per-script workarounds -- and it silently invalidates Authenticode signatures, so signed scripts fail verification for a reason no existing gate can name.

title: Fix the stale mios-ai.target Wants=mios-letta-server.service and gate dangling unit references
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- gives the unit migration a clean DAG oracle by making dangling `After=`/`Wants=`/`Requires=` edges a hard gate failure.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-ai.target` Wants only live units; the new dangling-ref assertion inside `check_dag_integrity` FAILS on a synthetic bad edge and PASSES on the cleaned tree; `just drift-gate` (or `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh`) is green.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-ai.target` carries `Wants=mios-letta-server.service`, but no such unit exists in the tree (letta was removed in the legacy `/v1`-only purge) -- a dead DAG edge systemd silently ignores. Repoint it at the live AI-plane units (`mios-agent-pipe.service` / `hermes-worker.service` per `[services.hermes]`), then extend `check_dag_integrity()` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` (around line 1998) so every `After=`/`Wants=`/`Requires=` token in `usr/lib/systemd/system/*.{service,target}` and `usr/share/containers/systemd/*` must resolve to a real unit file, a quadlet-derived generated service, or a well-known systemd target -- failing otherwise. Stage only the two edited files (never `git add -A`).
details.why: A load-bearing target currently pulls a unit that does not exist, so the AI plane's boot ordering is a lie no gate catches -- and without the dangling-ref assertion the compiled generator would faithfully reproduce the dead edge into all 168 units.

title: Deduplicate ceph-bootstrap.service vs mios-ceph-bootstrap.service into one canonical unit
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- shrinks the hand-maintained surface the generator must reproduce and kills a double-run hazard before migration starts.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one ceph bootstrap unit remains; no automation or greenboot reference points at the deleted name; `grep -r ceph-bootstrap.service` returns a single unit; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/systemd/system/ceph-bootstrap.service` and `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-ceph-bootstrap.service` both `ExecStart=/usr/libexec/mios/ceph-bootstrap.sh` as `Type=oneshot` first-boot units, differing only in `ConditionPathExists` (a `.bootstrapped` sentinel vs `/etc/ceph/ceph.conf`) and one `After=podman.socket` edge. Keep the `mios-`prefixed unit as canonical (Law 9 ONE-CANONICAL-NAME), fold the missing guards into it (sentinel + `StartLimitIntervalSec=0` + `ConditionVirtualization=no`), delete the unprefixed twin, and grep the tree -- `automation/*.sh` enable symlinks, greenboot checks, `78-greenboot.sh` -- to repoint every reference. Record the canonical name so the future `[units.*]` generator emits exactly one.
details.why: Two enabled units invoking the same first-boot script can both fire on a host whose sentinel and `/etc/ceph/ceph.conf` disagree, and duplicated hand-authored units are exactly the class WS-SYSTEMD exists to eliminate.

title: Capture byte-exact golden-master snapshots of all 161 hand-maintained units before migration
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- establishes the deviance oracle without which no strangler-fig unit migration can prove parity.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-unit-gen` reproduces the 161-file baseline with zero unexpected diffs; deliberately mutating one unit makes the test FAIL; the regen workflow is documented in the crate README.

details.what_how: Before touching any unit, characterize current behavior: add a Rust `trycmd`/`insta`-style fixture set under `tools/native/mios-unit-gen/tests/golden/` recording every file in `usr/lib/systemd/system/` byte-for-byte -- 84 `.service`, 10 `.timer`, 5 `.path`, 1 `.socket`, 11 `.target`, 4 `.mount` and 46 `.d` drop-ins -- as the frozen baseline. Provide a `cargo test` that diffs the committed tree against the snapshots plus a documented `cargo insta accept` regen path, mirroring how `generate-pod-quadlets.py --selftest` guards its renderer. Any later generator output must match these bytes or the diff is deliberately reviewed and accepted.
details.why: 161 units have no tests at all, so a generator rewrite would ship silent boot regressions across the whole fleet with nothing to compare against -- and once units start moving to SSOT, the pre-migration bytes are unrecoverable.

title: Scaffold the compiled mios-unit-gen crate (serde/miette/thiserror) in the native workspace
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- stands up the compiled façade behind which hand-authored units get replaced one family at a time.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build -p mios-unit-gen`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p mios-unit-gen -- -D warnings` all pass; `mios-unit-gen --selftest` exits 0; the crate is a workspace member.

details.what_how: Create `tools/native/mios-unit-gen` (bin + lib) and add it to `members` in `tools/native/Cargo.toml` (currently `mios-drift-runner`, `mios-version-check`, `mios-wallpaperd`). Model it on `generate-pod-quadlets.py`'s proven contract: a PURE renderer function, a `--check` drift mode, and a `--selftest`. Use serde+toml for typed deserialization of the mios.toml unit model, `thiserror` for internal resolver error enums, and `miette::Result` from `main` so a bad value points AT the offending mios.toml line/span. Ship workspace-level `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` config with the `clippy::unwrap_used` / `clippy::panic` restriction lints. No unit logic yet -- skeleton, arg parsing, TOML load, and a stub renderer returning empty.
details.why: Every unit family migrated after this inherits typed diagnostics and clippy gating for free; skipping the discipline up front means retrofitting it across a dozen families later, and the Rust plane still lacks the shellcheck-equivalent bash already has.

title: Define the [units.*] typed SSOT schema in mios.toml, mirroring the [containers.*] nested convention
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- turns 161 hand-authored files into projections of one typed source (Law 8 SSOT-PROJECTION, NS-3).
acceptance_criteria: `mios-unit-gen` deserializes `[units.*]` into typed structs and emits a miette span error on a bad shape; the ~5 encoded units render byte-identical to their golden snapshots; both repos' mios.toml parse under `tomllib` with a sane `wc -l`.

details.what_how: Add a `[units.<name>.<type>.<Section>]` nested-table block to `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, modeled on the existing `[containers.mios-*.Container/Unit/Install/Service]` convention that `render_nested_quadlet` already consumes, where `<type>` is `service|timer|path|socket|target|mount`. Deserialize it into typed Rust structs in `mios-unit-gen`: `Unit{description,after,wants,requires,condition,...}`, `Service{type,exec_start,environment,sandbox,...}`, `Install{wanted_by}`, plus Timer/Path/Socket variants. Preserve `resolve_env_vars`' rule that `${MIOS_PORT_*}` placeholders are KEPT, not resolved at generate time (they are baked at deploy by `34-render-quadlets.sh`). Per Law 15, mirror the schema stub/keys into the mios-bootstrap.git copy of the shared SSOT. Start by encoding ~5 representative simple units (`mios-podman-gc.service` + `.timer`, `mios-firstboot.target`) to prove round-trip.
details.why: Without one schema there is nothing for the generator to read, and every unit stays a hand-edited file whose values (ports, ordering, hardening) are invisible to the operator's single config surface.

title: Bake deny-by-default sandbox directives into the generator's Service renderer
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- makes the hardened posture the emitted default so no generated unit can regress into the unconfined majority.
acceptance_criteria: Generating a minimal `[units.*]` service yields every baseline hardening key; a unit listing an override omits/relaxes exactly that key and nothing else; the hermes-worker equivalent renders byte-identical to its golden snapshot; unit tests cover the default+override matrix.

details.what_how: Only 20/84 `.service` files set `NoNewPrivileges`, 18/84 set `ProtectSystem`, and 1/84 sets `SystemCallFilter` -- roughly 40 units have zero confinement. In `mios-unit-gen`'s Service renderer, emit a hardened baseline for every generated long-running unit unless explicitly overridden in `[units.<name>.service.sandbox]`: `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ProtectHome=yes`, `PrivateTmp=yes`, `SystemCallFilter=@system-service`, `RestrictAddressFamilies`, and `CapabilityBoundingSet` drop-all-plus-add-back, with `ReadWritePaths` as the only writable exception. Model the writable-path and `NoNewPrivileges=false` exceptions on the real `hermes-worker.service` (`ReadWritePaths=/etc/mios /var/lib/mios`, sudo grant) so migrated units keep working, and add a `[security.privileged_units]` roster for documented exceptions, parallel to `[security.privileged_quadlets].root`.
details.why: About 40 shipped services run unconfined today, and every hand-authored unit added since has depended on an author remembering to harden it -- a posture that has demonstrably not held and that the generator can fix permanently in one place.

goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- moves the install-ordering DAG itself into SSOT where the After/Wants/Requires graph can be validated centrally.

title: Float ListenStream from [ports] and migrate the socket unit family
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- proves the generator handles the port-float requirement, closing a bare-port-literal hole that feeds the zero-hardcodes campaign (Law 7 NO-HARDCODE).
acceptance_criteria: The socket `ListenStream` carries a `${MIOS_PORT_*}` placeholder resolving to 8091 at deploy; generator output matches golden; no bare `:8091` or `ListenStream=[0-9]` literal remains in the socket family; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `mios-cockpit-link.socket` hardcodes `ListenStream=0.0.0.0:8091` and `cockpit.socket.d/listen.conf` pins another literal `ListenStream` -- both must float from `[ports].cockpit_link` / `[ports].cockpit`. Migrate `mios-cockpit-link.socket` to `[units.mios-cockpit-link.socket]` whose `ListenStream` is emitted as `0.0.0.0:${MIOS_PORT_COCKPIT_LINK}`, preserving the deploy-time envsubst convention `34-render-quadlets.sh` bakes, and regenerate the `cockpit.socket.d` drop-in from SSOT. Prove byte-parity against golden after accounting for the placeholder -- either re-take the golden baseline in placeholder form or diff post-render.
details.why: Changing the cockpit-link port in mios.toml today leaves the socket listening on the old 8091, so SSOT and the running listener disagree -- and the `.d` drop-in makes the same literal wrong in two places.

title: Collapse the three parallel firewall port lists into one SSOT-derived generator
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- makes one `[firewall.open_ports]` selector the single declaration of what MiOS exposes, driving both the boot-time unit and the build-time firewall config.
acceptance_criteria: Adding one key to `[firewall.open_ports]` changes both the boot-time service and the build-time firewall config with zero hand-editing; the `.service` renders byte-identical (modulo the SSOT-driven list) to golden; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Exposed ports are enumerated THREE times: `[ports]` in `mios.toml`, `automation/44-firewall-ports.sh` (a `firewall-offline-cmd --add-port` per service), and `mios-firewall-ports.service`'s inline `ports=(...)` bash array with its own `:-` defaults. Introduce a `[firewall.open_ports]` SSOT selector -- a list of `[ports]` keys to expose on the public zone -- and have `mios-unit-gen` render BOTH the `mios-firewall-ports.service` ExecStart port array AND (via a small emitter) the port set `44-firewall-ports.sh` opens, from that one list. Demote both consumers to read the generated list, keeping the `${MIOS_PORT_*:-LIT}` fallback form, and hold byte-parity vs golden for the `.service`.
details.why: Three divergent copies of the exposed-port list mean a port can be opened at build but closed at boot (or the reverse) -- a live security and availability hazard where the firewall state depends on which of three files was last edited.

title: Generate the pgvector/backup/embed-backfill unit family from `[units.*]` with the DB port floated
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- no unit in the DB plane is hand-maintained and none ships unconfined.

title: Generate the web-plane host-side helper services (cockpit-link, ttyd, dashboard-issue) from SSOT
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the last hardcoded-port host services become a projection, with a clean host-unit vs container-quadlet split.

title: Model the 46 drop-in `.d/*.conf` override fragments as `[units.*.dropins]` and generate them
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- resource tuning becomes a one-line operator change instead of an edit across 46 override directories.
acceptance_criteria: All 46 fragments render byte-identical to golden from `[units.*.dropins]`, resource limits are SSOT-typed rather than free text, regenerating after a single SSOT edit changes only the intended fragment, and `cargo test` + drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: Enumerate the 46 `*.service.d` / `*.socket.d` / `*.target.d` directories (e.g. `mios-daemon.service.d/20-cpu-limit.conf` pinning `CPUQuota=800%`/`CPUWeight=20`/`Nice=10`, `mios-gpu-nvidia.service.d`, `greenboot-healthcheck.service.d`) and declare each as `[units.<base>.dropins.<fragment>]`, with resource limits promoted to a first-class `[units.*.resources]` sub-table (`CPUQuota`/`CPUWeight`/`Nice`/`MemoryMax`). Teach `mios-unit-gen` to emit the `.d/*.conf` files deterministically. Distinguish MiOS-owned drop-ins (regenerate fully) from drop-ins that override an upstream vendor unit (keep the file, but still declare it in SSOT so it is visible).
details.why: Drop-ins are the densest hand-maintenance tax in the unit surface — tuning the daemon's 800% CPU burst today means finding and editing one of 46 scattered `.conf` files with no schema, no validation and no gate.

title: Generate the oneshot infra tail (perms/init/WSL/flatpak families) with shared unit bases
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the whole `usr/lib/systemd/system` surface becomes a projection, the WS-SYSTEMD end-state.
acceptance_criteria: The oneshot tail renders byte-identical to golden, shared bases visibly collapse the repeated `After=`/`Condition=` blocks, every referenced `/usr/libexec/mios` backend still resolves on the built image, and `cargo test` + drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: Port the long tail of `Type=oneshot` units into `[units.*.service]`: `mios-libexec-perms`, `mios-additionalimagestores-perms`, `mios-git-root-init`, `mios-selinux-init`, `mios-role`, `mios-verify(-root)`, `mios-boot-diag`, `mios-cpu-isolate`, `mios-kvmfr-load`, `mios-sriov-init`, the `mios-wsl-*` family (early / init / runtime-dir / interop-priority / flatpak-export-sync / wslg-permissions-fix) and `mios-flatpak-init/install`. Group them by shared shape (perms fixers, WSL bring-up) behind a common base so duplicated `After=`/`Condition=` boilerplate collapses. Preserve every `ExecStart` path into `/usr/libexec/mios/*` verbatim (59 distinct backends are referenced tree-wide) and apply the sandbox baseline wherever a oneshot tolerates it.
details.why: This tail is the bulk of the 84 services; while it stays hand-authored the campaign cannot claim the unit surface is SSOT-derived, and each new perms/WSL unit is another copy-pasted file nobody validates.

title: Gate privileged/root service generation behind a justified `[security.privileged_units]` roster
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- elevation in generated units is explicit, justified and auditable rather than incidental.
acceptance_criteria: Privileged units render from SSOT and appear on `[security.privileged_units]` with justifications; adding a root service that is not on the roster makes the generator exit non-zero; the roster check is registered in the gate index; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Port the units that legitimately need elevation — `k3s.service`, `mios-k3s-init.service`, `mios-libvirtd-setup.service`, `mios-ha-bootstrap.service`, `mios-mok-enroll.service`, `mios-luks-enroll.service`, the deduped ceph bootstrap and `mios-freeipa-enroll.service` — into `[units.*.service]`, and cross-list each in a new `[security.privileged_units]` roster (parallel to `[security.privileged_quadlets].root`'s 13 entries) with a written justification. Make `mios-unit-gen` REFUSE to emit an unconfined/root `.service` that is absent from the roster, mirroring `check_quadlet_privilege`'s Law 6 logic for `.service` files, and back it with a new (or extended `check_unit_security`) drift-check.
details.why: Root units are the highest-blast-radius surface in the image, and a generator with no privilege policy makes privilege creep a one-line accident that no reviewer or gate would notice.

title: Run mios-unit-gen in the build and enforce it with a `check_units_generated` drift-gate
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- a hand-edited unit fails exactly like a drifted quadlet.
acceptance_criteria: The build phase regenerates units from SSOT; `mios-unit-gen --check` runs bare and deterministically and turns RED on a deliberate hand-edit; `check_units_generated` appears in the gate index and in `main()`; the negatives-before-main-gate CI ordering still holds; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Add `automation/33b-generate-units.sh` (sibling to `33-generate-quadlets.sh`, which invokes `generate-pod-quadlets.py`) that runs the compiled `mios-unit-gen` to re-emit `usr/lib/systemd/system/*` from `[units.*]`. Add `check_units_generated()` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` invoking `mios-unit-gen --check` under a CLEAN environment (`env -i`, the same determinism trick `check_pod_quadlets` uses at ~line 896, so exported `MIOS_*` vars cannot bake values into the comparison) and failing on any drift. Register it in `main()` (~line 6298) and in `tools/generate-gate-index.py` and `tools/generate-pipeline-index.py`. Stage explicit paths only — never `git add -A` in this tree.
details.why: A generator with no gate is decorative — without this, the first hand-edit to a generated unit is silently overwritten on the next build or silently persists, and 'derive, don't duplicate' stays an unenforced convention.

title: Extend the bare-port-literal check to systemd units (ListenStream / ExecStart / Environment)
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES -- systemd stops being the unscanned blind spot where floated ports regress to constants.
acceptance_criteria: The check FAILS on a synthetic unit containing a bare mapped port and PASSES on the floated tree; allowlist exemptions are honored; it is registered in the gate index; drift-gate green after the socket and AI-plane migrations.

details.what_how: `check_no_bare_port_literals` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh` ~line 1622) guards the config surfaces but not units, so `mios-cockpit-link.socket`'s `ListenStream=0.0.0.0:8091` and the AI-plane `ExecStart=`/`Environment=` port literals pass today. Extend it (or add `check_unit_port_float`) to scan `usr/lib/systemd/system/*.{service,socket,timer,path}` for any bare `:PORT` that maps to a known `[ports]` value but is not written as `${MIOS_PORT_*}`, honoring the exempt patterns in `[security.nohc_allowlist]`. Keep it SOFT while the families migrate and ratchet it hard once they land.
details.why: Without a unit-scoped gate, every port floated by the migration tasks can be quietly re-hardcoded by the next contributor, and the `[ports]` SSOT goes back to being advisory for the systemd surface.

title: Prove the Rust unit renderer with a Python reference oracle and a proptest differential harness
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- the compiled generator is proven equivalent to the legacy renderer, not spot-checked.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-unit-gen` runs the differential suite green over N random unit documents; a deliberately introduced Rust/Python divergence is caught and shrunk to a minimal case; the suite runs in CI.

details.what_how: Keep a thin Python reference renderer for `[units.*]` by extending `generate-pod-quadlets.py`'s `render_nested_quadlet` (it already renders arbitrary nested `Section.Key` tables) to target `usr/lib/systemd/system` output. Add a proptest suite in `mios-unit-gen` that generates random-but-valid `[units.*]` documents, renders each with BOTH the Rust generator and the Python reference (via subprocess), and asserts byte-identical output, letting proptest auto-shrink any divergence to a minimal failing document. Wire it into CI beside the golden tests.
details.why: Example-based golden tests miss exactly the edge cases that break a renderer port — quoting, list ordering, empty-value drop — and a divergence found after the strangler cut means shipping malformed units to a fleet.

title: Add cargo-deny / cargo-audit supply-chain gating for the native workspace
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- the new compiled tier ships with the vuln and license gating bash never had.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` run in CI and fail the build on a banned or vulnerable crate; `Cargo.lock` is committed; the license allow-list is enforced; the existing CI job order still holds.

details.what_how: `mios-unit-gen` introduces a real dependency surface (serde, toml, miette, thiserror, proptest) under `tools/native`. details.why: Moving system tooling into Rust without dependency gating imports an unaudited transitive tree into the image that produces every systemd unit — the highest-trust build artifact MiOS has.

title: Reconcile hardcoded `Environment=` service URLs in migrated units against `[ports]`/`[services.webtools]`
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES -- endpoints in units derive from SSOT instead of freezing stale literals into generated files.
acceptance_criteria: Every `Environment=` endpoint in the generated AI-plane units resolves from SSOT or carries a justified internal-port note; the searxng/firecrawl/crawl4ai disagreements are reconciled or documented; no unaccounted bare service URL remains; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Several units bake service URLs in `Environment=`: `hermes-worker.service` sets `SEARXNG_URL=http://localhost:8888`, `MIOS_CRAWL_SERVICE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11235`, `FIRECRAWL_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3002`, `HERMES_BACKEND_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11441` and `BROWSER_CDP_URL=:9223` — several of which disagree with canonical `[ports]` values (searxng=8899, firecrawl=8302, crawl4ai=8235). Reconcile each against `[ports]`/`[services.webtools]`, express them as `${MIOS_*}` placeholders in the generated `[units.*.service.Environment]` with `${VAR:-LIT}` fallback, and add the missing `[ports]`/`[network]` keys where a literal has no SSOT home. Flag genuine internal-vs-published-port distinctions instead of blindly rewriting them.
details.why: A worker pointing at `:8888` when searxng canonically moved to `:8899` is live breakage today, and generating the units as-is would freeze those wrong values in as the SSOT-blessed answer.

title: Generate the system and user `90-mios.preset` enablement rosters from `[units.*].enable`
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the enablement SSOT stops being a 271-line hand-maintained list.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-unit-gen --emit-preset` produces byte-identical system and user preset files vs the committed golden; `cargo test` parity is green; `just drift-gate` is green; the preset is regenerated during the build and staged by explicit path.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/90-mios.preset` (271 lines, ~150 enable/disable decisions including role-gated defaults and WSL fallbacks) and `usr/lib/systemd/user-preset/90-mios.preset` have no generator at all. Extend `mios-unit-gen` to emit both from `[units.<name>].enable` (bool) and `.scope` (`system|user`), preserving the rationale comments as `[units.*].comment`. Strangler-fig: generate to a temp path first, add a `--check` mode asserting byte-parity with the committed preset, flip the committed file to generated once green, and keep the hand-written list as the golden fixture. Upstream units MiOS only toggles (sshd, podman.socket, libvirtd, cockpit.socket) stay declarable via an `[units.<name>].external=true` marker so the generator sets enablement without authoring a unit body.
details.why: The preset's own comments (lines 212-225) record the `mios-ai-firstboot` incident where dropped enable lines left the AI plane silently DEAD on first boot — it is the most fragile surface in this domain and nothing generates or validates it.

title: Add `check_preset_roster_complete`: no orphan enable lines, no undeclared MiOS unit
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the 'silently dead on first boot' class becomes a gate failure, not a field report.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting any `mios-*.service` preset line, or renaming a unit without updating the preset, turns the gate RED naming the exact unit; adding the missing decision returns it green; the check is registered in both the negatives suite and the main gate.

details.what_how: Generalize the ad-hoc spot-check at `automation/98-drift-checks.sh:3369-3373` (which only asserts nut-server/nut-monitor have enable lines) into a full fitness function with two axes: (1) every enable/disable target in `90-mios.preset` resolves to a real unit under `usr/lib/systemd/system` or a known upstream unit, and (2) every MiOS-owned unit (`mios-*.service/.timer/.path/.target/.socket`) carries an explicit enable OR disable decision — under Fedora bootc, an undeclared unit is a silently disabled one. Implement it natively in `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs` with a bash `check_preset_roster` wrapper registered in the CHECKS array (~line 4794) and the dispatch (~line 6298), printing the offending unit names to stderr like sibling checks.
details.why: The documented `mios-ai-firstboot` incident is precisely this orphan/undeclared-unit class; the existing dangling-ref task covers `Wants=`/`After=` inside units, leaving the enablement-roster-vs-unit-files axis completely ungated.

**What+How:** Generalize the ad-hoc spot-check at `automation/98-drift-checks.sh:3369-3373` (which only asserts nut-server/nut-monitor have enable lines) into a full fitness function with two axes: (1) every enable/disable target in `90-mios.preset` resolves to a real unit under `usr/lib/systemd/system` or a known upstream unit, and (2) every MiOS-owned unit (`mios-*.service/.timer/.path/.target/.socket`) carries an explicit enable OR disable decision — under Fedora bootc, an undeclared unit is a silently disabled one. Implement it natively in `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs` with a bash `check_preset_roster` wrapper registered in the CHECKS array (~line 4794) and the dispatch (~line 6298), printing the offending unit names to stderr like sibling checks.
**Where:** `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (CHECKS registry + dispatch), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs, usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/90-mios.preset`
**Done When:** Deleting any `mios-*.service` preset line, or renaming a unit without updating the preset, turns the gate RED naming the exact unit; adding the missing decision returns it green; the check is registered in both the negatives suite and the main gate.
**Why:** The documented `mios-ai-firstboot` incident is precisely this orphan/undeclared-unit class; the existing dangling-ref task covers `Wants=`/`After=` inside units, leaving the enablement-roster-vs-unit-files axis completely ungated.
**Dep:** Generate 90-mios.preset enablement rosters from SSOT

title: Unify role-apply's runtime enablement with the generated `.target` units via `[units.*].roles`

acceptance_criteria: `role-apply` drives enablement from the SSOT-generated role map; a characterization test shows each archetype enables an identical unit set before and after; the `.target` `Wants=` and the role map both derive from one `[units.*].roles` source; drift-gate green.

Add an `[units.<name>].roles = ["desktop","k3s-master"]` membership field so `mios-unit-gen` emits BOTH the `.target`'s `Wants=` and a generated `/usr/share/mios/role-units.json` role→unit map that `role-apply` consumes in place of its hand-coded case statement. title: Subsume `generate-pod-quadlets.py` into mios-unit-gen behind a differential-parity harness
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- one compiled generator owns every systemd artifact instead of a Rust and a Python one running side by side.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-unit-gen` emits every file under `usr/share/containers/systemd` byte-identical to `generate-pod-quadlets.py` across the full SSOT; the Python generator is a shim or deleted and `33-generate-quadlets.sh` calls the binary; `cargo test`, the differential harness and the drift-gate are green.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py` (504 lines) already renders ~30 files under `usr/share/containers/systemd`: `.container`/`.network`/`.volume` via `render_nested_quadlet` (line 242) from `[containers.*]`/`[networks.*]`/`[volumes.*]`, and `.pod` via `render_pod_quadlet` (line 146) from `[pods.*]`, with env and `${VAR:-default}` and sidecar-digest resolution in `resolve_env_vars` (line 44). First capture golden snapshots of the ENTIRE `usr/share/containers/systemd` tree (the existing golden task covers only the 161 `usr/lib/systemd/system` units). Then port `render_nested_quadlet`, `render_pod_quadlet` and `resolve_env_vars` to Rust and run a differential harness feeding both generators the same `mios.toml`, asserting byte-identical output per file — only then demote the Python generator to a thin `exec mios-unit-gen` shim and delete it once the Rust path is drift-green.
details.why: Leaving the already-SSOT-generated container side un-converged ships TWO unit generators with two rendering semantics — and the quadlet tree the existing golden task omits has no parity net at all.

title: Preserve `Condition*`/`Assert*` substrate gating in the schema with a round-trip fidelity check
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- generated units keep firing only on the platform they were written for.
acceptance_criteria: Every `Condition*`/`Assert*` directive in the 161 golden units appears identically in the generated units; deliberately dropping a `ConditionVirtualization` in a fixture turns the check red; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: The 161 hand-maintained units carry verified substrate gating: 60 `ConditionPathExists=`, 40 `ConditionVirtualization=`, 4 `ConditionPathIsDirectory=`, 2 `ConditionPathExistsGlob=`, 1 `ConditionSecurity=` (e.g. `ConditionVirtualization=wsl` on the WSL-early units, `ConditionVirtualization=microsoft` on `mios-hyperv-enhanced`). Add first-class `[units.<name>].conditions` / `.asserts` lists to the schema, make the Service/Container renderer emit them verbatim, and add `check_condition_fidelity` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` asserting every `Condition*`/`Assert*` line in the golden set round-trips into generated output with identical operator, negation and glob semantics.
details.where: `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-wsl-early.service, usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-hyperv-enhanced.service, the golden snapshots, mios-unit-gen renderer, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
details.why: Losing a `ConditionVirtualization=wsl` or `=microsoft` gate makes a unit run on bare metal or QEMU where it bricks boot (226/NAMESPACE, per the preset's own `mios-wsl-early` warning) — a correctness axis the sandbox and port-float tasks do not touch.

title: Generate the Windows/WSL quadlet variants from the same SSOT with a Law 15 cross-repo parity gate
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the cross-platform unit surface projects from one SSOT instead of a hand-copied Windows fork.
acceptance_criteria: The Windows quadlets are generated from SSOT byte-identical to a golden capture; image/port/network parity vs the Linux quadlet is drift-gated; the SSOT change is present in both repos; `:latest`+SBOM intent is preserved with no hand-pinned digest.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/windows/quadlets/{mios-llm-light.container, mios.network}` are hand-maintained duplicates of the Linux quadlets (the Windows `mios-llm-light.container` hardcodes `Image=ghcr.io/mostlygeek/llama-swap:cuda`, listen `0.0.0.0:11450` and a WSL `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`). Add a Windows target/profile to `mios-unit-gen` so the Windows-scoped quadlets project from the SAME `[containers.*]`/`[networks.*]` SSOT with a `[units.<name>].platform` overlay for WSL-specific paths such as `/usr/lib/wsl/lib`, and add a drift-check asserting the Windows and Linux renders agree on image, port and network and differ only by declared platform deltas. Per Law 15 the shared SSOT change lands in BOTH `mios.git` and `mios-bootstrap.git`, and the port stays a `${MIOS_PORT_*:-11450}` float with the literal as fallback.
details.why: MiOS is explicitly cross-platform, yet the Windows quadlet tree is an ungenerated hand copy that silently diverges from the Linux SSOT — the exact divergence class this campaign exists to eliminate, and no other task touches it.

title: Model templated `@` instance units and preserve systemd `%`-specifiers in the generator
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- parameterized units survive generation as templates, not as flattened instances.
acceptance_criteria: Generated `@`-template units are byte-identical to golden with every `%`-specifier intact; declared instances such as `user@1000.service` are enabled via the generated preset; `cargo test` + drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Several units are systemd TEMPLATES: `usr/share/containers/systemd/mios-llm-worker@.container`, `usr/share/containers/systemd/users/mios-coderun-sandbox@.container`, plus drop-ins on `sshd-keygen@.service` and `user@.service`. Add `[units.<name>].template=true` and `.instances = [...]` to the schema, teach the renderer to emit the `@`-suffixed template file with `%i`/`%N`/`%p`/`%I` specifiers preserved VERBATIM (never resolved at generation time), and have the preset generator enable specific instances (e.g. `user@1000.service`, preset line 179). Golden-master each template file before porting, then assert the `%`-specifiers survive untouched.
details.why: A naive per-unit renderer either resolves `%i` at build time (producing one wrong frozen instance) or drops the template entirely; the GPU-detect-family task covers a static family, so nothing else guards specifier semantics.

title: Generate the user-scope quadlets and the user-preset (rootless user-manager scope)
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the user manager scope stops being an entirely hand-maintained island.
acceptance_criteria: User-scope quadlets and the user-preset generate byte-identical to golden; install targets are `default.target`/`graphical-session.target` rather than `multi-user.target`; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: MiOS ships USER-scope units distinct from system scope: `usr/share/containers/systemd/users/mios-coderun-sandbox@.container` (rootless, user systemd) and a user-preset enabling `mios-launcher.service`, `mios-computer-use-server.service` and the `mios-wsl-*` services under `WantedBy=default.target` / `graphical-session.target`. Add `[units.<name>].scope = "user"` so `mios-unit-gen` writes user-scope quadlets under `usr/share/containers/systemd/users/` and the user preset under `usr/lib/systemd/user-preset/`, applying the correct install target (`default.target`, never `multi-user.target`) and NO root/privileged sandbox posture. title: Retire the deploy-time `34-render-quadlets.sh` envsubst pass once values float at generation time
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- one render authority, so nothing re-mutates a generated unit after the build.
acceptance_criteria: `34-render-quadlets.sh` reports zero rewrites across all generated units; the phase is removed or reduced to legacy-only with no runtime placeholder left unrendered; boot-time smoke and drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `automation/34-render-quadlets.sh` performs IN-PLACE deploy-time rendering (`_render_with_envsubst` / `_render_with_bash`) over every deployed `.container`/`.network`/`.volume`/`.pod`/`.image`/`.service` (the `find` at line 184), substituting `${MIOS_*}` from the runtime env — a SECOND render mechanism parallel to the build-time generator. Once `mios-unit-gen` floats values from `[ports]`/`[services.*]` at generation with `${VAR:-LIT}` fallbacks baked in, this pass is redundant for generated units. Strangler-fig: mark generated units as already-floated, shrink the phase to touch only remaining non-generated files, prove it is a no-op on generated units (`rendered_count==0` for them), then delete the phase and its multi-LoRA special case (line 165) once all quadlets are generated.
details.why: Two authorities rendering the same placeholders means the deploy-time pass can silently rewrite a correctly generated unit; the demote-33 task retires the AUTHORING path but leaves this separate RENDER path live.

title: Gate every generated unit through `systemd-analyze verify` so structural breakage fails the build, not the boot
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- no generated unit ships that systemd itself cannot load, so mechanical generation is safe to trust.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture unit with a bad directive or a dangling `Requires=` fails the gate and prints the `systemd-analyze verify` output; a clean generation passes; the check SOFT-skips off-Linux and hard-gates in CI/bake.

details.what_how: Add a drift/build gate that runs `systemd-analyze verify` over every rendered `.service/.timer/.socket/.path/.target/.container`, catching unknown directives, malformed `Exec` lines, dangling referenced units and load errors before the image ships. This is the STRUCTURAL counterpart to the security ratchet (which only scores hardening). Implement the step natively in the `miosd` drift runner (`src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs`) with a bash `check_units_verify` wrapper registered in the `98-drift-checks.sh` CHECKS registry; SOFT-skip when `systemd-analyze` is absent (Windows dev host) using the same pattern as `check_resolver_twin_parity` (~line 4180) so it hard-gates only on Linux/CI.
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check + CHECKS registry), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs, usr/lib/systemd/system, usr/share/containers/systemd`
details.why: Today a subtly-malformed generated directive surfaces only as a boot-time load failure on a deployed host — the most expensive place to find it — and generating 168 units mechanically multiplies that exposure.
