**Where:** `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check + CHECKS registry), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs, usr/lib/systemd/system, usr/share/containers/systemd`
**Done When:** A fixture unit with a bad directive or a dangling `Requires=` fails the gate and prints the `systemd-analyze verify` output; a clean generation passes; the check SOFT-skips off-Linux and hard-gates in CI/bake.
**Why:** Today a subtly-malformed generated directive surfaces only as a boot-time load failure on a deployed host — the most expensive place to find it — and generating 168 units mechanically multiplies that exposure.
**Dep:** Wire mios-unit-gen into the build and add check_units_generated drift-gate

title: Detect After/Requires/Wants ordering cycles inside mios-unit-gen before any unit is rendered
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the generated ordering DAG is provably acyclic, so SSOT-driven units cannot deadlock boot.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with a deliberately-introduced cycle fails generation with the cycle path printed; the real SSOT generates a clean topo order; `cargo test` covers the cycle and self-dep cases; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Build the dependency graph inside `mios-unit-gen` with petgraph from the `[units.*]` `After/Requires/Wants/BindsTo` edges plus implied pod membership (`Pod=` implies `Wants=`/`After=` on the pod service), then run a topological sort / SCC check and FAIL generation on any cycle, printing the offending edge path. Also flag self-`Requires` and `Requires` without a matching `After` (a start-order race). Emit the resolved topo order as an artifact the ordering-migration tasks consume.
details.why: The existing tasks fix one known stale ref (`mios-ai.target Wants=`) and gate dangling refs, but nothing validates acyclicity — the failure mode that HANGS boot (systemd breaks a cycle arbitrarily) rather than merely 404ing a unit.

title: Make the generator emit the EnvironmentFile that backs every floated `${MIOS_PORT_*}`, and gate the contract
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- floated SSOT values in units resolve at runtime by construction, closing the loop between the generator and the env producers.
acceptance_criteria: Every generated unit referencing a floated `MIOS_*` carries the `EnvironmentFile` that supplies it and that var is emitted by the resolver; a fixture floating an unbacked var fails the gate; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: Floated port/URL vars only expand if an `EnvironmentFile` supplies them; the survey shows units already rely on `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/mios/install.env` (14x) and `-/etc/mios/userenv.sh` (6x), populated by `system-sync-env.sh` / `mios-env-snapshot`. Teach the Service/Container renderer that whenever it floats `${MIOS_PORT_*}` / `${MIOS_*_URL}` into `ExecStart`/`Environment`/`ListenStream` it must ALSO emit the matching `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/mios/userenv.sh` line. Add a native drift-check verifying every floated `MIOS_*` referenced by a generated unit is (a) actually produced by `userenv.sh`/`install.env` and (b) backed by an `EnvironmentFile` in that unit; SOFT-skip off-Linux.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/system-sync-env.sh, usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot, /etc/mios/userenv.sh (produced), generated units, mios-unit-gen renderer, automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
details.why: The port-float tasks all assume the var exists at runtime; an unbacked float expands to EMPTY, so the socket binds nothing or `ExecStart` runs a truncated command — a hard break that no current check catches.

title: Bind generated `User=`/`Group=` to the existing `[services.*]` uid/gid table so identity has exactly one source
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- unit generation adds a projection, never a THIRD parallel declaration of service identity.
acceptance_criteria: Generated units derive `User=`/`Group=` solely from `[services.*]`/`[accounts]`; a mismatch between a unit's owner and the `[services.*]` uid fails the gate; no unit re-declares a uid; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `mios.toml` already carries identity in `[services.<name>]` with user/uid/gid (`[services.forge]` user=mios-forge uid=816, `[services.pgvector]` uid=826, `[services.llamacpp]` uid=827, `[services.webtools]` uid=824), and that same table drives `usr/lib/sysusers.d/50-mios-services.conf`. Teach `mios-unit-gen` to resolve `User=`/`Group=`/`PrivateUsers` by looking up `[services.*]`/`[accounts]` through a `[units.<name>].service_account` reference instead of declaring identity in `[units.*]`. Add a drift-check that no generated unit hardcodes a `User=`/`Group=` disagreeing with `[services.*]`, and that every non-external MiOS service unit resolves an owner from that one table.
details.why: The campaign exists to kill parallel definitions (the operator flagged the triple-resolver smell); letting `[units.*]` carry its own identity would recreate exactly that divergence and desync units from `sysusers.d`, producing units that run as a uid the system never created.

title: Retire dead unit files together with their preset lines and SSOT blocks so the generator roster equals the live set
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- only units MiOS actually ships enter the `[units.*]` roster, so generation does not immortalize corpses.
acceptance_criteria: Each removed unit has no remaining unit file, preset line, SSOT block or inbound `Wants=`/`Requires=`; the generator's `[units.*]` roster equals the live shipped set; drift-gate + `systemd-analyze verify` green; changes staged by explicit path.

details.what_how: Enumerate genuinely-dead units by cross-checking preset `disable`-forever entries against inbound `Wants=`/`Requires=` refs, then remove — in one change — the unit file, its preset line, its `[containers.*]`/`[units.*]` SSOT block, and any dangling `Wants=`. Known candidates: `mios-code-server.service` (marked RETIRED and `disable`d at preset lines 153-156 yet `[containers.mios-code-server.*]` still sits inert at mios.toml 10126-10165), `mios-llm-heavy-alt.container` (alt variant), and the `[services.*]` migration notes referencing retired datastore UID 821 / CPU-inference UID 823. Verify each is truly orphaned first — the flatten-consolidation memo lists "legacy" units that are load-bearing. Stage explicit paths only; never `git add -A` (AGY shares the tree).
details.why: Migrating dead units into the generator would carve them permanently into SSOT and keep shipping inert `[containers.*]` blocks that mislead every future reader about what MiOS runs.

title: Gate that generated pods project faithfully to k3s so the cluster path cannot silently diverge
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- the pods SSOT stays authoritative for BOTH downstreams (Quadlets and k3s), not just the one the generator touches.
acceptance_criteria: Changing a pod's membership or port in SSOT without re-projecting k3s FAILS the gate; a consistent regeneration passes; the check SOFT-skips without podman; drift-gate green on Linux/CI.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-k3s-manifests.sh` projects the live pods under `usr/share/containers/systemd` (via `podman kube generate`) into k3s manifests under `usr/share/mios/k3s`, making the `.pod`/`.container` files the k8s workload SSOT too. Add a drift-check (or extend the existing pod-quadlets gate) asserting every `[pods.*]` member plus its floated image/port appears consistently in the generated k3s manifest set, and document that regenerating units REQUIRES re-running the k3s projection. SOFT-skip where podman is unavailable (off-Linux), matching the existing soft-gate pattern.
details.why: The generator work touches only the Quadlet side, so today a pod change lands in systemd while the k3s manifests keep the old membership/port — a silent third divergence surface, exactly what this campaign is meant to eliminate.

title: Build the `mios-config` typed layered SSOT resolver crate (figment) as the compiled peer of `mios_toml.py`
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- one compiled resolver every projected surface derives from, starting the collapse of the three parallel resolvers.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build -p mios-config` green; a `cargo test -p mios-config` differential test asserts `colors()` and `section()` byte-match the JSON emitted by `python3 usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` for the committed mios.toml; the crate is a workspace member.

details.what_how: Create library crate `tools/native/mios-config` (added to the `tools/native/Cargo.toml` workspace alongside mios-drift-runner/mios-version-check/mios-wallpaperd) that deserializes the three-layer overlay into typed structs via figment Toml providers in the EXACT order used by `mios-sync-theme` lines 27-30 and `mios_toml.load_merged`: vendor `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` < host `/etc/mios/mios.toml` < user `~/.config/mios/mios.toml`. Mirror `mios_toml.py` semantics exactly — expose `load_merged()`, `colors() -> BTreeMap`, `section(path)` — and reuse `tools/native/mios-ssot-walk`'s `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS`. Errors are thiserror enums wrapped by miette so a bad `[colors]` hex points at the offending span (byte offsets, not char counts). Do NOT touch the Python resolver yet.
details.why: Without a compiled resolver every Rust port would re-implement layering ad hoc, and the three divergent resolvers (`mios_toml.py`, the userenv.sh twins, globals.ps1) the operator flagged stay three forever.

title: Scaffold the `miosd dotfiles` clap subcommand as the compiled facade that initially execs the Python engine
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- a stable verb facade exists so surfaces migrate one slice at a time behind an unchanged CLI.
acceptance_criteria: `miosd dotfiles check|render|diff` produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit vs the Python engine (the golden-master trycmd fixtures replay green); `cargo build -p miosd` green.

details.what_how: Extend the `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/main.rs` Commands enum with `Dotfiles { verb, names, dry_run }` (verbs render/check/capture/apply/diff) and add `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/dotfiles/mod.rs`, mirroring the argv dispatch of `mios-dotfiles-render` main (lines 1212-1233). Depend on the `mios-config` crate and return `miette::Result` from each verb. Strangler seam: each verb initially just execs `usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render <verb> <names>`, forwarding the child's stdout/stderr/exit BYTE-FOR-BYTE. Add the serde/miette/insta dependency set to the miosd crate.
details.why: Without a stable facade every ported slice would change the caller contract, forcing drift-checks, wrappers and the Justfile to be rewired repeatedly instead of once.

title: Port the `render` and `capture` verbs, including the lossy-round-trip refusal, to Rust
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- the whole template kind (six color + two settings surfaces) can run Rust-first behind the toggle.

details.what_how: Reimplement `cmd_render` (954-971) and `cmd_capture` (1026-1082) in the miosd dotfiles module. `render` writes each surface's derived bytes to its committed target with `newline=''` fidelity (NO CRLF translation). `capture` is template-only: it replaces hex with `@MIOS:token@` via `_token_map` and REFUSES a lossy round-trip (a re-render must reproduce the artifact byte-for-byte). Preserve the capture guards `settings surface is hand-authored -- skipping` and `kind!=template -- skipping`. Verify render against the golden-master snapshots and capture round-trips on all six color templates.
details.why: Without render/capture the Rust path can only observe drift, never fix it, so the toggle stays permanently unflippable and the Python engine stays canonical; a CRLF or newline slip here would also mass-drift every committed artifact.

title: Add a kargs-flatten kind and fold `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline` off `tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py`
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- the boot-integrity projection baked inside the signed UKI is produced by the one compiled, tested engine.
acceptance_criteria: The engine's flatten byte-matches committed `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline`; `check_uki_cmdline_projection` green via the engine; `generate-uki-cmdline.py` demoted to a shim; both repos mirrored.

details.what_how: Implement a `kargs-flatten` derive kind in `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/dotfiles/` that concatenates the kargs arrays from every `usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml` (sorted by filename; 20+ drop-ins verified present) into a single-line `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline`, reproducing `tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py` (lines 23-33) including its trailing-newline shape. Register `[dotfiles.registry.uki-cmdline]` (kind=kargs-flatten, a SOURCE DIR rather than a single template), verify byte-match vs the committed cmdline, shim the generator to the engine, and rewire `check_uki_cmdline_projection` (98-drift-checks.sh line 5367). Parity is boot-integrity-critical — this cmdline is baked INSIDE the signed UKI (`enforcing=1`, LUKS args). Mirror in BOTH repos.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/miosd/src/dotfiles/ (new kargs-flatten kind), usr/share/mios/mios.toml, usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml, usr/lib/kernel/cmdline, tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (5367), mios-bootstrap.git mirror`
details.why: A mis-ordered or dropped karg in this file silently weakens Secure Boot / SELinux enforcement inside a SIGNED artifact — the failure is invisible at build time and unfixable at runtime without a re-sign.

title: Split the chrony PTP drop-in: projector owns the CONTENT, the service keeps the /dev/ptp0 probe
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- moves one more standalone renderer behind the single `[dotfiles.registry.*]` engine without losing hardware-conditional behavior.
acceptance_criteria: `check_chrony_ptp_dropin` is green while comparing an engine render (not bash syntax); the drop-in content is byte-derived from SSOT; the ptp0 gate in `mios-chrony-ptp.service` is textually unchanged; both repos carry any added mios.toml key.

details.what_how: Port `usr/libexec/mios/mios-chrony-ptp-dropin` (the chrony.d drop-in generator) so the miosd dotfiles engine derives the drop-in CONTENT from the `[network.ntp]`/PTP keys in mios.toml, while the runtime `/dev/ptp0` presence probe stays in `mios-chrony-ptp.service` (degrade-open: no ptp0 -> no drop-in installed). Rewire `check_chrony_ptp_dropin` (automation/98-drift-checks.sh line 5421) so it compares the engine's render against the expected drop-in instead of syntax-checking the bash producer. The split is the point: engine = projection, service = hardware decision. Per Law 15, mirror any new mios.toml key into mios-bootstrap.git.
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-chrony-ptp-dropin, usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-chrony-ptp.service, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (5421), src/mios-rs/miosd/src/dotfiles/, mios-bootstrap.git mirror if mios.toml changes`
details.why: Today a hardware probe and a config projection are welded into one bash script, so the drift-gate can only lint the script rather than verify the output -- and any future SSOT change to NTP settings silently bypasses the projector.

title: Convert the mios-sync-theme heredoc bridge (theme.json + mios-theme.css) into two registry surfaces
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- removes the last hand-written projection living inside the global theme-refresh script.
acceptance_criteria: the engine emits `theme.json` and `mios-theme.css` byte-identical to today's heredoc output; the heredoc is gone from mios-sync-theme; a drift surface gates both files; the registry block is identical in mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git.

details.what_how: Replace the embedded-Python heredoc at `usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme` lines 55-135 (which writes `theme.json` + `mios-theme.css` from `[colors]`/`[theme]`/`[theme.font]`) with two registry surfaces, `theme-bridge-json` and `theme-bridge-css`, backed by new templates `usr/share/mios/theme/templates/theme.json.tmpl` and `mios-theme.css.tmpl`. title: Add `check_projector_coverage`: prove no un-migrated standalone projector remains
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- makes "every projection routes through the one engine" a machine-checked invariant instead of a campaign intention.

title: Gate the projector crate with cargo-deny/cargo-audit and give it spanned miette diagnostics
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- gives the compiled projector the dependency-provenance and error-UX story bash never had.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` run as drift-gate steps and pass; a deliberately malformed hex in mios.toml produces a spanned miette diagnostic naming the line; Cargo.lock is committed; `just drift-gate` green.

details.what_how: Add `src/mios-rs/deny.toml` covering banned/duplicate crates, a license allow-list that operationalizes the FOSS-upstream posture, and RustSec advisories. Add Justfile drift-gate steps running `cargo deny check` + `cargo audit` over both the `src/mios-rs` and `tools/native` workspaces, with `Cargo.lock` committed as the reproducibility SSOT (per SBOM-not-hardcode: dependency digests are recorded at build, never hand-pinned). Convert every projector verb to return `miette::Result` so a bad `[colors]` hex or an unknown `@MIOS:token@` renders a source-spanned diagnostic pointing at the offending mios.toml line (byte offsets, not char counts). Reconfirm the clippy restriction lints still ban `panic`/`unwrap` on the projector path.
details.why: The projector is becoming a compiled dependency-carrying binary in the boot path with zero advisory scanning and zero license policy, and its failure mode today is an opaque error string that tells an operator nothing about which mios.toml line broke.

title: Delete mios-generate-icons' private regex `[colors]` resolver and feed it the engine-resolved palette
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- eliminates the fourth independent palette resolver so the palette is resolved exactly once.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-generate-icons` contains no mios.toml or `[colors]` reader of its own; the icon SVG set is drift-gated against a committed golden; `cargo test` and `just drift-gate` stay green with byte-identical SVG output versus the pre-change tree.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-generate-icons` reads `/etc/mios/theme/theme.json` first and otherwise falls back to its own hand-rolled regex scan of mios.toml `[colors]` (`_load_theme_json` / `_load_mios_toml`, the `_TOML_COLOR_KEYS` list) to stamp brand hex into XDG SVGs -- a color-projection surface entirely outside `[dotfiles.registry.*]`. Register the icon SVGs (`usr/share/icons/MiOS/**`) as a projector-owned surface (a new svg/icon derive kind, or a post-render hook handing the engine's already-resolved palette to shared codegen). Strangler-fig: keep the Python emitting SVGs but feed it the engine-resolved palette and drop `_load_mios_toml`, prove the emitted SVG set is byte-identical against a golden fixture, then demote the script to a thin shim.
details.why: A private regex scanner is exactly the divergent-resolver smell this campaign exists to kill, and this one silently drops the accent/info palette keys the SSOT owns -- so a palette change produces icons that disagree with every other surface.

title: Fold the build-time Hyprland theme bake into the registry and retire the `@@MIOS_COLOR_*@@` sed dialect
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- brings the compositor (the liquid-glass north-star surface) under the one token dialect and under check 25.
acceptance_criteria: hyprland.conf is a registered template surface containing no `@@...@@` tokens and no hardcoded hex; 65-bake-hyprland.sh runs no color sed; check 25 gates hyprland.conf; the build stays green with byte-identical output.

details.what_how: `automation/65-bake-hyprland.sh` projects `[colors]` into `usr/share/mios/hyprland/hyprland.conf` at BUILD time using a SECOND token dialect -- `@@MIOS_COLOR_ACCENT@@` / `@@MIOS_COLOR_INFO@@` / `@@MIOS_COLOR_MUTED@@` substituted by an in-script sed, with a hardcoded fallback `col.active_border` and `: "${MIOS_COLOR_ACCENT:=#1A407F}"`. Convert hyprland.conf into a registry template surface (`usr/share/mios/theme/templates/hyprland.conf.tmpl`, canonical `@MIOS:accent@`/`@MIOS:info@`/`@MIOS:muted@` tokens) targeting `usr/share/mios/hyprland/hyprland.conf`, so compositor colors AND the liquid-glass `decoration.rounding`/opacity derive through the one projector. Strangler-fig: `capture` the current file, delete only the sed block from 65-bake-hyprland.sh (leave the rest of the bake), prove byte-parity.
details.why: The compositor is a live theme surface using a rival token syntax plus a hardcoded fallback color -- a projection hole the drift-gate cannot see today, while the liquid-glass north star explicitly requires compositor effects to project FROM mios.toml.

title: Repoint the three runtime call sites (service unit, `mios dotfiles` verb, completion) at miosd, degrade-open
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- makes the compiled engine the thing that actually runs at boot and at the operator's prompt.
acceptance_criteria: unit, verb and completion all invoke miosd with Python only as degrade-open fallback; boot ordering and SuccessExitStatus are unchanged; `mios dotfiles status/diff/sync` behave identically on a booted MiOS-DEV VM.

details.what_how: Three non-drift-gate call sites still hardcode the Python scripts: `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sync-theme.service` (`ExecStart=/usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme`, `SuccessExitStatus=0 1`, ordered `Before=mios-agent-pipe.service hermes-dashboard.service`); the `dotfiles)` case in `etc/profile.d/mios-verbs.sh` (L110-122, dispatching to `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles` with a `/mnt/m/...` fallback); and the bash-completion word list (L185). Point ExecStart and the verb at the miosd binary (`miosd dotfiles sync`, `miosd dotfiles <status|diff|sync>`), preserving `SuccessExitStatus=0 1`, the boot ordering, and the `/mnt/m` fallback, and keep the Python path as a `command -v miosd || fallback` last resort so a missing binary never blocks boot.
details.why: The Rust port is inert until its real invokers call it; these two entry points are the boot oneshot and the operator verb, and neither is covered by the check-25 rewire task -- so the binary could ship complete and never execute.

title: Cross-compile miosd for Windows and add a windows-latest CI job for the live-apply path
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- keeps the Windows half of the projection at parity instead of stranding it on the deprecated Python.
acceptance_criteria: a windows-target miosd is built and distributed; `cargo test` is green on a Windows CI runner covering registry/WT/vscode apply; `miosd dotfiles apply` on Windows produces the same HKCU and settings.json result as the Python engine.

details.what_how: The apply/diff path is explicitly platform-branched: `_apply_live_registry` short-circuits on `os.name != 'nt'`, `_os_key()`/`_apply_target` select windows targets, and the Windows surfaces (`windows-registry` via `reg.exe add/query` read-back, `windows-terminal` LocalState settings.json, `vscode-colors` under `%APPDATA%`) only execute on Windows -- today via the Python engine reached from `Get-MiOS.ps1` / `mios-oscontrol-server.ps1`. Add an `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` target to the crate build, gate the reg.exe backup/add/query-verify logic behind `cfg(windows)`, ship the binary through the Windows install leg, and add a GitHub CI job running `cargo test` on windows-latest that exercises registry/WT/vscode apply against a mock `HKCU\Console\MiOS-Test`. Keep the Python engine as the Windows fallback until the binary lands.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/miosd/, tools/native/Cargo.toml, usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render (_apply_live_registry L758-846), *.ps1 install/oscontrol entry points, .github/ CI`
details.why: The entire reason the merge kinds exist is the Windows live-HOME apply; a Linux-only port would leave the registry/terminal/vscode surfaces on an engine slated for deletion, with no CI proving they still work.

title: Promote the runtime registry-schema invariants to a build-time drift-gate
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- turns a latent runtime `SystemExit(3)` into a caught PR failure and hardens the apply-target safety contract.
acceptance_criteria: a registry entry with a missing or untracked path, an absolute `apply.target`, or a dotted surface name fails the drift-gate at build time rather than at first run; the current registry passes unchanged.

details.what_how: Today `_load_surfaces` (usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render L874-929) enforces its invariants at RUNTIME -- missing template/target, unknown kind, a merge kind lacking `fixture.base`/`fixture.expected`, a `.` in a surface name -- so a mis-authored `[dotfiles.registry.*]` entry only fails when someone runs the engine. Promote them to a compiled fitness function (miosd plus a `check_*` in 98-drift-checks.sh) that deserializes the WHOLE registry and asserts: every `template`/`target`/`fixture.base`/`fixture.expected` is a git-TRACKED, present path; every `apply.target` is `HOME`/`%USERPROFILE%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%`/`%APPDATA%`-relative (never absolute outside HOME) or an `HKCU\` key; each merge kind carries its fixture pair; no surface name contains a dot. Reuse the typed `Surface` structs from the serde deserialization task.
details.why: An operator editing the registry through the Portal (ADR-0009) can author a surface that stays green in CI and only explodes at runtime -- including an `apply.target` that writes outside HOME.

title: Terminal step: native status/diff summary in miosd, then delete the Python engine and its wrapper
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- ends the strangler-fig with ONE projector in the tree rather than two forever.
acceptance_criteria: miosd renders the status/diff summary and tally natively; both Python files are deleted; no tracked file references them; `cargo test` and `just drift-gate` green with the `[migration]` toggle removed.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles` (255 lines) is a read-only orchestrator that SHELLS the engine and re-parses its stdout with a regex (`_LINE`) to print a per-surface OK/skip/change/refuse table plus tally (`_classify`/`_dest_of`/`_print_summary`/`_rc_for`). Reimplement that summary NATIVELY in `miosd dotfiles status/diff` -- no stdout scraping, since the Rust code already holds each surface's outcome. Then, after the `[migration]` toggle has defaulted every surface to Rust for the agreed soak and the goldens plus drift-gate have stayed green for N releases, DELETE both `usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render` (the engine) and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles` (the wrapper).
details.why: Keeping the Python engine and a stdout-scraping wrapper beside the Rust binary is precisely the duplication this campaign exists to remove, and without a dependency-ordered final delete the tree ships two projectors indefinitely.

title: Add a Law-15 cross-repo equivalence gate for the registry, templates and fixtures
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- keeps the shared dotfiles SSOT byte-identical across mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git through the riskiest phase of the migration.
acceptance_criteria: the gate detects an injected registry/template/fixture divergence between the two repos; both repos currently pass; the recipe is documented in the migration runbook.

details.what_how: The `[dotfiles.registry.*]` block, `usr/share/mios/theme/templates/*.tmpl` and `usr/share/mios/theme/fixtures/*` are shared SSOT surfaces, and mios-bootstrap is the sibling repo (present at `C:\mios-bootstrap`). Per Law 15 every change to them must land byte-identically in BOTH repos. Add a cross-repo equivalence fitness function -- a `check_*` that runs when the sibling repo is present, plus a documented `just verify-both-repos` recipe -- hashing the registry section and the templates/fixtures trees and FAILING on any divergence. Stage explicit paths in each repo; never `git add -A`, since AGY shares the tree.
details.why: Law 15 mandates mirroring shared SSOT surfaces, and a per-surface migration is exactly when the two repos skew apart unnoticed -- producing a bootstrap that projects a different theme than the OS.

title: Move wsl-theme-bridge's light/dark mapping into `[theme]` SSOT and make a flip re-project surfaces
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- closes the last theme consumer that neither reads from nor re-triggers the SSOT.
acceptance_criteria: the bridge sources interval and gtk/color-scheme mapping from mios.toml `[theme]`; a light/dark flip re-projects theme surfaces; the WSL-only guard and degrade-open behavior are byte-unchanged.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/wsl-theme-bridge.sh` polls the Windows `AppsUseLightTheme` registry value and maps it to a GNOME color-scheme plus gtk-theme, but the mapping is HARDCODED (`adw-gtk3-dark`/`adw-gtk3`, `prefer-dark`/`default`) and the 15s interval is a magic default. Move the poll interval, the gtk-theme names and the color-scheme mapping into mios.toml `[theme]` (read as `${VAR:-LIT}` with the current values as fallback), and on a detected light/dark flip trigger a projector re-render/apply through the miosd theme path so dependent surfaces re-project -- not just a `gsettings` write. Keep the WSL-only guard and the degrade-open exits verbatim.
details.why: The one surface that reacts to the host OS carries hardcoded theme names and a magic interval outside the SSOT, so an operator changing their theme in mios.toml gets a WSL session that ignores them.

title: Add a determinism gate: render twice under varied TZ/LANG/hash-seed and byte-compare
goal: E-22 Dotfiles projection: one engine, every surface, both platforms -- makes the drift-gate sound by proving projection is a pure function of the SSOT.
acceptance_criteria: the twice-render byte-comparison passes under varied TZ/LANG/hash seed; a deliberately injected nondeterminism (e.g. unordered map iteration) fails it; `cargo test` and `just drift-gate` are green.

details.what_how: The drift-gate assumes render/derive are pure, but the code reads a clock (`_utc_stamp` at L1149, for `.mios-bak` names) and relies on map ordering (`_derive_registry` uses `sort_keys=True`; `_json_deep_merge` preserves insertion order) -- so a Rust port could leak HashMap iteration order, locale-sensitive sorting, or an env/clock read into a COMMITTED artifact. Add a CI fitness function that runs `miosd dotfiles render` and each merge derive TWICE under different TZ, LANG and Rust hash seed and byte-compares the outputs, plus a static rule forbidding any clock or env read on the derive path except the apply-only backup timestamp. Wire it into the crate's `cargo test` and the drift-gate.
details.where: `src/mios-rs/miosd/, usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render (_utc_stamp L1149, _derive_registry sort_keys L755, _json_deep_merge L273), automation/98-drift-checks.sh`
details.why: A Rust==Python parity proptest does not prove run-to-run stability, so nondeterministic ordering could land in a committed artifact and show up as phantom drift-gate failures nobody can reproduce.

title: Freeze the resolver output as versioned golden-master fixtures before any port
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- installs the losslessness safety net that every later resolver rewrite is measured against.
acceptance_criteria: a cargo test snapshot-compares a live `mios-env-snapshot` run to `env-baseline.txt` and passes byte-identical; the `.snap` fixtures are committed via explicit path staging; the note records the insta review flow.

details.what_how: Capture the current observable resolver output as immutable golden masters so rewrites are checked against a recorded result rather than hand-written expectations. The three artifacts already exist: `usr/share/mios/reference/env-baseline.txt` (2475 emitted `MIOS_*` lines), `usr/share/mios/names.generated.txt` (503 canonical path->name rows), and `usr/share/mios/referenced_names.txt` (1181). Add a `mios-resolver-goldens` test target under `tools/native` (or a `tests/` dir) that copies all three into trycmd/insta `.snap` fixtures and asserts a fresh `bash usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot` run reproduces `env-baseline.txt` byte-for-byte under `LC_ALL=C`. Document the accept/review workflow (`cargo insta review`) in a short reference note so fixtures can only change deliberately.
details.why: The resolver is untested shell plus Python emitting 2475 keys; without a frozen golden, any port silently changes a key nobody notices until a service reads the wrong value at boot.

title: Extract the get_aliases prefix-family and per-key rules into ONE declarative derivation-graph table
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- the structural core: one table defines every dotted-path -> `MIOS_*` derivation.
acceptance_criteria: `alias-derivation.tsv` exists and, parsed by a check script, reproduces the EXACT alias set `get_aliases` emits for every path in `names.generated.txt` (503 rows) with zero diff; the file is mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: The derivation is currently a ~330-line hand-coded if/elif ladder in `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py::get_aliases` (lines ~224-557), partially and INCOMPLETELY re-implemented in `tools/native/generate-names-registry/src/main.rs::alias_for`, and again in `tools/generate-names-registry.py`. Author a single declarative data file -- `usr/share/mios/reference/alias-derivation.tsv` (or .toml) -- expressing the ~13 systematic prefix families (`ai.vllm.*` -> `MIOS_VLLM_*`, `ports.*` -> `MIOS_PORT_*`/`MIOS_*_PORT`, `identity.*` -> `MIOS_USER...`, `image.sidecars.*` -> `..._IMAGE`/`..._VERSION`, `services.*`, etc.) plus the enumerated per-key exceptions, in the same `canonical<TAB>alias<TAB>disposition` spirit as the existing `usr/share/mios/reference/value-aliases.tsv`. Lands as pure data with a schema-doc header -- no consumer is repointed yet. Mirror into mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.
details.why: Three divergent copies of the same derivation logic mean the Rust and Python name registries already disagree, and no compiled resolver can be written until there is one authoritative statement of the rules.

title: Make `mios_toml.py::get_aliases` read the derivation table instead of its if/elif ladder
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- converts the authoritative resolver from hand-maintained code to SSOT-derived data.
acceptance_criteria: `get_aliases` contains no per-section if/elif ladder; `names.generated.txt` and `env-baseline.txt` regenerate byte-identical; `check_names_registry`, `check_resolver_twin_equivalence` and `check_resolved_env_lossless` are all green.

details.what_how: Strangler-fig the Python resolver onto the new table: rewrite `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py::get_aliases` to load `usr/share/mios/reference/alias-derivation.tsv` once (module-level cache) and resolve a dotted path by longest-prefix-family match plus exact-key override, deleting the ~330-line if/elif body. Keep the old ladder callable behind a `MIOS_ALIAS_LEGACY=1` fallback for one release (degrade-open). Prove byte-parity by regenerating `names.generated.txt` and running `mios-env-snapshot`: the diff against the frozen 2475-line `env-baseline.txt` golden must be empty, and `check_resolver_twin_equivalence` (tools/check-resolver-twin.py, which imports `get_aliases`) must stay green because both twins now read the same table.
details.why: Until the authoritative resolver consumes the table, the table is unproven documentation and the compiled crates would adopt rules nothing validates.

title: Grow mios-ssot-walk from a stub into the one shared native walk + derivation library
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- one compiled library so the derivation logic cannot re-diverge across tools.
acceptance_criteria: mios-ssot-walk exposes `walk`/`process_val`/`alias_lookup` with `cargo test -p mios-ssot-walk` green; the crate is a workspace member; `alias_lookup` reproduces the `alias-derivation.tsv` rows.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-ssot-walk/src/lib.rs` is a near-empty stub (only `EXCLUDED_SECTIONS` and `is_excluded_section`). Grow it into the single shared Rust SSOT engine by porting `walk()` (mios_toml.py:564-576, the recursive section flattener that skips `routing.domains`), `process_val()` (mios_toml.py:578-589, bool/list/ports-stack-offset handling), the `WALK_MOSTLY_DEAD`/`WALK_EMIT_KEEP` sets (mios_toml.py:591-601), and an `alias_lookup()` that parses `usr/share/mios/reference/alias-derivation.tsv`. details.why: The empty stub is exactly why `generate-names-registry` shipped its own incomplete `alias_for`; without a real shared lib every new compiled tool re-implements the walk and re-introduces the divergence.

title: Rewrite the Rust generate-names-registry onto the shared lib and kill its incomplete `alias_for`
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- makes the compiled generator a faithful projector of the same registry the Python one emits.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust generator's output is byte-identical to `tools/generate-names-registry.py`'s output and to the committed `names.generated.txt`; the crate is a workspace member with a passing trycmd snapshot.

title: Cut check_names_registry over to the compiled generate-names-registry and demote the Python generator to a thin exec shim
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- finishes one strangler-fig lane so a libexec-tier bash/Python generator is replaced by a compiled binary only after byte-parity is proven.
acceptance_criteria: check_names_registry validates against the compiled generator and is green on the full tree with the Python script out of the hot path; a negative test that stales `names.generated.txt` still fails the gate.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh::check_names_registry` (line 2064) today shells `tools/generate-names-registry.py` to validate that `names.generated.txt` and `referenced_names.txt` are fresh. Switch the check to invoke `tools/native/target/release/generate-names-registry` when that binary is present and fall back to the Python script only when it is absent (degrade-open, matching the existing python3-missing pattern). Then reduce `tools/generate-names-registry.py` to a shim that execs the binary, preserving the stable entrypoint name and the `git ls-files` referenced-name scan. Keep the byte-parity assertion inside the check so any future shim-vs-binary divergence fails loudly rather than silently picking a winner.
details.why: Two live implementations of the registry generator can drift apart the moment either side is edited, and the drift-gate would keep validating the slower, unhardened one.

title: Scaffold the mios-resolve crate: a typed layered resolver whose `--emit-env` matches env-baseline exactly
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- replaces the highest-traffic shell string-munging surface in the tree with a compiled, type-checked resolver core.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo run -p mios-resolve -- --emit-env` under `HOME=/nonexistent` with vendor-only layers diffs empty against `env-baseline.txt`; the crate builds clean under `clippy -D warnings`; the toggle stays off so nothing is rerouted.

details.what_how: Create `tools/native/mios-resolve` composing the same ordered providers `userenv.sh` does: vendor `/usr/share/mios/mios.toml` < host `/etc/mios/mios.toml` < user `~/.config/mios/mios.toml`, each expanded by its `mios.d/*.toml` fragments in tier-major lexical order, with empty-string-never-overrides. Use figment (or serde+toml) to deserialize into typed structs -- the struct IS the schema, failing loudly on shape errors -- then serialize the `MIOS_*` projection from the typed model through `mios-ssot-walk::alias_lookup`, applying `process_val`'s ports `stack_offset` and the post-load pgvector `listen_loopback -> MIOS_PG_BIND_ADDR` transform (userenv.sh:258-261). Gate activation behind `[migration].use_rust_resolver` (default off). Do NOT reroute `userenv.sh` in this slice; it produces only the binary plus a `--emit-env` mode compared against `env-baseline.txt`.
details.why: Today a shell/Python resolver silently yields a wrong string on an edge-case layer merge and that value flows straight into a Quadlet -- there is no type system anywhere between mios.toml and a running container.

title: Golden trycmd/insta snapshots pinning mios-resolve to the shell oracle across all four layer scenarios
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- supplies the characterization harness that must prove byte-parity BEFORE any shell resolver path is deleted.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-resolve` runs all four scenario snapshots green, and deliberately altering one fixture value flips a snapshot -- proving the tests bite rather than rubber-stamp.

details.what_how: Add snapshot tests covering the layered scenarios the twins support: (1) vendor-only (`env-baseline.txt`), (2) vendor+host overlay, (3) vendor+host+user overlay, (4) vendor plus a `mios.d/*.toml` fragment tier-major merge. Use trycmd for whole-CLI stdout and exit code of `mios-resolve --emit-env`, and insta `.snap` files for the structured typed-model dump. Reuse the frozen goldens and add small fixture TOMLs under the crate's `tests/` for the overlay cases, pinning `LC_ALL=C` for deterministic ordering. Any deviation becomes an explicit accept/review event.
details.why: Without recorded goldens the compiled resolver can drift from the shell result in a scenario nobody hand-wrote an expectation for, and the divergence surfaces as a broken service at first boot.

title: Differential proptest harness running random-valid mios.toml through both the userenv.sh oracle and mios-resolve
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- lands the proptest differential oracle that makes the compiled plane trustworthy rather than merely tested by example.
acceptance_criteria: the difftest passes over >=256 generated documents with zero divergence, and an intentionally-introduced resolver bug is caught and shrunk to a minimal counterexample; the harness is documented alongside `check-resolver-twin.py`.

details.what_how: Mechanize the Global-Unification lossless-diff gate as property-based differential testing. Add a proptest generator emitting random-but-valid mios.toml documents (varying `[ports]` ints, `[identity]`/`[locale]` strings, `[ai.vllm]`/`[ai.sglang]` toggles, `[image.sidecars]` refs, `[colors]` hexes); for each document run BOTH the bash oracle (`source tools/lib/userenv.sh; env | grep ^MIOS_`) and `mios-resolve --emit-env`, asserting the emitted key set AND every value are identical. proptest auto-shrinks any divergence to a minimal failing mios.toml. Wire it as `cargo test -p mios-resolve --features difftest` and as a SOFT CI step (it needs bash), mirroring `check_resolver_twin_equivalence`'s Linux-only posture.
details.why: Hand-written examples only cover the shapes someone thought of; the divergences that ship are the ones nobody imagined, and today nothing generates them.

title: Route userenv.sh through mios-resolve behind the toggle, keeping the Python heredoc as the degrade-open fallback
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the actual strangler cutover: old and new resolvers coexist behind one SSOT value, provably lossless in both states.
acceptance_criteria: with `use_rust_resolver=false` the resolved env is byte-identical to today; with `=true` both `just` and `mios-env-snapshot` reproduce `env-baseline.txt`; `check_userenv_parity` stays green and the lossless gate passes in both toggle states.

details.what_how: `tools/lib/userenv.sh` (byte-identical twin `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh`, enforced by flatten check 27) resolves by running an embedded Python heredoc (lines 114-241) that imports `mios_toml` and prints exports. Add a front door in `_mios_load_unified`: when `[migration].use_rust_resolver` is true AND `tools/native/target/release/mios-resolve` exists, eval its `--emit-env` output; otherwise fall through to the existing heredoc unchanged in `${...:-}` degrade-open style. Because both twins must stay byte-identical, apply the edit to `tools/lib/userenv.sh` and re-run the resync so `check_userenv_parity` holds. With the toggle OFF the resolution path must be bit-for-bit what it is today.
details.why: Until the compiled resolver is actually on the path it is dead code -- and a cutover without a toggle means the only rollback for a bad resolve is a revert-and-rebuild while every service reads wrong values.

title: Give mios-resolve miette/thiserror diagnostics that point at the offending mios.toml span
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- the operator-facing half of the compiled resolver: config failures become compiler-grade, span-anchored reports.
acceptance_criteria: feeding mios-resolve a mios.toml with a bad `[ports]` value or malformed `[colors]` hex prints a miette diagnostic with the correct highlighted span; internal errors are typed thiserror variants; `clippy -D warnings` is clean.

details.what_how: Adopt the two-layer CLI error standard. Define thiserror enums for internal/library errors (parse failure, unknown section, type mismatch, bad hex in `[colors]`, non-int in `[ports]`) that drift-gates can match programmatically, and wrap them with miette for end-user diagnostics carrying source spans, labels and help text, returning `miette::Result` from `main`. Compute spans from byte offsets rather than char counts so UTF-8 highlights land correctly. A malformed `[colors].bg`, or a string where a port int is required, must print a report pointing AT the line in mios.toml.
details.why: Today a mistyped SSOT value produces an opaque bash failure string or, worse, a silent empty default -- the operator gets no line number and the gates get no matchable error variant.

title: Unify the emitted `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` vs consumed `MIOS_VLLM_*` mismatch through the derivation table
goal: E-10 One canonical name -- closes the named canonical-walk/consumer mismatch so no capability carries a second name (Law 9).
acceptance_criteria: exactly one canonical vllm/sglang key family remains per concept; `check_var_closure` is green; no consumer references a dropped alias; the env-baseline diff is reviewed and intentional.

details.what_how: The alias engine emits BOTH the canonical `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` (from the `ai.vllm.*` walk) and the short `MIOS_VLLM_*` (a `get_aliases` special case, `mios_toml.py:227-232`), while consumers reference the short form -- a value-duplicating pair. In `alias-derivation.tsv` declare the short `MIOS_VLLM_*`/`MIOS_SGLANG_*` as the single canonical key and the long `MIOS_AI_VLLM_*` as an explicit derive alias, or drop it entirely if `referenced_names.txt` shows no consumer. Confirm with `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py` that the referenced set stays a subset of the emitted set. Repoint straggler consumers (grep `MIOS_AI_VLLM_` across `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/server.py` and the vllm Quadlet/unit) to the short canonical, and bump `env-baseline.txt` deliberately if the emitted set legitimately shrinks.
details.why: An emitter and a consumer that disagree on a key name is a silent-empty bug class -- the inference lane reads an unset variable and falls back rather than failing.

title: Expand Rust mios-version-check to subsume the whole check_version_ssot surface, then demote the bash check
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- collapses enforcement of the ~79 version-dupe pairs into one compiled gate so a version is declared once.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust binary raises every violation `check_version_ssot` can raise (verified by seeding a mismatch in each surface) and the bash check delegates under the toggle with its own path still green; negatives cover os-release and Cargo.toml drift.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-version-check/src/main.rs` today compares only `VERSION`, mios.toml `[meta].mios_version` and the single root Containerfile ARG. The authoritative bash `check_version_ssot` (98-drift-checks.sh:3598-~3700) does far more: `os-release` VERSION/VERSION_ID/BUILD_ID/PRETTY_NAME/CPE_NAME, ALL `*Containerfile*` via `git ls-files`, every `tools/native` Cargo.toml version, the root mios.toml, plus a git-ls-files literal scan for stray `v?0.x.y`. Port each of those into the Rust binary (git ls-files or walkdir) emitting the same violation lines, then demote `check_version_ssot` to delegate to the binary when `[migration].use_rust_version_check` is true, keeping the bash body as fallback.
details.why: The version family is the largest value-dupe cluster in the tree and its only enforcement is a sprawling bash function nobody can safely extend -- so new version surfaces get added ungated.

title: Generate the globals.{ps1,sh} identity and UID/GID fallback literals from mios.toml instead of authoring them twice
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES -- removes a hand-maintained literal family from the resolver fallback path so there is a key to float TO.
acceptance_criteria: every uid/gid/user/subuid literal in globals.{ps1,sh} is generated from mios.toml with no hand-authored `else {N}`; `check_globals_ports` fails a seeded uid drift; the mios.toml change is mirrored into mios-bootstrap.git per Law 15.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/globals.ps1` (and its sibling `automation/lib/globals.sh`) hand-maintain `else { N }` fallbacks -- `MIOS_USER='mios'`, `MIOS_UID=1000`, `MIOS_FORGE_UID=816`, `MIOS_CEPH_UID=819`, `MIOS_SEARXNG_UID=818`, `MIOS_HERMES_UID=820`, `MIOS_SUBUID_START=100000` (globals.ps1:33-59) -- duplicating values that belong in mios.toml `[identity]`, `[accounts]` and per-service uid/gid. Add the missing keys to mios.toml, then generate the fallback blocks at build time (extend the existing sync path or add a `mios-sync-globals` codegen step that writes the else-literals from the resolved env) so neither globals file is authored by hand. Extend `check_globals_ports` (98-drift-checks.sh:1829) to gate the uid/gid/user literals the same way it already gates `MIOS_PORT_*` defaults.
details.why: A service uid changed in mios.toml but not in the two globals fallbacks yields containers whose files are owned by the wrong account on any host where the resolver degrades to defaults.

title: Normalize root paths in mios-env-snapshot so a differing `$ROOT`/`$HOME` can never false-drift the lossless gate
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- makes the lossless invariant hold in CI, which every later namespace-collapse step depends on.
acceptance_criteria: `env-baseline.txt` contains no host-specific absolute prefixes; `check_resolved_env_lossless` passes from two different `$ROOT`/`$HOME` locations; a negative test proves a genuine value change still fails; both userenv.sh copies stay byte-identical.

details.what_how: `env-baseline.txt` line 332 bakes a host-specific path -- `MIOS_BOOTSTRAP_REPO_URL=C:/mios-bootstrap`, captured on the Windows dev host -- so `check_resolved_env_lossless` (98-drift-checks.sh:6061) would diff and fail on a Linux runner. Extend `usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot` (which already pins `HOME=/nonexistent` and `MIOS_ROOT`) to rewrite any absolute repo-root or bootstrap-root prefix in emitted values to a stable placeholder token (`@ROOT@` / `@BOOTSTRAP@`) before the final sort, and mirror the same normalization in the `normalize_path` helper in `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh:126-133`, which is Windows-drive-only today. Regenerate a root-agnostic `env-baseline.txt` and add a `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` case that runs the snapshot from a DIFFERENT `$ROOT` and still matches.
details.why: A baseline embedding its capture host's path is a latent CI-red that will block every future resolver change the first time the gate runs off that machine.

title: Make check_no_duplicate_value_key actually call `_violation` instead of unconditionally passing
goal: E-09 One value, one name -- turns the campaign's keystone fitness function from decorative into enforcing.
acceptance_criteria: the check raises `_violation` on an undeclared value-dup and is green on the current tree; a seeded undeclared dup key fails in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`; allowlisted pairs still pass.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh::check_no_duplicate_value_key` (line 6097) computes value-duplicate groups inside a Python heredoc but only prints `DUPLICATE_VALUES_FOUND:{len(dups)}` and then unconditionally echoes `passed` -- it never calls `_violation`, so it enforces nothing. Rework it to ratchet against an allowlist in `usr/share/mios/reference/value-aliases.tsv` (`canonical<TAB>alias<TAB>disposition`): a group of >=2 keys sharing a value is permitted only when every pair is declared derive/delete/keep-distinct there, and any NEW unallowlisted value-duplicating key raises `_violation`. Keep the existing `EXEMPT_VALUES` (true/false, small ints, canonical ports) and reuse the `mios-env-snapshot` resolution the check already performs.
details.why: A gate that can never fail is worse than no gate -- the whole de-duplication campaign is currently reporting success while new duplicate keys land unimpeded.

title: Bake the native SSOT workspace once, deterministically, instead of running cargo inside drift-check bodies
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- makes the compiled tooling a digest-stable build artifact with a pinned lockfile as the reproducibility SSOT.
acceptance_criteria: one build step compiles the workspace `--release --locked` with a deterministic epoch; no check body invokes `cargo build`; two independent builds produce identical binary digests for the SSOT crates.

details.what_how: Native binaries are built three different ways today: `Containerfile:49` has a bare `cargo build --release`, `98-drift-checks.sh:4880` runs `cargo build --manifest-path ... -p mios-ssot-lint` on demand inside a check, and `automation/85-bake-plan.sh` merely probes for a prebuilt `mios-bake-plan`. Consolidate into one deterministic step (an automation phase or `just native-build --release`) that compiles the whole workspace with `--locked` and `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` keyed off the git commit time, staging `mios-resolve`, `generate-names-registry`, `mios-ssot-lint` and `mios-version-check` to a known path. Check bodies then only EXEC the prebuilt binary and hard-fail when it is missing rather than compiling it themselves. Commit and honor `tools/native/Cargo.lock`.
details.why: Compiling inside a check makes the gate's runtime depend on a toolchain and network state that the bake does not control -- it is slow, non-reproducible, and can pass on one machine while failing on the runner.

title: Add cargo-deny + cargo-audit supply-chain drift-gates with Cargo.lock as the SSOT
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- gives the Rust plane the dependency-surface gate that bash never needed and Rust cannot ship without.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo deny check` and `cargo audit` pass on the committed lockfile; `check_native_supply_chain` is registered and fails on a seeded banned or advisory-carrying crate; the license allow-list is documented.

details.what_how: The native workspace has no dependency gate at all. Add `tools/native/deny.toml` covering banned and duplicate crates, a license allow-list operationalizing the FOSS-upstream posture, and RustSec advisories; then add `check_native_supply_chain` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` running `cargo deny --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml check` and `cargo audit --file tools/native/Cargo.lock`, SOFT-skipping when the tools are absent per the established python3/cargo-missing pattern. Commit `tools/native/Cargo.lock` as the reproducibility SSOT -- consistent with SBOM-not-hardcode, dependency digests recorded rather than hand-pinned. Register the gate immediately after the clippy/fmt gate so the native lint chain runs as one block.
details.why: Every crate added to the workspace pulls a transitive tree nobody reviews -- an advisory or an incompatible license lands in the shipped image with no signal at all.

title: Reconcile the two divergent alias-derivation implementations behind a get_aliases parity gate
goal: E-10 One canonical name -- makes `names.generated.txt` a complete registry so the one-canonical-name check has the full alias surface to police.
acceptance_criteria: `names.generated.txt` includes the identity/locale/portal/a2a/ai/ports/sidecar aliases it omits today; `check_alias_derivation_parity` is registered and green; the regenerated registry is staged by explicit path.

details.what_how: `tools/generate-names-registry.py._alias_for` maps only `ai.vllm.*` and `ai.sglang.*`, while `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py.get_aliases` maps roughly 30 families (identity, locale, portal, a2a, `ai.*`, `paths.*`, pgvector/pg, `image.sidecars.*`, `ports.*`, ...) -- so `names.generated.txt` silently under-reports the real alias surface. Add `check_alias_derivation_parity` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that imports `get_aliases` and asserts, for every dotted path in the walked SSOT, that the registry generator emits an identical alias set, failing loudly on any family `_alias_for` omits. title: Bring `/etc/mios/install.env` under the one resolver with a lossless parity and quoting-safety gate
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan -- eliminates a third, ungated serialization of the namespace so the lossless invariant covers what services actually read.
acceptance_criteria: install.env is provably a projection of the resolved namespace (parity check green); a planted `$`-bearing or space-bearing value fails the quoting-safety invariant; the check is registered in `main()`.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/system-sync-env.sh` generates `/etc/mios/install.env` -- a third namespace serialization consumed by three incompatible parsers (systemd `EnvironmentFile=`, `bash source`, `podman --env-file`) -- yet the only lossless gate, `check_resolved_env_lossless`, snapshots `userenv.sh` exports and never looks at it. Re-derive install.env generation from the same resolver path `mios-env-snapshot` uses, then add `check_install_env_parity` that renders install.env in a clean env and diffs its `KEY=value` set against the resolved `MIOS_*` baseline, accounting for the documented secret-eviction and bare-value quoting rules. Add a quoting-safety invariant asserting no value contains shell metacharacters, whitespace or `$` that would break any of the three parsers.
details.why: install.env feeds systemd units and podman at first boot -- if the namespace collapses while install.env tracks a stale SSOT, services read values the resolver stopped emitting, and the lossless gate reports green throughout.

title: Add a PowerShell env-snapshot leg and a cross-plane parity gate (globals.ps1 vs userenv.sh)
goal: E-03 PowerShell surface -- puts the Windows-plane resolver under the same output-parity discipline as the bash twin.

title: Add a namespace bijection / collision invariant gate over the derivation table
goal: E-10 One canonical name -- guarantees key injectivity so no two SSOT facts can collapse onto one env name.
acceptance_criteria: `check_namespace_bijection` is registered and green on the current tree; a planted colliding alias fails it; intentional shared aliases (e.g. `MIOS_HOSTNAME` from `identity.hostname` vs `user.hostname`) live in an explicit allowlist rather than being tolerated silently.

details.what_how: `check_no_duplicate_value_key` targets equal VALUES; nothing asserts KEY injectivity -- that no two distinct dotted paths derive the same `MIOS_*` name and no alias collides with a canonical emitted from a different path. Given `get_aliases`' ~30-family if/elif ladder (`ports.*` emits both `MIOS_PORT_x` and `MIOS_x_PORT`; `image.sidecars.*` emits `_IMAGE` and `_VERSION`), an accidental collision silently makes one path shadow another. Add `check_namespace_bijection` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` -- and fold it into `mios-ssot-lint` -- walking the full SSOT, building the `path -> {canonical, aliases}` map, and failing on any env name reachable from more than one distinct path unless explicitly whitelisted as an intentional shared alias.
details.why: A two-paths-to-one-name collision is a data-loss bug -- one operator setting overwrites another with no error -- and the value-duplicate check cannot see it.

title: Census and collapse the ~79 version-dupe pairs rooted in `image.sidecars.*` to one SBOM-derived source
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening -- enforces ADR-0003, that a resolved version is build-recorded SBOM data and never a hand-authored SSOT literal.
acceptance_criteria: the version-family census is committed; duplicated per-sidecar version literals derive from one SBOM-recorded source; `check_version_family_collapse` is green; the full drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: The `get_aliases` `image.sidecars.*` branch emits `MIOS_{name}_IMAGE` plus `MIOS_{name}_VERSION` per sidecar which, combined with per-component version keys elsewhere, is where the ~79 version-dupe pairs live -- distinct from the `meta.mios_version` parity that `mios-version-check` covers. Enumerate every `MIOS_*_VERSION` in `env-baseline.txt`, group equal values, and collapse each family to one canonical resolved from the SBOM/baked manifest (float `:latest` intent, record the digest at build) instead of duplicated literals in `[image.sidecars]`. Add `check_version_family_collapse` asserting no two version keys carry the same hand-authored literal that should instead derive from a single SBOM source.
details.why: Nothing today collapses the per-component version family -- `mios-version-check` only validates the single top-level `mios_version` -- so a sidecar bump must be hand-edited in several places and any missed copy pins an image to a stale version.

title: Replace the MIOS_ENV_BASELINE_BUMP=1 blanket whitewash with a reviewed baseline-regen tool + an added/removed changes manifest
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- makes the losslessness invariant that guards every collapse step auditable instead of overridable by one env var.
acceptance_criteria: `env-baseline.txt` can only be regenerated through `just baseline-regen`; a bump whose `env-baseline.changes.tsv` disagrees with the real added/removed set FAILS `check_resolved_env_lossless`; the full drift-gate is green.

details.what_how: `check_resolved_env_lossless` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` today honors `MIOS_ENV_BASELINE_BUMP=1` as a blanket override that blesses ANY change to `env-baseline.txt`, so an unintended namespace mutation passes unexamined. Add `tools/mios-baseline-update.py` plus a `just baseline-regen` recipe that regenerates `usr/share/mios/reference/env-baseline.txt` AND emits a machine-readable `usr/share/mios/reference/env-baseline.changes.tsv` enumerating the added / removed / renamed keys for that commit. Then rewrite the gate so a bump is accepted only when the committed changes manifest matches the actual computed diff of the baseline -- turning the escape hatch into a reviewed artifact.
details.why: A lossless gate whose only bypass is an unaudited env var is not lossless. Mid-collapse, an accidentally dropped key ships silently and the regression surfaces later as a missing runtime value with no commit to bisect to.

title: Enforce LF/no-BOM/trailing-newline determinism for the Rust resolver, golden fixtures and env-baseline on a Windows checkout
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- keeps the byte-exact lossless diff trustworthy on the cross-platform checkout the resolver is actually developed in.
acceptance_criteria: a deliberately CRLF/BOM-injected fixture is normalized on ingest and produces unchanged resolved output; a CRLF-committed baseline FAILS the new normalization assertion; the drift-gate is green on both an LF checkout and a CRLF checkout.

details.what_how: `mios-env-snapshot` already needed an `LC_ALL=C` fix to stop locale-driven sort drift; the same determinism hazard hits the compiled resolver and its golden fixtures on the `C:\MiOS` Windows checkout, where `core.autocrlf` rewrites LF to CRLF and editors prepend a BOM, false-drifting the lossless and golden-master gates. Add a `.gitattributes` pinning `eol=lf` (and `-text` binary-safety where appropriate) over `usr/share/mios/reference/*.txt`, `usr/share/mios/names.generated.txt`, the `tools/native/**/tests` fixture trees and `mios.toml`; add a normalization assertion (no CRLF, no BOM, file ends in a newline) to the census and lossless checks; and make the file reads in `mios-ssot-walk` / `mios-resolve` strip CRLF and a leading BOM on ingest so a mixed checkout can never change resolved output.
details.why: The resolver is explicitly cross-platform and this very tree lives on Windows; a compiled resolver reading files byte-for-byte will false-drift on CRLF/BOM, and the bash tools only ever escaped this partially via `LC_ALL=C`.

title: Law-15: mirror the derivation-table SSOT into mios-bootstrap.git and audit its hardcoded namespace literals
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the 2523-key MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- extends the one-value-derived rule to the one repo every other GUP task ignores.
acceptance_criteria: no un-fallback-guarded namespace literal remains in `bootstrap.ps1` or `bootstrap.sh`; the shared SSOT surface is byte-identical across `mios.git` and `mios-bootstrap.git`; every commit stages explicit paths only (never `git add -A`).

details.what_how: `mios-bootstrap.git` (`bootstrap.ps1` / `bootstrap.sh`) ships no resolver copy, yet it is a Law-15 shared surface that can hardcode ports, image names, users and `MIOS_*` keys the SSOT owns. Grep both entrypoints for `MIOS_*` and for literal ports/hosts/image refs; route each through the SSOT-derived set using the `${VAR:-LIT}` degrade-open form that retains the literal as a fallback; and where the derivation-graph table / names registry is genuinely shared, mirror it into `mios-bootstrap.git` so both repos stay byte-synced. Add a cross-repo parity note or test asserting the shared tokens match `mios.git`.
details.why: Law 15 requires shared SSOT surfaces to be verified and mirrored in BOTH repos; the namespace collapse is exactly such a surface, so bootstrap silently keeps serving retired spellings after the waves land.

title: Anchor the mios-hardcode-lint localhost:80 / :443 allowlist patterns so they stop masking the whole :80xx range
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- repairs the lint bug that silently disarms the NO-HARDCODE gate, making the entire campaign enforced rather than advisory.
acceptance_criteria: `exempt_patterns` are anchored in both repos' `mios.toml`; running `mios-hardcode-lint` over a fixture line containing `http://localhost:8090` now REPORTS the `:8090` hardcode where it previously PASSed; the coupled float edits keep `check_no_hardcode` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` green.

details.what_how: In `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` `[security.nohc_allowlist].exempt_patterns` (lines 842-861) the entries `localhost:80`, `localhost:443`, `127\.0\.0\.1:80` and `127\.0\.0\.1:443` are consumed as UNANCHORED `re.search` patterns by `mios-hardcode-lint` (lines 176-182 and 221-227 iterate `exempt_rx` and set `is_line_exempt` on the whole line). Because `localhost:8090` / `8091` / `8033` / `8053` / `8080` all begin with the literal `localhost:80`, any line carrying those ports is spuriously exempted and its real hardcode goes unflagged. Anchor each with a non-digit lookahead: `localhost:80(?![0-9])`, `localhost:443(?![0-9])`, `127\.0\.0\.1:80(?![0-9])`, `127\.0\.0\.1:443(?![0-9])`. This is a shared SSOT surface, so mirror the edit in BOTH `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` and `C:/mios-bootstrap/mios.toml` (Law 15). Land it COUPLED with the float edits it newly exposes so the gate goes green in the same PR rather than red on merge.
details.why: This one substring bug exempts every published `:80xx` port (cockpit, cockpit_link, open_webui, adguard_ui, guacamole) from the NO-HARDCODE gate -- the gate reports green today while the violations it exists to catch sit in the tree.

title: Extend mios-hardcode-lint's _CODE_EXT to systemd units so usr/lib/systemd/system stops being an unscanned blind spot
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- makes the gate-red unit and quadlet trees visible to the lint so every float below is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: the lint scans `.service`/`.socket`/`.container`/`.timer`/`.conf`; a fixture unit with a bare `ListenStream=0.0.0.0:8090` is REPORTED while `${MIOS_NETWORK_BIND_ALL}:${MIOS_PORT_COCKPIT}` PASSes; `check_no_hardcode` exercises the unit tree.

details.what_how: `_CODE_EXT` in `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` (line 25) is `('.py','.sh','.bash','.toml','.yml','.yaml','.ps1','.psm1')` -- it omits `.service`, `.socket`, `.container`, `.timer` and `.conf`, so `usr/lib/systemd/system/**` and `usr/share/containers/systemd/**` are never port/IP-scanned despite carrying dozens of literals (`cockpit.socket.d/listen.conf` `ListenStream=0.0.0.0:8090`; `hermes-worker.service` `:8888`/`:11235`/`:3002`/`:11441`/`:9223`; `mios-account-sync.service` `127.0.0.1:8432`; `mios-agents.service` `0.0.0.0:8800`). Add the unit and quadlet extensions to `_CODE_EXT` and route them through the existing generic `_check_ports_ips` path (line 212), which is already `#`/`;`/`//`-comment aware; treat `Environment=`, `ExecStart=`, `ListenStream=` and `--bind` values as code. Ship a golden fixture (a synthetic unit with one hardcoded and one `${VAR}`-floated port) proving the scan before wiring it. Keep the `${MIOS_*:-lit}` form exempt, and mirror the `_CODE_EXT` change into the Rust port's scope so the two implementations stay identical.
details.why: The operator named `usr/lib/systemd/system/**` as gate-red, but the lint literally cannot see it -- every unit float in this workstream would land unverified and could silently regress.

title: Route Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1's doubled 100.79.3.50 tailscale fallback through [network].win_tailscale_ip
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- makes the only routable-IP literal in the tree operator-defined rather than baked.
acceptance_criteria: the `.ps1` contains no bare `100.79.3.50` (it reads `$script:MIOS_NETWORK_WIN_TAILSCALE_IP`); the `tailscale ip` probe still wins when tailscale is present; `globals.ps1` exposes the key with `100.79.3.50` as its documented default; the script still runs on a host without tailscale.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/windows/Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1` lines 42-43 hardcode the tailnet IP twice as a degrade-open fallback: `$tsIp = try { (& tailscale ip --4).Trim() } catch { '100.79.3.50' }` plus the validation reassignment. Replace the literal with a value sourced from SSOT -- read `MIOS_NETWORK_WIN_TAILSCALE_IP` as projected through the PowerShell twin `automation/lib/globals.ps1`, keeping the `tailscale ip` probe as the primary and falling back to `$script:MIOS_NETWORK_WIN_TAILSCALE_IP` (which itself carries `100.79.3.50` as its documented `:-lit` default in globals.ps1). This file is currently in the nohc `exempt_files` list, but the literal should be SSOT-derived regardless; add the globals.ps1 default in the same PR. No bootstrap mirror is needed for the helper itself, but the `win_tailscale_ip` key it reads IS mirrored under Law 15 by the `[network]` task.
details.why: A specific tailnet address baked twice into a shipped Windows helper means any operator on a different tailnet silently gets the wrong proxy target with no config surface to correct it.

title: Retire or float the dead SurrealDB DB_URL localhost:8000 that the allowlist anchor exposes
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- clears the first genuine violation the anchored lint uncovers inside `usr/lib/mios`.
acceptance_criteria: post-anchor `mios-hardcode-lint` reports no `localhost:8000` in `db.py`; either the dead constant is removed with no broken importers (agent-pipe tests pass) or it is floated to a real SSOT port; `server.py` is aligned.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/mios_pipe/db.py` line 14 (`DB_URL = "http://localhost:8000"`) and `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/server.py` line 1348 (`os.environ.get("MIOS_DB_URL", "http://localhost:8000")`) reference the retired SurrealDB endpoint. `db.py` is NOT in nohc `exempt_files`, so once the `localhost:80` anchor lands (it currently masks `localhost:8000` through the substring bug) `db.py:14` becomes a hard violation. Per the legacy-purge decision the AI plane is Postgres/pgvector-only, so first VERIFY `:8000` is dead -- grep for live importers of `mios_pipe.db.DB_URL` and readers of `MIOS_DB_URL`. If dead, delete the constant or module, or repoint it to the pgvector DSN; if a live shim remains, float it to a `${MIOS_PORT_PGVECTOR}`-derived value or a dedicated key. `server.py` is in `exempt_files` and will not red the gate, but fix it in the same PR for consistency. Stage explicit paths only.
details.why: A retired SurrealDB relic still sitting in the agent-pipe import path is both a live gate violation and a trap for the next reader, who has no signal that `:8000` no longer exists.

title: Capture golden-master trycmd fixtures for mios-hardcode-lint as the parity oracle before the Rust port
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- establishes the characterization harness that lets a bash/Python verb be replaced with a proven-equivalent binary.
acceptance_criteria: the fixtures directory exists covering all seven violation classes plus PASS and SOFT; each fixture's expected output was generated by running the current Python tool; the corpus is committed by explicit path and documented as the port oracle.

details.what_how: Characterize the current Python `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` as the parity oracle before any porting. Build a fixture corpus under a new `tools/native/mios-hardcode-lint/tests/cli/` with one case per observable class the tool emits: PASS (clean tree), DATE-IN-COMMENT, DATE-IN-STRING (py), HEADER risk (stranded BOM / shebang not on line 1), HARDCODED-PORT/IP (both the py tokenizer path and the generic path), PLAINTEXT-CHPASSWD (ventoy autorun), and the `MIOS_HARDCODE_LINT_SOFT=1` advisory exit-0 path. Record each as a trycmd `.trycmd`/`.toml` fixture capturing argv, stdout, stderr and exit code as produced by the Python tool today. These become the accept/review snapshots the Rust port must reproduce byte for byte.
details.why: Without a captured oracle the Rust rewrite can only be hoped equivalent, and a lint that changes behavior during a port either goes quietly permissive (violations ship) or noisily strict (the gate reds on nothing).

title: Port mios-hardcode-lint to a std-only Rust crate behind the identical CLI facade (strangler)
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the template slice for migrating a leaf libexec verb to compiled, memory-safe code with no interface change.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build -p mios-hardcode-lint` succeeds; `cargo test -p mios-hardcode-lint` passes every trycmd golden fixture byte for byte; the Rust binary and the Python tool produce identical violation sets over the live repo; the Python tool is untouched and the fallback is intact.

details.what_how: Create `tools/native/mios-hardcode-lint` modeled on the existing zero-dependency std-only crate `mios-ssot-lint` (`tools/native/mios-ssot-lint/src/main.rs`). Reimplement every scan the Python tool performs: the `_DATE` regex in `#`-comments and py docstrings (`_date_in_comment_py` / `_generic`), whitespace-led date-in-string (`_date_in_string_py`), `_header_risk` (BOM/shebang), `_check_ports_ips[_py]` with the `_PORT_PATTERNS` + `_IP_PATTERN` + `_is_routable_ip` logic (RFC1918 plus CGNAT 100.64/10 plus loopback exclusions), the ventoy chpasswd check, and reading `[security.nohc_allowlist]` `exempt_files`/`exempt_patterns` from `mios.toml` through the layered resolver (a small std TOML read or the shared `mios-ssot-walk` lib). Match the anchored exempt patterns and the extended `_CODE_EXT` (units). Keep the Python tool in place as the fallback -- do NOT delete it. Add trycmd tests running the golden-master corpus asserting byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit.
details.why: The lint that enforces NO-HARDCODE is itself an unhardened interpreted script with no type safety and no test suite; until it is compiled and characterized, the gate's own correctness rests on nothing.

title: Add mios-hardcode-lint to the Rust workspace and gate it with clippy -D warnings, fmt, cargo-deny/audit
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- gives the Rust plane the shellcheck-equivalent MiOS has never had.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build`, `clippy`, `fmt`, `deny` and `audit` all pass for the crate under `-D warnings`; `unwrap`/`panic`/`todo` are denied and absent from the source; the crate is a workspace member sharing `Cargo.lock`; the gate steps run and are green.

details.what_how: `tools/native/Cargo.toml` `[workspace].members` currently lists only `mios-drift-runner`, `mios-version-check` and `mios-wallpaperd`; the `mios-ssot-lint`/`-walk`/`-aiplane-lint`/`-bake-plan`/`generate-names-registry` crates build standalone. Add `mios-hardcode-lint` to `members` so it builds under the workspace and shares `Cargo.lock` (the reproducibility SSOT). Wire CI/drift-gate steps: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p mios-hardcode-lint -- -D warnings` with targeted restriction lints (`clippy::unwrap_used`, `clippy::panic`, `clippy::todo` denied, so the tool can never panic on a malformed source file, matching the Python tool's degrade-open try/except); plus `cargo deny check` (bans/licenses/advisories) and `cargo audit` against the committed `Cargo.lock`. Order these BEFORE the main drift gate, consistent with the negatives-before-main-gate CI ordering.
details.why: MiOS has no shellcheck CI at all; a compiled crate landing without clippy, fmt and supply-chain checks just relocates the unlinted surface from Python into Rust and adds a dependency tree nobody audits.
