title: Wire the Rust mios-hardcode-lint into drift-gate 98 as a strangler shim with a dual-run parity window
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- starts porting the checks themselves to native Rust so the gate stops being fragile bash, without a risky big-bang cutover.
acceptance_criteria: `check_no_hardcode` runs the Rust binary when built and the Python tool otherwise; the parity window logs zero divergence across the repo; flipping the `[migration]` toggle switches implementation without a rebuild; drift-gate green under both settings.

details.what_how: `check_no_hardcode()` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` (lines 978-996) invokes the Python `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint`. Change it to prefer the built Rust binary at `$ROOT/tools/native/target/release/mios-hardcode-lint` (or debug) when present and fall back to the Python tool otherwise, keeping the verb-name facade identical to callers. For an initial parity window run BOTH and raise `_violation` only if the results DIFFER or either fails (dual-run oracle), logging every divergence; once a gap-free window is observed, demote the invocation to the Rust binary with Python as pure fallback. Gate the swap behind an SSOT toggle in `mios.toml` (e.g. `[migration] use_rust_hardcode_lint`, oxidizr-style per-verb opt-out) so a regression rolls back by flipping one value rather than reverting the build. Keep exit semantics, including soft-mode env passthrough, identical.
details.why: A hard cutover of a gate check has no rollback short of reverting a build; without the dual-run window and the SSOT toggle, any behavioral gap in the new binary reds (or worse, greens) the whole tree with no way to bisect which implementation was at fault.

title: Add check_internal_ports_distinct as a fitness function asserting every [ports].*_internal differs from its published sibling
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- encode the internal!=published false-friend rule as machine-checked policy instead of human vigilance.
acceptance_criteria: the check runs in the gate and PASSes on current SSOT; setting `searxng_internal=8899` (equal to published) reds it; the pairing map is read from TOML, not embedded in the check; the check carries an ADR-0012 number.

details.what_how: Add `check_internal_ports_distinct` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh`, following the existing `check_*` shape (a python3 heredoc reading `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` via tomllib, as `check_container_ports` does at line 1400). It FAILS if any internal key equals its published sibling: `searxng_internal != searxng`, `firecrawl_internal != firecrawl`, `crawl4ai_internal != crawl4ai`, `cockpit_internal != cockpit`. The pairing map must come from a small `[ports.internal_pairs]` table in mios.toml -- never hardcoded in the gate -- mirroring the read-allowlists-from-TOML pattern already used at 98-drift-checks.sh line 2929, so future pairs are declared once. Register the check in the gate's dispatch list and assign it a check number per ADR-0012. Mirror the SSOT table into `C:/mios-bootstrap/mios.toml`.
details.why: Today nothing stops an editor from "tidying" firecrawl 3002 into 8302 and silently collapsing an internal bind onto its published port -- a runtime break discovered only in production rather than at build time.

title: Anchor every remaining bare-port exempt_pattern and document the false-friend pairs inline in both repos
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- close the unanchored-allowlist class that spuriously exempts real `:80xx` violations.
acceptance_criteria: every bare-port exempt pattern is anchored in both repos; the false-friend comment block is present; `mios-hardcode-lint` still PASSes the intentionally-exempt canonical ports (:8640/:8642/:4317) while no longer exempting their numeric neighbours.

details.what_how: Beyond localhost:80/443, the bare-port exemptions in `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.nohc_allowlist].exempt_patterns` (lines 850-861: `:8640`, `:8642`, `:4317`, `:11436`, `:8644`, `:11435`, `:9222`, `:8283`) are unanchored substrings consumed by `re.search`, so each can match inside a longer numeric run. Anchor each with a leading colon plus a trailing non-digit lookahead (e.g. `":8640(?![0-9])"`), and drop entries that become redundant once the port floats to a key -- `:11436` once `[ports].igpu` ships, `:8283` if letta is retired. Add a comment block above the list enumerating the internal!=published false-friends (firecrawl 3002!=8302, searxng 8888!=8899, crawl4ai 11235!=8235, forgejo 3000!=8300, pg 5432!=8432, SSH 2222!=8222, and the intentional `MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT :8640`) so a future editor cannot silently merge them. Mirror both edits into `C:/mios-bootstrap/mios.toml` per Law 15.
details.why: The same unanchored-substring defect that let `localhost:80` mask real violations lives in every one of these entries, so the lint currently under-reports and the campaign cannot trust its own green.

title: Prove Python/Rust hardcode-lint equivalence with a proptest differential-parity harness before deleting the Python tool
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- a proptest differential oracle is what converts a strangler shim into an actual retirement.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test --features difftest` runs proptest over the generated corpora; Python and Rust violation sets match across all cases; a deliberately introduced Rust regression is caught and shrunk to a minimal reproducer.

details.what_how: In `tools/native/mios-hardcode-lint` add a proptest-based differential test (dev-dependency `proptest`) that generates random-but-plausible corpora: synthetic `.py`/`.sh`/`.ps1`/`.service`/`.container` files mixing floated `${MIOS_*:-lit}` placeholders, bare ports (1-65535), RFC1918/CGNAT/loopback IPs, dated comments and header-BOM/shebang permutations, plus randomized `[security.nohc_allowlist]` exempt_files/exempt_patterns. For each generated case run BOTH implementations -- the Python `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` via subprocess as the oracle and the Rust binary -- and assert the emitted `(path, line, class)` violation SETS are identical; proptest auto-shrinks any divergence to a minimal failing file. Feature-gate it as a nightly/opt-in `cargo test` so it never slows the main gate.
details.why: Example-based golden fixtures only spot-check, so the Python tool stays shipped forever as an untrusted fallback -- two lints to maintain and two chances to disagree about what counts as a hardcode.

title: Add check_no_residual_placeholders so a floated unit can never ship an unexpanded ${MIOS_*} to systemd
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- guard the one failure mode the float campaign itself creates, so floating a port never becomes a mis-bind.
acceptance_criteria: check_no_residual_placeholders is registered and green; leaving one un-allowlisted `${MIOS_PORT_FOO}` in a test unit turns the gate red; `just drift-gate` passes on the real tree.

details.what_how: `34-render-quadlets.sh` only rewrites files whose content matches its `'\${MIOS_'` grep gate (line 159) and bakes `${VAR:-lit}` at build time because systemd `Environment=` does NOT expand shell syntax at unit load. Every float task in this workstream adds a `${MIOS_PORT_*:-lit}` to a `.service`/`.socket`/`.conf`; if the render step is skipped or the var is missing from the allowlists, systemd stores the LITERAL string `${MIOS_PORT_X:-8643}` as the value and the service mis-binds. Add `check_no_residual_placeholders()` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh`, registered in the run list near `check_container_ports` (~line 6305), walking the deployed unit and quadlet trees and FAILING on any surviving `${MIOS_` token -- proving the render ran to completion. Implement it as a small std-only Python heredoc mirroring the existing checks' shape (exit 1 on violation).
details.where: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check_no_residual_placeholders, run-list ~6305); asserts over usr/lib/systemd/system/**, usr/share/containers/systemd/**, etc/containers/systemd/**`
details.why: This is the highest-severity hazard the campaign introduces and nothing guards it today -- grepping 98-drift-checks.sh for residual/unrendered/placeholder returns zero hits -- so an unrendered placeholder ships as a hard runtime mis-bind, not a lint smell.

title: Reconcile the two divergent render allowlists and gate their parity with check_render_allowlist_parity
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- a floated var must render identically on every host, so the two hand-maintained renderer allowlists must be one set.
acceptance_criteria: the two allowlists are verified equal-set; check_render_allowlist_parity is registered and green; adding a placeholder to only one list reds the gate; the K3S and OPENCODE naming is reconciled.

details.what_how: The two allowlists in `34-render-quadlets.sh` already DISAGREE: the envsubst list (line 76) names `MIOS_K3S_API_PORT` while the bash-fallback loop (line 99) names `MIOS_PORT_K3S_API` for the same port, and `MIOS_PORT_OPENCODE_GATEWAY` appears only in the bash list -- so a var covered by one renderer but not the other renders differently on hosts with vs without envsubst, a cross-host reproducibility break. First reconcile the lists to an identical set, picking the canonical `MIOS_PORT_*` name and keeping the literal fallback. Then add `check_render_allowlist_parity()` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that (a) asserts the envsubst allowlist set equals the bash-fallback set and (b) scans every rendered unit/quadlet for `${MIOS_*}` placeholders and asserts each appears in BOTH lists.
details.why: The K3S name mismatch and bash-only OPENCODE entry are an already-present, already-shipped bug proving the duplication diverges silently; without the gate every new floated var can land in one list only and behave differently per host.

**Goal:** E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- shared SSOT surfaces move in both repos together (Law 15) or CI hard-fails the moment the vendor keys land.
**What+How:** `check_bootstrap_ports_drift` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:1468`) parses `../mios-bootstrap/mios.toml` (the sibling exists, 76KB) and FAILS when its `[ports]` set diverges from the vendor mios.toml -- so every `[network]` key and `[ports].*_internal` false-friend added by the sibling WS-ZEROHC tasks reds this gate until mirrored. Add the identical `[network]` keys (loopback / bind_all / win_tailscale_ip) and the internal-port keys to the bootstrap repo's mios.toml, staging the explicit path only (never `git add -A`; AGY shares the tree). Then verify the check's comparison scope still treats internal keys correctly, extending its allow-diff logic if it currently compares strict equality over the full `[ports]` table.
**Where:** `../mios-bootstrap/mios.toml ([network] + [ports]); automation/98-drift-checks.sh:1468 check_bootstrap_ports_drift`
**Done When:** both repos' mios.toml carry the same `[network]`/`[ports.*_internal]` keys; check_bootstrap_ports_drift is green; a tomllib parse plus a `wc -l` sanity check of the bootstrap file succeeds.
**Why:** This is a blocking dependency rather than cleanup -- the bootstrap-ports drift-check hard-fails CI the instant the vendor keys land, so the whole float campaign stalls behind it.
**Dep:** Add the [network] SSOT keys (loopback/bind_all/win_tailscale_ip) and derive MIOS_PG_BIND_ADDR from them

title: Float the redundant MIOS_PORT_AGENT_PIPE and the llama.cpp lane-hint literals in mios-agent-pipe.service
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- a unit that both sources install.env AND re-pins the same value is a live drift source that must resolve to one place.
acceptance_criteria: rendering the unit through 34-render-quadlets on a default host yields byte-identical port values (8640/11436/11450); no bare 8640/11436/11450 literal remains outside a `:-` fallback; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `mios-agent-pipe.service` re-hardcodes ports the SSOT already supplies: line 49's `Environment=MIOS_PORT_AGENT_PIPE=8640` duplicates the value `35-render-ports.sh` already writes to `/etc/mios/install.env` (loaded by the `EnvironmentFile` at line 48), and lines 79-80 pin the iGPU/light-lane ports as `MIOS_NO_TOOL_CHOICE_HINTS=11436` and `MIOS_KV_PAGING_HINTS=11436,11450`. Convert line 49 to the render placeholder `${MIOS_PORT_AGENT_PIPE:-8640}` -- `34-render-quadlets` processes `*.service` per its find at line 184 -- and rewrite the hint lists to `${MIOS_PORT_IGPU:-11436}` / `${MIOS_PORT_WIN_LLM_LIGHT:-11450}`, keeping the literal as the `:-` fallback so the unit still degrades open.
details.why: Today an operator can change the agent-pipe port in mios.toml and the unit keeps 8640 -- the AI front door named by `MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT` silently ignores the SSOT.

title: Lift the hardcoded llama.cpp lane ports across mios_pipe/** onto the shared SSOT resolver, module by module
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- `usr/lib/mios` is the gate-red zone and must carry no port constants, including in the hottest path of the agent pipe.
acceptance_criteria: no lane-port integer literal remains outside an env-default in these modules; the existing agent-pipe tests pass; check_no_bare_port_literals is green; endpoints resolve to the same values as before via env.

details.what_how: `server.py` already composes lane endpoints from `_LIGHT_BASE`, but its sibling modules still pin lane ports as literals: `mios_pipe/kernel/config.py` (`:11450` at 113/194/240, `:11434` at 274), `mios_pipe/routing/{planner,agentreg,chat,dci,refine,swarm}.py` (`:11434`/`:11436`/`:11450`), `mios_pipe/vram_scheduler.py` (`:11434` at 134-135) and `mios_endpoints.py` (`:11436`). Only server.py is allowlisted, so these are governed today solely by `check_no_bare_port_literals`' hardcoded banned list. Lift each to the shared resolver -- read `MIOS_PORT_WIN_LLM_LIGHT` / `MIOS_PORT_LLM_CUDA_INTERNAL` / `MIOS_PORT_LLM_HEAVY_INTERNAL` / `MIOS_PORT_IGPU` via `os.environ`, or via a `_LANE_BASE` helper mirroring server.py's `_LIGHT_BASE` -- keeping the literal as the `dict.get` default. Work strangler-style module by module, using each module's own unit tests as characterization.
details.why: server.py was floated but the kernel/routing modules that actually BUILD the request URLs were not, so moving a lane in mios.toml still leaves every real dispatch pointed at the old port.

title: Derive check_no_bare_port_literals' banned lane-port list from the [ports] SSOT instead of hardcoding it
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- a zero-hardcodes gate that hardcodes its own port table cannot be the enforcement plane for the rule.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh:1630` sets `banned_ports = ["11450","11441","11440","11451","11434","11435"]` -- a hand-maintained list that already omits `:11436` (igpu) and drifts whenever a lane moves. title: Add [ports].forge_internal=3000 and float the localhost:3000 git-origin literals in the Forgejo firstboot producers
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- every named false-friend needs an SSOT key to float TO, including forgejo 3000 != 8300.
acceptance_criteria: the forge_internal key is present; the rendered producers resolve to `:3000`; no active `localhost:3000` literal remains outside a `:-` fallback; drift-gate and check_container_ports are green with 3000 recognized as an internal false-friend.

details.what_how: Forgejo publishes at `[ports].forge_http=8300` but binds its own default `:3000` internally, and the firstboot producers talk to `localhost:3000` directly: `mios-git-root-init.service` (unit doc + Description), `mios-forge-firstboot.service:14`, and the libexec producers `usr/libexec/mios/git-root-init.sh` and `forge-firstboot.sh`. Add `forge_internal = 3000` to `[ports]`, register `MIOS_PORT_FORGE_INTERNAL` in BOTH `34-render-quadlets` allowlists, and rewrite the active `:3000` references to `${MIOS_PORT_FORGE_INTERNAL:-3000}`. details.why: The false-friend list explicitly names forgejo 3000 != 8300 to preserve, yet nothing in the campaign adds the key or floats the firstboot git-origin references that hardcode it -- so the one place a Forgejo port move would break is the one place still hand-written.

title: Add a tailnet-IP (100.64.0.0/10) regression fitness function so floated tailscale IPs cannot creep back
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- a float without a gate is a temporary state; the guard is what makes it permanent.
acceptance_criteria: a stray `100.x.y.z` literal that is not the SSOT value reds the gate; the SSOT `win_tailscale_ip` value itself does not; the check is green on the real tree.

details.what_how: `_is_routable_ip` in `usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint` (line 153) returns False for the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT/tailnet range, so `100.79.3.50` and any other hardcoded tailscale IP is NEVER flagged -- meaning after the `Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1` float nothing prevents the literal returning. Add a dedicated scan: either a new branch in the lint that flags 100.64/10 literals unless they equal `[network].win_tailscale_ip`, or a `check_no_tailnet_ip_literal()` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` reading that SSOT value -- so the ONLY permitted tailnet literal is the SSOT-declared one. Port the same rule into the Rust lint when it lands.
details.why: The CGNAT range is currently invisible to the lint, so the tailscale IP the campaign just floated can be re-pasted anywhere tomorrow and no gate will say a word.

title: Narrow the blanket exempt_files globs that hide usr/libexec, usr/share/mios and firstboot from the port/IP scan
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- the tree must default to SCANNED, with exemptions enumerated per file rather than per directory.
acceptance_criteria: the `.*/usr/libexec/.*` and `.*/usr/share/mios/.*` blanket globs are removed or replaced by an enumerated minimal file list; mios-hardcode-lint is green over the newly-scanned tree; both repos are mirrored.

details.what_how: The `[security.nohc_allowlist].exempt_files` block (mios.toml lines 812-841) exempts whole trees from the port/IP scan: `.*/usr/libexec/.*` (273 tools), `.*/usr/share/mios/.*`, `.*firstboot\.sh$`, `.*firstboot$`, `.*/automation/.*`, `.*/windows/.*`. Once the gate-red zone (`usr/lib/mios` + systemd) is clean, `usr/libexec/mios` becomes the next blind spot -- and the named firstboot producers (`mios-ai-firstboot`, `forge-firstboot.sh`, `mios-hermes-firstboot`) are double-exempt. Incrementally replace each blanket directory glob with narrow per-file exemptions for the files that legitimately need one, after their clusters have floated. Do this LAST, per cluster, staging explicit mios.toml edits and mirroring to the bootstrap repo (Law 15).
details.why: Zero-hardcodes reports green today largely because a regex hides 273 tools and the very firstboot producers this campaign names -- the blanket globs are the structural blind spot the whole effort exists to remove.

title: Correct the mios-ttyd-launch fallbacks to the SSOT ttyd ports and strip the stale :7681/:7682 comment literals
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- a `:-` fallback that disagrees with SSOT is a latent wrong-port bind, not a safe default.
acceptance_criteria: the launcher's `:-` fallbacks equal the SSOT ttyd_bash/ttyd_powershell values; no 7681/7682 literal remains in the ttyd units or launcher except an explicit SSOT-matching fallback; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-ttyd-launch` defaults PORT to `${MIOS_PORT_TTYD_BASH:-7681}` / `${MIOS_PORT_TTYD_POWERSHELL:-7682}` (lines 70, 73), but `[ports]` defines `ttyd_bash=8681` / `ttyd_powershell=8682` -- the launcher's fallback is ttyd's UPSTREAM default, not MiOS's SSOT value, so a host with an empty env silently binds the wrong port. Correct the fallbacks to `:-8681` / `:-8682`, and strip the stale `localhost:7681` / `:7682` literals from the unit doc-headers (`mios-ttyd-bash.service:2,5`; `mios-ttyd-powershell.service:5`) that would otherwise confuse the systemd-unit lint once it starts scanning comments.
details.why: Any host that starts ttyd without the env populated binds 7681/7682 instead of 8681/8682 today -- a silent wrong-port terminal -- and the stale comments will red the systemd lint the moment it scans them.

title: Add cosign signing to the Forgejo publisher so both forges sign every pushed tag
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- restore the equal-publisher invariant by making Forgejo-published digests as verifiable as GitHub's.
acceptance_criteria: build-mios.yml pushes then signs each published tag; `cosign verify` succeeds against a Forgejo-published digest; grep for cosign in build-mios.yml is non-empty; drift-gate green; the change is present in both repos.

details.what_how: `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` signs every pushed tag with keyless cosign (the 'Install cosign' / 'Cosign keyless sign' steps, lines 442-471), but grepping for cosign/attest/sign in `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml` returns NOTHING -- Forgejo-published digests ship unsigned. Add a matching signing step to build-mios.yml: install cosign v2.x (see the cosign-v3 pinning task), `source ./tools/lib/userenv.sh`, `cosign login` the registry host derived from `MIOS_IMAGE_NAME` (parity with the GitHub push-login), then `cosign sign --yes` each pushed tag. Forgejo has no GitHub OIDC issuer, so sign with the shared MiOS key (the `COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY` secret already referenced in generate-mok-key.sh's secrets note) resolving to ONE identity policy, while GitHub stays keyless. Mirror the workflow change in both mios.git and mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15); stage explicit paths.
details.why: Half the fleet's images are unverifiable today, so the release-topology promise that GitHub and Forgejo are equal bit-for-bit publishers is false wherever it matters most -- at signature verification.

title: Collapse the two divergent LUKS SSOT tables onto [security.luks] and make the recovery keyslot unconditional
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- clevis/LUKS TPM binding must be SSOT-wired and drift-gated rather than shipped as dead code.
acceptance_criteria: both tools read `[security.luks]`; mios-luks-enroll enrolls a recovery keyslot unconditionally and rejects `recovery=false`; no consumer references `[security.disk_encryption]`; drift-gate and negatives are green; the SSOT is mirrored in both repos.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-09 brief P1-14: the tables still disagree -- [security.luks] (enabled = false, pin tpm2, pcrs '7') against [security.disk_encryption] (pcrs [7, 14], recovery, systemd-cryptenroll, fido2) -- although task_1354 is marked done for the collapse. Operator ruling Q6 (2026-10-09) settles the direction: fold [security.luks] into [security.disk_encryption], the opposite of this title. Install-time encryption: task_3561.

details.what_how: Two conflicting LUKS config surfaces exist: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen` reads `[security.luks]` (enabled/pin/pcrs, mios.toml lines 8745-8748) while `usr/libexec/mios/mios-luks-enroll` reads `config['security']['disk_encryption']` (mode/backend/pcrs/recovery, lines 24-27) -- a table that does NOT exist in mios.toml, so mios-luks-enroll is a permanent no-op with `mode` defaulting to 'none'. Collapse both consumers onto `[security.luks]`, adding `mode`, `backend` and `recovery` keys there, and default `pcrs` to '7' (Secure-Boot state, which survives kernel/initramfs bumps unlike PCR0/9). Make the recovery keyslot UNCONDITIONAL: today `recovery = de.get('recovery', True)` lets an operator set false and brick a fleet on any firmware or MOK change, exactly the hazard enroll-mok.sh lines 207-213 warn about. Update `check_clevis_luks` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:4321`) and add a check that mios-luks-enroll parses the unified table. Mirror the SSOT edit in both repos (Law 15); stage explicit paths.
details.why: Disk-unlock enrollment is dead code reading a table that does not exist, so operators believe they have TPM-bound encryption they do not have -- and the one escape hatch, a recovery keyslot, is optional enough to brick a fleet after a firmware update.

title: Pin CI cosign to v2.x legacy-attachment format so bootc/rpm-ostree policy can discover the signatures
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- signatures must land in a format the image-policy enforcement layer can actually read.
acceptance_criteria: CI signs with cosign v2.x; the pushed digest carries a `.sig` sigstore attachment rather than a v3 referrers bundle, verifiable by rpm-ostree/containers-image policy; both workflows are pinned; drift-gate green; Law 15 mirrored.

details.what_how: `automation/49-cosign-policy.sh` pins the in-image cosign to v2.x because 'v3+ breaks rpm-ostree OCI 1.1 bundle format' (header lines 11/25/32), yet CI installs `sigstore/cosign-installer@v3` and signs with the v3 CLI (`.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` line 444). cosign v3's signing-bundle format is NOT discoverable by containers-image/rpm-ostree policy (bootc #528 / rpm-ostree #5509), so a strict sigstoreSigned policy would silently fail to verify CI signatures. Pin cosign-installer with `cosign-release: v2.6.4` -- matching `COSIGN_FALLBACK_VERSION` at 49-cosign-policy.sh line 32 -- and/or export the legacy-attachment env so signatures land as sigstore attachments; the `usr/lib/containers/registries.d/` yamls already set `use-sigstore-attachments: true`. Apply identically to the new Forgejo signing step. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Until this lands every downstream verification silently fails on format grounds, so the strict-policy work built on top of it would appear to work while enforcing nothing.

title: Generate a real sigstoreSigned policy.json from [security.sigstore] instead of insecureAcceptEverything
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- convert signing effort into actual boot integrity for the immutable host.
acceptance_criteria: with `policy_mode=sigstoreSigned` the generated policy.json carries a sigstoreSigned rule keyed to the MiOS repo and mios-cosign.pub; `generate-cosign-policy.py --check` passes; `skopeo copy` admits a signed image and rejects an unsigned one under the policy; drift-gate green; mirrored in both repos.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-09: superseded by operator ruling Q4 (2026-10-09), filed as task_3536: /etc/containers/policy.json rendered by mios-gen from a typed [security.sigstore], enforcing sigstoreSigned for ghcr.io/mios-dev (brief P0-1). generate-cosign-policy.py named here is retired (ported to mios-gen).

details.what_how: `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py` emits ONLY `{"default":[{"type":"insecureAcceptEverything"}]}` (the `[security.sigstore].policy_mode` default, mios.toml lines 781-784) and the committed `usr/lib/containers/policy.json` matches -- so an immutable bootc host boots and upgrades into ANY image. Extend the generator so `policy_mode='sigstoreSigned'` emits a `transports.docker.<repo>` rule of type `sigstoreSigned` with `keyPath: /usr/share/pki/containers/mios-cosign.pub` and `signedIdentity: {type: matchRepository}`, plus `allowed_identities` from the SSOT list (currently empty) for the keyless path. Preserve the `--check` byte-parity mode (JSON comparison, lines 40-56). registries.d already advertises attachments, so only the policy body and the SSOT flag change; flip `policy_mode` to sigstoreSigned only AFTER signatures land on both forges. Mirror the SSOT plus generated policy.json in both repos (Law 15); stage explicit paths, never `git add -A`.
details.why: An immutable OS that trusts every image has no boot integrity at all -- the strongest property of the bootc model is currently switched off by a one-line default.

title: Attach the Syft SBOM to the published digest as a signed cosign attestation on both forges
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- provenance means SBOM + baked manifest, which requires the SBOM to travel WITH the image.
acceptance_criteria: `cosign verify-attestation --type spdx <published digest>` returns the SBOM predicate on both forges; the CI step is green; ADR-0003 references the attestation; Law 15 mirrored.

details.what_how: `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` writes CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs into `/usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom` as in-tree files only (lines 60-66); they are never attached to the image, so downstream bootc hosts and scanners cannot run `cosign verify-attestation --type spdx`. Add a CI step on BOTH forges, after Push and alongside the sign step, that reads the baked SPDX from the pushed image (or re-runs `syft <digest>`) and runs `cosign attest --yes --type spdx --predicate <sbom.spdx.json> <digest>` under the same cosign v2 identity as the signing step. Record the attestation in `artifacts/sbom/binaries.tsv` provenance per ADR-0003. Do NOT touch 90-generate-sbom.sh's degrade-open build path -- it must still exit 0 with no egress. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
details.why: An SBOM nobody outside the build can pull is not provenance -- a consumer of the published image has no verifiable inventory of what they just booted.

title: Emit signed SLSA build provenance for the published image, recording which forge built the digest
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- two independent publishers of the 'same' digest are only trustworthy if each build is independently attributable.
acceptance_criteria: a signed SLSA provenance attestation is attached to the published digest on both forges; slsa-verifier or `cosign verify-attestation --type slsaprovenance` resolves it; the predicate names the building forge; Law 15 mirrored.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-09 brief P1-10: no attest step; the image is signed by tag; COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL is obsolete. Fix: podman push --digestfile, then actions/attest push-to-registry (L2; L3 from a reusable workflow; free for public repos); on Forgejo, cosign attest --type slsaprovenance. Unverified (brief section 7): actions/attest push-to-registry against GHCR referrers; public Fulcio trusting a self-hosted Forgejo OIDC issuer.

details.what_how: Grepping for slsa/provenance in both workflows returns nothing -- there is no build-provenance attestation. On GitHub, add `actions/attest-build-provenance@v1` (or the slsa-github-generator reusable workflow) bound to the pushed image digest, using the job's existing `permissions: id-token: write`. The predicate MUST record which forge built the digest (source repo + workflow ref) so GitHub- and Forgejo-built digests remain distinguishable under the equal-publishers model. For Forgejo, which has no GitHub OIDC, emit an equivalent in-toto predicate signed with the shared MiOS cosign key via `cosign attest --type slsaprovenance`. Add a companion CI/drift-gate verification with slsa-verifier or `cosign verify-attestation`. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Without provenance there is no non-falsifiable record of HOW a digest was built, so an operator cannot tell a legitimate Forgejo build from an injected one.

title: Make the image build reproducible via a git-derived SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and timestamp rewrite
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- byte-identical digests across publishers are the precondition for the equal-publisher release topology.
acceptance_criteria: two independent CI builds of the same commit produce byte-identical image digests; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is derived from git commit time; base images are digest-pinned; both forges patched; Law 15 mirrored.

details.what_how: The CI `sudo podman build` (`.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` lines 301-312) sets no `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and no timestamp normalization, so file and layer mtimes vary run to run and a third party cannot reproduce the published digest. Add `--timestamp "$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"` (and `--rewrite-timestamp` where buildah supports it) with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git -C "$ROOT" log -1 --format=%ct)` so the epoch is DETERMINISTIC and immune to build.sh's git-reset -- per the `/ IS $ROOT` note in the drift-gate local-verify memo. Ensure base images are digest-pinned. Apply to both forges and to `automation/build.sh` where it drives the OCI build. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Today the two forges provably cannot publish the same digest for the same commit, so the 'bit-for-bit equal publishers' invariant is unenforceable and nobody can independently reproduce a shipped image.

### task_2124 -- Make the image build reproducible via a git-derived SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and timestamp rewrite  (WS-SBOM | P2 | M)
**Goal:** E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- byte-identical digests across publishers are the precondition for the equal-publisher release topology.
**What+How:** The CI `sudo podman build` (`.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` lines 301-312) sets no `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and no timestamp normalization, so file and layer mtimes vary run to run and a third party cannot reproduce the published digest. Add `--timestamp "$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"` (and `--rewrite-timestamp` where buildah supports it) with `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git -C "$ROOT" log -1 --format=%ct)` so the epoch is DETERMINISTIC and immune to build.sh's git-reset -- per the `/ IS $ROOT` note in the drift-gate local-verify memo. Ensure base images are digest-pinned. Apply to both forges and to `automation/build.sh` where it drives the OCI build. Mirror in both repos (Law 15).
**Where:** `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml (line 301), automation/build.sh, .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml`
**Done When:** two independent CI builds of the same commit produce byte-identical image digests; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is derived from git commit time; base images are digest-pinned; both forges patched; Law 15 mirrored.
**Why:** Today the two forges provably cannot publish the same digest for the same commit, so the 'bit-for-bit equal publishers' invariant is unenforceable and nobody can independently reproduce a shipped image.
**Dep:** none

title: Add a cargo-deny gate (licenses, advisories, bans) covering every native crate in both workspaces
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the compiled tier needs the dependency-surface gate that bash never had.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo deny check` passes for both workspaces covering every member crate; a deliberately GPL or duplicated dependency fails it; CI and `just drift-gate` both run it; config mirrored in both repos.

details.what_how: No cargo-deny config exists (grep for deny.toml returns nothing). Add `tools/native/deny.toml` and `src/mios-rs/deny.toml` with `[advisories]` denying RustSec advisories, `[licenses]` carrying an allow-list that operationalizes the FOSS posture (Apache-2.0/MIT/BSD-*/ISC/Unicode-3.0), and `[bans]` denying duplicate crate versions and wildcard deps. The `tools/native` workspace `members` list (Cargo.toml lines 3-7) currently names only mios-drift-runner, mios-version-check and mios-wallpaperd, while crate directories also exist for generate-names-registry, mios-aiplane-lint, mios-bake-plan, mios-ssot-lint and mios-ssot-walk -- ADD them so the gate covers ALL native crates. Wire `cargo deny check` into `just drift-gate` (Justfile ~line 81) and a CI step, preserving the negatives-before-main-gate ordering. Mirror the config in both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Five native crates are outside the workspace members list and therefore outside every gate, and no license or advisory check exists at all -- a banned-license or vulnerable transitive dep can ship into the image today with nothing to stop it.

title: Gate both Rust workspaces on `cargo audit --deny warnings` over committed lockfiles
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the compiled tier's dependency set is continuously checked against RustSec, not merely locked.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo audit` runs green in CI and in `just drift-gate` over both lockfiles; injecting a known-vulnerable dependency version turns the gate red; a failed advisory-DB fetch warns and continues instead of failing the build; both repos carry the change.

details.what_how: `grep cargo-audit` over the tree returns empty: no advisory scan exists. Add a `cargo audit --deny warnings` step to `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` and a matching `just drift-gate` entry, run over BOTH `tools/native/Cargo.lock` (already committed) and `src/mios-rs/Cargo.lock` (created by the lockfile task). Keep it a SEPARATE step from cargo-deny so an advisory-only failure is diagnosable on its own. Preserve the negatives-before-main gate ordering. Cache the RustSec advisory DB in CI to dodge rate limits and degrade-open on a DB-fetch miss, mirroring the `api.github.com` fallback posture already used in `automation/49-cosign-policy.sh`. Mirror the workflow + Justfile change into mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15).
details.why: Build scripts and proc-macros execute arbitrary code during `cargo build`, so today every crate pulled into the OS build plane is unscreened against published advisories and a known-CVE dependency can ship inside `miosd` with nothing to notice.

title: Make `clippy -Dwarnings` + rustfmt the compiled plane's missing shellcheck, with panic/unwrap bans
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the Rust tier gets the static gate the shell tier never had.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green and gate both CI and `just drift-gate` across both workspaces; the restriction lints are active in migrated crate roots; adding a stray `.unwrap()` to a verb fails the build; both repos carry the config.

details.what_how: The tech-debt map records that MiOS has NO shellcheck CI job; migrated code can close that class for free. Add a CI step plus a `just drift-gate` step (Justfile ~line 81) running `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` for BOTH workspaces (`tools/native`, `src/mios-rs`). In each migrated crate root add targeted restriction lints -- `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::todo)]` -- rather than blanket `clippy::restriction`, so a supply-chain verb physically cannot ship a panic path. This becomes the enforcement backstop every subsequent WS-SBOM port lands against. Mirror the config into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Ported verbs currently land with no static gate at all, so formatting drift and panic-on-`unwrap` paths enter the signed image unchallenged -- the exact defect class shellcheck would have caught in the bash they replaced.

title: Commit `src/mios-rs/Cargo.lock` and build miosd with `--locked`
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the pinned lockfile becomes the dependency reproducibility SSOT every audit gate consumes.
acceptance_criteria: `src/mios-rs/Cargo.lock` is committed and not ignored; `cargo build --locked` builds miosd; bumping a dependency now requires an explicit lockfile update rather than happening implicitly; cargo-audit/vet/auditable have a fixed set to scan; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `tools/native` ships a committed `Cargo.lock`; `src/mios-rs` does NOT (only `Cargo.toml` + `miosd/`), and the Containerfile rust-builder runs a FLOATING `cargo build --release` (Containerfile line 49), so miosd's dependency graph can silently drift build-to-build -- contradicting ADR-0003's "dependency digests resolved+recorded at build". Generate and commit `src/mios-rs/Cargo.lock`, confirm `.gitignore` does not exclude it, and change the Containerfile rust-builder (lines 44-50) plus every CI cargo invocation to `cargo build --release --locked`. Stage explicit paths only -- AGY shares the tree, never `git add -A`. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Without a committed lockfile the shipped daemon is non-reproducible and unauditable -- two bakes of the same commit can embed different dependency versions, and no advisory gate downstream can name what was actually built.

title: Add a pip-audit gate over the agent-plane venv and the python libexec fleet
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the Python half of the image gets the same dependency-vuln screening as the Rust half.
acceptance_criteria: pip-audit runs in CI over the agent venv/requirements and fails on a known-vulnerable pin; the offline bake warns and continues; the report lands in `artifacts/sbom`; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: MiOS ships ~122 python libexec tools plus the agent-pipe FastAPI plane in a venv built by `automation/72-hermes-agent.sh`, with no dependency-vuln scan at all (`grep pip-audit` -> empty) -- the python analog of the Rust gap. Add a pip-audit gate: run `pip-audit -r <requirements>` (or `pip-audit --strict` against the built `/usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv`) in `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` and in `just drift-gate`. DEGRADE-OPEN in the offline OCI bake (no egress -> warn and skip, matching `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh`'s exit-0 posture) but FAIL-CLOSED in CI where egress exists. Emit the report into `usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/` beside `binaries.tsv`. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: The 122-tool python plane plus the FastAPI agent front door is the largest unaudited dependency surface in the image, and a vulnerable transitive pin reaches the operator's machine today with nothing between it and them.

title: Port generate-cosign-policy.py to a typed compiled `mios-cosign-policy` with golden parity
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the boot-integrity policy generator becomes compiled, typed and parity-proven.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-cosign-policy` reproduces the committed `policy.json` byte-for-byte (trycmd green) and `--check` parity holds; `generate-cosign-policy.py` is a delegating shim; `cargo test`, `just drift-gate` and clippy -Dwarnings are green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: Once the sigstoreSigned work makes the policy non-trivial, port the generator into a new `tools/native/mios-cosign-policy` workspace member that deserializes `[security.sigstore]` into a typed serde/toml struct -- the struct IS the schema and fails loudly on shape errors, unlike today's best-effort try/except that silently falls back to `insecureAcceptEverything` (`tools/generate-cosign-policy.py` lines 21-28). Strangler-fig: keep the python as a thin shim exec'ing the binary when present (current python path otherwise), prove byte-parity of BOTH `--check` and the generated `usr/lib/containers/policy.json` against the committed file via a trycmd golden fixture, THEN delete the python body. Emit miette diagnostics from the `mios-diag` crate pointing at the offending SSOT line on a malformed rule. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: The file that decides which container signatures the OS trusts is currently produced by a script that degrades to "trust everything" on any parse hiccup -- a malformed SSOT edit disarms boot integrity with no error.

title: Establish a shared `mios-diag` thiserror+miette crate for the migrated supply-chain verbs
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- one error/diagnostic foundation every port builds on instead of each reinventing one.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-diag` builds, exports a Result alias plus a span-carrying TOML-error helper, is a workspace member covered by the clippy/deny/audit gates, and is consumed by at least one ported verb; `cargo test` green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: Add a shared library crate `tools/native/mios-diag` providing the two-layer error model the WS-SBOM ports need: `thiserror`-defined matchable error enums for internal/resolver failures (so drift-gates can match programmatically) and `miette` end-user diagnostics with source spans, labels and help text, so a bad `[security.*]` or port value in `mios.toml` is highlighted AT its line with actionable help. Use byte offsets, not char counts, so UTF-8 spans highlight correctly. Register it in the `tools/native` workspace members and depend on it from the ported verbs (`mios-cosign-policy`, `mios-mok`, `mios-oscap-gate`). Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Without a shared foundation each port invents its own error handling, producing the same opaque bash-grade error strings in compiled form -- and the operator still gets no pointer to the mios.toml line that broke.

title: Stand up a trycmd + insta golden-master harness as the parity oracle for every port
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- no script is deleted until its exact current behavior is recorded and reproduced.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test` runs trycmd+insta over fixtures encoding the exact current bash/python output; a deliberate output change fails the snapshot and is reviewable via `cargo insta review`; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: Before any WS-SBOM port touches behavior, add `trycmd` (whole-CLI stdout/stderr/exit snapshots) and `insta` (structured snapshots with `cargo insta review`) as dev-dependencies in `tools/native`, and capture the CURRENT observable output of each migration target as committed fixtures: `tools/generate-cosign-policy.py` (including `--check`), `usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscap-gate` over sample ARF files, `automation/enroll-mok.sh --status` over recorded mokutil fixtures, `usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen`, plus the current `usr/lib/containers/policy.json` and the `MIOS_*` env projection. These fixtures become the oracle every port must reproduce byte-for-byte, mechanizing the recurring quadlet-digest-drift and SSOT-projection-drift classes into reviewable accept/review snapshots. Follows the existing `automation/test_generate-sbom.sh` test pattern. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Every port scheduled behind this one would otherwise be a rewrite with no oracle -- a silent behavior change in the cosign policy, the MOK probe or the compliance gate would ship undetected.

title: Add a systemd sandbox fitness function over every long-running unit
goal: E-18 Generate the 168 systemd units from SSOT -- no unit silently loses its hardening, enforced as a check rather than a convention.
acceptance_criteria: the linter/gate flags any non-exempt Service unit below the directive floor; the privileged roster and documented deviations are exempt via SSOT; adding a bare new unit fails the gate; negatives-before-main ordering preserved; `just drift-gate` green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: Only ~10 of the 84 units carry the high-value confinement directives (`grep NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict` in `usr/lib/systemd/system/` hits `hermes-worker.service` lines 87-95, hermes-dashboard, a few `mios-*` units); a newly-added long-running unit can regress to zero confinement with nothing catching it. Add a compiled `tools/native/mios-unit-sandbox-lint` plus a new check in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` that STATIC-lints each `[Service]` unit against a required directive floor -- `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `PrivateTmp`, a bounded `CapabilityBoundingSet`, `SystemCallFilter=@system-service` -- and FAILS units below it, EXEMPTING the operator-defined `[security.privileged_quadlets].root` roster (`mios.toml` lines 786-804, the only sanctioned exceptions). Honor documented per-unit deviations (e.g. hermes-worker's `NoNewPrivileges=false` sudo grant, line 92) through an SSOT exempt list, never a hardcode. Where `systemd-analyze security` is available in the runtime CI phase, score units and fail above an exposure threshold. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).

title: Set fapolicyd `integrity=sha256` and derive the trust DB from built image content
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- allowlisting moves from path identity to content identity, making the image an immutable execution environment.
acceptance_criteria: `fapolicyd.conf` ships `integrity = sha256` on both the `/usr/lib` and `/etc` paths; the trust DB derives from image content; a binary overlaid at a trusted path is denied execution; a drift-check asserts the setting; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `automation/40-fapolicyd-trust.sh` sets `trust = file,rpmdb` (line 22) but never sets `integrity`, which defaults to `none` -- so fapolicyd allowlists by PATH only and a writable or overlay-tampered binary sitting at a trusted path still executes. Add an SSOT-driven `integrity = sha256` line through the same sed loop over BOTH the `/usr/lib` and `/etc` `fapolicyd.conf` copies (USR-OVER-ETC parity, lines 19-23), and confirm the trust DB is generated FROM built image content: `automation/51-hardening.sh` already runs `fagenrules --load` + `fapolicyd-cli --update` (lines 35-40) over the RPM/OCI file set -- verify that covers OCI-added binaries, not just rpmdb. Keep the `|| true` degrade-open so a missing fagenrules cannot brick the bake. Add a drift-check asserting `integrity=sha256` on both conf paths. Mirror the SSOT key into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Path-only allowlisting means fapolicyd currently approves whatever occupies a trusted path, so an overlay or `/var` tamper defeats the entire immutable-execution premise the image is built on.

title: Derive greenboot's critical-service list from SSOT and probe Hermes :8642 at boot
goal: E-19 Wire the shipped-but-unwired runtime capabilities -- greenboot health coverage becomes SSOT-derived and actually covers the AI plane.
acceptance_criteria: `check_greenboot` derives its service list from `[greenboot].critical_services` with no hardcoded triple; a `required.d` check probes Hermes `:8642`; editing the SSOT list visibly changes what the gate enforces; greenboot rolls back on a failed AI-plane boot; drift-gate and negatives green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` `check_greenboot` HARDCODES `critical_services=("agent-pipe" "llm-light" "pgvector")` (line 4305), duplicating `[greenboot].critical_services` in `mios.toml` (line 8751) -- the exact derive-don't-duplicate smell -- and the `required.d` health-check scripts never probe the AI-plane endpoint. Make `check_greenboot` READ `[greenboot].critical_services` from SSOT via `mios_toml.py` with a `${VAR:-agent-pipe llm-light pgvector}` fallback instead of the literal array, and add a `usr/lib/greenboot/check/required.d/` check that curls the canonical Hermes endpoint `:8642` plus the core Quadlets, so a signed-but-broken publish trips the boot counter and rolls back rather than rolling a fleet forward into a dead AI plane. Optionally compile the health check into a `mios-greenboot-healthcheck` binary reading the same SSOT (greenboot-rs is the upstream bootc direction). Mirror the SSOT into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: The gate asserts a service list copied by hand into the checker, so it drifts from the real SSOT the moment either side changes -- and with no AI-plane probe a broken publish boots "healthy" with a dead front door.

title: Assert the required security kargs so `enforcing=1` cannot drop out of the signed UKI cmdline
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the signed UKI's security properties become a fitness function, not an assumption.
acceptance_criteria: the gate fails when a required security karg is absent from the rendered cmdline; the required set is SSOT-defined; `enforcing=1` presence is explicitly asserted; drift-gate and negatives green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: The UKI cmdline is flattened by `tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py` and drift-checked for PROJECTION parity (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh` `check_uki_cmdline_projection`, line 5367), but NOTHING asserts the security-critical kargs are actually present -- `enforcing=1` (SELinux, which must be baked INSIDE the signed UKI so it cannot be toggled at the boot menu), `lockdown=`, and the LUKS/rootfs args could silently disappear and still pass. Add an SSOT `[security.kargs].required` list plus a drift-check that FAILS when `usr/lib/kernel/cmdline` (rendered by `automation/76-uki-render.sh`) is missing any required token, with a `${...:-enforcing=1 lockdown=integrity}` fallback. Mirror the SSOT into both repos (Law 15).
details.where: `automation/76-uki-render.sh, tools/generate-uki-cmdline.py, usr/lib/kernel/cmdline, usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/*.toml, automation/98-drift-checks.sh (check_uki_cmdline_projection, line 5367), usr/share/mios/mios.toml`
details.why: Projection parity only proves the cmdline matches its generator -- an edit that drops `enforcing=1` or `lockdown=` today ships a signed UKI with SELinux permissive and every gate stays green.

title: Make MOK key generation and enrollment operator-defined via `[security.secureboot]`
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- Secure Boot trust custody becomes an operator SSOT input projected into the build, not a MiOS constant.
acceptance_criteria: both scripts read CN, key bits, validity and cert path from `[security.secureboot]` with literal fallbacks; changing the CN in SSOT visibly changes the generated cert; no private key material enters `mios.toml`; drift-gate green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `automation/generate-mok-key.sh` HARDCODES the cert CN ("MiOS Module Signing Key", line 54), key size (2048, lines 47/65) and validity (3650d, line 72), and `automation/enroll-mok.sh` HARDCODES the key search paths (`/etc/pki/mios/mok.der`, `akmods-ublue.der`; `pick_key` lines 100-110) -- none operator-defined, contradicting the SSOT-operator-defined north star. Add `[security.secureboot]` (`cn`, `key_bits`, `validity_days`, `cert_path`, `enroll_on_firstboot`) and project it into both scripts through `mios_toml.py` using `${VAR:-<current literal>}` fallbacks so behavior is byte-unchanged when unset. PRIVATE key material stays out of SSOT (it remains a GitHub secret per `generate-mok-key.sh` lines 105-107); only public policy/identity is operator-defined. Mirror the SSOT into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: An operator deploying MiOS cannot today name their own signing identity or key policy without editing shipped automation, which is precisely the hand-edited-config class the SSOT north star forbids.

title: Port enroll-mok.sh's `status_probe` to a compiled `mios-mok --status` with differential parity
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- Secure-Boot state parsing stops being sed/grep string-munging.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-mok --status` emits the identical state string as the bash probe across the fixtures; `enroll-mok.sh` delegates to it with a bash fallback; differential/trycmd parity green; clippy -Dwarnings clean; `just drift-gate` green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `automation/enroll-mok.sh` `status_probe` (lines 47-98) parses `mokutil --sb-state/--list-enrolled/--list-new` and `openssl x509` output through brittle sed/grep/tr pipelines (fingerprint normalization lines 74-78, CN extraction line 87). Port the READ-ONLY probe into a new `tools/native/mios-mok` crate that still shells `mokutil`/`openssl` but parses in typed Rust, emitting exactly one of `enrolled|pending|not-enrolled|no-secureboot|conflict`. Strangler-fig: demote `status_probe` to call the binary when present with the bash path as fallback, prove byte-parity of the emitted state against the bash version via a differential/trycmd golden over recorded mokutil fixtures, THEN delete the bash probe. Leave the WRITE path (`mokutil --import --root-pw`, line 188) in bash for now since it needs an interactive root password. Return miette diagnostics via `mios-diag`. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Enrollment decisions branch on a state string produced by fragile text pipelines -- a formatting change in `mokutil` output silently misclassifies Secure Boot state and the wrong enrollment path runs.

title: Enforce cosign signature + attestation at k3s admission for runtime sidecars
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the signature policy extends past the host boundary to everything pulled at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: a rendered admission policy enforces cosign identity + attestation on k3s image pulls; an unsigned test image is rejected and a MiOS-signed one admitted; the policy is SSOT-templated and toggled off by default; drift-gate green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: MiOS runs k3s (`automation/36-ceph-k3s.sh`, `automation/37-k3s-selinux.sh`, `usr/share/containers/systemd/mios-k3s.container`), so sidecar/workload images pulled at RUNTIME are an unverified surface the OS-plane `policy.json` never sees. Add a Kyverno (or sigstore policy-controller) admission policy TEMPLATED FROM `[security.sigstore]` -- the same cosign identity and attestation checks the OS plane enforces -- admitting only images with a valid cosign signature plus an SBOM/SLSA attestation matching the MiOS identity, rejecting the rest, so the AI-plane `/v1` sidecars cannot be swapped for unsigned images. Render the policy from SSOT under the canonical-port/NO-HARDCODE allowlist model, and ship it DISABLED by default behind an operator toggle (the "inert until wired" convention). Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: Host-plane signing stops at the boundary, so k3s can pull an unsigned inference sidecar onto a fully-verified host today -- reopening precisely the substitution gap signing exists to close.

title: Bootstrap on-disk signature-policy enforcement at firstboot, gated on the SSOT flag
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the sigstoreSigned policy.json actually gates `bootc upgrade` instead of sitting inert.

Follow the existing firstboot-producer conventions (`usr/libexec/mios/*firstboot*`, degrade-open, `ConditionPathExists`). Mirror the unit and SSOT into both repos (Law 15).
details.where: `usr/libexec/mios/ (new firstboot enforcer), usr/lib/systemd/system/ (new firstboot unit), usr/lib/containers/policy.json, automation/49-cosign-policy.sh, usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.sigstore]`

title: Gate ADR-0003: every floating binary download must record a binaries.tsv row
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- "resolved and recorded at build" becomes an enforced fitness function instead of a convention.
acceptance_criteria: the gate enumerates every download site and fails on an unrecorded binary fetch; the exempt list is SSOT-defined; adding a new un-recorded `curl|sh` fails the build; drift-gate and negatives green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `automation/49-cosign-policy.sh` correctly records its cosign download to `binaries.tsv` (`record_version` line 42, append line 62), but ADR-0003 requires EVERY floating binary download to be resolved and recorded -- and roughly 11 automation steps (`06-enable-external-repos`, `21-virt`, `25-gpu-cdi-toolkits`, `36-ceph-k3s`, `56-fonts`, `57-gnome`, `62-oh-my-posh`, `90-generate-sbom`, others) run `scurl` / `curl -sfL … | sh` with no matching row. Add a compiled linter plus a new `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` check that scans `automation/*.sh` for network-fetch sites (`scurl`, `curl -sfL`, `| sh -s`) and FAILS any that installs a binary without a corresponding `record_version`/binaries.tsv append. title: Port mios-oscap-gate to a compiled Rust verb with golden ARF fixtures
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- the fail-closed compliance verdict runs on memory-safe, tested code.
acceptance_criteria: the Rust gate reproduces the python count and exit code over the golden ARF fixtures (insta green); the python is a shim; `86-oscap-compliance.sh` drives it unchanged; `cargo test` and clippy -Dwarnings green; both repos carry it.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscap-gate` is a pure-stdlib python ARF/XCCDF severity parser that decides the BOOT-02 compliance build VERDICT (it counts FAILED rules at or above `[compliance].severity_gate` and is called from `automation/86-oscap-compliance.sh` line 111). Port it to a compiled, typed `tools/native/mios-oscap-gate` using quick-xml, namespace-agnostic by local tag name, preserving the `high>medium>low` plus `any` ranking and the fail-closed exit codes 0/1/2. Strangler-fig: capture current python output over a set of golden ARF fixtures via insta, keep the python as a thin shim exec'ing the binary when present, prove byte-parity of the printed count and exit code, THEN delete the python body. `86-oscap-compliance.sh`'s `GATE_BIN` resolution already prefers the installed path (lines 106-108), so the swap-in is transparent. Mirror into both repos (Law 15).
details.why: An untested python script parsing untrusted XML currently holds a veto over whether the image is compliant enough to ship, and a parser bug either blocks a good build or passes a non-compliant one.

title: Add a scheduled vuln scan that verify-pulls the attested SBOM and scans the digest
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the attestation is continuously consumed, closing the loop on `:latest`-intent reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: the scheduled workflow verify-pulls the SBOM attestation and scans it with grype/trivy; a seeded CVE fails or reports; it runs against the digest rather than a tag; the Forgejo sibling or shared workflow exists.

details.what_how: The attested SBOM enables scanning the exact shipped bits, but nothing consumes it. Add a scheduled (cron) GitHub workflow reusing the `.github/workflows/url-probe.yml` scheduled-workflow shape that pulls the published digest's SPDX attestation via `cosign verify-attestation --type spdx` and runs grype (or trivy) against it, failing or filing an issue on new CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs. Because GitHub and Forgejo publish equal digests, scan the DIGEST, not a tag. Mirror as a Forgejo sibling or a shared reusable workflow (Law 15).
details.why: A published image ages into vulnerability silently -- nothing rechecks the shipped bits between bakes, so the SBOM is written and never read.

title: Enforce RPM package + repo GPG verification from an SSOT `[security.rpm]` policy
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the base package layer is signature-verified, so the signing chain has a verified root.
acceptance_criteria: no generated `.repo` sets `gpgcheck=0` outside the SSOT allowlist; `check_rpm_gpgcheck` is green in `just drift-gate`; the vendored-mirror bake installs RPM-signature-verified packages.

details.what_how: `automation/05-repos.sh` writes the vendored Fedora-44 mirror with `gpgcheck=0` AND `repo_gpgcheck=0` (lines 61, 63, 71, 73), so packages install with NO signature check, and `repo_gpgcheck=0` recurs across the metalink repos. Add a `[security.rpm]` SSOT table (`require_gpgcheck=true`, plus an explicit allowlist of dev-tree repos permitted `repo_gpgcheck=0` for unsigned metalink metadata only) and a compiled fitness function -- extend the `tools/native/mios-ssot-lint` crate plus a `check_rpm_gpgcheck` in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` -- that FAILS if any generated `.repo` sets `gpgcheck=0` outside the allowlist. For the vendored mirror, import the F44 RPM-GPG key locally, flip `gpgcheck=1`, and record the key fingerprint to `artifacts/sbom`. Strangler: land the gate WARN-only, then flip to enforce.
details.why: `gpgcheck=0` means the RPM layer accepts unsigned packages -- the largest untargeted supply-chain surface in the image, and every cosign/SBOM control downstream is moot while the base package layer is unverified.

title: Verify and digest-pin the base image at build, recording it to provenance
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the largest ingested artifact in the OS is signature-verified and digest-recorded like everything else.
acceptance_criteria: the bake resolves and records the ucore-hci digest and builds FROM that digest; a build-host policy rejects an unsigned or foreign base image; `bound-images.tsv` carries the base-image row.

details.what_how: The Containerfile builds `FROM ARG BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/ublue-os/ucore-hci:stable-nvidia`, a floating tag with no build-host verification policy, so the entire OS inherits an unverified, unpinned base. Add a build-host containers-policy requiring a `sigstoreSigned` match for `ghcr.io/ublue-os/*` (ublue publishes cosign signatures), resolve tag->digest at bake time, build FROM the resolved digest for reproducibility, and append the base digest row to `usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/bound-images.tsv` per ADR-0003. details.why: An unpinned, unverified `FROM` tag is a silent whole-OS substitution vector: two bakes can produce different systems from the same commit, and the single largest ingested artifact is currently the least verified thing in the tree.

title: Fail-closed signing of out-of-tree kernel modules under Secure Boot
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the boot chain has no unsigned-module gap left between UKI and userspace.
acceptance_criteria: in enforce mode the bake fails on any unsigned out-of-tree module; the drift-gate lists and verifies every baked `.ko` signature; kvmfr is signed in the standard bake with byte-parity against the old shell signer.

details.what_how: `automation/68-bake-kvmfr.sh` signs `kvmfr.ko` only when the akmods private key is present and otherwise WARNs and ships the module UNSIGNED (lines 126-131); under kernel lockdown a required unsigned kmod (kvmfr, for Looking Glass) then silently fails to load. Add `[security.secureboot].enforce_module_signing`; when set, the signer FAILS the bake if any `/usr/lib/modules/**/extra/*.ko` lacks a signature (verified via `modinfo -F sig_id`), and a drift-gate enumerates every baked out-of-tree `.ko` and asserts each is signed. Port the signer into a small compiled `mios-modsign` verb reusable by kvmfr and future kmods; keep the degrade-open behavior only while `enforce_module_signing` is false.
details.why: Secure Boot plus UKI signing is worthless if out-of-tree modules load unsigned -- and in the failure case that exists today the module instead vanishes silently, breaking Looking Glass with no build error.

title: Verify bound-image digests at firstboot before the 47GB whale pull
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the digests recorded at bake are actually enforced where the artifacts land.
acceptance_criteria: firstboot pulls the whales by their bake-recorded digest and verifies signatures when the SSOT flag is on; a digest mismatch aborts the pull; the tag-pull degrade-open path still works when the flag is off.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bound-images-firstboot` (66 lines) web-pulls the evicted vLLM/SGLang whales (~47GB) on first boot with NO signature or digest verification, even though `mios-bake-group` already recorded their resolved digests to `usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/bound-images.tsv` at bake (lines 129-134). Pin the firstboot pull to the recorded digest (`podman pull image@sha256:...`, cross-checked against `bound-images.tsv`) and enforce the on-disk `policy.json` so a compromised registry cannot swap the inference engine. Degrade-open: when the SSOT flag is off, fall back to the current tag pull. Fold the logic into a compiled verb sharing `usr/libexec/mios/mios-policy-arbiter`.
details.why: The firstboot tier is a live TOCTOU hole -- digests are captured at bake but the two biggest artifacts are re-pulled unverified on the operator's machine, exactly where a registry MITM does the most damage, and the producer never consults the policy that was installed for it.

### task_2150 -- Verify bound-image digests at firstboot before the 47GB whale pull  (WS-SBOM | P1 | M)
**Goal:** E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- the digests recorded at bake are actually enforced where the artifacts land.
**What+How:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bound-images-firstboot` (66 lines) web-pulls the evicted vLLM/SGLang whales (~47GB) on first boot with NO signature or digest verification, even though `mios-bake-group` already recorded their resolved digests to `usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/bound-images.tsv` at bake (lines 129-134). Pin the firstboot pull to the recorded digest (`podman pull image@sha256:...`, cross-checked against `bound-images.tsv`) and enforce the on-disk `policy.json` so a compromised registry cannot swap the inference engine. Degrade-open: when the SSOT flag is off, fall back to the current tag pull. Fold the logic into a compiled verb sharing `usr/libexec/mios/mios-policy-arbiter`.
**Where:** `usr/libexec/mios/mios-bound-images-firstboot, usr/share/mios/artifacts/sbom/bound-images.tsv, usr/lib/containers/policy.json, usr/share/mios/mios.toml [security.sigstore]`
**Done When:** firstboot pulls the whales by their bake-recorded digest and verifies signatures when the SSOT flag is on; a digest mismatch aborts the pull; the tag-pull degrade-open path still works when the flag is off.
**Why:** The firstboot tier is a live TOCTOU hole -- digests are captured at bake but the two biggest artifacts are re-pulled unverified on the operator's machine, exactly where a registry MITM does the most damage, and the producer never consults the policy that was installed for it.
**Dep:** Bootstrap on-disk signature-policy enforcement at firstboot gated on the SSOT flag

title: Gate both CI publishers on a gitleaks scan of the git tree AND the exported OCI rootfs
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- no credential ever reaches a published layer, so "signed" also means "clean".
acceptance_criteria: The gitleaks gate runs in both CI publishers and in the drift-gate; a deliberately planted test secret turns all three red; the three shipped public keys are allowlisted and do not trip it.

details.what_how: No gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets is wired anywhere today; the tooling exists only as written intent in `usr/share/doc/mios/reference/audit-security.md`. Add a gitleaks step to BOTH publishers (`.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` and `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml`, kept identical per the GitHub-equals-Forgejo release topology and Law 15) that scans (a) the git tree and (b) the exported OCI rootfs, so credentials baked into a layer are caught even when they were never committed. Add a lightweight companion check in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` asserting `usr/share/mios` carries no secrets, and commit a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlisting the shipped public keys (`fulcio_v1.crt.pem`, `rekor.pub`, `mios-cosign.pub`) so the gate does not cry wolf on legitimate material.
details.why: A token baked into a layer or committed into the SSOT is an immediate supply-chain compromise that signing cannot detect -- a correctly signed image with an embedded secret is still poisoned -- and Law-15 dual-repo work multiplies the chance of an accidental credential commit while the control is entirely absent.

title: Fold the three duplicate MOK/secure-boot scripts into one compiled mios-mok verb
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- one authoritative Secure Boot codepath instead of three hand-maintained divergent ones.
acceptance_criteria: A single `mios-mok` binary exposes gen/enroll/status subcommands; the three scripts are gone (or reduced to <=3-line shims); the drift-gate is green and the binary's output is byte-identical to the captured golden.

details.what_how: Three overlapping MOK tools exist: `automation/generate-mok-key.sh` (RSA key generation), `automation/enroll-mok.sh` (mokutil enroll, 215 lines), and `usr/libexec/mios/mios-enroll-secure-boot` (enrolls the ublue akmods MOK). Once the `mios-mok` verb lands from the status_probe port, fold key-gen, enroll and ublue-key enroll into subcommands of that one compiled verb in `src/mios-rs`, keyed off `[security.secureboot]` in mios.toml rather than script-local constants. Demote the three scripts to <=3-line shims that call the binary, prove byte-parity against the captured golden, then delete the shims -- staging explicit paths only, never `git add -A`, because AGY shares the tree.
details.why: Three divergent MOK codepaths are a correctness hazard with a hard failure mode -- an enroll that disagrees with the key it was generated against bricks Secure Boot on the target machine -- and the retirement/cleanup half is what the two MOK porting tasks set up but never finish.

title: Add a greenboot required.d self-attestation check that auto-rolls-back a tampered running image
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- runtime integrity is continuously attested, not just verified once at publish and once at firstboot.
acceptance_criteria: A tampered or unsigned running image fails the greenboot required check and triggers a rollback to the previous deployment; a correctly signed image passes; the check reads its identity constraints from SSOT with no literals.

details.what_how: `automation/78-greenboot.sh` already wires greenboot's `required.d`/`green.d`/`red.d` directories, but nothing verifies the RUNNING image's own signature, so an offline-tampered deployment boots green forever. Add an SSOT-derived check under `/etc/greenboot/check/required.d` (shipped via the system_files overlay) that verifies the booted bootc deployment digest against the on-disk `usr/lib/containers/policy.json` (cosign verify / `bootc image verify`). A failed verify marks the boot RED, which makes greenboot roll back to the last-good deployment automatically. Derive the enable flag and the identity constraints from `[greenboot]` and `[security.sigstore]` so the check composes with the firstboot policy install instead of hardcoding an issuer or a digest.
details.why: Signing at publish plus verifying at firstboot leaves every subsequent boot completely unattested, so a machine tampered with after install stays green indefinitely; the greenboot-health and firstboot-policy tasks each cover one end and neither closes the loop.

title: Hash-pin the agent-plane and finetune pip installs with --require-hashes
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- install-time wheel integrity for the highest-trust runtime in the image.
acceptance_criteria: Both pip installs run with `--require-hashes` against committed hash-locked files; a tampered wheel is rejected at install time; the new drift-gate check fails if any requirement lacks a hash.

details.what_how: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/requirements.txt` and `usr/share/mios/finetune/requirements.txt` are installed by `automation/72-hermes-agent.sh` and `automation/73-model-prep.sh` with no hashes at all -- the string `--require-hashes` appears nowhere in the tree -- so a compromised PyPI or mirror can inject a malicious wheel straight into the agent plane. Generate fully hash-locked requirement files via `pip-compile --generate-hashes`, commit them, switch both installers to `pip install --require-hashes`, record the resolved wheels into the SBOM artifacts, and add a drift-gate check asserting every requirement line carries a hash. This is install-time integrity and is deliberately distinct from the advisory-only pip-audit gate.
details.why: The agent plane is the most privileged runtime in MiOS -- it drives OS-control verbs -- yet it currently pulls Python dependencies with zero integrity pinning, and pip-audit only reports known CVEs while doing nothing whatsoever against a substituted wheel.

title: Make a non-empty SBOM a fail-closed publish gate while bake stays degrade-open
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- every published image is guaranteed to carry the provenance record that reproducibility is defined by.
acceptance_criteria: A PUBLISH build with a missing or empty SBOM/TSV fails the gate; the bake step still degrades open; local and non-publish builds are unaffected.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-09 brief P1-2: 90-generate-sbom.sh is set +e and exits 0 on failure while marked fatal; it runs `curl ... main | sh` at bake (Law 12, task_2148); syft is stripped later, so 92-export-sbom.sh writes a one-package placeholder; check_sbom_metadata passes when the SBOM is absent and its test asserts the degrade-open. Fix: [security.sbom]; generate in CI from the pushed digest; mios-gate sbom fails closed; delete the placeholder writer; attach and sign the SBOM (task_2122). Upstream: ucore validate-sbom.py fails closed; actions/attest 4.1 sbom-path.

details.what_how: `automation/90-generate-sbom.sh` is deliberately degrade-open (always exits 0), so the CycloneDX + SPDX SBOM can silently vanish on any syft or egress hiccup, and `check_sbom_metadata` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:4096`) only validates STRUCTURE of files that exist -- it never asserts existence. Add a PUBLISH-gated fitness function (in `automation/99-postcheck.sh` plus a CI step guarded on `PUBLISH == 'true'`) asserting the published image carries a non-empty CycloneDX AND SPDX SBOM plus all three TSVs (binaries, bound-images, models). Bake keeps its degrade-open behaviour; only publish is fail-closed. Distinct from the binaries.tsv recording gate and from the attach-attestation task.
details.why: Degrade-open silently ships images with no SBOM at all, which means the attach-SBOM-attestation and scan-the-attested-SBOM tasks downstream have nothing to attest or scan; a presence gate at publish is the missing floor under the entire SBOM control stack.

title: Add a CI determinism job that bakes twice and diffs the resulting image manifests
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- reproducibility becomes a measured CI fact rather than an asserted property.
acceptance_criteria: Two back-to-back bakes produce identical manifest digests (or a diffoscope report showing only allowlisted deltas), and the job has been promoted from report-only to required.

details.what_how: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` appears nowhere in the tree today, and once the reproducible-build task lands it only ENABLES determinism without proving it. Add a job to both publishers that bakes the OCI image twice back-to-back and asserts byte-identical rootfs/manifest digests, or else emits a diffoscope report containing only allowlisted nondeterministic paths (logs, timestamps outside SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH's control). Strangler-style rollout: ship it report-only and non-blocking first, then promote it to a required check once it has been consistently green.
details.why: An unverified SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH claim is exactly the aspirational security assertion this campaign exists to convert into something gated; without the verification half, the SLSA/provenance story rests on an untested assumption.
