title: Consolidate the two Rust workspaces into one and re-home all eight native crates as members
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- a closed workspace so one cargo invocation can gate every line of compiled MiOS code.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo metadata --manifest-path tools/native/Cargo.toml --no-deps` lists all 8 crates plus miosd as workspace members; `cargo build --workspace --locked` compiles every one; no Cargo.toml directory in the tree remains outside a workspace.

details.what_how: `tools/native/Cargo.toml` lists only 3 members (mios-drift-runner, mios-version-check, mios-wallpaperd) while 5 crate directories on disk (generate-names-registry, mios-aiplane-lint, mios-bake-plan, mios-ssot-lint, mios-ssot-walk) sit OUTSIDE the workspace, and `src/mios-rs/` is a SECOND, separate workspace holding miosd. Any `cargo test`/`cargo clippy --workspace` therefore silently skips the orphans. Add every crate as an explicit `members` entry (keeping mios-ssot-walk as a lib) and fold `src/mios-rs/miosd` into the same workspace so one cargo invocation covers all compiled code. Retarget -- do not break -- the `cargo build --release` of src/mios-rs at `Containerfile:46-49` so it points at the unified manifest; stage explicit paths only.
details.why: Orphaned crates escape every cargo gate, so the entire test/clippy/deny/audit stack this workstream builds is meaningless until the workspace is closed -- five crates are currently uncompiled and untested by CI.

title: Pin Cargo.lock as a reproducibility SSOT and move crate versions to workspace inheritance
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the version literal is single-sourced and dependency resolution is recorded, not re-resolved.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build --workspace --locked` succeeds with zero lockfile churn; check_version_ssot fails when any member Cargo.toml version differs from mios.toml's mios_version; a grep finds no literal `version = "` in any member manifest.

details.what_how: `tools/native/mios-version-check/Cargo.toml` hardcodes `version = "0.3.0"` while its siblings use `version.workspace = true`, and `check_version_ssot` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:3629-3634`) only inspects 3 hand-listed Cargo.tomls, so that literal can drift undetected. Switch every literal-version member to `version.workspace = true`, commit the resolved `tools/native/Cargo.lock` and `src/mios-rs/Cargo.lock`, and make every CI and build cargo call pass `--locked`. Extend the Cargo loop in check_version_ssot to iterate ALL members discovered via `cargo metadata` instead of the hand-listed three, so a newly added crate cannot dodge the version gate.
details.why: A committed lockfile operationalizes SBOM-not-hardcode (dependency versions recorded at build rather than hand-pinned in source) and closes the TD-2 version-duplication drift class that currently lets one crate quietly ship the wrong version string.

title: Add a fast, cached pre-bake rust-gate CI job running cargo build + test on every PR
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- a 4-minute fail lane so a broken Rust port never reaches the hour-long bake.
acceptance_criteria: PRs show a rust-gate check that builds and tests the whole workspace in under 5 minutes with a warm cache; a failing `cargo test` blocks merge; the identical job exists in the Forgejo workflow.

details.what_how: CI has ZERO cargo steps today: the drift-gate and build jobs in `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` never compile or test any Rust, leaving miosd/drift.rs and 7 tools crates entirely ungated. Add a `rust-gate` job (`runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, `needs: []` so it runs in parallel with drift-gate and before build) that installs the pinned toolchain via rustup, restores `~/.cargo` and `target/` with actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock, then runs `cargo build --workspace --locked` and `cargo test --workspace --locked`. Mirror the job byte-for-byte into `.forgejo/workflows/`, since GitHub and Forgejo are equal publishers (Law 15).
details.why: A compiled-tested-code campaign with no cargo CI is unenforced -- every subsequent port in this workstream assumes this gate exists, and without it a Rust regression is only discovered an hour later at bake time, or not at all.

**What+How:** CI has ZERO cargo steps today: the drift-gate and build jobs in `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml` never compile or test any Rust, leaving miosd/drift.rs and 7 tools crates entirely ungated. title: Enforce cargo clippy -D warnings with restriction lints banning panic/unwrap in system verbs
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the strictly-stronger shellcheck the compiled tier needs, tuned so a verb cannot panic on bad config.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` is green and blocks CI on any regression; `clippy::unwrap_used` and `clippy::panic` are denied workspace-wide; miosd/drift.rs contains no unjustified unwrap.

details.what_how: Add a `[workspace.lints.clippy]` table to `tools/native/Cargo.toml` and `src/mios-rs/Cargo.toml` setting `-D warnings` plus targeted restriction lints at deny: `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unimplemented` -- because a system verb that panics on a malformed mios.toml is a fleet-wide hazard. Add `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` to the rust-gate job. Where existing code trips the lints (`src/mios-rs/miosd/src/drift.rs` has an `.unwrap()` on a Regex and an `unwrap_or_default()`), fix it or add a narrowly scoped `#[allow]` carrying a justification comment -- never a blanket allow at crate root.
details.why: The tech-debt map records that MiOS has no shellcheck-equivalent for its compiled tier, so panic-on-bad-config bugs that bash never guarded against are shipping unreviewed into binaries that run as system verbs.

title: Add a cargo-deny supply-chain gate covering licenses, bans, sources and advisories
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the FOSS-licensing posture encoded as machine-checked policy rather than as an assumption.

title: Add a fast cargo-audit RustSec advisory gate to the pre-bake lane
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- a per-PR security tripwire that fires in seconds, not at bake time.
acceptance_criteria: rust-gate runs `cargo audit` against the committed Cargo.lock and fails on any advisory; a deliberately vulnerable pinned dependency turns the job red.

details.what_how: Distinct from the heavier cargo-deny full check, add a quick `cargo audit --deny warnings` step (RustSec advisory database only) to the fast rust-gate job, so a newly disclosed CVE in a transitive dependency fails a PR immediately rather than waiting on the license and ban scans. details.why: Without a fast advisory check, a known-vulnerable dependency can sit in the lockfile across many merges before any slower scan notices, and a security regression discovered at bake time has already cost an hour of runner budget.

goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- one command reproduces the full CI verdict on a developer machine.

title: Stand up a trycmd CLI-snapshot harness pinning Rust mios-ssot-lint byte-for-byte to 97-ssot-lint.sh
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the reusable golden-master pattern every strangler-fig verb port will copy.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-ssot-lint` runs the trycmd snapshot; changing the Rust output without updating the golden fails the test; the committed golden matches current 97-ssot-lint.sh output.

details.what_how: `check_ssot_lint_equivalence` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:4870-4917`) already proves the Rust `mios-ssot-lint` is byte-identical to bash `automation/97-ssot-lint.sh`, but only via an ad-hoc shell diff. Formalize it as a real trycmd snapshot test INSIDE the crate: add trycmd as a dev-dependency, capture the current bash output over the repo fixture as a `.trycmd` golden (stdout, stderr and exit code), and assert the Rust binary reproduces it exactly. details.why: Without an accept/review characterization oracle, every verb port is a hope-based rewrite, and the existing ad-hoc twin-diff cannot be reused by the other 143 libexec tools that still need porting.

title: Add insta snapshots of the userenv.sh MIOS_* env projection as the golden the Rust resolver must reproduce
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the resolver port becomes a measured deviation-from-golden exercise instead of a rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo insta test` produces a stable MIOS_* projection snapshot, and any resolver change that alters a key or value fails until `cargo insta accept` is run under review.

details.what_how: Create a resolver-parity test module that shells `tools/lib/userenv.sh` against the committed `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, captures the full sorted `MIOS_*` KEY=VALUE projection, and stores it as an insta `.snap` golden -- normalizing root paths the same way `check_resolver_twin_equivalence` does with `env -i`. That snapshot becomes the byte-for-byte target for the future figment/serde Rust resolver: when a value is ported, the `.snap` must not change. Wire `cargo insta test` into the rust-gate job and commit the accepted `.snap` files.
details.where: `tools/native/ (new resolver-parity crate or tests/), tools/lib/userenv.sh, usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh, usr/share/mios/mios.toml, tools/check-resolver-twin.py (normalization reference)`
details.why: A single wrong resolved value silently breaks a Quadlet at runtime with no build-time signal, so porting the resolver without a committed golden risks a fleet-visible regression that nothing in CI would catch.

goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the eval removal at a security boundary is proven safe rather than hoped safe.

title: proptest differential resolver oracle: random mios.toml asserts mios_toml.py and userenv.sh emit identical MIOS_
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- Law 13 twin-equivalence becomes a fuzzed invariant instead of a spot check.

details.what_how: `tools/check-resolver-twin.py` only spot-checks the Python-vs-shell resolver twins; upgrade it to property-based differential testing. title: proptest round-trip: typed serde config to MIOS_* and back is identity for the resolver-core crate
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the compiled resolver proves its env projection is lossless before bash is retired.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test` round-trips generated typed configs through MIOS_* and back under proptest asserting identity, with failures shrinking to the minimal offending field.

details.what_how: As the ad-hoc parsers collapse into one typed resolver (figment/serde deserializing mios.toml into structs, with MIOS_* becoming a serialization FROM that model), add a proptest round-trip invariant: for a generated typed config value, serialize to MIOS_* env, re-deserialize, and assert structural identity with no lossy string-munging. This is the resolver-core crate's self-consistency proof and directly supports collapsing `mios_toml.py`, `mios_env.py` and userenv.sh's roughly 200 manual tuples into a single schema.
details.why: Retiring the bash resolver without a losslessness proof means a config field can silently degrade through the env projection, and the failure would only appear as a misbehaving service on a deployed host.

title: proptest mios-ssot-walk for determinism, stable ordering and key-collision freedom
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- the one-canonical-name law is hardened against fuzzed SSOT input.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p mios-ssot-walk` runs the determinism, ordering and collision invariants under proptest, and a synthetic colliding table fails and shrinks to a minimal case.

details.what_how: `mios-ssot-walk` (a lib crate) is the canonical SSOT walk that feeds the names registry. Add proptest cases generating nested TOML tables and asserting the walk is (a) deterministic across repeated runs, (b) stable-ordered under systemd `.d` lexical semantics, and (c) collision-free -- no two distinct paths may flatten to the same MIOS_* key, the exact class guarded by `check_names_registry` (`automation/98-drift-checks.sh:2064`) and `check_no_duplicate_value_key` (`:6097`). title: Add a mypy --strict gate over usr/lib/mios with a shrink-only per-module opt-out baseline
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- brings mypy to the Python plane so the AI-plane half of the SSOT resolver is machine-checked, not asserted.
acceptance_criteria: `mypy --strict` passes for the ratcheted module set and gates CI; adding a module to the opt-out roster fails; `mios_toml.py` and `mios_env.py` are strict-clean.

details.what_how: `automation/lint-python.sh` today only does `ast.parse`/py_compile -- zero type checking. Add a `mypy.ini` with global `strict = True` plus a `[mypy-*]` per-module opt-out roster seeded permissive for the legacy agent-pipe modules, and enforce that the roster may only SHRINK (a newly-added untyped module fails). Add a `check_mypy` step to `lint-python.sh` and to the drift-gate Python step in CI, degrading open ONLY when mypy is genuinely absent. Type the two resolver leaves first -- `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` and `usr/lib/mios/mios_env.py` -- to strict-clean, since they are the code being ported to Rust.
details.why: `ast.parse` catches only syntax, so every type-confusion bug in the AI plane ships today; without it the resolver port has no typed contract to port against.

goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- gives Python the fast static hazard scan bash already gets from shellcheck.

goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- proves the compiled-tier test suites actually have teeth before they are trusted as the byte-parity net for the Rust port.

title: Add check_migration_ratchet: bash-script count may only fall, cargo-test count may only rise
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and libexec tool fleet -- gives the strangler-fig migration a directional gate so it cannot stall or backslide.

title: Land candidate Law 17 THIN-GLUE-BUDGET + check_bash_thin_glue_budget
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- turns "bash is thin glue only" from a stated policy into a numbered, registered, enforced law (ADR + `[laws]` row + check).
acceptance_criteria: A new >200-line non-shim bash script fails `check_bash_thin_glue_budget`; the grandfather roster is shrink-only; Law 17 appears in `mios.toml [laws]` in BOTH repos; a negative test exists.

details.what_how: Law 14 TARGET-LANGUAGES (`mios.toml [laws]`, enforced by `check_target_languages:3814`) only blocks NEW non-target-language files -- it puts no cap on bash size or complexity, so a 900-line bash program is legal today. Add Law 17 THIN-GLUE-BUDGET to the `[laws]` table plus a `check_bash_thin_glue_budget` fitness-function failing any bash script under `automation/` or `usr/libexec/mios/` that exceeds the threshold (>200 lines OR >8 functions OR non-trivial control flow) unless it sits on a shrink-only roster in a new `mios.toml [laws.thin_glue].grandfathered`. Register in `main()` and in `check_law_enforcers:5698`, add a negative test, mirror the `[laws]`/`[laws.thin_glue]` SSOT into mios-bootstrap.git (Law 15), and update the law list in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. Seed the roster from today's oversized scripts so the gate lands green and can only tighten.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([laws] + new [laws.thin_glue]), automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check + main + :5698), tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh, mios-bootstrap repo [laws] mirror, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md law list`
details.why: Without a size budget the language law is toothless -- new bash programs keep landing legally, and every later port has no defined ceiling to shrink under.

title: Add check_shim_delegates: a demoted bash verb must be a thin shim that execs its Rust binary
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier -- keeps the strangler-fig parallel-run window honest so bash and Rust cannot silently diverge mid-port.
acceptance_criteria: A verb listed as ported that still carries business logic fails the check; a ported verb whose crate is not a workspace member fails; a negative test exists.

details.what_how: As leaf verbs are ported, the bash original is demoted to a thin shim behind the new binary. Add a `check_shim_delegates` fitness-function that reads a new `mios.toml [migration.ported_verbs]` roster mapping verb -> crate and asserts, for each listed verb, that it (a) is under a tiny line budget, (b) actually execs/dispatches to its Rust binary or the `${VAR:-LIT}` fallback, and (c) names a crate that is a resolved workspace member and builds. The deprecated alias `usr/libexec/mios/mios-theme-render` -- an 11-line delegator to `mios-dotfiles-render` -- is the shape precedent. Register in `main()` and add a negative.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml ([migration.ported_verbs]), automation/98-drift-checks.sh (new check + main), usr/libexec/mios/mios-theme-render (precedent), tools/native/Cargo.toml, tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`
details.why: A "ported" verb whose bash still holds real logic means two divergent implementations of the same behavior ship in the image, with no signal for which one ran.

title: Mirror every test/lint gate into .forgejo and add check_ci_workflow_parity
goal: E-16 The bake plane / release topology -- makes the declared GitHub == Forgejo equality mechanically true for the gate set, not just the build.
acceptance_criteria: `check_ci_workflow_parity` fails a step-removed mutated Forgejo copy and passes the parity'd pair; both workflows enumerate an identical gate-step set; `just drift-gate` + negatives green.

details.what_how: `.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml` (187 lines) is a hand-copied and already-DIVERGENT fork of `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml`: it carries its own inline agent-pipe test loop (no SKIP list, no shellcheck install) and lacks the rust/mypy/ruff/PS gates this campaign adds. Add `check_ci_workflow_parity` to `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` (registered in `main()`, negative in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh`) that parses both YAMLs and fails when the set of named gate steps -- shellcheck, lint-python, 97-ssot-lint, 98-drift-checks, negatives, rust-gate, mypy, ruff, pytest, PS gates -- is not identical, then bring the Forgejo file up to parity. Stage both workflow files explicitly.
details.why: The two publishers are declared bit-for-bit equal but already differ, so every gate added to GitHub becomes a false-green hole on the Forgejo side.

title: Pin a rust-toolchain.toml (channel + clippy/rustfmt/llvm-tools) for CI, local and build-stage parity
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance -- makes the Rust gates reproducible by pinning the compiler, not just the dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo +<pinned> --version` matches across CI and the build stage; clippy/rustfmt/llvm-cov components resolve from the pin; rust-gate is green with no rustup auto-download of a floating channel.

details.what_how: No `rust-toolchain.toml` exists anywhere in the tree (verified), yet the `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, cargo-deny and cargo-mutants tasks all assume a fixed toolchain, and `mios-wallpaperd/Cargo.toml` notes the toolchain is provisioned at stage time by `Install-MiosRust`. Add `rust-toolchain.toml` at the consolidated workspace root pinning an exact stable channel plus `components = [clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview]` and the target triple(s). Wire the pre-bake rust-gate and the build-stage Rust provisioner to honor it so all three environments agree; keep the literal channel an overridable default and stage the file explicitly.
details.why: `Cargo.lock` pins deps but not the compiler, so clippy/fmt/coverage/mutants results differ between a developer's machine and the runner -- gates that pass locally and fail in CI (or worse, the reverse).

goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- makes characterization goldens deterministic so the byte-parity strategy for the Rust port is trustworthy.

title: Add check_no_pending_snapshots + a single `just test-accept` golden-refresh entrypoint
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- keeps the snapshot suites authoritative instead of accumulating orphan pending files that mask real drift.
acceptance_criteria: A committed `*.snap.new` trips the check; `just test-accept` is the sole refresh path and leaves the tree clean; drift-gate + negatives green.

details.what_how: insta and trycmd emit `*.snap.new` / pending-accept files and goldenfile only writes updates under an env flag, so a stale or half-accepted snapshot can be committed unnoticed. title: Add a three-way resolver equivalence CI job executing globals.ps1 under pwsh against the python and shell twins
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- proves all THREE resolver twins emit the identical `MIOS_*` projection from one `mios.toml`.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs `globals.ps1` under pwsh and asserts its full `MIOS_*` set equals the python + shell twins; a seeded divergence in a NON-port key trips `check_globals_env_equivalence`; negative + drift-gate green.

details.what_how: The resolver has three twins, not two: `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py`, `tools/lib/userenv.sh` (== `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh`) and `automation/lib/globals.ps1` (220 lines). The differential-oracle proptest compares only python vs shell; `globals.ps1` is spot-checked for ports (`check_globals_ports`) and image name (`check_globals_image_parity`) but never for the full `MIOS_*` set and never actually EXECUTED (CI is ubuntu-only). Add a CI step that installs pwsh, dot-sources `globals.ps1`, dumps its `MIOS_*` projection, normalizes, and diffs it byte-for-byte against the python and shell projections over the same `mios.toml`; wire a `check_globals_env_equivalence` into `98-drift-checks.sh` with a negative. Degrade open ONLY when pwsh genuinely cannot be provisioned.
details.why: Every non-port, non-image key in the PowerShell resolver can drift undetected today, so a Windows host can resolve a different SSOT than the Linux host built from the same `mios.toml`.

goal: E-03 PowerShell surface -- supplies the runner the PS parse/PSSA/Pester gates need in order to exist at all.

title: Add check_no_silent_tool_skips: gated checks must fail closed under MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- eliminates the highest-frequency false-green class so a green gate means the checks actually ran.
acceptance_criteria: With `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1` and python3/tomllib/shellcheck stubbed absent, the affected checks FAIL rather than skip; the negative proves the fail-closed path; drift-gate stays green when the tools are present.

details.what_how: Many drift checks self-skip when a tool is absent: `check_test_hermeticity` and `check_negative_test_coverage` `return 0` without python3, `check_globals_image_parity` returns 0 without tomllib, `automation/lint-python.sh` exits 2 (treated as pass) with no python3 -- so a tool-poor runner reports green even though CI sets `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`. Add `check_no_silent_tool_skips` that scans `98-drift-checks.sh` and `lint-*.sh` for `command -v ... || return 0` and bare-skip patterns and, under `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`, requires each site to `_violation` (fail loud). Convert the offending sites to honor REQUIRE_TOOLS and add a negative.
details.why: A green drift-gate on a tool-poor runner is a lie -- real violations merge because the check that would have caught them quietly returned 0.

goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- turns "skipped here, runs there" from an unverified claim into a gated fact.

details.what_how: The drift-gate job hardcodes `SKIP=" test_mios_config_audit.py test_mios_redact.py test_mios_vector.py test_mios_gateway_agent.py test_mios_gateway_queue.py test_mios_admission.py test_mios_mcp_pool.py test_mios_bench_harness.py "` and asserts these run in the build-job venv gate -- but nothing proves the build job invokes them, and the Forgejo copy has a DIFFERENT (empty) skip loop. title: Add check_negatives_are_effective: each test_ fn must inject, assert-FAIL, restore, assert-PASS
goal: E-06 Test and documentation harness -- makes the negatives harness real mutation testing rather than a name-substring check.
acceptance_criteria: A stubbed always-pass `test_` fn trips `check_negatives_are_effective`; all 89 existing negatives satisfy the structural contract; drift-gate green.

details.what_how: `check_negative_test_coverage` only asserts that a required check's NAME appears as a substring somewhere in `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` -- it never verifies the 89 `test_` functions mutate state and observe a red->green transition, so an always-passing stub satisfies it. Add `check_negatives_are_effective` that structurally verifies each `test_` fn calls its target check TWICE around a mutation (once expecting failure via the `if ... ; then die` form, once expecting success after restore), mirroring the established `test_version_ssot` contract, and flags any `test_` fn that never invokes `98-drift-checks.sh` with a failing expectation. Add a self-negative.
details.why: An inert negative gives false assurance that a fitness-function is guarded -- the gate can silently lose its ability to fail and the harness still reports full coverage.

title: Extend the sibling-test ratchet from agent-pipe to `tools/*.py` and `usr/libexec/mios/*.py` via a shrink-only grandfather baseline
goal: E-05 Test and CI governance: the quality gates that make compiled code trustworthy -- makes "every Python surface carries a characterization test" machine-enforced instead of true only for agent-pipe, so compiled/ported code has a parity oracle to be trusted against.
acceptance_criteria: adding a new untested `tools/` or `libexec` `.py` module trips the check; growing the grandfathered baseline fails; agent-pipe behavior is unchanged; `just drift-gate` and the negatives run green.

title: Make native `mios-config` schema-GENERIC so a mios.toml section change never forces a Rust recompile
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- one generic resolver walk shared by every surface, so the native tier reads exactly the operator-defined key space the Python resolver does rather than a second, hand-typed copy of the schema.
acceptance_criteria: a test proves adding/removing an arbitrary `[foo.bar]` section needs ZERO Rust edits; `cargo build && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` all pass; no `skip_deserializing` hack remains in the crate.

details.what_how: `usr/share/mios/configurator/mios.html` declares 619 `data-key="section.field"` dotted paths; a generic writer sets them in mios.toml; `usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py` then WALKS the file generically (`deep_merge` / `section()` / `isinstance(dict)` recursion, zero hardcoded schema). `src/mios-rs/mios-config` regressed this by hard-typing every section as a Rust struct, which broke `[packages]` (a `sections=[...]` master list plus per-group `[packages.<name>]` tables) and forced a `skip_deserializing` band-aid to green the gate. Keep hard types for ONLY the few stable fields a `run_*` actually reads (`meta.mios_version`, `meta.fedora_version`, `build.ratchet.max_phase_scripts`, `build.phases.list`, `identity.username`); read everything else (packages, repos, security, network, power, compliance) through `toml::Value` plus a dotted-path lookup mirroring `mios_toml.py`'s `section(data, name)`. Delete dead `PackageSectionConfig`/`RepoConfig` unless a `run_*` constructs them (watch clippy `dead_code` on pub items) and remove `skip_deserializing`.
details.why: every operator edit to mios.toml -- the one config surface the product promises -- otherwise requires a Rust recompile, and the struct mismatch already silently disabled `[packages]` deserialization.

title: Inventory EVERY hardcoded version literal in the tree into one classified TSV burn-down report
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- produces the enumerated worklist without which "SSOT carries version INTENT only" cannot be finished or measured.
acceptance_criteria: the TSV carries a class for every version token, two consecutive runs are byte-identical, and the class-(c) total is logged in full with no silent truncation.

details.what_how: The live bug was `rancher/k3s` bumped to `v1.36.2-k3s1` in mios.toml while the Kubernetes DNF repo in `automation/06-enable-external-repos.sh` stayed pinned at `v1.32` -- proof that ad-hoc pinning is spread across container tags, DNF repo minors, Python wheel pins, model tags, COPR `fedora-NN` endpoints and Quadlet labels. Write `tools/audit-version-literals.py` (pure, offline, no third-party deps) that scans for version-shaped tokens (`:v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?`, `stable:/v\d+\.\d+`, `fedora-\d+`, `@sha256:`, `==\d+\.\d+`, image `:tag` refs), classifies each as (a) SSOT-definition, (b) SSOT-derived/placeholder or (c) HARDCODED-literal, and writes `usr/share/mios/reference/version-literals-audit.tsv` with path, line, token, class and a suggested SSOT key. Exempt SBOM/lockfiles, `.repo` fixtures, CHANGELOG/history and the SSOT itself. The class-(c) count is the campaign metric driving task_2204..task_2207.
details.why: without the inventory each stale pin is only found by an operator noticing a broken repo months later, exactly as the k3s/k8s mismatch was.

title: Establish ONE version SSOT and convert every consumer to a derivation (the k3s→k8s cascade, generalized)
goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- one declared value, every downstream version derived, so a single SSOT bump propagates without a second hand edit.
acceptance_criteria: a test that bumps the k3s tag in a temp copy of the SSOT and diffs derived outputs shows the k8s repo minor, the Quadlets and the manifests all moved with ZERO other edits; the 3-way py/sh/ps1 resolver-equivalence checks stay green.

details.what_how: Consolidate version definitions into `mios.toml [image.sidecars]` (image refs) plus a new `[versions]` table for non-image numbers (k8s minor derivable from the k3s tag, wheel pins, tool versions), each mapped to a `MIOS_*` by `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` and its `.ps1`/`globals.ps1` twins (Law 15 double-repo). Then walk task_2203's class-(c) list and convert each literal to a derivation: DNF repo minors computed off `$MIOS_K3S_VERSION` (`grep -oE 'v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'`, the shape the `5793d4ac` hotfix used), COPR endpoints on `${FEDORA_VERSION}`, Quadlet labels keeping `${VAR}` placeholders. Never reintroduce a bare literal; use `${VAR:-safe-default}` only where a fallback is genuinely required.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml`, `usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh` (+ `.ps1` / `globals.ps1` twins), every consumer named in the 1562 audit
details.why: today `MIOS_K3S_VERSION` exists but most versions have no single home, so each bump is a manual multi-file sweep that silently half-lands and ships a mismatched repo.

title: Widen `check_no_hardcoded_ssot_literal` from `fedora-NN` only to ALL version literals, with an ANCHORED allowlist
goal: E-12 ZERO-HARDCODES: float every remaining literal out of code -- turns the float-latest cascade into a permanent invariant rather than a one-time cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: re-hardcoding any k8s/k3s/fedora version outside the SSOT turns the gate RED; the negative test proves the failure path; the full drift-gate plus negatives are green and the gate index is regenerated.

details.what_how: The gate in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh` greps only `fedora-[0-9]{2}`, so it would not have caught the stale k8s `v1.32`. Generalize it to flag `stable:/v\d+\.\d+`, `rancher/k3s:v…`, other pinned image `:vX.Y.Z` tags and bare `fedora-\d+` across `automation/`, `usr/share/mios/` and `usr/share/containers/`, exempting only (a) the SSOT `[image.sidecars]`/`[versions]` definitions, (b) `${VAR}` / `${VAR:-default}` derivations, or (c) entries explicitly allowlisted in `mios.toml [security.nohc_allowlist]` -- using the ANCHORED allowlist pattern, not the unanchored form that spuriously exempted real `:80xx` violations. Rendered Quadlets are already covered by `check_pod_quadlets`, so once they float `${FEDORA_VERSION}` no blanket directory exemption is needed. Add negatives that inject a bare `v1.32`, assert FAIL, restore, assert PASS.
details.why: with the check scoped to one regex, the exact class of drift the campaign just fixed can reappear on the next commit and no gate will notice.

title: Give image refs `:latest` INTENT with digests resolved at BUILD, and record the offline-vendored pin exception in an ADR
goal: E-15 SBOM and supply-chain hardening as compiled, gated policy -- makes "reproducible = baked manifest + SBOM" true, with every legitimate pin justified rather than assumed.
acceptance_criteria: every sidecar's float-or-pin decision is recorded in the ADR; the baked SBOM manifest holds the resolved digests; no `@sha256` is hand-typed anywhere in the SSOT.

details.what_how: Per ADR-0003, digests and versions are SBOM data resolved at build, never hand-typed in SSOT. For registry-pulled sidecars express `:latest` (or a floating major) in `[image.sidecars]` and let the build resolve and record the `@sha256` into the baked SBOM manifest -- reconciling this with the `_sidecar_image` digest-SSOT fallback already in `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py`. For OFFLINE-vendored artifacts (the k3s tarball, the hermes wheel) do NOT float: write an ADR under `docs/adr/` stating why that specific version is pinned for the mirror and how a bump flows (bump SSOT → re-vendor → digest re-recorded), so the float-vs-pin tension is an explicit recorded decision instead of undocumented drift.
details.where: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml [image.sidecars]`, `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py` (`_sidecar_image`), the build SBOM step, a new/updated ADR under `docs/adr/`
details.why: hand-pinned digests in SSOT go stale invisibly and are the root of the recurring Quadlet-digest-drift class, while blind floating would break byte-reproducible offline install.

title: Gate AI-hint manifest freshness so `manifest.json` stops carrying stale version snapshots
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- every generated projection is regenerated-or-red, never quietly stale.
acceptance_criteria: editing a script without regenerating its manifest trips the new check; every manifest is byte-fresh; grepping the manifests for `v1.32` returns nothing.

details.what_how: `automation/manifest.json` still embeds the OLD `stable:/v1.32` and its old comments inside the `full_content` snapshot AFTER the script itself was fixed, because `tools/generate-ai-manifest.py` runs only best-effort from `automation/ai-bootstrap.sh` and is not gated. Add a `--check` mode to the generator (regenerate to a temp dir, diff against the committed file, exit non-zero on drift), make output deterministic (sorted keys, normalized newlines) so it does not thrash, wire it into the docgen CI leg, and add a `check_ai_manifests_fresh` drift-check that fails closed under `MIOS_DRIFT_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`. Regenerate every `manifest.json` and `root-manifest.json` once to clear the current staleness.
details.where: `tools/generate-ai-manifest.py`, `automation/98-drift-checks.sh`, the docgen CI job, all `*/manifest.json` and `root-manifest.json`
details.why: the manifests are the AI-hint layer's view of the tree, so a stale snapshot re-teaches an agent the exact literal the campaign just purged.

goal: E-14 Float latest globally -- which variables float is itself operator-declared config, not a fact compiled into a generator.

details.why: the renderer currently decides policy that belongs to the operator, so every new floating variable is a code change plus a review round-trip.

title: Vendor `aiohttp` and the full hermes-agent dependency closure into the offline wheels dir, and fail the phase when it is incomplete
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image -- the baked image must actually contain a working agent plane, not a venv that merely appears installed.
acceptance_criteria: the phase builds the venv with no network and emits no WARN; deliberately deleting one wheel fails the phase; the bake log reports 0 warned for this step.

details.what_how: `automation/72-hermes-agent.sh` fails its offline install with `ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement aiohttp (from versions: none)` and degrades to `WARN Agent-venv offline install incomplete`, so the published image ships a hermes-agent venv with no HTTP client. `usr/share/mios/vendored/wheels/` lacks the full closure. Resolve hermes-agent's `pyproject.toml` against `usr/share/mios/agents/constraints.txt` using `pip download --only-binary=:all:` for the image's Python (3.13), commit the resulting wheels, and change the phase to FAIL rather than WARN when the closure is incomplete so the regression cannot recur silently.
details.why: the agent plane is the product, and a WARN-not-FAIL path means every published image today carries a hermes venv that cannot make an HTTP request.

title: Fix `37-k3s-selinux.sh` exiting 1 on the flat-layout vendored policy tarball
goal: E-16 The bake plane: what is present in the image -- a clean, unambiguous bake where a non-zero phase exit always means a real failure.
acceptance_criteria: the bake reports 0 warned; on a host where the policy is genuinely unavailable the script emits an explicit `mios_skip` with a logged reason rather than a bare non-zero exit.

details.what_how: The bake logged `[WARN] 37-k3s-selinux.sh (2s) exit=1`. Root cause: the vendored tarball is k3s-selinux-0.1.1-rc2, whose sources (`k3s.te k3s.fc k3s.if k3s.sh`) sit FLAT at the archive root with no `policy/` directory, while the detector knew only the >=0.2 nested `policy/<distro>/` layout and fell back to an unguarded `find policy ...` that aborted the phase under `set -euo pipefail`. Fix: add a flat-layout branch, guard the `find`, skip the self-copy (`cp ./k3s.* .` errors under `set -e`), turn missing sources into a `mios_skip` that logs the locations searched instead of `exit 1`, and verify extraction actually produced `k3s.te` before trusting it.
details.why: it was the only warning left in an otherwise clean 67-script bake, and a bare `exit=1` is indistinguishable from a real build failure for anyone reading the log.

title: Fold drift-checks 28 and 52 into `check_globals_generated` and delete their literal parsers
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- one byte-level check per generated artifact, with no hidden coupling constraining the generator.
acceptance_criteria: 28/52 delegate or are retired with 130 still covering them; `render-globals.py` carries no formatting workaround for either; the negatives still catch a hand-edit to `globals.sh`/`globals.ps1`.

details.what_how: `check_globals_ports` (28) and `check_globals_image_parity` (52) scrape literals out of `automation/lib/globals.{sh,ps1}` with bespoke regexes (`else { <digits> }`, `MIOS_IMAGE_NAME:=`). Those files are now generated in full and byte-gated by check 130, so 28/52 are redundant AND actively constrain the renderer's output shape -- it must keep emitting `:=` and bare integers, and keep a `$defaultImageName` line nothing reads, purely to satisfy them. Replace their bodies with a delegation to `check_globals_generated` (or retire them with coverage preserved by 130), delete the literal parsers, drop the shape workarounds from `tools/render-globals.py`, and regenerate the gate index.
details.why: the coupling already cost two CI round-trips and it blocks task_1809, which stays open until the renderer can choose its own output format.

title: Build and install the `mios-resolver` binary into the image and cut generation over to it behind a differential gate
goal: E-01 Compiled native tier: Rust-port the build orchestrator and the libexec tool fleet -- moves the resolver from a crate that merely compiles to the code the product actually runs.
acceptance_criteria: the binary is present in the baked image; the differential gate is green; a booted image demonstrably takes the native branch in `userenv.sh`.

details.what_how: `tools/render-globals.py` and the `[ports]` derivation run through the PYTHON resolver (`usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py`); the Rust `mios-resolver` mirrors that logic in `ports.rs` / `emit_ps.rs` / `emit_shell.rs` but is never built into the image, so `userenv.sh`'s `command -v mios-resolver` branch is dead in production. Add a bake phase that compiles `tools/native` and installs the binary to `/usr/libexec/mios/mios-resolver`, keeping a degrade-chain to the Python path when the binary is absent. Then add a differential drift-check asserting `mios-resolver --emit=shell|powershell|json` is byte-identical to the Python render against the real SSOT.
details.why: the entire WS-RESOLVER crate is inert today -- it compiles and passes its own tests while nothing in the shipped product ever calls it -- and task_2218 cannot start until it does.

title: Wire or delete the inert `[migration]` and `[versions]` SSOT tables
goal: E-08 Global Unification Plan: collapse the MIOS_* namespace to one-value-derived -- every SSOT key has exactly one live consumer, and version facts are declared once.
acceptance_criteria: every key in both tables has a consumer a grep can find, or the tables no longer exist; a newly added inert top-level table fails the gate.

details.what_how: `[migration].use_rust_resolver_*` has ZERO consumers (grep-verified), and `[versions]` duplicates data already flowing from `[image.sidecars]` (`MIOS_K3S_VERSION` is emitted from the sidecar tag today) -- both read as live config to anyone opening mios.toml or the configurator. Pick one: (a) make `userenv.sh` / `mios_toml.py` actually honour `[migration]` when choosing the native vs Python resolver, and make `[versions]` the single source that `[image.sidecars]` tags derive FROM; or (b) delete both tables and record the reasoning in the ADR. Then add a drift-check that fails on any re-introduced inert top-level table.
details.why: inert SSOT is worse than absent SSOT -- an operator flips `use_rust_resolver_*` in the configurator, nothing changes, and trust in the one config surface is gone.

title: Clear the `check_var_closure` "referenced but NOT emitted" backlog and flip the check from SOFT to hard-fail
goal: E-10 One canonical name: the unified names/keys registry -- closes the referenced-but-unemitted key-library drift class the epic names explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: the closure report is empty and the check hard-fails; introducing a newly referenced-but-unemitted variable turns the gate RED.

details.what_how: `check_var_closure` reports ~180 referenced-but-unemitted names. With the generated resolvers and renderers now excluded as emitters, the remainder is real signal in three classes: (1) PREFIX ARTEFACTS -- `MIOS_A2A_`, `MIOS_AGENT_`, `MIOS_PORT_` are regex captures of dynamic expansions like `MIOS_PORT_${name}`, so teach `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py` to drop a trailing-`_` capture that is a strict prefix of a known name; (2) DOUBLE-PREFIX -- `[mios]` walks to `MIOS_MIOS_NAME` / `MIOS_MIOS_FIND_ALIASES_*`, so either alias the `mios.*` section to a single `MIOS_` prefix in `get_aliases()` or rename the section; (3) GENUINELY MISSING -- `MIOS_CONVERGE_*` and `MIOS_COLOR_ANSI_*` are emitted only into `globals.sh`, so confirm the resolver emits them too. Then convert the check from SOFT WARNING to a hard violation.
details.why: a soft warning printing 180 lines every run is not a gate -- real key-library regressions are already hiding inside that noise.

title: Enforce `tools/sync-generated.sh` in CI instead of trusting contributors to run the renderers in order
goal: E-07 The drift-gate as the enforcement plane -- the regeneration ordering constraint becomes executable rather than documented.
acceptance_criteria: a deliberately stale manifest fails the new step with the precise file list; the step is green on a synced tree; both workflows carry it.

details.what_how: Several generated artefacts (AI manifests, `globals.{sh,ps1}`, pod Quadlets, the names registry, `env-baseline.txt`) go stale on any edit under `automation/` or `tools/`, and the only defence is remembering to run the renderers in the right dependency order. Add it to both publisher workflows so GitHub and Forgejo stay equal.
details.why: stale-artefact failures cost more CI round-trips than any real defect during the port campaign, and each one arrives as five separate unhelpful "X is stale" gate messages.

title: Make `mios-template-engine` honour its documented contract or retire it into `mios-new`
goal: E-04 One template per file type + the `mios new` scaffolder -- one generator with one contract, which is the precondition for a conformance gate.
acceptance_criteria: exactly one scaffolder with one contract remains; no post-generation relocation workaround exists; no orphaned entry point or doc reference is left behind.

details.what_how: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-template-engine` advertises `<kind> <target_filepath> [description]` but delegates to `mios-new`, which is name-addressed and picks its own canonical destination; the shim then relocates the result and re-substitutes `{{description}}` -- it works, but it is a workaround. It also has ZERO callers (grep-verified: only itself and AGY-TASKS.md). Either give `mios-new` real `--out <path>` and `--description` flags and reduce the engine to a straight pass-through, or delete `mios-template-engine` and update every doc under `usr/share/doc/mios/` that mentions it.
details.why: two overlapping scaffolders is precisely the duplication this campaign exists to remove, and the documented contract currently lies to anyone who reads it.

title: Reconcile in-container port fallbacks with the host allocation and record the rule in SSOT
goal: E-13 Ports are allocated from SSOT, not hand-assigned -- the last place a port literal legitimately differs from SSOT becomes documented and gated rather than folklore.

details.what_how: Several Quadlets pass `${MIOS_PORT_X:-<upstream-default>}` where the fallback is the UPSTREAM in-container port (pgvector 5432, vllm 11441, cpu-node 11451, crawl4ai 11235), so fallback and SSOT deliberately disagree -- defensible, but nowhere recorded. Meanwhile `[ports.categories.sidecar]` now allocates real keys for the sidecar daemons (guacd, redis, chrome_cdp, otelcol, pxe_hub_api, forge_ssh_git). Decide per service whether the container binds the SSOT port or the upstream default behind a host-side publish, write that decision into the `[ports.categories]` `doc` field, and make each `:-N` fallback consistent with the decision.
details.why: a reader cannot currently tell an intentional upstream-default fallback from a stale literal, so both are copied forward and neither is checked.

title: Fix mios-ai-tag's multi-line hint orphaning and repair the 22 damaged headers
goal: D-1 The comment corpus is lossless -- a re-tag can never truncate or split a header, so every downstream doc generator reads whole prose.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-ai-tag --selftest` passes; a full `--no-llm --dry-run` over the tree reports zero diffs on already-tagged files; no `AI-related:` line in the tree ends in a comma.

details.what_how: `AI_LINE_RE` matches only lines containing an `AI-*:` marker, so a wrapped continuation survives `retag()`'s strip and the fresh block is inserted MID-SENTENCE between the hint and its orphan; `existing_hint()` then regexes a single line and drops the remainder -- a lossy round-trip. Replace the line filter with a REGION strip (first `AI_LINE_RE` match, then consume forward while the line matches `^<marker>\s{2,}\S` or `AI_LINE_RE`), and make `existing_hint()` join continuation lines with a single space before `_clean()`. Then repair the 22 already-damaged files, detectable as `AI-related:` lines ending in a dangling comma: `usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme`, `mios-sync-toml`, `mios-sync-to-root`, `usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sync-theme.service`, `installation/mios-install.sh`, `installation/README.md`, and mios-ai-tag's OWN header (line 2 is truncated at "...(AI-hint purpose"). Add `--selftest` round-tripping fixtures for shebang / BOM / CRLF / md front-matter / wrapped hint.
details.why: generating a manual from a corpus with silent truncation bakes the truncation into the product, and every later step reads this corpus.

title: Close mios-ai-tag's SKIP_DIR and EXT gaps (65k vendored files in, 98 orphaned tags out)
goal: D-2 The taggable corpus is exactly the authored corpus -- no vendored tree can enter it and no authored file can be locked out of its own tagger.
acceptance_criteria: a walk from the drive root yields 2,142 authored files and zero `.rustup` paths; `mios-ai-hint-coverage --json` denominator includes the 52 Rust files.

details.what_how: `SKIP_DIR` excludes `.venv`/`node_modules`/`target`/`site-packages` but NOT `.rustup`, so `mios-ai-tag --root /mnt/c/MiOS` would walk 65,133 vendored Rust-toolchain files (61,792 `.html` + 3,108 `.js`), find no existing hint, and issue ~65k teacher calls before writing `AI-hint` comments into the Rust standard-library docs. Add `\.rustup`, `\.tmp\.driveupload` (Drive's hardlink dedup cache), `tr_clone`, `tr_remote`, `shellcheck-v[0-9.]+`. Conversely 98 files already carry hand-written headers whose extensions are absent from `EXT` and can therefore never be refreshed: `.rs` 52, `.snap` 19, `.psm1` 15, `.qml` 7, `.nft` 2, `.ks`/`.template`/`.defaults` 1 each. Add all eight to `EXT` and map `.rs` to the `slash` comment style.
details.why: one accidental root-scoped run currently rewrites 65k vendored files and burns 65k inference calls; meanwhile the whole Rust native tier is invisible to its own tagger.

title: Resolve mios-ai-tag's hint cap, teacher endpoint and teacher model from SSOT
goal: E-7 Law 7 NO-HARDCODE holds in the tagger itself -- the tool that documents the codebase must not be the one carrying phantom constants.
acceptance_criteria: no numeric or model literal remains in the tagger; `mios-hardcode-lint` is clean on the file; a re-tag leaves the 363 long hints byte-identical.

details.what_how: `_clean()` hardcodes a 260-char cap, `--teacher-endpoint` defaults to `localhost:${MIOS_PORT_LLM_LIGHT:-8450}` while mios.toml uses 8500 and the tool's own header says 11450, and `--teacher-model` defaults to `gemma4:12b`, a string that appears nowhere in SSOT. Resolve all three through the shared `mios_toml` resolver exactly as the sibling `mios-ai-hint-coverage` already does: `[ai_tag].hint_max_chars`, `[ai_tag].teacher_port_key` -> `[ports]`, `[ai_tag].teacher_model` (validated against `[ai].available_models`). Ship `hint_max_chars = 3000` so the 363 hand-written over-cap hints (max 2,837 chars) survive the next run; task_2229 ratchets it back to 260 once they are harvested.
details.why: three different values for one port and a model that does not exist mean the teacher path is untested folklore, and the 260 cap is a live data-loss trigger worth ~100k characters of prose.

title: Build the comment lexer + classifier library with the 30-fixture unit test
goal: D-3 "Stay in code" vs "migrate to docs" is a mechanical, testable function -- not a judgement call made once per file by whoever is reading it.
acceptance_criteria: all 30 fixtures pass; aggregate counts over the real tree land within 3% of STAY ~5,000 / MIGRATE ~1,900 / DROP ~400 / READONLY 42; `test_mios_manual.py` runs inside `just drift-gate` beside `test_mios_docgen.py`.

details.what_how: New `usr/lib/mios/mios_comments.py` (beside `mios_toml.py`, the established shared-library home) exporting `lex(path) -> list[Block]` and `classify(block, policy, refindex) -> Verdict`. Lex per language via `mios_ai_tag.comment_style()`, with three overrides: Python via `tokenize` COMMENT tokens + `ast` docstrings (NEVER regex -- regex miscounts multi-line data strings as prose), PowerShell `<# #>`, Rust `///`/`//!`. Classify with the ordered first-match rule set R0..R7 in BUILD-SPEC section 2: generated-artifact -> llm-payload -> header -> commented-out-code -> banner -> size+signal -> inline -> stale axis. Every threshold and every signal regex comes from `[docs]`/`[docs.signals]`, never from code. Ship `usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_manual.py` with the 30 named fixtures, each asserting an exact `(class, reason)` pair, including the boundary case `mios-tailscale-serve.ps1:67` (2 lines, ~28 words, why-signal, no narrative-signal -> STAY via the mid-size rule).
details.why: without a fixed classifier the ratchet has no comparable number and "we migrated some comments" is unmeasurable.

title: Land `mios-manual` with the corpus ledger and retire generate-manual.py
goal: D-4 One documentation CLI exists, it reads the repo, and its output is reproducible byte-for-byte between a developer and CI.
acceptance_criteria: `mios-manual ledger --check` is green on a clean tree; two runs from different CWDs produce byte-identical output; `tools/generate-manual.py` and the `manual:` Justfile target are gone.

details.what_how: New `usr/libexec/mios/mios-manual` with six subcommands (`render`, `audit`, `coverage`, `harvest`, `prune`, `ledger`). Corpus = `mios_ai_tag.walk()` INTERSECT `git ls-files` -- adopt `generate-ai-manifest.py`'s `tracked_files()` determinism rule verbatim, since a filesystem walk makes the artifact a function of the developer's working directory and can then never match a clean CI regeneration. Emit `usr/share/mios/reference/manual-corpus.tsv` (path, span, lines, words, sha12, class, reason, as, stale, landed_doc, landed_anchor, landed_words, pruned), carrying `landed_*` forward by `sha12` so reformatting the surrounding code never loses a landing record, and retaining pruned rows as tombstones. Retire `tools/generate-manual.py`: it imports only `os/argparse/shutil`, performs zero repo reads, is 1311 lines of hardcoded literal, ships 21 of 43 links broken, and `shutil.rmtree`s `usr/share/doc/mios/manual/` unconditionally BEFORE and independent of `--output`. `mios-manual --out` must never delete a path it was not asked to write.
details.why: the two surfaces in this repo that are actually documentation are the only two with no drift gate, which is exactly why the shipped manual has 21 dead links and 50 `file:///C:/MiOS/` paths inside a Linux OS's docs.

title: Create the authored manual tree and gate manual.md with `render --check` (the real task_1289)

**What+How:** `mios-manual render` emits `reference/ports.md` (from `[ports.categories]` + `[ports]`), `reference/laws.md` (from `[laws]`, 16 rows, plus the 12 root exceptions), `reference/pipeline.md` (from `[build.pipeline]`), `reference/cli.md` (113 `[verbs.*]` + the `usr/libexec/mios/` backends), `reference/units.md` (from the UNIT FILES, not `mios.toml [units.*]` and never `globals.*`), and `usr/share/doc/mios/README.md` -- 130 baked doc files currently have NO entry point on a host. Every derived section ends with a `<!-- derived from ... -->` provenance line. These are the single answers the 1,155 stale port refs across 122 of 225 files can then be rewritten against; note the SSOT's OWN inline comments are stale too (`mios.toml:9438` says Open WebUI is at `:3033`, `:9439-9440` cites a port 9119 that exists nowhere), so a prose fix that trusts mios.toml comments re-imports the errors.

**Done When:** all six files are generated, gate 152 covers them, and every port/law/stage number in them equals the SSOT value.
**Why:** a reader cannot get a straight answer to "what port is X on", "how many laws are there" or "what does build step N do"; every doc that answers directly is wrong, and one agent-facing contract file states a law that does not exist.

title: Harvest the 363 over-cap AI-hints into docs, then prune them behind the landing gate
goal: D-7 The ~100k characters of prose currently hiding in the `AI-hint:` field live in documentation, and the tagger's own cap becomes safe to re-impose.
acceptance_criteria: harvest and prune are SEPARATE commits with `audit --deletions` green between them; a full `mios-ai-tag --no-llm` pass is byte-identical afterwards; gate 154 goes red if a harvested passage is gutted.

details.what_how: 363 hints (18.9%) exceed the tagger's 260-char `_clean()` cap and were therefore NOT written by `mios-ai-tag` -- they are hand-written mini-documents topping out at 2,837 chars (`mios_pipe/routing/agent_call.py`), 2,642 (`swarm.py`), 2,158 (`a2a.py`), 2,128 (`web_research.py`), 1,980 (`vision.py`), 1,947 (`mios_dispatch.py`). Run `mios-manual harvest --class=overlong-hint --apply` to write each into `usr/share/doc/mios/manual/_harvest/<slug>.md` annotated `<!-- mios-src: <path>:<a>-<b> sha=<sha12> -->`, filling the ledger's `landed_*` columns; SOURCE IS NOT TOUCHED in this step. Land drift check 154 `check_comment_landing` (pointer resolution + landing predicate for pruned rows + `landed_doc` may never be cleared). ONLY THEN run `prune --class=overlong-hint --only-landed --apply`, which replaces each hint with a `<=260`-char summary plus an `AI-doc:` row and REFUSES any block whose predicate is false. Finally ratchet `[ai_tag].hint_max_chars` back to 260 and `max_overlong_hints` to 0.
details.why: this is the single largest data-loss hazard in the tree -- `existing_hint()` re-applies the 260-char cap on reuse, so the very next tagger run silently truncates all 363.

title: Land the comment ratchet and its monotone guard
goal: D-8 Narrative comment volume can only go down, and "raise the ceiling" is a gate violation rather than a one-character fix.
acceptance_criteria: both gates are enforcing at the measured baseline, both RED edits have been observed red and reverted, and the ratchet number appears in `just drift-gate` output.

details.what_how: Drift check 155 `check_comment_ratchet` asserts `unmigrated_narrative <= [docs].max_unmigrated_narrative`, `stale_refs <= [docs].max_stale_refs`, `overlong_hints <= [ai_tag].max_overlong_hints` and `undocumented_components <= [docs].max_undocumented_components`, resolving each ceiling with the layered pattern `mios-ai-hint-coverage` already uses (CLI > env > mios.toml > permissive report-only fallback). Drift check 156 `check_doc_ratchet_monotone` then asserts every one of those four ceilings is `<=` the value in `usr/share/mios/reference/doc-ratchet-floor.tsv`, which `mios-manual coverage --write-floor` can only ever LOWER (it writes `min(recorded, current)`). Both need negative tests: a 12-line 60-word narrative block added to a scratch `usr/lib/mios/*.py` must turn 155 red, and incrementing any ceiling by 1 must turn 156 red. Neither may be added to `[testing].negative_coverage_exempt` -- both are exercisable with a pure text edit on a Linux runner.
details.why: gate 155 alone is unfalsifiable in practice -- this repo has a documented history of gates that cannot fail, and a ratchet whose ceiling is freely raisable is exactly one of them.

title: Harvest the narrative mass: mios.toml, the two Windows entry points, and the agent-pipe tree
goal: D-9 The 1,764 narrative blocks / 16,481 lines / ~150k words of design prose living in comments become chapters and ADRs.
acceptance_criteria: each wave lands as harvest-commit then prune-commit with `audit --deletions` green between; `max_unmigrated_narrative` has fallen by the wave size; no source block was deleted without a ledger row proving its landing.

details.what_how: Harvest in yield order, one wave per commit, each followed by a gated prune. Wave A: `usr/share/mios/mios.toml` (36,159 narrative words / 4,050 lines), `build-mios.ps1` (23,791 / 2,975) and `Get-MiOS.ps1` (17,041 / 2,032) -- three files hold 55% of all narrative. Wave B: `usr/lib/mios/agent-pipe/**`, 14 of the top 25 files (`memory/pg.py`, `routing/dag_exec.py`, `mios_surface.py`, `scheduler/preempt.py`, `federation/a2a.py`, `routing/agentreg.py`, `server.py`, `mios_dispatch.py`, ...), assembled as ONE "agent-pipe architecture" chapter -- which is what those module docstrings collectively already are. Wave C: every `as=adr-candidate` block becomes a real ADR, starting with `.github/workflows/mios-ci.yml:282` (42 lines giving root cause, exact error text and operator confirmation for the rootful-podman GID-remap bake failure) and `mios.toml:5457` (90 lines, the crawl4ai container scrapped, citing Law 5). Wave D: systemd/Quadlet prologues into `reference/units.md` -- config formats are comment-DOMINATED (`.rules` 78%, `.conf` 64%, `.preset` 54%, `.service`/`.timer` 43%, `.toml` 39%) and are the real design-intent surface. Lower `[docs].max_unmigrated_narrative` and the floor after each wave.
details.why: this is the extraction prize -- ~150k words of decisions, rejected alternatives and incident history that today only an agent reading whole files can find.

title: Stop projecting AI-hint prose into globals.{sh,ps1} and gate it
goal: Law 8 The generated resolvers carry VALUES, not documentation, and a unit's narrative has exactly one home.
acceptance_criteria: both resolvers shrink by ~1.1 MB combined, gate 157 is green, and appending one `MIOS_UNITS_TEST_COMMENT='# AI-hint: x'` line turns it red.

details.what_how: `automation/lib/globals.sh` and `globals.ps1` each carry 129 `AI-hint:` blocks as `MIOS_UNITS_*_COMMENT` environment-variable VALUES -- 1.19 MB of generated shell/PowerShell that is mostly prose, and the fourth home of every unit sentence (unit file -> `mios.toml [units.*]`, 182 tables / 115 `comment=` keys -> globals.sh -> globals.ps1), which is why both resolvers show exactly 486 narrative lines. Teach `tools/render-globals.py` to skip the `comment` key, re-run `bash tools/sync-generated.sh`, and add drift check 157 `check_no_generated_prose_in_resolvers` asserting zero `AI-hint:` and zero `MIOS_UNITS_[A-Z0-9_]*_COMMENT=` in either file. THIS MUST LAND AFTER task_2231 wave D: the unit narrative it deletes must already be harvested from the unit files, or the projection removes the only copy some readers have.
details.why: one stale sentence about `hermes-agent.service` on `:8642` currently exists in four materially different file formats, and fixing the doc fixes none of the others.

title: Retire the comment graveyard and the unified-knowledge dump
goal: D-10 No documentation surface is built by scraping deleted comments or dumping whole files.
acceptance_criteria: all three are gone, `ai-bootstrap.sh` and `sync-wiki.py` consume the audit JSON, and the markdown corpus drops from 9.99 MB to ~5.9 MB.

details.what_how: `usr/share/doc/mios/knowledge/recovered_comments.md` is 4.13 MB / 60,019 lines / 801 file sections -- 42% of the entire markdown corpus -- and `tools/lib/extract_comments.py:29-34` builds it from git diffs by harvesting ONLY DELETED comment lines: a graveyard, stale by construction, whose first entry is already contradicted by `automation/lib/globals.sh:170`. Run `mios-manual audit --corpus-extra` over it ONCE as a rescue pass, harvest anything classified MIGRATE whose target still resolves, then delete both the file and the extractor. Separately retire `tools/generate-unified-knowledge.py`: it walks CWD not `--root`, has no CLI and no `--check`, its category taxonomy keys off `specs/core`/`specs/memory`/`evals/` (only `specs/engineering` exists, so nearly everything lands in "other" and never enters the semantic index), its extension filter is inverted so any dotfile sweeps in, and its three-regex redaction misses `sk-proj-*`, `ghp_*`, PEM and JWT while the output is copied into agent-visible scratch. Replace the RAG-seeding use with `mios-manual audit --json`.
details.why: 42% of the doc corpus by bytes is mechanically-transcribed deleted comments shipped into `/usr/share/doc/`, and one commit has already re-duplicated part of it back into manual.md.

title: Collapse the 69-copy boilerplate, the 3 duplicate doc pairs, and mios-codebase-index's rival taggability
goal: D-11 Every fact has one home; the codebase is quickly auditable because there is nothing to cross-check.
acceptance_criteria: the boilerplate exists once; the three pairs are one file each with a pointer; `mios-codebase-index` defines zero taggability constants of its own and its file count matches `mios-ai-hint-coverage`'s denominator.

details.what_how: (1) The two-paragraph "MiOS is one thing built two ways at once ... `bootc upgrade` it like a `git pull` ... `bootc rollback` it like a Ctrl-Z" block appears in 69 files (~48 KB) and every copy drifts independently -- some name GNOME 50, some name ports, some name lanes. Replace all 69 with `<!-- MIOS-GEN:boilerplate:what-mios-is -->` rendered from the single authored chapter. (2) De-duplicate the three near-verbatim doc pairs (~116 KB, already diverging on facts): `docs/design/doc-mios-metal.md` <-> `concepts/mios-metal-architecture.md`, `doc-container-runtime.md` <-> `concepts/container-os-runtime.md`, `doc-foss-upstream.md` <-> `concepts/foss-upstream-map.md`; add `docs/design/README.md` marking that tree process-only, the pattern `usr/share/doc/mios/archive/` already models. (3) Delete `mios-codebase-index`'s private `EXT`/`BASENAMES`/`SKIP_DIR`/`SKIP_SUFFIX` -- a second, already-diverged definition of the corpus that includes `.json` (which mios-ai-tag explicitly skips as comment-less) -- and import `mios-ai-tag` through the same `SourceFileLoader` shim `mios-ai-hint-coverage` uses.
details.why: "fewer, more feature-complete components" is unachievable while three tools disagree about which files exist and one paragraph has 69 independently-drifting copies.

title: Port the comment lexer hot path to Rust behind the unchanged mios-manual CLI

title: Project [blade.requires] to k3s nodeSelectors and Pacemaker location rules
goal: E-18 One SSOT declaration drives every consumer -- a placement constraint stops being hand-maintained in two scheduler dialects.

details.what_how: `[blade.requires]` maps a service to the capabilities it needs and `[blade.archetypes]` maps an archetype to the capabilities it grants; today only systemd `ConditionPathExists` gating consumes them. title: Give every GPU-gated service a CPU fallback lane so placement never refuses
acceptance_criteria: a GPU-gated unit started on a GPU-less blade serves `/v1/models` from the CPU lane; the caller's endpoint is unchanged; a drift-check asserts every `gpu-serving` requirement declares a fallback.

details.what_how: ADR-0017 D2: a service requiring `gpu-serving` that lands on a GPU-less blade must start its CPU lane rather than fail to schedule. title: Implement local-first failover ordering with asymmetric anti-flap dwell
acceptance_criteria: killing a service restarts it in place without a migration event; killing the machine migrates it; a link flapping faster than `recover_dwell_s` produces exactly one migration, not one per flap.

details.what_how: Implement `[blade.placement].failover_order = ["local","localhost","cluster"]` and the `[blade.collapse]` dwell values. A failed workload is retried in place before the cluster is asked to allocate it elsewhere. Release back to the mesh uses `recover_dwell_s`, which is deliberately several times `dwell_s`.
details.why: most failures are a crashed process on a healthy machine where a restart is the whole fix; migrating first turns two seconds into a cold start and possibly a volume move.

title: Add origin-node id and logical timestamp to the pgvector schema
acceptance_criteria: every row in the six tables carries origin + logical timestamp; existing rows are backfilled; a drift-check fails if `[blade.reconcile].enabled = true` while any of the six lacks the columns.

details.what_how: ADR-0017 D5 states the merge rules are not implementable without provenance on every row. Add an origin-node id and a logical timestamp to `knowledge`, `agent_memory`, `event`, `session`, `scratch` and `config_kv` in `usr/share/mios/postgres/schema-init.sql`, backfilled to the local node for existing rows. details.why: enabling divergence without provenance produces a merge nobody can compute and silent data loss on rejoin.

title: Implement the per-class reconcile rules, with config_kv conflicts raised to the operator
acceptance_criteria: a simulated partition with writes on both sides reconciles losslessly for the first three classes; a divergent `config_kv` key blocks reconcile and names the conflicting keys; only then may `enabled` flip to true.

details.what_how: Implement the four merge classes from ADR-0017 D5: union-by-hash for `knowledge`/embeddings, append-ordered for `agent_memory`/`event`, last-writer-wins for `session`/`scratch`, and conflict-is-error for `config_kv`. The last is deliberately NOT auto-merged -- a `config_kv` divergence surfaces to the operator, because config is intent and silently picking a winner lets a partition change policy.
details.why: the availability choice in ADR-0017 is only affordable if each data class has a fixed rule decided in advance; a vague rule is how this design fails.

acceptance_criteria: with the blade unreachable, the dashboard states "blade unreachable" and `/v1` returns a named error rather than a model failure; greenboot records the check without failing the boot.

## WS-THESIS -- the four open campaigns

MiOS is a proof of an idea (ROADMAP.md, "What this roadmap is evidence for").
These four close the gaps between what the thesis claims and what the tree can
demonstrate. Nothing new starts until they do.

title: Audit every drift-check for falsifiability
goal: Thesis part 1 -- a check that cannot fail asserts a proof that does not exist, so a hollow gate does not merely miss bugs, it falsifies the claim that drift is mechanically impossible.
acceptance_criteria: every dispatched check has a negative test that demonstrably fails on an injected defect; `check_negative_coverage` passes with an empty exempt list, or each exemption states why the check is structurally unfalsifiable.

details.what_how: For each of the 181 checks in `automation/98-drift-checks.sh`, establish the edit that makes it RED and prove it with a negative test. Known failure shapes to look for, all found in this tree: violations written to stderr while the wrapper captures stdout; `2>&1` placed after a heredoc delimiter where it redirects nothing; inverted polarity (`if out=$(...)` instead of `if ! out=...`); a target path or generator that does not exist so `regen_and_diff` returns Skip; an empty SSOT list so the loop runs zero times; a `-maxdepth` that cannot reach the files the check names.
details.why: four hollow checks were found in a single session, three of them shipped green for weeks. The count of undiscovered ones is unknown, which is the problem.

title: Make stale-ref measurement enforceable, then enforce it
goal: `[docs].max_stale_refs` becomes a real ceiling instead of a number nobody measured.
acceptance_criteria: every remaining dangling token is a genuine broken reference, the ceiling equals that count, a negative test breaches it, and `check_docs_ratchet` fails when the count rises.

statements: `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_docs_ratchet` reports `stale-refs=N/N` with the ceiling equal to the measurement, AND adding an `# AI-related: automation/no-such-file.sh` line to a tracked file turns it red.

details.what_how: The measurement was broken outright -- the allowlist was matched with `re.search`, where `C:\mios-bootstrap\Get-MiOS.ps1` is an invalid pattern (bad escape `\m`), so the checker crashed rather than counted. Repaired, it reported 1101, of which 376 hits were `/usr/bin/env` from shebang lines. `RefIndex` now knows runtime path prefixes, units and containers declared in mios.toml, `emit_exports()` keys and `referenced_names.txt`, leaving 446. Drive that to a number that is entirely real: resolve pod/short names (`mios-hermes`, `mios-gpu`, `mios-heavy`, `mios-resolver`), decide whether `/etc/mios/*` runtime-created paths are references or state, and treat `mios-bootstrap` as the sibling repo it is. THEN set the ceiling and remove the "(reported, not a ceiling)" qualifier.
details.why: a ceiling of 0 sat in the SSOT next to a measurement that had never once completed. Both a fake zero and an enshrined 446 of noise are the same defect.
details.do_not: raise [docs].max_stale_refs to whatever the count happens to be without first making every remaining hit a genuine broken reference. A ceiling over noise measures nothing.

title: Strengthen check_negatives_are_effective past substring matching
goal: The gate that judges negative tests must judge behaviour, not spelling.
acceptance_criteria: a test that only logs a check name, and a test whose assertion sits beyond 1500 characters, are both reported; the existing suite still passes.

statements: a test that only mentions a check name in a `log` line, and a test whose assertion sits beyond 1500 characters, are BOTH reported by `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_negatives_are_effective`.

details.what_how: It currently reads the first 1500 characters of each `test_*` function and requires the substring `die`/`return 1`/`FAIL`/`exit 1` AND one of `98-drift-checks.sh`/`97-ssot-lint.sh`/`check_`. A test satisfies it by MENTIONING a check name in a log line while never invoking one, and a test longer than 1500 characters can hide its assertion past the window. Replace with a structural check: parse each function, require at least one invocation of a gate entry point, and require that invocation to appear in a condition whose failure branch calls `die`.
details.why: this is the gate guarding every other gate's evidence. Substring matching makes it the easiest one in the tree to satisfy without meaning it.
details.do_not: keep substring matching. A test satisfied by spelling `check_x` in a log line is the defect, not the fix.

title: Lint for detections discarded by pipefail
goal: No test can pass its detector and fail its harness.
acceptance_criteria: the lint is a registered gate with a negative test, and every piped grep in the suite either reads from `echo`/`printf` or is converted to capture-then-match.

statements: `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_pipefail_grep_lint` goes red when a `somecmd | grep -q x` is added to tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh, and green when removed.

details.what_how: `tests/drift-gate-negatives.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail`. `generator | grep -q "msg"` returns the GENERATOR's exit status when it exits non-zero -- which a validation failure always does -- so a matched grep is thrown away and the test dies reporting the opposite of what happened. This cost a CI round trip on `test_bake_unresolved_image`. Add a lint that flags any `| grep` in the suite whose left side is not `echo`/`printf`, and require the captured-variable form.
details.why: the harness silently inverting a result is indistinguishable from a broken detector, and sends the reader to the wrong file.
details.do_not: exempt the suite's own `echo ... | grep` lines by name. Match on the LEFT side being echo/printf, so a new piped grep is caught automatically.

title: Audit every hash-keyed round trip for silent row loss
goal: No generator drops data by deduplicating on a content hash.
acceptance_criteria: each round trip either preserves row count or asserts it, and a test writes a fixture containing duplicates and proves nothing is lost.

statements: a fixture containing duplicate rows survives a read-write round trip: row count in equals row count out, asserted by a test.

details.what_how: `mios-manual`'s `_read_ledger` keyed rows by `sha12`; identical comment text is common, so reading `manual-corpus.tsv` into that dict and writing `list(rows.values())` back turned 9669 rows into 8564. A harvest followed by a commit without `sync-generated` would have deleted 1105 census rows. Fixed by a `Ledger` type that keeps every row. Now sweep: any place a generated artifact is read into a dict keyed by hash, name, or path-stem and written back. Check `tools/generate-names-registry.py`, `automation/lib/mios_var_closure.py`, `tools/generate-pod-quadlets.py`, `tools/generate-bake-plan.py` and the manifest writers.
details.why: the loss is invisible: the file still parses, the gate still passes, and a ninth of the evidence is gone.
details.do_not: eyeball the row count once. mios-manual's ledger lost 1105 of 9669 rows silently and the file still parsed -- only an asserted count catches it.

title: Prove every generator is host-independent
goal: A generated artifact must not depend on which machine regenerated it.
acceptance_criteria: the differential gate is registered with a negative test, and every generator produces byte-identical output under both configurations.

statements: `bash automation/98-drift-checks.sh check_generator_host_parity` goes red when any `fnmatchcase` is reverted to `fnmatch`, and every generator emits byte-identical output under forced case-sensitive and case-insensitive git config.

details.what_how: `usr/share/doc/mios/reference/tool-index.md` was reported out of sync by CI while clean locally, through several rounds of guessing. `fnmatch.fnmatch` normalises case on Windows, so `usr/libexec/mios/mios-*` matched `MiOS-Mon.py` there and not on Linux, and each side reverted the other. Seven call sites are now `fnmatchcase`. Sweep the remaining host-dependent inputs: `os.walk` ordering, `sorted()` on paths without an explicit key, locale-dependent case folding, `os.sep` leaking into content, line endings written by generators, and any use of the filesystem where `git ls-files` is meant. Then add a gate that regenerates under a forced-case-insensitive and a forced-case-sensitive configuration and requires identical bytes.
details.why: an artifact whose content depends on the host cannot be gated at all -- CI and the contributor take turns reverting each other and neither is wrong.
details.do_not: fix only the fnmatch instances. os.walk ordering, bare sorted(), locale case-folding, os.sep leaking into content and filesystem-vs-git-tracked are the same class.
